```text
1	# dev
2	
3	A thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
4	
5	It exists to stop four things collapsing into one:
6	
7	```
8	git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
9	git worktree    a disposable local checkout
10	herdr / tmux / zellij
11	                a per-host live runtime
12	dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
13	```
14	
15	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. `dev` persists
16	human intent Git cannot answer—task **state/owner/next action/context**, stable
17	asset identity, catalog metadata, repository quick notes, and experiment
18	lifecycle—and a few explicit machine policies such as generated SSH/fleet
19	fragments. OpenSSH, Git, and each remote machine remain authoritative for the
20	connection, code, and host-local state they own. Live Git status stays live;
21	logical size measurements are explicitly disposable cache.
22	
23	## The problem
24	
25	When a terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only record of what you are
26	working on, nothing can ever be closed: closing a workspace loses the thread.
27	So the sidebar grows to thirty-odd entries and stops being scannable, which
28	defeats the point of having one.
29	
30	The fix is not discipline. It is giving "what am I working on" a home outside
31	the runtime, so closing a session is just closing a session.
32	
33	Bare `dev` opens an interactive dashboard when it has a terminal, and prints
34	the plain listing when piped — so `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as
35	expected.
36	
37	```
38	$ dev ls
39	   TASK                   STATE  REPO       BRANCH                    GIT   AGE  SESSION       NEXT
40	🔥 token refresh          HOT    atp-sipui  fix/gx-security-recovery  ↑2 ●  2h   herdr:working add the regression test
41	🌤 orderbook experiment   WARM   trading    exp/orderbook-v2          clean 6d   —             compare against the baseline
42	❄️ settings redesign      COLD   website    feat/settings             clean 3w   —             pick up after the API lands
43	```
44	
45	## Install
46	
47	### Homebrew (macOS)
48	
49	```bash
50	brew install daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli
51	dev config init  # detects this machine's repo roots and writes a config
52	```
53	
54	The formula installs the `dev` binary plus bash, zsh and fish completions. It
55	does not write into your home directory or install the bundled agent skill.
56	Each stable release updates the tap automatically. A Homebrew-owned `dev`
57	never self-replaces: `dev upgrade` delegates to the matching `brew upgrade`
58	command, which preserves Homebrew's install records, linking, rollback, and cleanup.
59	Maintainers can retry or backfill formula publication for an existing release
60	with `gh workflow run publish-homebrew.yml -f version=vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`.
61	
62	### Scoop (Windows)
63	
64	```powershell
65	scoop bucket add dev-cli https://github.com/daviddwlee84/scoop-bucket
66	scoop install dev-cli
67	```
68	
69	The manifest for each release is also attached to the GitHub release as
70	`dev-cli.json` if you prefer `scoop install <url>`.
71	
72	### Go or source
73	
74	```bash
75	go install github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/cmd/dev@latest
76	# Pin @v0.2.7 instead when you need a reproducible install.
77	# Or from a checkout: make install  # also installs the bundled agent skill
78	```
79	
80	Every release also publishes `darwin/arm64`, `darwin/amd64`, `linux/amd64`,
81	`linux/arm64` (`.tar.gz`) and `windows/amd64`, `windows/arm64` (`.zip`) archives
82	with a `SHA256SUMS` file, so a binary can be verified without a Go toolchain.
83	
84	To find out whether the binary you have is current, and to update it:
85	
86	```bash
87	dev version           # what this build is, and whether it is a published release
88	dev version --check    # also ask GitHub for the newest release (cached for a day)
89	dev doctor            # reports the running version, install owner/path, and PATH collisions
90	dev upgrade --check    # report whether a newer release exists
91	dev upgrade            # delegate to its owner, or verify and replace a standalone binary
92	```
93	
94	`dev upgrade` replaces the binary in place only for a standalone install. If
95	Homebrew, Scoop or `go install` owns the file, it runs that tool's upgrade
96	command instead; release automation advances the Homebrew tap so that command
97	can see every stable tag. Once a day an interactive `dev` command prints a one-line hint
98	when a newer release is cached; set `[update] check = false` in `config.toml`
99	(or export `DEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`) to silence it. Every network call here is
100	either explicit or a best-effort background refresh — `dev --version` and
101	`dev doctor` stay local and work offline.
102	
103	### Windows
104	
105	`dev` builds and runs on Windows, and core commands work. Native Windows support
106	also covers SSH host discovery/managed fragments, OpenSSH key generation and
107	bootstrap ACL checks, and fleet transport to POSIX or Windows OpenSSH servers.
108	Windows fleet targets launch only dev's allowlisted hidden helpers through an
109	encoded PowerShell command. There is no tmux, Zellij or Herdr on the controller,
110	so `dev` uses the no-multiplexer backend (it prints a `cd` directive the shell
111	wrapper consumes). Use the PowerShell wrapper:
112	
113	```powershell
114	Invoke-Expression (& dev shell-init powershell | Out-String)
115	```
116	
117	For a non-Homebrew install, generate completion files wherever your shell loads
118	them:
119	
120	```bash
121	mkdir -p ~/.zfunc ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions ~/.config/fish/completions
122	dev completion zsh  > ~/.zfunc/_dev
123	dev completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/dev
124	dev completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/dev.fish
125	```
126	
127	Tab completion includes commands and flags plus local tasks, repositories,
128	worktrees, statically discovered SSH aliases, help topics, and bundled gitignore
129	templates. Completion never queries a forge, runs `ssh`/`Match exec`, or touches
130	the network.
131	
132	Add the directory-changing wrapper to your shell rc file:
133	
134	```bash
135	eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # zsh
136	eval "$(dev shell-init bash)"     # bash
137	dev shell-init fish | source      # fish
138	```
139	
140	```powershell
141	Invoke-Expression (& dev shell-init powershell | Out-String)   # PowerShell
142	```
143	
144	A child process cannot change its parent's working directory, so the wrapper
145	passes directory changes back through a private, child-only file descriptor
146	while leaving normal stdout/stderr connected to the terminal. That preserves
147	the interactive TUI and normal pipe behavior.
148	
149	The agent skill is an explicit, optional post-install step:
150	
151	```bash
152	dev skill install
153	dev skill list --all    # native project/global inventory across repositories
154	dev mcp list --all     # static, sanitized MCP declarations for five agents
155	dev doctor             # what works on this machine, and what degrades
156	```
157	
158	Only **git** is required at runtime. The system `ssh` client enables SSH host
159	inspection, probing, bootstrap, and fleet transport; `ssh-keygen` enables public
160	companion derivation and key generation; PowerShell is needed on a Windows
161	OpenSSH target. `herdr`, `tmux`, `zellij`, `gh`, `glab`, and Azure CLI each enable
162	other capabilities and degrade cleanly when absent. `dev doctor` checks these
163	capabilities locally without evaluating an alias or contacting a host.
164	
165	## Onboard OpenSSH hosts
166	
167	OpenSSH remains the source of truth. Dev can read exact aliases from the active
168	user Include closure, but it mutates only canonical files in its dedicated
169	namespace and never rewrites a foreign `Host` block.
170	
171	Run the one-time initialization as a report, then explicitly apply it:
172	
173	```bash
174	dev ssh init                         # exact plan; no write
175	dev ssh init --apply                 # confirm interactively
176	dev ssh init --apply --yes           # confirm the local plan non-interactively
177	```
178	
179	The only root directive dev installs is `Include ~/.ssh/dev.d/*.conf`, placed
180	before the first `Host` or `Match`. If root metadata or the managed namespace
181	cannot be preserved safely, init makes no change and gives manual placement
182	guidance.
183	
184	Discover aliases statically, then cross into OpenSSH evaluation only when needed:
185	
186	```bash
187	dev ssh list                         # no ssh, resolver, Match exec, agent, or network
188	dev ssh list --format tsv            # alias/status/owner/source/line/fleet rows
189	dev ssh list --json                  # one schema-versioned object
190	dev ssh show lab                     # definitions plus plain `ssh -G lab`
191	dev ssh probe lab                    # one fresh BatchMode login, sharing disabled
192	```
193	
194	`show` includes system configuration because it runs plain `ssh -G`; configured
195	`Match exec` and resolver behavior may run. `probe` preserves the user's host-key
196	and known-hosts policy. Static discovery reports incomplete/dynamic closure and
197	conflicts instead of calling uncertain aliases usable.
198	
199	Setup is one idempotent command for new managed aliases, existing managed
200	aliases, and read-only foreign aliases:
201	
202	```bash
203	dev ssh setup lab --hostname 192.0.2.20 --config-only
204	dev ssh setup lab --hostname 192.0.2.20 --key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 \
205	  --target-os posix
206	dev ssh setup lab --key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 --target-os posix --fleet
207	dev ssh setup winlab --hostname 198.51.100.30 --generate-key \
208	  --key-path ~/.ssh/id_winlab --target-os windows --fleet
209	dev ssh setup lab --key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 --target-os posix --dry-run
210	```
211	
212	Full setup requires exactly one explicit `--key` or `--generate-key`. Generated
213	keys are Ed25519; noninteractive generation additionally requires
214	`--no-passphrase`, while an interactive `ssh-keygen` owns hidden passphrase
215	prompts. A private/security-key identity passed to `--key` must have a validated
216	`.pub` companion; dev may derive a missing public companion with confirmed
217	`ssh-keygen -y`, but never reads or transfers private bytes.
218	
219	ProxyJump routes are resolved outermost-first. Use repeatable
220	`--hop-os alias=posix|windows` when a hop's OS cannot be determined; already
221	working jumps are not modified unless `--install-on-working-jump` is explicit.
222	Windows standard accounts use their profile `authorized_keys`; administrator
223	group accounts require `--windows-admin-authorized-keys` before dev can target
224	the shared administrators file, and elevation can still require manual action.
225	
226	`--fleet` is a separate, explicit durable decision. Dev writes a generated
227	`remotes.d/ssh-<alias>.toml` only after exact-key proof and a second fresh
228	ordinary alias login succeed. A remote without `dev` still onboards successfully
229	and later appears as fleet `no-dev`. Failures after local setup retain valid
230	config/generated keys and report partial or unknown remote state so rerunning can
231	converge.
232	
233	Removal is deliberately narrower than setup:
234	
235	```bash
236	dev ssh remove lab --dry-run
237	dev ssh remove lab --yes
238	dev ssh remove lab --fleet --yes       # remove generated fleet fragment first
239	```
240	
241	It removes only a structurally valid dev-owned host fragment and, with explicit
242	`--fleet`, its generated fleet fragment. It never removes the shared Include,
243	local keys, `known_hosts` entries, or remote `authorized_keys`; key rotation and
244	revocation remain manual. A primary user-authored `remotes.toml` reference blocks
245	removal until it is changed with `dev fleet config edit`.
246	
247	| Data | Authority / owner | Durability |
248	|---|---|---|
249	| root SSH config and foreign Includes/`Host` blocks | user + OpenSSH | durable; read-only to dev except the exact managed Include |
250	| `~/.ssh/dev.d/<alias>.conf` | `dev ssh setup/remove` | durable managed connection fragment |
251	| private/public key pair | user + native `ssh-keygen` | durable; generated assets are retained, never removed by `ssh remove` |
252	| primary `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/remotes.toml` | user via `dev fleet config init/edit` | durable, byte-for-byte user-authored |
253	| sibling `remotes.d/ssh-<alias>.toml` | `dev ssh setup/remove --fleet` | durable generated fleet registration |
254	| remote paths/tasks/runtime | that remote machine's `dev` | host-local authority, never copied into controller config |
255	| `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/fleet/` | controller cache | disposable snapshot |
256	
257	See [SSH host onboarding](docs/guides/ssh-hosts.md) and
258	[Remote repository fleet](docs/guides/remote-fleet.md) for full contracts.
259	
260	## Create, clone, or set up a repository
261	
262	Repository bootstrap works from any directory. Bare `dev repo new` opens an
263	interactive flow that chooses the destination under the configured
264	`project_root`, previews the setup, and confirms before writing anything:
265	
266	```bash
267	dev repo new                                  # interactive new-repository flow
268	dev repo create api --preset agent-ready      # `create` is an alias for `new`
269	dev repo new owner/api                        # clear clone reference: preserve history/origin
270	dev repo new api --template owner/starters --template-subdir go/service
271	dev repo new api --check-in stage -m "chore: initialize api"
272	dev repo clone owner/api                      # owner/name or a Git URL
273	dev repo setup . --preset agent-ready         # add the same setup to an existing repo
274	```
275	
276	`repo new NAME` keeps the small scripted default: `main`, README, and an
277	initial commit. When the argument is clearly a Git URL, local Git path, or
278	owner/name, however, `new`/`create` routes to the clone flow and preserves the
279	source history and configured remote; `repo clone` remains the explicit spelling.
280	Clone can optionally apply a preset after the checkout exists, while `repo setup` repeat-safely merges native
281	initializers and preset files into a repository you already have. Custom hooks
282	and skill setup remain responsible for their own idempotency. Use `--dry-run`
283	to inspect the available plan without mutating the target repository.
284	
285	`repo new` can also start from a content snapshot rather than an empty tree.
286	`--template` accepts a local directory/repository, Git URL, or owner/name;
287	`--template-ref` selects a branch, tag, or commit, and `--template-subdir`
288	selects a confined folder within the source. The snapshot becomes a fresh Git
289	history: source `.git` metadata is never copied, template files win scaffold
290	conflicts, regular-file modes are preserved, and traversal, symlinks, and
291	special files fail before the destination is created. A local Git working tree
292	without `--template-ref` includes existing tracked files plus untracked,
293	non-ignored files; Git-ignored files are omitted. A non-Git directory snapshots
294	its complete current tree. The same `template`, `template_ref`, and
295	`template_subdir` keys can live in a preset, which makes one starter catalog
296	repository with a preset per subfolder practical.
297	
298	Human confirmation and dry-run plans preview the selected file paths (with a
299	bounded list) and warn when the source is a live local snapshot rather than a
300	commit. URL userinfo is removed from rendered summaries and errors. Filesystem
301	walking and writes are confined relative to held `os.Root` handles, and source
302	file content is read from the handle that was validated instead of reopening a
303	mutable path.
304	
305	Bootstrap's check-in is explicit:
306	
307	| `--check-in` | Result |
308	|---|---|
309	| `commit` | stage and commit generated files, then permit commit-dependent publishing/hooks |
310	| `stage` | `git add -A` for human review, but do not commit or run `after_commit` hooks |
311	| `none` | leave generated files unstaged and uncommitted |
312	| `auto` | for `repo new`, use the preset's compatible default; clone/setup otherwise perform no automatic check-in |
313	
314	`--message` supplies the commit or staged draft message. In `stage` mode dev
315	best-effort writes the worktree-local `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT`; current lazygit
316	uses it to prefill lowercase `c`. An existing different draft is preserved with
317	a warning. This is a lazygit integration detail, not Git `commit.template`.
318	Staged setup cannot create an upstream or use the worktree-creating `start`
319	handoff; review and commit it first. The existing `repo setup --commit` remains
320	a compatibility spelling for `--check-in=commit`. If the lazygit draft cannot
321	be written, dev reports a warning but keeps the successfully staged index for
322	manual review and commit.
323	
324	The built-in `agent-ready` preset adds a starter `AGENTS.md`, a common
325	`.gitignore` section, and project-scoped Claude plans. If selected, the optional
326	`agent-history-hygiene` and `project-knowledge-harness` skills are installed and
327	dev's reviewed built-in initializers create the pre-commit/gitleaks and
328	TODO/backlog/pitfalls surfaces during bootstrap; setup does not wait for a later
329	agent to happen to trigger the skill. The history initializer also ensures
330	`.specstory/.gitignore` contains rules for SpecStory's machine-local
331	`.project.json` and generated `statistics.json`—not `.specstory/history/`, which
332	remains part of the review trail. Existing custom ignore content and file mode
333	are preserved; only missing managed rules are appended. Skills with the same
334	source and identical agent targets are sent to the installer together, while
335	each skill's declared setup still runs in its own phase. Presets may also declare
336	typed inputs, repository-contained file templates, and ordered
337	`before_commit`/`after_commit`/`after_remote` hooks.
338	
339	When `gh` or `glab` is installed and authenticated, the wizard can create a
340	GitHub or GitLab upstream using the local repository name and description,
341	choose its namespace and visibility, add `origin`, and optionally push the
342	initial/current branch. Local-only is the default and published repos
343	default private. A forge or push failure leaves the local repository and any
344	already-created upstream intact, with recovery information instead of deleting
345	work.
346	
347	TTY text fields in the repository, task-start, and finish wizards support
348	inline insertion plus Left/Right, Home/End, Delete/Backspace, and Esc/Ctrl-C
349	cancellation. Arrow keys are interpreted by the editor rather than appearing
350	as literal `^[[C`/`^[[D`; piped and buffered non-TTY input keeps its existing
351	line-oriented behavior.
352	
353	The no-argument new-repository wizard places detailed file, template, input,
354	and skill questions behind a default-no “Customize preset and template
355	options?” gate. The normal `agent-ready` path therefore uses its reviewed
356	defaults; answer yes when you want to override individual choices.
357	
358	The final handoff is explicit:
359	
360	| Handoff | Result |
361	|---|---|
362	| `stay` | print the result and leave the shell where it is |
363	| `cd` | enter the repository through the trusted `shell-init` wrapper |
364	| `open` | open the configured Herdr/tmux/Zellij runtime; fall back to `cd` when runtime is `none` |
365	| `start` | continue into the existing `dev start` task wizard with this repository fixed |
366	
367	Neither bootstrap nor a default `dev start` launches a coding agent. They
368	prepare the repository, checkout, and optional runtime surface. An explicit
369	worktree-mode `dev start --run '<shell command>'` can dispatch one command to a
370	new first-class Herdr root pane; it never chooses an agent profile or permission
371	mode on the user's behalf.
372	
373	Global custom presets live in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/scaffolds.toml`. A project
374	may commit `.dev-cli/config.toml` for allowlisted worktree/setup wizard defaults
375	and `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml` for project presets, templates, hooks, and skill
376	setup. Project files cannot override host paths, runtime selection, forge
377	inventory, credentials, state, stats, update policy, or TUI policy. Legacy
378	`.dev.toml` worktree settings remain readable; the `.dev-cli` files win when
379	both are present. See [Commands and configuration](docs/reference/commands-config.md#repository-bootstrap)
380	for the schema, precedence, and executable-config trust boundary.
381	
382	## The lifecycle
383	
384	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
385	|---|---|---|---|
386	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
387	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session normally closed | back within days |
388	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
389	| ✅ `done` | merged | may still be open | **MERGED**, waiting for external retirement |
390	
391	READY/MERGED/RETIRED are derived milestones, not new persisted task states.
392	An agent prepares and exits; an external coordinator integrates and retires it.
393	
394	```bash
395	dev start                                            # interactive managed-task wizard
396	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main     # non-interactive fast path → hot
397	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main \
398	  --run 'specstory run codex -c "codex"' --focus      # dispatch, then switch to the exact new pane
399	dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip      # → warm; self-runtime stays alive until exit
400	dev park --cold --push                               # → cold, only from outside the target runtime
401	dev resume "token refresh"                           # → hot, rebuilt if needed
402	dev flow api                                          # preview the repository lifecycle, plan first
403	
404	dev prepare --session claude:<uuid> --plan .claude/plans/task.md
405	dev artifact finalize --intent <id> --writer-stopped # manual post-wrapper proof
406	dev done                                             # TTY finish wizard
407	dev done --ff                                        # → done/MERGED; runtime + worktree kept
408	dev retire "token refresh" --delete-branch           # external close/wait/remove → RETIRED
409	
410	dev done --pr                                        # open review; keep task/worktree
411	dev done --merged --base-ref origin/main             # verify commit-preserving merge
412	dev sweep                                            # report drift and cleanup-pending work
413	dev sweep --merged-worktrees                         # from main: audit contained linked worktrees
414	dev sweep --merged-worktrees --apply                 # confirm each safe retirement
415	```
416	
417	On a TTY, bare `dev done` reports branch ahead/behind and classifies every
418	staged, unstaged and untracked path against the base before offering
419	commit-all, discard-all or cancel. Unique discard requires typing `DROP`;
420	scripts use `--dirty=commit --message ...` or `--dirty=discard --yes`.
421	
422	### A task does not have to mean a worktree
423	
424	Choose the lightest mode that preserves the boundary you need:
425	
426	```bash
427	# No task, no branch, no worktree: just open the canonical repo for ad-hoc work.
428	dev repo open api
429	
430	# Track a quick change directly on the branch already checked out (usually main).
431	dev start api --task "fix typo" --direct
432	
433	# Use a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout, but no linked worktree.
434	dev start api --task "small feature" --branch-only --base main
435	
436	# Default: independent branch + worktree, provisioned and runtime-opened.
437	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main
438	```
439	
440	Direct work can be parked WARM and resumed, but cannot go COLD because the
441	canonical checkout cannot be removed. `dev done` on a clean direct task needs
442	no `--ff` or `--pr`: the work is already on its destination branch.
443	
444	Start direct for one change stream, then create a normal worktree task later
445	when real parallelism appears. A new worktree starts from committed HEAD; dirty
446	main changes are deliberately not smuggled into it, so checkpoint first when
447	the parallel task depends on them.
448	
449	### Guarded Git transactions
450	
451	`dev git` wraps only operations that need durable receipts or failure recovery;
452	it does not replace ordinary Git aliases:
453	
454	```bash
455	dev git uncommit              # soft reset; save old OID/message receipt
456	dev git recommit              # commit -C the receipt, then clear it
457	dev git pull-rebase           # exact stash OID + --index restore; never stash@{0}
458	dev git amend-all             # add -A + amend --no-edit, with normal hooks
459	dev git amend-all --exclude-agent-artifacts
460	dev git setup --print         # print optional aliases; never edit config
461	```
462	
463	Published commit rewrites require `--rewrite-published`. `amend-all` includes
464	agent artifacts by default only when a project scanner is present (or the user
465	explicitly accepts `--allow-unscanned-artifacts`).
466	
467	For automation, `dev start … --json` emits one pure creation object with absolute
468	paths and transient runtime facts. Only a newly created first-class Herdr
469	worktree with a non-empty exact `root_pane_id` is a launch target; reuse,
470	fallback, Tmux, none, or missing pane data fails closed. Worktree starts use the
471	same `repo/branch` label as `dev wt create` and pins the Git-derived parent
472	checkout with Herdr `--cwd`, preserving native nested repository/worktree
473	grouping without separate provenance metadata.
474	
475	For a human one-liner, `--run '<shell command>'` uses that same exact-pane proof
476	and sends the command to the new worktree's interactive shell. It is incompatible
477	with `--json`, `--direct`, `--branch-only`, and non-Herdr runtimes. It only
478	confirms dispatch, never waits for command completion or reports its exit code;
479	add `--focus` when the caller should switch or attach after dispatch.
480	
481	Herdr-aware writer claims—`start --direct`, `start --branch-only`, and
482	`resume`—reject another recognized agent in the same canonical Git worktree.
483	Every state, including `idle`, `done`, and `unknown`, is occupied. Pure
484	`repo open`, `wt open`, and TUI Enter reuse/focus the live owner without
485	claiming another writer. `--allow-shared-checkout` is only for explicitly
486	coordinated disjoint ownership; normal new-worktree creation remains allowed.
487	
488	Task runtime handles carry their backend name and are validated against live
489	checkout coverage before reuse or close. Destructive cleanup additionally
490	resolves every covering pane. A caller inside the target, a mixed workspace, or
491	a working/blocked/waiting agent always stops retirement; unknown status needs an
492	external `--close-unknown`. `dev done` never closes or removes anything.
493	
494	### Repository flow preview
495	
496	`dev flow [repo]` is a preview-labelled, full-screen, TTY-only state-machine UI.
497	It is independent of the six-view `dev tui` dashboard. From a canonical or linked
498	checkout, `dev flow` resolves the canonical repository and focuses that exact
499	surface; outside Git it opens a filterable repository picker. An explicit
500	`dev flow api` overrides cwd.
501	
502	The left panel is the union of Git's registered worktrees and task records that
503	have no checkout, including normal COLD and DONE tasks. Rows are labelled
504	`canonical`, `managed`, `unmanaged`, `harness`, `task-only`, or `conflict`.
505	Canonical worktrees are never removable; harness-owned and ambiguous/conflicting
506	rows have no destructive path. An exact unmanaged linked checkout can be
507	**Adopted** by creating task metadata without changing Git bytes, or **Removed**
508	only when clean and safe; removal is non-force and always preserves the branch.
509	
510	The center distinguishes persisted task intent (`HOT`, `WARM`, `COLD`, `DONE`)
511	from observed Git/worktree/runtime/artifact facts. Unknown, failed, loading, or
512	stale evidence never becomes a false clean/closed fact. `runtime=none` leaves
513	session occupancy unobserved, but the local Git/task snapshot can still be fresh;
514	metadata-only adoption then remains WARM.
515	
516	The right panel offers concrete mode/state actions: warm/cold park, resume,
517	direct or fast-forward completion, review handoff, verified-merge completion,
518	and DONE retirement where legal. The preview deliberately excludes dirty
519	commit/discard, WIP checkpoint, shared-writer, ownership-takeover, and unknown-
520	runtime overrides. A blocked plan shows its exact evidence, remediation, and CLI
521	fallback; existing command flags remain available outside the preview.
522	
523	```text
524	j/k or ↑/↓       choose a surface      h/l or ←/→     choose an action
525	Tab/Shift-Tab    move panel focus       Enter          build a plan, never apply
526	r                reload local facts    R              Fetch refs / Query review / Both
527	Esc              back out              ?              evidence and key help
528	```
529	
530	A READY plan shows ordered conditions/effects, retained resources, network and
531	destructive markers, and its exact PlanID. Press `y` only for a non-typed plan;
532	typed branch deletion requires the displayed token and `Enter`. Apply locks and
533	reloads the task revision plus repository, checkout, refs, runtime, artifact, and
534	remote identities. Any change rejects the stale plan before a new effect. Once an
535	effect starts, quit/refresh waits for the retained step ledger; partial success
536	means completed effects remain completed and recovery is explicit.
537	
538	Startup and `r` never fetch or query a forge. `R` runs only the confirmed choice
539	and keeps its evidence in this TUI run: named ref OIDs plus portable review
540	existence, open/draft/merged/closed state, URL, provider, and observation time.
541	It does not query review decisions or checks. Completion records DONE while
542	keeping branch, checkout, and runtime resources; Retire cleans them from outside
543	the target. Raw Git and configured external tools remain outside these
544	`dev`-mediated locks and safety checks.
545	
546	### The dashboard
547	
548	Bare `dev` (or `dev tui`) opens seven lists, switched with `tab`:
549	
550	- **TASKS** — the change streams dev is tracking. What am I working on.
551	- **REPOS** — durable repositories under the scan roots, with branch, dirty
552	  state, owned size, runtime, worktrees and task tally. What do I have here.
553	- **FLEET** — repository and activity facts from configured remote machines.
554	  The TUI hides this machine by default because REPOS already shows it; `a`
555	  includes local rows. Enter opens the remote checkout through Herdr when
556	  possible, then SSH. `dev fleet list` continues to include this machine.
557	- **TRY** — dated scratch experiments, including non-Git folders, with durable
558	  tags/notes and explicit active/deprecated/archived/graduated state.
559	- **REMOTE** — repositories visible through authenticated forge CLIs, including
560	  configured Azure DevOps projects, marked when a local repo or Try exists.
561	  What can I open or clone.
562	- **SKILLS** — native project/global agent-skill inventory across canonical
563	  repositories plus the startup checkout, with local presence/integrity and an
564	  explicitly checked upstream freshness state.
565	- **MCP** — sanitized static MCP declarations for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor,
566	  Gemini CLI, and OpenCode. It reports configured scopes and resolves only
567	  Claude's documented project-approval settings; it does not claim connection
568	  health or a generally effective merged runtime configuration.
569	
570	The first view is constructed before runtime auto-detection, project-root lookup,
571	cache decoding, shell-based tool checks, or the optional release refresh can
572	finish. TASKS, REPOS, and TRY then publish independently from one shared local
573	load cycle; REMOTE, FLEET, SKILLS, and MCP remain lazy. A cached REMOTE/FLEET snapshot
574	is immediately usable but is tracked separately from a current live result.
575	Every requested view has its own generation, so `r` cancels the old read, a late
576	result cannot replace a newer one, a failed refresh keeps usable rows visible,
577	and a successful empty result clears obsolete rows. Warning-only SKILLS/MCP
578	source diagnostics keep a fresh partial snapshot, and a visible dependent view
579	resumes automatically after a failed REPOS generation is repaired and reloaded.
580	
581	TASKS, REPOS and TRY use the same services as their non-interactive commands.
582	Git-backed Tries appear in TRY rather than being duplicated in REPOS; REMOTE
583	still knows that local checkout exists. The repo list matters on day one: with
584	forty repositories and no tasks recorded yet, a task-only dashboard would just
585	be empty.
586	
587	Navigation is vim-style, arrows alongside:
588	
589	```
590	j k        move                 ctrl+d ctrl+u   half a page
591	g G        top / bottom         h l / tab       previous / next view
592	/          filter as you type   esc             clear, then quit
593	```
594	
595	`enter` opens a selected row only when its checkout is currently valid. Inside Herdr/tmux/Zellij it
596	switches the current client; outside it exits the dashboard and attaches to
597	the target session. A COLD worktree task requires `dev resume`; a missing or
598	unregistered worktree requires `dev sweep` first so artifacts can be salvaged
599	before the task is resumed or reaped. A wide TASKS table includes `REPO`; its
600	compact layout keeps repository/path in the selected detail pane. In TASKS, `p`
601	parks and prompts for the next action and `c` edits it. In REPOS, `enter` is pure ad-hoc open,
602	`space` expands linked worktrees inline, `m` edits repository tags/summary,
603	`s` starts an isolated worktree task, and `d` starts a tracked direct task.
604	On TASKS and REPOS, `n` quick-adds a repository thought and `N` opens its notes
605	overlay. Expanded children carry their own Git/session/task state and can be
606	opened directly. In TRY, `n` creates or clones an experiment;
607	`space` opens mark/deprecate/archive/restore/graduate actions; `a` includes
608	retained history. SKILLS reuses the accepted REPOS snapshot, adds the exact
609	startup worktree when distinct, and scans global paths once. `a` opens the
610	upstream interactive installer, `c` performs the opt-in read-only network check
611	after the local snapshot has loaded, and `u` confirms before updating only the
612	selected lock-managed skill in that row's checkout. Source checks hash Git object
613	bytes without running checkout filters; non-ASCII provider folder hashes that
614	cannot be reproduced portably remain unverifiable. Mutations skip repository-local
615	PATH shims and are serialized across `dev` processes. `r` reloads local state
616	without checking the network. MCP only filters/reloads static declarations; it
617	never starts a server or helper. `?` opens the complete context-sensitive key map. That makes
618	the branch/worktree and lifecycle costs explicit rather than silently applying
619	them to every directory.
620	
621	For a one-run startup/readiness trace, name an absolute file that does not exist:
622	
623	```bash
624	DEV_TUI_TRACE=/tmp/dev-tui-trace.json dev
625	```
626	
627	The file is created with private permissions after the alternate screen is
628	restored and before a selected runtime is activated. It contains only a bounded,
629	versioned list of relative microsecond timings, aggregate row counts, and
630	categorical view/generation/outcome fields; it never includes project names,
631	paths, commands, key values,
632	URLs, runtime handles, or raw errors, and it is not written to `stats.db` or sent
633	anywhere. `tui.initial_view_returned` means the Bubble Tea view string was built,
634	not that a terminal rasterized it. Cache acceptance, live snapshot acceptance,
635	and load completion are separate events; there is no artificial “all tabs ready”
636	event because REMOTE, FLEET, SKILLS, and MCP may never be visited.
637	
638	REPOS also has an agent-handoff copy menu. Press `y`, then `y` for contextual
639	Markdown, `p` for the checkout path, `b` for the branch, `s` for runtime/agent
640	sessions, or `w` for every linked-worktree path. Parent `yy` includes the whole
641	repo; child `yy` includes only that worktree. The same full context is
642	pipe-friendly outside the TUI:
643	
644	```bash
645	dev repo context api
646	dev repo context          # current repo, even from inside a linked worktree
647	dev repo context --json   # additive schema-v1 automation contract
648	dev repo context --refresh  # live forge + configured fleet probes
649	```
650	
651	Local checkout, Git, task, worktree, and runtime facts are always collected live
652	without network access. External forge/fleet facts come from private caches by
653	default and retain their source, age, freshness, completeness, and errors; only
654	`--refresh` performs network probes. Readiness stays split by checkout, task, and
655	worktree scope, and unknown evidence is never rendered as clean.
656	
657	**External tools are configured, not fixed.** They run through your shell in
658	the selected row's checkout; the dashboard suspends and redraws when they exit:
659	
660	```toml
661	[[tui.tools]]
662	key  = "L"
663	name = "lazygit"
664	run  = "lazygit"
665	
666	[[tui.tools]]
667	key  = "V"
668	name = "nvim"
669	run  = "nvim ."
670	
671	[[tui.tools]]
672	key  = "B"
673	name = "vibe"
674	run  = "vibe"
675	interactive = true     # load + evaluate aliases/functions after shell rc
676	
677	[[tui.tools]]
678	key  = "P"
679	name = "plans here"
680	run  = "claude-plans-here"
681	interactive = true
682	```
683	
684	`dev config init` writes the defaults out in full rather than leaving them
685	implicit, and `dev tui tools` shows what is bound here and whether each one is
686	actually installed. The dashboard checks bindings in a bounded background load
687	after its first view; unresolved or missing programs are not offered, and
688	rendering never launches a login shell. A tool cannot take a key the dashboard
689	already uses; dev reports the clash on load.
690	
691	REMOTE loads lazily, so dashboard startup never waits on the network. Its
692	private XDG cache is decoded after the first view and contains the complete
693	paginated inventory. Fresh rows are reused without network access; stale rows
694	remain searchable while a background refresh runs. Cache payload size and
695	identity fields are validated before display, and a source fingerprint binds
696	the cache to configured GH/GL hosts and Azure targets so another endpoint is
697	never seeded automatically. GitLab inventory passes `GITLAB_HOST` (or
698	`GLAB_HOST`, default `gitlab.com`) explicitly, so the current repository cannot
699	silently select another authenticated host. A successful empty provider inventory replaces old
700	rows instead of resurrecting them later. `r` forces a
701	refresh of all configured forge providers.
702	`/` searches provider, owner/name, visibility and description; `vis:private`
703	is an exact visibility filter. Enter opens a local clone,
704	and `c` confirms before cloning an absent repo into `project_root`. The same
705	inventory is available without the full-screen UI via `dev repo remote [query]`;
706	`--cached` is its instant/offline form.
707	
708	SKILLS also loads lazily. Native reads use the versioned `skills@1.5.23`
709	77-agent path registry and lock files; they never start Node, `skills`, or `npx`.
710	Use `dev skill list --all` for canonical repositories, `--repo` for one checkout,
711	and `--check` only when a remote freshness check is wanted; checks hash Git object
712	bytes without checkout filters. MCP is separately available through `dev mcp
713	list`; it reads five agents' static config formats, resolves only Claude's documented
714	project approvals, and redacts secret-bearing values before producing rows or JSON.
715	
716	Azure DevOps Services inventory is opt-in because `az repos list` requires an
717	organization and team project. Repeat the target for every project wanted:
718	
719	```toml
720	[[forge.azure_devops]]
721	organization = "https://dev.azure.com/acme"
722	project = "Platform"
723	```
724	
725	Install Azure CLI's `azure-devops` extension and authenticate with Azure CLI.
726	`dev` does not install extensions, change Azure defaults or store credentials.
727	Azure DevOps Server/on-premises is not supported by the official extension.
728	REPOS has an explicit LIVE column (`herdr:working`, `herdr:idle`, …). Multiple
729	repo sessions collapse to `herdr:N live`; expanding the repo reveals each
730	checkout and whether its session is live or closed. External and turn-scoped
731	agent worktrees remain visible with `(external)` / `(ephemeral)` labels, so the
732	tree always reconciles with WT. `H` opens the selected repo's
733	one-year activity heatmap and `e` edits config. Returning from the editor, or
734	pressing `r`, reparses config and reloads data/tool bindings without restarting
735	the TUI; a runtime-backend change is reported as requiring restart.
736	
737	REPOS includes `LATEST`, defined as the newest dirty-file mtime, commit time, or
738	task update, plus asynchronous `SIZE`. Size is portable logical bytes:
739	
740	- `checkout_bytes` excludes only the checkout root's `.git` entry.
741	- `private_git_bytes` belongs only to this checkout and is included in
742	  `owned_bytes`, the table value.
743	- `shared_git_bytes` is shown separately and never charged to every linked
744	  worktree. `+S` means shared Git storage exists but is not reclaimable with
745	  that row.
746	
747	Measurements stream in after the first frame, use a 10-minute private XDG cache,
748	and can be forced with `r`; unreadable subtrees display a lower bound (`≥`).
749	Columns and default ordering are config:
750	
751	```toml
752	[tui.repos]
753	columns = ["repo", "branch", "git", "size", "live", "latest", "worktrees", "tasks"]
754	sort = "activity"       # activity | latest | name | git | size | tasks
755	reverse = false
756	```
757	
758	In REPOS and TRY, `O` cycles sort and `R` reverses it. Structured filters include
759	`tag:important`, `remote:none`, `size:>1GiB`, `phase:deprecated` and
760	`where:archived` where applicable. Local repo probes run with bounded
761	parallelism, and the alternate screen appears before they finish.
762	
763	See `dev help tui` for the full key map.
764	
765	### Experiments and local-data risk
766	
767	`dev try <name>` keeps its low-friction positional grammar. Lifecycle management
768	uses the separate plural group, so `dev try archive` still means "open/create a
769	Try named archive":
770	
771	```bash
772	dev tries list --json                 # active, present Tries
773	dev tries list --all --sizes          # include deprecated/archived history
774	dev tries mark redis --add important --note "compare streams"
775	dev tries deprecate redis             # intent only; files do not move
776	dev tries archive redis               # reversible move under tries_root/.dev
777	dev tries restore redis
778	dev tries graduate redis -c Infra     # same service as dev graduate
779	```
780	
781	Archive is organization, **not disk reclamation**: it moves the directory to a
782	hidden location on the same filesystem and preserves its stable catalog ID.
783	Phase 1 deliberately has no `evict`, recursive delete, or automatic remote
784	backup. Safe local removal needs repo-wide ref verification and remains a
785	follow-up rather than treating "has a remote" as proof.
786	
787	The catalog also exposes personal repository tags/notes (`dev repo mark`). To
788	find local Git state at risk before any future cleanup:
789	
790	```bash
791	dev repo list --no-remote              # no configured remotes at all
792	dev repo list --local-only             # at least one branch lacks remote upstream
793	dev repo list --multiple-remotes
794	dev repo list --multiple-upstreams     # branches track more than one remote
795	dev repo list --sizes --json           # full remotes/branches/size contract
796	```
797	
798	`no remote`, `local-only branch`, and `multiple upstreams` are distinct facts.
799	They do not claim whether commit objects are present remotely; a future reclaim
800	preflight must compare every local head/tag/note/stash against actual remote
801	refs immediately before removal.
802	
803	Going cold is safe because **the branch is the identity and the directory is a
804	cache**. `dev park --cold` refuses unless the branch is pushed, and `dev resume`
805	rebuilds the checkout from `origin/<branch>`. Once that holds, the local
806	filesystem stops being a graveyard of half-finished worktrees.
807	
808	## Rich Git state
809	
810	Every inventory surface uses the same compact, starship-like status:
811	
812	```text
813	⇕⇡3⇣2 =1 +4 !2 ?3
814	```
815	
816	- `⇡` / `⇣` / `⇕` — ahead, behind, diverged
817	- `=` — conflicted paths
818	- `+` — staged paths
819	- `!` — unstaged paths
820	- `?` — untracked paths
821	
822	`dev status` and the TUI detail pane also show the unique changed-path total
823	and type breakdown (added / modified / deleted / renamed). A path staged and
824	then modified again is one changed path, while correctly appearing in both the
825	staged and unstaged categories. JSON output exposes all counts separately.
826	`dev status` also renders independent local `checkout`, `task`, and `worktree`
827	readiness outcomes. It never contacts a forge/fleet host, and unavailable task,
828	runtime, or worktree evidence remains indeterminate instead of looking clean.
829	
830	## Worktree ownership
831	
832	Three mechanisms create git worktrees. `dev` takes one position so nobody has
833	to improvise:
834	
835	| Kind | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
836	|---|---|---|---|
837	| Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff | **`dev`** | `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<slug>` | until external `dev retire` |
838	| Harness-owned turn-scoped subagent isolation | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` (gitignored) | owned by that harness; no history-relocation guarantee |
839	| `herdr worktree create` | **not used** — `dev` runs `git worktree add`, then `herdr worktree open --path …` | — | — |
840	
841	**If code, history, or plans must remain reviewable—or you may return tomorrow—
842	use `dev`.**
843	
844	`dev` does not delegate placement to herdr because the path policy has to hold
845	on machines without herdr. It creates the checkout with plain git and asks
846	herdr only to *open* it — which still surfaces it in the sidebar grouped under
847	its parent repo with its own branch and ahead/behind row.
848	
849	`dev` refuses to create a worktree inside a repository: a checkout nested in
850	another checkout makes every indexer, file watcher and `rg` run see a second
851	copy of the tree.
852	
853	### Provisioning
854	
855	A worktree is a clean checkout — no `node_modules`, no `.venv`, no `.env`.
856	Without provisioning, every new one starts broken. `dev` copies the gitignored
857	files you list, optionally symlinks heavy directories, and runs a setup
858	command detected from the lockfiles. Included files must remain the same
859	regular file through open; source swaps and symlinked destination parents are
860	refused, existing destinations are reported as skipped, and contents are never
861	logged:
862	
863	```toml
864	[worktree]
865	include     = [".env", ".env.local"]   # only files that are ALSO gitignored
866	link        = []                       # opt-in; sharing node_modules is risky
867	post_create = "auto"                   # uv.lock → uv sync, package-lock.json → npm ci, …
868	
869	# Separate opt-in export policy for dev fleet files; worktree.include is never
870	# inherited for off-machine transfer.
871	[local_files]
872	include = [".env", ".mcp/**"]
873	```
874	
875	`[local_files]` may be committed in `.dev-cli/config.toml`, but it only proposes
876	portable patterns. Nothing leaves the host until an explicit `dev fleet files`
877	invocation selects one target; every pattern expands locally to sorted exact
878	paths before the protocol begins.
879	
880	`.claude/settings.local.json` is not a universal include. Add that exact path
881	only for an explicitly selected sticky/plain-Claude launcher and verify it
882	arrives. `claude-copilot-once` preserves an existing Copilot pin and creates/
883	removes only one it added when absent; its proxy must already run.
884	`codex-copilot-once` injects backend via CLI and may auto-start its proxy path,
885	so neither wrapper needs the copied file.
886	
887	**Copy or reinstall?** Reinstalling is always correct but can take minutes;
888	copying is fast but only sound for dependency trees carrying no absolute paths.
889	That is a per-ecosystem fact, not a preference, so dev knows it:
890	
891	```toml
892	[worktree]
893	strategy = "reinstall"      # reinstall | copy | link | skip
894	
895	[worktree.strategies]
896	node = "copy"               # node_modules copies soundly
897	```
898	
899	Asking to copy a virtualenv is refused with the reason — it bakes its own
900	absolute path into `pyvenv.cfg` and `bin/activate` — and narrowed back to
901	reinstalling rather than silently producing a broken checkout.
902	
903	`dev wt plan` shows exactly what a new worktree of a repository would get:
904	which project types were detected, which tools are missing, and every file and
905	command involved. `dev wt plan --write` seeds
906	`<repo>/.dev-cli/config.toml` from it, so
907	a project can commit its own setup and every machine provisions the same way.
908	
909	```
910	$ dev wt plan
911	PROJECT  MANAGER  FROM               DEPENDENCIES  TOOL
912	node     npm      package-lock.json  node_modules  installed
913	python   uv       uv.lock            .venv         installed
914	
915	   ACTION    WHAT          WHY
916	✓  copy      .env          gitignored, so the checkout would not have it
917	✓  copy-dir  node_modules  npm dependencies, copied instead of reinstalling
918	✓  run       uv sync       uv.lock detected
919	```
920

955	### Repository quick notes
956	
957	Quick thoughts live beside repos in dev state, not inside each checkout:
958	
959	```bash
960	dev note add "try event subscription" --repo api --tag idea
961	dev note list api
962	dev note search "event subscription"
963	dev note edit <id-or-prefix>
964	dev note delete <id-or-prefix>
965	```
966	
967	An ID prefix must be unique and at least eight characters.
968	
969	In TASKS/REPOS, `n` quick-adds and `N` opens a browse/search/edit/delete overlay.
970	A REMOTE row supports notes only after it has a local clone; TRY keeps `n` for
971	creating experiments. Add `notes` to `[tui.repos].columns` for the count;
972	repository detail shows count/latest preview, and task detail does so when the
973	task resolves to a loaded repository row.
974	
975	Durable Markdown lives under configured
976	`paths.state_dir/notes/<catalog-id>/`, defaulting to
977	`$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes/<catalog-id>/`. The catalog ID survives path moves,
978	symlink indexes and linked worktrees. `dev` does not synchronize notes or
979	catalog state; synchronize both when attachments must travel between hosts.
980	The disposable `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db` is only an FTS index:
981	
982	```bash
983	dev cache clear notes                    # Markdown remains
984	dev note search "event"                 # index rebuilds automatically
985	dev note reindex                         # explicit rebuild
986	```
987	
988	`repo mark --note` remains a single catalog summary and is not overwritten.
989	`dev repo list --json` always includes `notes.count` and adds
990	`latest_id`/`latest_preview`/`latest_updated` when a latest note exists;
991	`dev note list/search/show --json` expose complete note records. Structured task
992	systems such as td/beads remain optional future adapters rather than creating
993	dot-folders automatically.
994	
995	### Machine-wide summary
996	
997	`dev summary` is the quick context dump for the whole machine. It combines
998	repositories, present Tries, worktrees, tasks, runtime sessions, recovery risk,
999	latest activity and one recent commit into Markdown suitable for a person or an
1000	agent. Active work is expanded; quiet projects remain in a compact index:
1001	
1002	```bash
1003	dev summary
1004	dev summary --attention
1005	dev summary --detail compact --no-runtime
1006	dev summary --recent-commits 3 --sizes
1007	dev summary --json | jq '.projects[] | select(.active)'
1008	dev summary | opencode run "give me a quick view of this machine"
1009	```
1010	
1011	Use `dev journal` when the question has a date range, and `dev repo context`
1012	when one repository needs every checkout/task/session detail.
1013	
1014	### Development journal
1015	
1016	`dev journal` emits Markdown designed for a daily/weekly report or direct input
1017	to another tool. It does not invoke an AI agent or persist the generated prose:
1018	
1019	```bash
1020	dev journal
1021	dev journal --since 7d --metrics
1022	dev journal --since 3mo --granularity branch
1023	dev journal --author teammate@example.com --since 30d --json
1024	dev journal --since 7d | opencode run "summarize this development journal"
1025	```
1026	
1027	The default `auto` view expands commits, keeping complete repo/branch totals
1028	while limiting details to the newest 100 commits. Pass `--max-commits 0` for an
1029	unabridged report. The current user's report can also include source-separated
1030	session/WakaTime evidence, task intent and dirty linked worktrees whose latest
1031	file mtime falls inside the requested calendar-day range.
1032	
1033	`dev stats` draws a contribution-style heatmap from two sources: a sampler
1034	watching live agent sessions (the only way to count time spent reading and
1035	debugging, including sessions in external linked worktrees), and git history (which backfills the past and survives losing the
1036	database). WakaTime can be imported alongside for editor time.
1037	
1038	```bash
1039	dev stats backfill                          # seed all repos from git history
1040	dev stats backfill --repo api               # seed only one repo
1041	dev stats sample --interval 5m              # from cron, every five minutes
1042	dev stats import-wakatime                   # optional
1043	dev stats path                              # durable SQLite location
1044	dev stats clear --repo api                  # guarded selective deletion
1045	```
1046	
1047	In the TUI, select a repo and press `H`. If it has no data, `b` backfills only
1048	that repo and refreshes the panel; `r` merely rereads existing stats data.
1049	
1050	Stats are **data**, not cache: session samples and WakaTime imports may not be
1051	reconstructible. They live at `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/stats.db` and clearing them
1052	requires a scope plus confirmation (`--repo`, `--source`, or `--all`).
1053	Regenerable data lives separately:
1054	
1055	```bash
1056	dev cache list
1057	dev cache path
1058	dev cache clear remote
1059	dev cache clear notes          # FTS only; Markdown remains
1060	dev cache clear fleet
1061	dev cache clear size
1062	dev cache clear gitignore
1063	dev cache clear licenses
1064	dev cache clear all
1065	```
1066	
1067	Those remove only regenerable files under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/` (remote
1068	inventory, note FTS, size measurements and gitignore templates) and never touch
1069	`stats.db`, durable note Markdown or project data.
1070	
1071	## Bootstrapping an existing machine
1072	
1073	There is nothing to migrate for ordinary use: `dev` discovers repositories
1074	below `scan_roots` and at exact `repo_paths`, and never requires a particular physical layout.
1075	When you want a recursive audit or a curated navigation layer, bootstrap is the
1076	explicit path:
1077	
1078	```bash
1079	dev bootstrap ~/code /mnt/work                    # recursive report, no changes
1080	dev bootstrap ~/code --json                       # machine-readable inventory
1081	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects           # plan a flat symlink catalog
1082	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects --apply   # create only the ready links
1083	dev bootstrap ~/old --move ~/Projects             # plan physical moves
1084	```
1085	
1086	The scanner classifies canonical checkouts, linked worktrees, bare repositories
1087	and symlink aliases, deduplicating by Git common-directory identity rather than
1088	path.
1089	
1090	**A symlink index is the default recommendation.** It gives a flat,
1091	metadata-aware navigation root while every physical repository stays exactly
1092	where it was. Put the index first in `scan_roots` and that alias becomes the UI;
1093	normal discovery follows direct repo symlinks and deduplicates index + physical
1094	paths.
1095	
1096	Physical move exists, but refuses dirty repos, linked worktrees anywhere in the
1097	clone, live sessions, a current shell inside, aliases that would break,
1098	occupied destinations and cross-filesystem renames. A plan with any blocked row
1099	moves nothing. `--config-out` writes a fresh config for the resulting root
1100	without silently rewriting the user's current one. See `dev help bootstrap`.
1101	
1102	## Adopting work in flight
1103	
1104	There is nothing to migrate. `dev` discovers repositories wherever your scan
1105	roots point and **never moves, renames or deletes anything** you already have.
1106	`dev config init` probes the conventional locations — `~/Documents/Program`,
1107	`~/src`, `~/code`, a `GHQ_ROOT`, and so on — counts the repositories in each,
1108	and writes only the ones that exist:
1109	
1110	```
1111	$ dev config init
1112	wrote ~/.config/dev/config.toml
1113	
1114	Detected:
1115	ROOT                 REPOS  ROLE
1116	~/Documents/Program  40     scan root, new projects land here
1117	~/src                16     scan root
1118	```
1119	
1120	Repositories are discovered; *tasks* are not. `dev adopt` finds the work
1121	already in flight — linked worktrees from any tool, live runtime sessions, and
1122	local branches ahead of the default branch — and offers to record it. It skips
1123	branches already merged, and the turn-scoped worktrees an agent harness cleans
1124	up itself:
1125	
1126	```bash
1127	dev adopt            # report only
1128	dev adopt --apply    # record as tasks; nothing on disk changes
1129	```
1130	
1131	A worktree you already have somewhere else keeps working exactly as it did —
1132	`dev` records the path git reports rather than relocating it. Full detail in
1133	`dev help adopting`.
1134	
1135	## .gitignore
1136	
1137	```bash
1138	dev gitignore                 # detect the languages from the repo's files
1139	dev gitignore python node     # or say so explicitly
1140	dev gitignore --offline       # cached and bundled templates only
1141	```
1142	
1143	Language sections come from [GitHub's templates](https://github.com/github/gitignore),
1144	fetched once and cached. On top of those it adds what no language template
1145	covers: the host platform's junk files, editor state, local env files, and
1146	ephemeral coding-agent state such as linked worktrees and local settings.
1147	Review artifacts such as SpecStory histories and agent plans remain trackable
1148	unless you add your own ignore rule for them.
1149	
1150	Everything it writes goes inside a delimited block, so re-running updates that
1151	block and leaves rules you added by hand alone.
1152	
1153	## Configuration
1154	
1155	`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml`. Write a commented starter with
1156	`dev config init`; see the effective settings with `dev config show`; open the
1157	actual file in `$VISUAL` / `$EDITOR` with either form:
1158	
1159	```bash
1160	dev edit
1161	dev config edit
1162	DEV_EDITOR=unused dev edit --editor "code --wait"   # explicit override
1163	```
1164	
1165	If the file does not exist, `edit` generates the machine-detected starter first
1166	rather than opening an empty file. Resolution is `--editor` → `$VISUAL` →
1167	`$EDITOR` → `nvim` → `vim` → `vi`.
1168	
1169	Every path is configurable, because the right answer depends on the machine —
1170	a faster volume, a different naming convention:
1171	
1172	```toml
1173	[paths]
1174	scan_roots    = ["~/Documents/Program", "~/src/tries"]
1175	repo_paths    = ["~/.local/share/chezmoi"] # exact repos outside useful roots
1176	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/worktrees"
1177	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}/{{branch|slug}}"
1178	state_dir     = "~/.local/share/dev"        # point at a git repo to sync it
1179	```
1180	
1181	`state_dir/tasks/*.toml` stores task intent; `state_dir/assets/*.toml` stores
1182	stable repository/Try identity, tags, one metadata summary, experiment
1183	lifecycle and per-host locations; `state_dir/notes/<catalog-id>/*.md` stores
1184	multiple repository quick notes; `state_dir/artifact-intents/v1/*.json` stores
1185	versioned post-writer handoffs and commit receipts. Git status, logical byte
1186	counts and `.specstory/statistics.json` are derived rather than durable review
1187	history. Size cache lives in `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/sizes-v1.json` and is safe to
1188	delete.
1189	
1190	Template variables: `worktree_root`, `repo`, `repo_path`, `branch`, `category`,
1191	`host`, `date`. Filters: `|slug` (`feat/auth/x` → `feat-auth-x`), `|lower`,
1192	`|base`. A typo in a variable name fails at load, not as a directory literally
1193	named `{{rep}}`.
1194	
1195	A flat project layout is already first-class — it needs no migration and no
1196	special mode:
1197	
1198	```toml
1199	[paths]
1200	scan_roots   = ["~/code"]
1201	project_root = "~/code"       # repo new/clone/graduate land at ~/code/<repo>
1202	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/wt"
1203	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}--{{branch|slug}}"
1204	```
1205	
1206	Omit `--category` and canonical repos stay flat. Categories are metadata the
1207	user may choose, never a directory structure dev imposes.
1208	
1209	## Multiple machines
1210	
1211	Do not sync worktrees or runtime state. Sync branches, and let the remote be
1212	the handoff boundary:
1213	
1214	```bash
1215	dev park --cold --push      # on the machine holding the work
1216	dev resume <task> --fetch   # on the machine picking it up
1217	```
1218	
1219	`dev` records an owner host per task and refuses to resume someone else's
1220	without `--force`. Two machines committing to one branch is the reliable way
1221	to produce a conflict here; the ownership check prevents it.
1222	
1223	Configure fleet profiles separately from each machine's host-local paths. The
1224	primary file remains user-authored:
1225	
1226	```toml
1227	# $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/remotes.toml
1228	schema_version = 1
1229	
1230	[defaults]
1231	connect_timeout = "15s"
1232	command_timeout = "5m"
1233	cache_ttl = "15m"
1234	max_parallel = 4
1235	dev_path = "auto"
1236	
1237	[[hosts]]
1238	<<<<<<< HEAD
1239	name = "lab"
1240	ssh_alias = "lab"
1241	remote_os = "posix"       # omitted still means posix
1242	```
1243	
1244	An explicit `dev ssh setup winlab --key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 --target-os windows --fleet`
1245	instead generates the strict sibling
1246	`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/remotes.d/ssh-winlab.toml`; it never rewrites the primary
1247	file. A custom `--remotes /srv/dev/lab.toml` uses `/srv/dev/lab.d`, while a path
1248	without `.toml` appends `.d`. Fleet loads the primary first, then validated
1249	managed fragments in lexical order, and applies defaults after the merge.
1250	Duplicate names always fail. Existing primary profiles may share an SSH alias,
1251	but any alias collision involving a generated fragment fails closed.
1252	
1253	`dev fleet config show` prints the effective merge, redacts plaintext passwords,
1254	and identifies generated hosts with instructions to use `dev ssh setup/remove`.
1255	`dev fleet config edit` and the FLEET TUI `e` key continue to open only primary
1256	`remotes.toml`; generated registrations have a different owner.
1257	=======
1258	name = "jingle"
1259	ssh_alias = "jingle-235"
1260	# After `dev fleet machine-id jingle` and independent verification:
1261	machine_id = "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000"
1262	```
1263	
1264	The UUID pin is optional for read-only inventory and diagnostics, but mandatory
1265	for `fleet files --apply`. `dev fleet machine-id <host>` is itself read-only: it
1266	shows the observed UUID, the configured value, and `unpinned`, `match`, or
1267	`mismatch`; it never edits `remotes.toml`.
1268	>>>>>>> 7b0ec57925f80dc61c6d197ebf5213f7ea39919b
1269	
1270	`dev fleet list` runs each machine's own `dev`, so its XDG config and paths stay
1271	host-local. `remote_os = "windows"` selects the encoded, argument-allowlisted
1272	PowerShell launcher and Windows target-path semantics; POSIX is the compatible
1273	default and uses the existing shell launcher. Missing `dev` installations are
1274	reported as `no-dev`; unreachable hosts can fall back to the last private XDG
1275	snapshot. Cache identity includes the complete SSH endpoint, including port and
1276	remote OS. The FLEET TUI view reuses the accepted REPOS snapshot for its local
1277	host instead of scanning twice, but exposes configured remote hosts by default;
1278	press `a` to include this machine. Enter opens a selected path through remote
1279	Herdr when available, otherwise through an SSH login shell. The CLI output
1280	remains the full local-plus-remote inventory.
1281	
1282	`dev fleet sync <repo> --push` publishes the clean source branch, then fetches
1283	matching clones by normalized Git remote identity. Only a clean checkout of the
1284	same branch that is strictly behind is fast-forwarded. Dirty, ahead, divergent,
1285	ambiguous and unreachable targets remain untouched and make the command fail;
1286	hosts without `dev` or without that repository are explicitly ignored.
1287	
1288	`dev fleet files [repo-or-path] --to <host>` is a separate, one-shot channel for
1289	explicit ignored local files:
1290	
1291	```bash
1292	dev fleet files api --to jingle                    # plan only
1293	dev fleet files api --to jingle --apply --yes      # create absent files
1294	dev fleet files api --to jingle --replace --apply  # separately authorize conflicts
1295	```
1296	
1297	The source and target must already be the same fetch identity, attached branch,
1298	and exact commit. Both Git configurations must classify every selected path as
1299	untracked and ignored. Only bounded regular files are accepted (128 files,
1300	8 MiB each, 32 MiB total at most); directories, links, special files, nested
1301	repositories, `.git`, and submodule boundaries fail closed. The target reopens
1302	held roots, journals before staging payloads, publishes owner-only files
1303	atomically, and rolls back changed files on failure. It deliberately leaves
1304	unprovably-owned empty parent directories rather than risk deleting another
1305	process's replacement. Native Windows payload apply remains disabled.
1306	
1307	This is **not** repository/task ownership transfer, backup, restore, or clone
1308	eviction. It does not clone a missing target, switch branches, run provisioning,
1309	synchronize catalog/notes, delete source files, watch for changes, or merge in
1310	both directions.
1311	
1312	## The agent skill
1313	
1314	`dev` ships the agent skill that documents it, embedded in the binary — the
1315	same pattern `herdr --skill` uses. A skill vendored separately drifts from the
1316	tool it describes, and an agent reading a stale command list is worse than one
1317	reading none.
1318	
1319	```bash
1320	dev skill list                 # current checkout + global native inventory
1321	dev skill list --all --check --json
1322	dev skill list --repo api --project
1323	dev skill add                  # interactive wizard for daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills
1324	dev skill update project-knowledge-harness --global --yes
1325	dev skill install              # → ~/.agents/skills/dev-cli, symlinked into ~/.claude/skills
1326	dev mcp list --all --json      # sanitized static declarations; never health probes
1327	dev --skill                    # print it, for a dotfiles installer to sync
1328	dev skill sync                 # regenerate the command reference from the command tree
1329	dev skill sync --check         # fail if it has drifted — wire into CI
1330	```
1331	
1332	`dev skill add [package]` is only a shortcut into the upstream interactive
1333	wizard. It never selects all skills or agents. Listing is native and never runs
1334	`skills`, npm, `npx`, or project code. Add/update are explicit actions, require
1335	a directly installed `skills` executable, and may access the network; `dev` skips
1336	repository-local `node_modules` candidates, rejects source-less update locks, and
1337	serializes provider processes. `--all` scans each configured canonical checkout
1338	once, while the TUI also includes its exact startup linked worktree when distinct
1339	and reads global paths once. Freshness hashes Git object bytes without checkout
1340	filters or autocrlf transforms; locale-dependent non-ASCII folder hashes stay
1341	unverifiable. Lock hashes describe upstream freshness, not installed-file integrity;
1342	only the embedded `dev-cli` skill can verify that every bundled file matches
1343	(additional user files are ignored).
1344	
1345	`dev mcp list` inventories declarations from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini
1346	CLI, and OpenCode files. It keeps scopes separate, honors absolute
1347	`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, retains exact Claude local project keys, and resolves only
1348	Claude's documented user/project/local/managed project approvals. It deliberately
1349	omits runtime health, a generally effective merged configuration, plugin caches,
1350	hosted connectors, remote organization config, and command-line-only config.
1351	Environment/header/OAuth values, raw arguments, URL credentials, and indirect file
1352	contents never enter normalized output; only safe reference names and finite
1353	policy/count facts remain.
1354	
1355	The skill defers to the companion `git-workflow` skill for commit conventions,
1356	SemVer and branch naming rather than restating them. It owns what is new: the
1357	worktree ownership rule, the task lifecycle, and how `dev` and herdr divide
1358	responsibility.
1359	
1360	## Development
1361	
1362	```bash
1363	make          # fmt, vet, test, build
1364	make test
1365	make e2e      # drives the real binary through a full lifecycle in a sandbox
1366	make skill-check
1367	```
1368	
1369	Tests build throwaway repositories under `t.TempDir()` via
1370	`internal/gitx/gittest`, and the runtime adapters share one contract suite that
1371	skips backends not installed on the machine — so the suite is meaningful in CI
1372	(where only the null backend exists) and locally (where herdr and tmux do).
