```text
1	---
2	description: Render deterministic operational context or hand it to a configured local agent without creating a second lifecycle authority.
3	authority: project
4	status: stable
5	verified_on: 2026-09-02
6	tested_with: OpenCode 1.18.25
7	---
8	
9	# Prompt handoffs
10	
11	`dev prompt` collects a read-only snapshot, places it in a built-in prompt, and
12	either prints it or gives it to a local command you configured. It is a context
13	handoff, not an agent loop, scheduler, permission manager, or lifecycle engine.
14	
15	!!! info "Freshness"
16	    **Authority:** `internal/cli/prompt_command.go`, `internal/promptkit`,
17	    `internal/handoff`, `internal/closeout`, and `internal/retire/audit.go` ·
18	    **Status:** stable · **Verified:** 2026-09-02.
19	
20	## Escalate only as far as needed
21	
22	```text
23	dev status / dev sweep / dev repo context
24	    |
25	    +-- facts are sufficient --> use done, park, sweep, or retire
26	    |
27	    +-- dev prompt render <recipe> --> inspect or copy the exact prompt
28	    +-- dev prompt run <recipe>    --> bounded one-shot analysis, no user stdin
29	    +-- dev prompt open <recipe>   --> foreground conversation in this terminal
30	```
31	
32	Prefer the deterministic lifecycle command when the next step is already clear.
33	Render when a person or another tool only needs the context. Use `run` for a
34	finite unattended answer. Use `open` only when a semantic question needs a
35	conversation, such as resolving what a conflicted change should mean.
36	
37	All three modes collect the same recipe context. The receiving agent may explain
38	or prioritize it, but `dev` does not parse that reply, run a follow-up turn, or
39	convert it into approval for a mutation.
40	
41	## The three recipes
42	
43	```bash
44	dev prompt list
45	dev prompt list --json
46	dev prompt render pr-triage
47	dev prompt render session-close
48	dev prompt render workspace-closeout [repo-or-checkout]
49	```
50	
51	| Recipe | Scope | Read-only result |
52	|---|---|---|
53	| `pr-triage` | account/local forge inbox | Orders requests you authored or were asked to review under merge/review/fix/wait/inspect. It accepts the same query and `--scope`, `--role`, `--state`, `--repo`, `--all-repos`, `--linked`, and `--limit` filters as `dev pr list`. |
54	| `session-close` | selected runtime on this machine | Classifies sessions for runtime closure, checkpoint/park, keeping open, or inspection. It includes session/pane identity, recognized activity, matching task status, and artifact status where available. |
55	| `workspace-closeout` | one repository | Joins tasks, every known checkout, live Git status, runtime coverage, artifacts, and pull requests, then includes a full read-only retirement audit for each checkout. `--base` supplies the audit base for an unmanaged linked worktree. |
56	
57	Each rendered prompt carries a JSON envelope with `schema_version: 1`, the recipe
58	and context versions, generation time, host, scope, target where applicable,
59	capabilities, warnings, and recipe-specific context. Collected repository text,
60	branch names, request titles, and notes are data rather than instructions.
61	Missing or failed evidence remains an explicit capability gap or warning; it is
62	never changed into a reassuring clean/empty value.
63	
64	## Choose render, run, or open
65	
66	| Mode | Agent required? | Prompt transport | User stdin | Default timeout | Runtime behavior |
67	|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
68	| `render` | no | stdout | untouched | none | starts no process and touches no runtime |
69	| `run` | yes | `stdin`, private `file`, or one `argv` element | never passed through | 10 minutes | waits for one batch process in the recipe working directory |
70	| `open` | yes | private `file` or one `argv` element | attached to the child | none | runs one foreground process in the current terminal/TTY |
71	
72	Examples:
73	
74	```bash
75	dev prompt render pr-triage --role reviewer --repo owner/api
76	dev prompt run session-close --agent my-agent
77	dev prompt run pr-triage --dry-run
78	dev prompt open workspace-closeout . --agent my-agent
79	dev prompt open workspace-closeout . --dry-run
80	```
81	
82	`--dry-run` resolves the agent, working directory, transport, timeout, and safe
83	command preview, then prints the complete rendered prompt without starting the
84	process. It therefore makes no writer claim. A real `run` or `open` is treated as
85	a writer claim when its working directory is a checkout, even though the recipe
86	asks for read-only analysis; the shared-checkout occupancy guard still applies.
87	Unlike a command the current agent runs to continue its own work, a handoff is a
88	new agent claim, so the invoking agent's pane is **not** excluded. Use
89	`--allow-shared-checkout` only after coordinating disjoint ownership.
90	
91	`open` requires an interactive terminal unless it is a dry run and does not
92	accept a timeout. Only `run` accepts a timeout and gains a 10-minute default when
93	the value is absent or zero. When a batch timeout expires, `dev` terminates the
94	launcher process tree so a descendant agent cannot continue modifying the
95	checkout after the handoff returns.
96	
97	## Host-only agent configuration
98	
99	There is no built-in agent, vendor, or default launcher. Configure one or more
100	local commands in the user config returned by `dev config path`:
101	
102	```toml
103	[[agent]]
104	name = "my-agent"
105	default = true
106	
107	[agent.run]
108	command = ["my-agent", "--batch"]
109	input = "stdin"
110	timeout = "10m"
111	
112	[agent.open]
113	command = ["my-agent", "{{prompt_file}}"]
114	input = "file"
115	```
116	
117	### Concrete OpenCode example
118	
119	OpenCode 1.18.25 exposes `opencode run [message..]`; adding `--interactive`
120	keeps a direct split-footer conversation. File input works well for a large
121	workspace snapshot because `-f/--file` attaches the private prompt file while a
122	short message tells OpenCode how to treat it:
123	
124	```toml
125	[[agent]]
126	name = "opencode"
127	default = true
128	
129	[agent.run]
130	command = ["opencode", "run", "--file", "{{prompt_file}}", "Read the attached dev prompt and follow its instructions."]
131	input = "file"
132	timeout = "10m"
133	
134	[agent.open]
135	command = ["opencode", "run", "--interactive", "--file", "{{prompt_file}}", "Read the attached dev prompt, explain the evidence, and ask before changing anything."]
136	input = "file"
137	```
138	
139	This is documentation, not a built-in default. Re-check `opencode run --help`
140	after upgrading; do not add `--auto`, because that would change the configured
141	agent's approval policy.
142	
143	Selection is deterministic:
144	
145	1. `--agent NAME` selects that name (matching is case-insensitive).
146	2. Without it, the one entry with `default = true` is selected.
147	3. Without a default, the sole configured `[[agent]]` is selected.
148	4. Multiple entries with no default are ambiguous and fail with their names.
149	
150	Names are required, cannot have surrounding whitespace, and must be unique
151	case-insensitively. At most one entry may be the default. Each agent must define
152	at least one of `[agent.run]` or `[agent.open]`; asking for an undefined mode
153	fails rather than borrowing the other launcher.
154	
155	A launcher has these fields:
156	
157	| Field | Constraint |
158	|---|---|
159	| `command = ["program", "arg", ...]` | Direct argv. The first element must be non-empty. Set exactly one of `command` and `shell`. Preferred because it does not invoke a shell. |
160	| `shell = "static command"` | Runs through `$SHELL -c`. It must be static and cannot contain prompt placeholders. |
161	| `input = "stdin"` | `run` only. The prompt is the child's finite stdin; no placeholder is allowed. |
162	| `input = "file"` | For `command`, exactly one whole argv element must be `{{prompt_file}}`. For `shell`, reference `$DEV_PROMPT_FILE` or `${DEV_PROMPT_FILE}`. |
163	| `input = "argv"` | `command` only, with exactly one whole argv element `{{prompt}}`. The rendered prompt is limited to 100 KiB. |
164	| `timeout = "10m"` | `run` only; optional non-negative duration, with 10 minutes when omitted/zero. `open` rejects a timeout because safe interactive process-tree cancellation needs terminal job control. |
165	| `load_shell_rc = true` | Optional and valid only with `shell`; uses `$SHELL -lic` instead of `-c`. |
166	
167	Placeholders must be complete command elements; embedded forms such as
168	`--prompt={{prompt}}` are rejected. For file transport, `dev` creates a temporary
169	0700 directory and 0600 `prompt.md`, then removes it after the child exits.
170	Prompt contents are never interpolated into shell text.
171	
172	`[[agent]]` is machine-owned executable policy. A repository's
173	`.dev-cli/config.toml` is not allowed to define it, so checking out a project
174	cannot choose a command for `dev` to execute.
175	
176	## Permissions and mutation boundary
177	
178	The built-in recipes instruct the receiver to analyze and quote possible next
179	commands, not to approve, merge, rebase, close, delete, or retire anything.
180	However, `dev prompt` is not a sandbox: the configured child retains whatever
181	filesystem, network, tool, and approval policy its own command gives it. `dev`
182	does not add a permissive mode, reduce permissions, answer an approval prompt,
183	or edit configuration.
184	
185	No agent answer is authoritative. Review it, then invoke `dev done`, `dev park`,
186	`dev sweep`, or `dev retire` yourself. Those commands recollect and revalidate
187	fresh state at their mutation boundaries.
188	
189	## Current-terminal and Herdr boundary
190	
191	`dev prompt open` does **not** create, focus, reuse, or inject into a Herdr, tmux,
192	or Zellij surface. It starts the configured process in the foreground of the
193	terminal that invoked it. Inside Herdr, that naturally means the current pane.
194	If a separate Herdr pane is wanted, create or focus that pane manually, enter the
195	exact checkout there, and run `dev prompt open ...` from that terminal.
196	
197	This is separate from `dev start --run '<shell command>'`. That command may
198	dispatch shell text only to the exact root pane returned for a newly created
199	first-class Herdr worktree; reused, fallback, unverified, and non-Herdr surfaces
200	fail closed. `prompt open` does not widen or reuse that exact-pane contract.
201	
202	## What the closeout classifications mean
203	
204	`session-close` reports **runtime closure only**. A recognized covering agent in
205	`idle` or `done` may satisfy the activity gate, but that only says its current
206	turn settled. It does not prove that changes were committed, artifacts were
207	finalized, review completed, or task intent is done. Caller-contained,
208	mixed-purpose, active, unrecognized, and insufficiently observed sessions do not
209	become close candidates.
210	
211	`workspace-closeout` is broader, but still advisory. Its retirement audit checks
212	target kind, worktree registration and path, status availability, cleanliness,
213	in-progress Git operations, known base and branch containment, task state,
214	artifact reachability/finalization, and runtime eligibility. Only a deterministic
215	`retirement.status` of `eligible` may be suggested for retirement, and even that
216	is not authorization: `dev retire` must recollect and revalidate before changing
217	anything. A merged pull request is evidence only and cannot substitute for any
218	of those gates.
219	
220	## Rebase conflicts
221	
222	Start with the deterministic transaction rather than an agent:
223	
224	```bash
225	dev done <task> --ff
226	# or, for an update of the current branch
227	dev git pull-rebase
228	```
229	
230	If Git stops at a conflict, stay in that exact checkout and open the full
231	workspace context there:
232	
233	```bash
234	dev prompt open workspace-closeout . --agent my-agent
235	```
236	
237	Use the conversation to decide the semantic resolution. Only after the operator
238	chooses should the Git rebase be continued or aborted. Then rerun the original
239	lifecycle command so it derives fresh state. The prompt launcher never resolves
240	the conflict, chooses continue versus abort, force-pushes, or grants cleanup
241	permission on its own.
242	
243	## Scheduling and statelessness
244	
245	`dev` has no daemon, queue, or scheduler. Every `render`, `run`, or `open`
246	invocation collects a fresh snapshot and forgets the agent's answer when the
247	process exits. A scheduler may invoke a non-interactive `run`, but must choose a
248	configured batch command and accept its timeout/error behavior. `open` is a
249	foreground TTY operation and is not a scheduled-job surface.
250	
251	## Related pages
252	
253	- [Pull request inbox](pull-request-inbox.md)
254	- [Agent-safe retirement](agent-safe-retirement.md)
255	- [Parallel agents and runtimes](parallel-agents-runtimes.md)
256	- [Commands and configuration](../reference/commands-config.md)
257	- [Compatibility and known limitations](../reference/compatibility.md)
258
```

165	## Permission 與 mutation boundary
166	
167	Built-in recipe 要求接收端分析並 quote 可能的 next command，不要 approve、merge、

174	並驗證 fresh state。
175	
176	## Current-terminal 與 Herdr boundary
177	
178	`dev prompt open` **不會**建立、focus、reuse 或 inject Herdr、tmux 或 Zellij
179	surface。它在呼叫它的 terminal foreground 啟動 configured process。在 Herdr 裡，
180	自然就是留在目前 pane。若想用另一個 Herdr pane，請手動建立或 focus 該 pane、在其中
181	進入 exact checkout，再從該 terminal 執行 `dev prompt open ...`。
182	
183	這與 `dev start --run '<shell command>'` 分開。後者只可將 shell text dispatch 到
184	本次新建 first-class Herdr worktree 回傳的 exact root pane；reused、fallback、
185	unverified 與 non-Herdr surface 都 fail closed。`prompt open` 不會擴大或 reuse 這份
186	exact-pane contract。
187	
188	## Closeout classification 的意義
189	
190	`session-close` 只回報 **runtime closure**。Recognized covering agent 為 `idle` 或
191	`done` 時可能通過 activity gate，但只代表 current turn settled；它不證明 changes 已
192	commit、artifacts 已 finalize、review 已完成或 task intent 已 done。Caller-contained、
193	mixed-purpose、active、unrecognized 與 observation 不足的 session 都不會成為 close candidate。
194	
195	`workspace-closeout` 範圍較完整，但仍只是 advisory。Retirement audit 會檢查 target
196	kind、worktree registration/path、status availability、cleanliness、in-progress Git
197	operation、known base/branch containment、task state、artifact reachability/finalization
198	與 runtime eligibility。只有 deterministic `retirement.status` 為 `eligible` 才能被建議
199	retire；即使如此也不是 authorization：`dev retire` 必須在 mutation 前重新收集並驗證。
200	Merged pull request 只是 evidence，不能替代任何 gate。
201	
202	## Rebase conflict
203	
204	先使用 deterministic transaction，不要先找 agent：
205	
206	```bash
207	dev done <task> --ff
208	# 或更新目前 branch
209	dev git pull-rebase
210	```
211	
212	若 Git 停在 conflict，留在該 exact checkout，從那裡開啟完整 workspace context：
213	
214	```bash
215	dev prompt open workspace-closeout . --agent my-agent
216	```
217	
218	用對話決定 semantic resolution。只有 operator 選擇後才 continue 或 abort Git rebase，
219	之後重新執行原本 lifecycle command，讓它取得 fresh state。Prompt launcher 絕不會自行
220	resolve conflict、選 continue/abort、force-push 或授予 cleanup permission。
221	
222	## Scheduling 與 statelessness
223	
224	`dev` 沒有 daemon、queue 或 scheduler。每次 `render`、`run`、`open` 都收集 fresh
225	snapshot，process 結束後不保存 agent answer。Scheduler 可以呼叫 non-interactive
226	`run`，但必須選 configured batch command，並接受其 timeout/error behavior。`open` 是
227	foreground TTY operation，不是 scheduled-job surface。
228	
229	## 相關頁面
230	
231	- [Pull request inbox](pull-request-inbox.zh-TW.md)
232	- [Agent-safe retirement](agent-safe-retirement.zh-TW.md)
233	- [平行 Agent 與 Runtime](parallel-agents-runtimes.zh-TW.md)
234	- [命令與設定](../reference/commands-config.zh-TW.md)
235	- [相容性與已知限制](../reference/compatibility.zh-TW.md)
236
```

```text
1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.
4	
5	The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and releases use [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
6	
7	## [Unreleased]
8	
9	### Added
10	
11	- `dev pr list` shows the pull and merge requests you opened and the ones
12	  awaiting your review, and joins reported head branches to local task and
13	  checkout health. Account and per-repository surfaces remain explicit;
14	  personal per-repository queries may call once per requested role, engaged
15	  repositories bound the default local scope, and `--all-repos` widens it.
16	  `--actions` and schema-versioned `--json` emit reviewable `gh`/`glab` command
17	  strings; `dev` prints them and never runs them.
18	- `dev prompt list|render|run|open` provides a provider-neutral prompt handoff.
19	  Built-in `pr-triage`, `session-close`, and `workspace-closeout` recipes collect
20	  deterministic read-only context. `render` prints it, `run` launches a bounded
21	  batch command with no user stdin (10-minute default), and `open` launches a
22	  foreground conversation in the current terminal with no default timeout.
23	  There is no built-in vendor, agent, or launcher, and `dev` never parses the
24	  reply, loops, mutates lifecycle state, or changes permissions.
25	- Agent launchers use host-only nested configuration: `[[agent]]` selects a
26	  unique name/default, while `[agent.run]` and `[agent.open]` independently set
27	  direct `command` argv or static `shell`, `stdin|file|argv` input, plus optional
28	  batch timeout/shell-RC policy. `open` rejects stdin and timeout, prompts are never interpolated
29	  into shell text, and repository `.dev-cli/config.toml` cannot define agents.
30	
31	### Changed
32	
33	- `dev doctor` now reports whether `gh` and `glab` are signed in, not only
34	  whether they are installed, with the exact login command for each.
35	
36	### Fixed
37	
38	- Pull-request `--repo` selectors now constrain both account rows and local
39	  query targets, and JSON reports the effective scope after non-open account
40	  requests narrow to local collection. Schema version 1 local joins distinguish
41	  `expected_branch` from `live_branch`, report checkout existence, worktree
42	  registration and status availability/errors independently, and include Git
43	  status only when the expected branch is actually checked out. Fork pull
44	  requests join against their source repository (resolving GitLab source project
45	  IDs when needed), canonical/unmanaged/external worktrees join without a task,
46	  duplicate local clones no longer suppress the remote query, and ambiguous
47	  same-branch local evidence fails closed instead of choosing a clone. Provider
48	  host identity is preserved so an enterprise remote is never queried against
49	  the public forge, partial failures appear in JSON `warnings`, and stale GitHub
50	  checks are not reported as passing.
51	- The Zellij runtime no longer fails every session listing when an exited
52	  session is left in Zellij's namespace. Zellij keeps exited sessions
53	  resurrectable, and `dump-layout` against one errors with `There is no active
54	  session!`, which previously turned `dev ls`, `dev doctor` and the TUI runtime
55	  join into an error. Exited sessions are now excluded from the live view, and
56	  `dev start` refuses to create over a name an exited session still owns
57	  instead of silently resurrecting its old layout at the old directory. If a
58	  live session exits between listing and layout inspection, creation now also
59	  fails closed rather than falling through to resurrection. Only Zellij's exact
60	  exited marker is recognized; a live session name containing `EXITED` remains live.
61	- An unauthenticated `gh` or `glab` no longer surfaces its full command line
62	  in the TUI REMOTE footer, in `dev repo remote` warnings, or in the cached
63	  provider status. A rejected credential now reads as, for example,
64	  ``glab is signed out — run `glab auth login --hostname gitlab.com` ``, with
65	  the original command and provider output preserved in the wrapped error.
66	  Rate limits, permission and network failures keep their full diagnostic text,
67	  because signing in again would not fix them. Classification inspects provider
68	  stderr rather than argv, so a title or description containing `auth login`
69	  cannot turn an unrelated failure into a sign-in warning. GitLab probing now honors
70	  `GLAB_HOST` as well as `GITLAB_HOST`, and reviewer inventory explicitly uses
71	  account scope instead of GitLab's authored-by-me default.
72	- Prompt handoffs now treat the invoking agent as an existing writer rather
73	  than excluding its pane, so one agent cannot launch another in the same
74	  checkout without the shared-checkout override. Batch timeout cancellation
75	  terminates the launcher process tree rather than leaving a descendant agent
76	  running after `dev` removes its prompt file.
77	- Session and workspace prompts now reuse retirement's pane/mixed-workspace and
78	  agent-status policy, Git branch relation logic, and read-only artifact
79	  reachability inspection. Missing or failed evidence remains unknown instead
80	  of being converted into a known blocker or safe zero value.
81	
82	## [0.2.4] - 2026-09-01
83	
84	### Added
85	
86	- Stable releases now render and publish `Formula/dev-cli.rb` to
87	  `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`. The release job requires a fine-grained
88	  `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN`, fails visibly when the distribution update cannot be
89	  published, and has a manual workflow for retrying or backfilling an existing
90	  stable release without creating another tag. Homebrew installs remain
91	  package-manager-owned rather than letting `dev upgrade` overwrite a Cellar
92	  binary.
93	
94	### Changed
95	
96	- `dev upgrade` now delegates directly to the detected Homebrew, Scoop, or
97	  `go install` owner after confirmation, while standalone binaries retain the
98	  verified in-place replacement path.
99	- `dev doctor` now reports the running executable's install owner and resolved
100	  path, and warns when another `dev` binary on `PATH` could shadow it.
```

759	### Prompt handoffs
760	
761	Escalate only as far as the situation needs: use `dev status`, `dev sweep`, or a
762	lifecycle command when deterministic facts already answer the question; use
763	`dev prompt render <recipe>` to inspect or copy context; use `run` for a bounded
764	batch answer; and use `open` only when a foreground conversation can resolve a
765	semantic question.
766	
767	The built-in recipes are `pr-triage`, `session-close`, and
768	`workspace-closeout`. They collect read-only deterministic context and instruct
769	the receiver not to mutate it. `dev` never parses an agent reply, starts a loop,
770	or treats the reply as permission for `done`, `park`, `sweep`, or `retire`.
771	There is no built-in vendor or launcher: host config defines nested
772	`[agent.run]` and `[agent.open]` commands. `run` receives finite prompt input and
773	defaults to a 10-minute timeout; `open` reserves stdin for the conversation,
774	has no default timeout, and stays in the current terminal/pane. It does not
775	create, focus, or reuse a Herdr/tmux/Zellij surface. See
776	[Prompt handoffs](docs/guides/prompt-handoffs.md) for configuration, transport,
777	permission, closeout-audit, and rebase-conflict boundaries.
778

786	dev note search "event subscription"
787	dev note edit <id-or-prefix>
788	dev note delete <id-or-prefix>
789	```

127	`dev` guards writer-claiming direct/branch starts and resume when another
128	recognized Herdr agent occupies the same canonical Git worktree. Every state,
129	including `idle`, `done`, and `unknown`, is occupied; Herdr resolves the current
130	pane before excluding it. Pure repo/worktree/TUI open is navigation to the live
131	owner, not writer authorization. Never add `--allow-shared-checkout` unless
132	agents already have coordinated disjoint file ownership.
133	
134	A new external agent does not inherit the parent permission mode, and a resumed
135	Claude fork does not restore bypass. Inspect the effective SpecStory/provider
136	command: local wrappers may already be elevated, so never claim they are safe or
137	append a conflicting mode. Herdr `done` is turn-settled—not cleanup done.

84	### Prompt recipes and structured behavior
85	
86	`dev prompt list --json` returns sorted recipe metadata (`name`, `summary`,
87	`scope`, optional `target_usage`, and `context_version`). The three recipes are
88	`pr-triage`, `session-close`, and `workspace-closeout`.
89	
90	`dev prompt render <recipe>` prints a Markdown prompt whose JSON envelope has
91	`schema_version: 1`, recipe/context versions, generation time, host, scope,
92	optional target, capabilities, warnings, and recipe context. Collection is
93	read-only and missing evidence stays explicit. `run` and `open` render the same
94	envelope before selecting a launcher:
95	
96	| Command | Process contract |
97	|---|---|
98	| `dev prompt run <recipe> [--agent NAME] [--dry-run]` | One batch process; no user stdin; prompt may use stdin/file/argv; waits with a 10-minute default timeout. |
99	| `dev prompt open <recipe> [--agent NAME] [--dry-run]` | One foreground process attached to the current terminal/TTY; prompt must use file/argv so stdin remains conversational; no default timeout. |
100	
101	`--agent` wins, otherwise the unique configured default wins, otherwise the sole
102	agent wins. Multiple agents with no default fail as ambiguous. Dry-run shows the
103	resolved mode, cwd, transport, timeout, safe command markers, and complete
104	prompt, and starts nothing. Real launches in a checkout remain subject to the
105	writer-occupancy guard. `dev` never parses a reply, starts an agent loop, changes
106	permissions, or treats advice as lifecycle authorization. `open` never creates,
107	focuses, or reuses a Herdr/tmux/Zellij surface; inside Herdr it remains in the
108	current pane. See [Prompt handoffs](../guides/prompt-handoffs.md).

113	`new`/`create` distinguishes a plain repository name from a clear clone
114	reference:
115	
116	| Command | Behavior |
117	|---|---|
118	| `dev repo new` | interactive wizard; its first field accepts either a new name or a clone reference |
119	| `dev repo new NAME` / `dev repo create NAME` | create a new local repository; a clear Git URL, local Git path, or owner/name instead routes to clone and preserves history/remote |
120	| `dev repo clone [owner/name\|url]` | clone into the configured destination, then optionally apply a preset; setup defaults off |
121	| `dev repo setup [repo-or-path]` | repeat-safely merge native initializers and preset files into an existing clean checkout; defaults to the current repository and does not commit unless requested |
122

315	categorical timings plus aggregate row counts rather than names, paths, or raw

361	  rendered prompt size is 100 KiB.

363	Embedded placeholder forms are rejected. Omitted/zero timeout resolves to 10
364	minutes for `run`; `open` has no deadline and rejects a timeout. See
365	[Prompt handoffs](../guides/prompt-handoffs.md) for recipe and runtime safety.

217	## Bootstrapping and adopting an existing machine
218	
219	Read `references/bootstrap.md` before recursively scanning paths, creating a
220	symlink index, moving physical repositories, or generating layout config. Move
221	is destructive and must follow its report → review → apply procedure.
222	
223	There is nothing to migrate for ordinary use. `dev` discovers repositories through
224	`paths.scan_roots` plus exact `paths.repo_paths` and never moves, renames or deletes anything.
225	
226	```bash
227	dev config init     # detects this machine's roots; every value stays editable
228	dev adopt           # report existing worktrees, sessions and unmerged branches
229	dev adopt --apply   # record them as tasks (nothing on disk changes)
230	```
231	
232	Do not assume the user's layout is `~/Documents/Program`. Run `dev config show`
233	or `dev repo list` to see what this machine is actually configured for.
234	
235	## Creating and setting up repositories
236	
237	Read `references/repository-bootstrap.md` before creating a published repo,
238	running project-owned hooks, or installing setup-capable skills. A bare
239	`dev repo new` is interactive; `dev repo new NAME` deliberately retains the
240	minimal README + initial-commit contract. A clear Git URL, local Git path, or
241	`owner/name` argument to `new` or `create` automatically clones and preserves
242	its remote; template and upstream-creation flags cannot accompany that route.
243	Explicit `repo clone` remains available when scripts should state acquisition
244	directly.
245	`repo new --template` snapshots a local directory or Git tree into a fresh
246	history; it is not a clone. `--template-ref` and `--template-subdir` select the
247	exact source tree.
248	
249	Use `--check-in=commit|stage|none` to choose whether generated changes are
250	committed, staged for human review, or left unstaged (`auto` follows a new
251	repository's preset and otherwise defaults to none). `repo setup --commit`
252	remains the compatibility spelling for commit.
253	Stage mode cannot create an upstream and cannot hand dirty setup directly to
254	`start`.
255	
256	On a TTY, wizard fields are real inline editors: arrows, Home/End,
257	Backspace and Delete edit typed text rather than inserting escape sequences.
```
</details></tool-use>

+type promptAgentInventory struct {
+	Name        string                       `json:"name"`
+	Description string                       `json:"description"`
+	Default     bool                         `json:"default"`
+	Run         promptAgentLauncherInventory `json:"run"`
+	Open        promptAgentLauncherInventory `json:"open"`
+}
+
+type promptAgentLauncherInventory struct {
+	Configured bool   `json:"configured"`
+	Kind       string `json:"kind"`
+	Executable string `json:"executable"`
+}
+
+func newPromptAgentsCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
+	var jsonOut bool
+	cmd := &cobra.Command{
+		Use:   "agents",
+		Short: "List configured agent profiles without private launch details",
+		Args:  cobra.NoArgs,
+		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
+			profiles := promptAgentInventoryRows(app.Cfg.Agents)
+			if jsonOut {
+				encoder := json.NewEncoder(app.Out)
+				encoder.SetIndent("", "  ")
+				return encoder.Encode(profiles)
+			}
+			if len(profiles) == 0 {
+				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No agent profiles configured.")
+				return nil
+			}
+			table := app.newTable("PROFILE", "DEFAULT", "RUN", "OPEN", "DESCRIPTION")
+			for _, profile := range profiles {
+				defaultValue := "—"
+				if profile.Default {
+					defaultValue = "yes"
+				}
+				table.Add(profile.Name, defaultValue, promptAgentLauncherDisplay(profile.Run),
+					promptAgentLauncherDisplay(profile.Open), dash(promptAgentHumanDescription(profile.Description)))
+			}
+			table.Render(app.Out)
+			return nil
+		},
+	}
+	cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&jsonOut, "json", false, "emit stable structured agent metadata")
+	return cmd
+}
+
+func promptAgentInventoryRows(agents []config.Agent) []promptAgentInventory {
+	sorted := append([]config.Agent(nil), agents...)
+	sort.Slice(sorted, func(i, j int) bool {
+		left, right := strings.ToLower(sorted[i].Name), strings.ToLower(sorted[j].Name)
+		if left == right {
+			return sorted[i].Name < sorted[j].Name
+		}
+		return left < right
+	})
+	rows := make([]promptAgentInventory, 0, len(sorted))
+	for _, agent := range sorted {
+		rows = append(rows, promptAgentInventory{
+			Name: agent.Name, Description: agent.Description, Default: agent.Default,
+			Run: promptAgentLauncherInventoryFor(agent.Run), Open: promptAgentLauncherInventoryFor(agent.Open),
+		})
+	}
+	return rows
+}
+
+func promptAgentLauncherInventoryFor(launcher config.AgentLauncher) promptAgentLauncherInventory {
+	switch {
+	case len(launcher.Command) > 0:
+		return promptAgentLauncherInventory{Configured: true, Kind: "command", Executable: filepath.Base(launcher.Command[0])}
+	case strings.TrimSpace(launcher.Shell) != "":
+		return promptAgentLauncherInventory{Configured: true, Kind: "shell"}
+	default:
+		return promptAgentLauncherInventory{Kind: "none"}
+	}
+}
+
+func promptAgentLauncherDisplay(launcher promptAgentLauncherInventory) string {
+	switch launcher.Kind {
+	case "command":
+		return launcher.Executable
+	case "shell":
+		return "shell"
+	default:
+		return "—"
+	}
+}
+
+func promptAgentHumanDescription(description string) string {
+	return strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ").Replace(strings.TrimSpace(description))
+}

+func TestPromptAgentsInventoryIsSortedRedactedAndStable(t *testing.T) {
+	h := newHarness(t)
+	appendConfig(t, h.configPath, `
+[[agent]]
+name = "zeta"
+description = "Interactive profile"
+[agent.open]
+shell = 'printf shell-source-secret < "$DEV_PROMPT_FILE"'
+input = "file"
+
+[[agent]]
+name = "alpha"
+description = "Batch profile"
+default = true
+[agent.run]
+command = ["/private/argv-directory-secret/alpha", "--token=argv-value-secret"]
+input = "stdin"
+`)
+
+	out := h.mustRun("prompt", "agents")
+	for _, want := range []string{"PROFILE", "DEFAULT", "RUN", "OPEN", "DESCRIPTION", "alpha", "zeta", "shell"} {
+		if !strings.Contains(out, want) {
+			t.Errorf("agent inventory missing %q:\n%s", want, out)
+		}
+	}
+	if strings.Index(out, "alpha") > strings.Index(out, "zeta") {
+		t.Errorf("agent inventory is not sorted:\n%s", out)
+	}
+	for _, secret := range []string{"argv-directory-secret", "argv-value-secret", "shell-source-secret", h.configPath} {
+		if strings.Contains(out, secret) {
+			t.Errorf("human inventory leaked %q:\n%s", secret, out)
+		}
+	}
+
+	out = h.mustRun("prompt", "agents", "--json")
+	var got []map[string]any
+	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(out), &got); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("prompt agents --json: %v\n%s", err, out)
+	}
+	want := []map[string]any{
+		{
+			"name": "alpha", "description": "Batch profile", "default": true,
+			"run":  map[string]any{"configured": true, "kind": "command", "executable": "alpha"},
+			"open": map[string]any{"configured": false, "kind": "none", "executable": ""},
+		},
+		{
+			"name": "zeta", "description": "Interactive profile", "default": false,
+			"run":  map[string]any{"configured": false, "kind": "none", "executable": ""},
+			"open": map[string]any{"configured": true, "kind": "shell", "executable": ""},
+		},
+	}
+	if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
+		t.Fatalf("agent inventory schema/content mismatch:\n got: %#v\nwant: %#v", got, want)
+	}
+	for _, secret := range []string{"argv-directory-secret", "argv-value-secret", "shell-source-secret", h.configPath} {
+		if strings.Contains(out, secret) {
+			t.Errorf("JSON inventory leaked %q:\n%s", secret, out)
+		}
+	}
+}

128	func promptAgentInventoryRows(agents []config.Agent) []promptAgentInventory {
129		sorted := append([]config.Agent(nil), agents...)
130		sort.Slice(sorted, func(i, j int) bool {
131			left, right := strings.ToLower(sorted[i].Name), strings.ToLower(sorted[j].Name)
132			if left == right {
133				return sorted[i].Name < sorted[j].Name
134			}
135			return left < right
136		})
137		rows := make([]promptAgentInventory, 0, len(sorted))
138		for _, agent := range sorted {
139			rows = append(rows, promptAgentInventory{
140				Name: agent.Name, Description: agent.Description, Default: agent.Default,
141				Run: promptAgentLauncherInventoryFor(agent.Run), Open: promptAgentLauncherInventoryFor(agent.Open),
142			})
143		}
144		return rows
145	}

147	func promptAgentLauncherInventoryFor(launcher config.AgentLauncher) promptAgentLauncherInventory {

149		case len(launcher.Command) > 0:
150			return promptAgentLauncherInventory{Configured: true, Kind: "command", Executable: filepath.Base(launcher.Command[0])}
151		case strings.TrimSpace(launcher.Shell) != "":
152			return promptAgentLauncherInventory{Configured: true, Kind: "shell"}
153		default:
154			return promptAgentLauncherInventory{Kind: "none"}

273	func executePrompt(app *App, mode promptMode, agentName string, dryRun bool, recipeName string, collect promptCollect) error {
274		recipe, ok := promptkit.Lookup(recipeName)
275		if !ok {
276			return fmt.Errorf("unknown prompt recipe %q", recipeName)
277		}
278		var selection promptLauncherSelection
279		if mode != promptRender {
280			var err error
281			selection, err = resolvePromptLauncher(app, mode, agentName, dryRun)
282			if err != nil {
283				return err
284			}
285		}
286	
287		snapshot, err := collect(ctxOf())
288		if err != nil {
289			return err
290		}
291		if snapshot.WorkingDirectory == "" {
292			snapshot.WorkingDirectory = currentDirectory()
293		}
294		if snapshot.Target != nil && snapshot.Target.WorkingDirectory == "" {
295			snapshot.Target.WorkingDirectory = snapshot.WorkingDirectory
296		}
297		generatedAt := time.Now().UTC()
298		rendered, _, err := promptkit.Render(recipe, snapshot, generatedAt, config.Hostname())
299		if err != nil {
300			return err
301		}
302		if mode == promptRender {
303			fmt.Fprint(app.Out, rendered)
304			if !strings.HasSuffix(rendered, "\n") {
305				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
306			}
307			return nil
308		}
309	
310		agent := selection.Agent
311		handoffMode := selection.Mode
312		launcherConfig := selection.Launcher
313		// Starting an external coding agent is a new writer claim even when the
314		// recipe asks only for analysis. Unlike an existing agent continuing its own
315		// work, this guard does not exclude the caller pane: an agent must not launch
316		// a second writer beside itself without the explicit shared-checkout override.
317		// Dry-run starts no writer and therefore needs no claim.
318		if !dryRun {
319			if _, isCheckout := canonicalWorktreeRoot(ctxOf(), snapshot.WorkingDirectory); isCheckout {
320				if err := guardNewAgentCheckout(ctxOf(), app, app.Runtime(), snapshot.WorkingDirectory); err != nil {
321					return err
322				}
323			}
324		}
325	
326		spec := handoff.Spec{
327			Mode: handoffMode, Launcher: launcherConfig.Handoff(handoffMode),
328			Prompt: rendered, Dir: snapshot.WorkingDirectory, ShellPath: shellPath(),
329			In: app.In, Out: app.Out, Err: app.Err,
330		}
331		preview, err := handoff.Run(ctxOf(), handoff.Spec{
332			Mode: spec.Mode, Launcher: spec.Launcher, Prompt: spec.Prompt, Dir: spec.Dir,
333			ShellPath: spec.ShellPath, In: spec.In, Out: spec.Out, Err: spec.Err, DryRun: true,
334		})
335		if err != nil {
336			return fmt.Errorf("agent %q: %w", agent.Name, err)
337		}
338		if dryRun {
339			renderPromptDryRun(app, agent.Name, preview, rendered)
340			return nil
341		}
342		app.warnf("running agent %q in %s: %s", agent.Name, config.Contract(spec.Dir), previewCommand(preview))
343		if _, err := handoff.Run(ctxOf(), spec); err != nil {
344			return fmt.Errorf("agent %q: %w", agent.Name, err)
345		}
346		return nil
347	}

349	type promptLauncherSelection struct {
350		Agent    config.Agent
351		Mode     handoff.Mode
352		Launcher config.AgentLauncher
353	}
354	
355	func resolvePromptLauncher(app *App, mode promptMode, name string, dryRun bool) (promptLauncherSelection, error) {
356		handoffMode, ok := promptHandoffMode(mode)
357		if !ok {
358			return promptLauncherSelection{}, fmt.Errorf("prompt mode %q has no agent launcher", mode)
359		}
360		agent, ok := app.Cfg.AgentByName(name)
361		if !ok {
362			return promptLauncherSelection{}, promptAgentError(app, name, handoffMode)
363		}
364		launcher := promptAgentLauncher(agent, handoffMode)
365		if !launcher.Configured() {
366			return promptLauncherSelection{}, fmt.Errorf("agent %q has no [agent.%s] launcher; %s",
367				agent.Name, handoffMode, promptAgentModeGuidance(app.Cfg.Agents, handoffMode))
368		}
369		if handoffMode == handoff.ModeOpen && !dryRun && !app.interactive() {
370			return promptLauncherSelection{}, errors.New("prompt open needs an interactive terminal; use prompt render or prompt run instead")
371		}
372		return promptLauncherSelection{Agent: agent, Mode: handoffMode, Launcher: launcher}, nil
373	}
374	
375	func promptHandoffMode(mode promptMode) (handoff.Mode, bool) {
376		switch mode {
377		case promptRun:
378			return handoff.ModeRun, true
379		case promptOpen:
380			return handoff.ModeOpen, true
381		default:
382			return "", false
383		}
384	}
385	
386	func promptAgentLauncher(agent config.Agent, mode handoff.Mode) config.AgentLauncher {
387		if mode == handoff.ModeOpen {
388			return agent.Open
389		}
390		return agent.Run
391	}
392	
393	func promptAgentError(app *App, name string, mode handoff.Mode) error {
394		guidance := promptAgentModeGuidance(app.Cfg.Agents, mode)
395		if len(app.Cfg.Agents) == 0 {
396			return fmt.Errorf(`no [[agent]] is configured; add one to %s, for example:
397	
398	[[agent]]
399	name = "my-agent"
400	description = "My local coding agent"
401	default = true
402	[agent.run]
403	command = ["my-agent", "--print"]
404	input = "stdin"
405	[agent.open]
406	command = ["my-agent", "{{prompt_file}}"]
407	input = "file"
408	
409	%s`, config.Contract(config.ConfigFile()), guidance)
410		}
411		if strings.TrimSpace(name) == "" {
412			return fmt.Errorf("more than one [[agent]] is configured and none is the default; %s", guidance)
413		}
414		return fmt.Errorf("unknown agent %q; %s", name, guidance)
415	}
416	
417	func promptAgentModeGuidance(agents []config.Agent, mode handoff.Mode) string {
418		names := promptAgentNamesForMode(agents, mode)
419		available := "none"
420		if len(names) > 0 {
421			available = strings.Join(names, ", ")
422		}
423		return fmt.Sprintf("%s-capable profiles: %s; inspect with `dev prompt agents`", mode, available)
424	}
425	
426	func promptAgentNamesForMode(agents []config.Agent, mode handoff.Mode) []string {
427		names := make([]string, 0, len(agents))
428		for _, agent := range agents {
429			if promptAgentLauncher(agent, mode).Configured() {
430				names = append(names, agent.Name)
431			}
432		}
433		sort.Slice(names, func(i, j int) bool {
434			left, right := strings.ToLower(names[i]), strings.ToLower(names[j])
435			if left == right {
436				return names[i] < names[j]
437			}
438			return left < right
439		})
440		return names
441	}

443	func renderPromptDryRun(app *App, agent string, preview handoff.Preview, prompt string) {
444		timeout := "none"
445		if preview.Timeout > 0 {
446			timeout = preview.Timeout.String()
447		}
448		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "agent: %s\nmode: %s\ncwd: %s\ntransport: %s\ntimeout: %s\ncommand: %s\n\n--- prompt ---\n%s",
449			agent, preview.Mode, preview.Dir, preview.Transport, timeout, previewCommand(preview), prompt)
450		if !strings.HasSuffix(prompt, "\n") {
451			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
452		}
453	}
454	
455	func previewCommand(preview handoff.Preview) string {
456		if preview.Shell != "" {
457			return preview.Shell
458		}
459		parts := make([]string, 0, len(preview.Command))
460		for _, argument := range preview.Command {
461			parts = append(parts, shellQuote(argument))
462		}
463		return strings.Join(parts, " ")
464	}

466	func currentDirectory() string {
467		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
468		if err != nil {
469			return "."
470		}
471		return cwd
472	}
473	
474	func value(pointer *string) string {
475		if pointer == nil {
476			return ""
477		}
478		return *pointer
479	}

481	func valueBool(pointer *bool) bool {
482		return pointer != nil && *pointer
483	}

45	func completePromptAgents(app *App, mode promptMode) cobra.CompletionFunc {
46		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
47			if !app.loadCompletion() {

49			}

57				if left == right {

115	func taskCompletionRef(all []*task.Task, target *task.Task, ref, typed string) (string, bool) {
116		if len(typed) > len(ref) || !strings.EqualFold(ref[:len(typed)], typed) {
117			return "", false
118		}
119		candidate := typed + ref[len(typed):]
120		var exact []*task.Task
121		for _, t := range all {
122			if t.ID == candidate || t.Branch == candidate {
123				exact = append(exact, t)
124			}
125		}
126		if len(exact) > 0 {
127			return candidate, len(exact) == 1 && exact[0].ID == target.ID
128		}
129		needle := strings.ToLower(candidate)
130		var match *task.Task
131		for _, t := range all {
132			haystack := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
133			if !strings.Contains(haystack, needle) {
134				continue
135			}
136			if match != nil {
137				return "", false
138			}
139			match = t
140		}
141		return candidate, match != nil && match.ID == target.ID
142	}

308		return func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string, toComplete string) ([]string, cobra.ShellCompDirective) {
309			prefix, current := "", toComplete
310			if i := strings.LastIndexByte(toComplete, ','); i >= 0 {
311				prefix, current = toComplete[:i+1], toComplete[i+1:]
312			}
313			used := make(map[string]bool)
314			for _, value := range strings.Split(strings.TrimSuffix(prefix, ","), ",") {
315				used[value] = value != ""
316			}
317			out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
318			for _, value := range values {
319				candidate := prefix + value
320				if !used[value] && strings.HasPrefix(value, current) {

589	// validateAgents rejects an agent definition that could not run, or that could
590	// run in a way the user did not mean.
591	func (c Config) validateAgents() error {
592		seen := map[string]int{}
593		defaultAt := -1
594		for i, agent := range c.Agents {
595			name := strings.TrimSpace(agent.Name)
596			if name == "" {
597				return fmt.Errorf("agent[%d].name must not be empty", i)
598			}
599			if name != agent.Name {
600				return fmt.Errorf("agent[%d].name %q must not have surrounding whitespace", i, agent.Name)
601			}
602			if previous, exists := seen[strings.ToLower(name)]; exists {
603				return fmt.Errorf("agent[%d].name %q duplicates agent[%d]", i, name, previous)
604			}
605			seen[strings.ToLower(name)] = i
606	
607			if !agent.Run.Configured() && !agent.Open.Configured() {
608				return fmt.Errorf("agent[%d] %q: configure run or open", i, name)
609			}
610			for mode, launcher := range map[handoff.Mode]AgentLauncher{
611				handoff.ModeRun: agent.Run, handoff.ModeOpen: agent.Open,
612			} {
613				if !launcher.Configured() {
614					continue
615				}
616				if launcher.Timeout.Duration < 0 {
617					return fmt.Errorf("agent[%d].%s.timeout must not be negative", i, mode)
618				}
619				if err := handoff.Validate(mode, launcher.Handoff(mode)); err != nil {
620					return fmt.Errorf("agent[%d].%s: %w", i, mode, err)
621				}
622			}
623	
624			if agent.Default {
625				if defaultAt >= 0 {
626					return fmt.Errorf("agent[%d] %q: agent[%d] is already the default", i, name, defaultAt)
627				}
628				defaultAt = i
629			}
630		}
631		return nil
632	}

Base directory for this skill: /Users/zhouhanru/Worktrees/dev-cli/feat-pr-ci-scan/.claude/skills/agent-history-hygiene

# agent-history-hygiene

Keep agent chat transcripts and plan files committed together with the
code they produced, without leaking secrets. Pairs with the
`redact-agent-secrets` + `gitleaks` pre-commit hooks the skill installs.

Three surfaces, separated by purpose:

| Surface                          | Question it answers                                          |
|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| `find-session.sh`                | "Which transcript / plan file is *my* current session?"      |
| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`       | "Which agent files belong in the next commit?"               |
| `bootstrap-project.sh`           | "How do I get pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor into a repo?" |
| `scan-staged.sh`                 | "Is there a leaked secret in what I'm about to commit?"      |
| `probe-specstory-redaction.py`   | "What does SpecStory already redact, so we don't redo it?"   |
| `references/remediation.md`      | "I already pushed a secret — now what?"                      |

## Core invariants

1. **Agent transcripts and plan files are committed alongside the diff
   that produced them.** Never add them to `.gitignore`. An agent that
   drops these from a commit has broken the user's review trail.
2. **Rotate at the provider before any git rewrite.** The only act
   that revokes a leaked credential is rotation. History rewriting
   scrubs bytes on one clone and leaves them on every other.
3. **`git push --force` against a shared branch is never the fix for a
   leak.** At best it's useless; at worst it destroys teammate work and
   silently re-introduces the secret when someone merges their old
   history back.

## When to use this skill

Use it when the user (or you) surface any of:

- "Commit my chat" / "save the specstory session" / "include the plan
  file in this commit" / "把 plan 跟 specstory 一起 commit 進去".
- You see dirty `.specstory/history/*.md`, `.claude/plans/*.md`,
  `.cursor/plans/*.md`, or any other configured agent artifact during
  `git status` and you're about to commit a feature.
- "Scrub this transcript" / "redact my key" / "gitleaks flagged my
  chat history".
- "Set up pre-commit for this repo" / "I'm starting a new project — how
  do I get the hook stack?" / "bootstrap secret scanning here".
- "I pushed a `.env`" / "a secret went to main" / "do I need to force
  push?" — the agent must steer to `references/remediation.md` and
  stop the user from force-pushing reflexively.

## When NOT to use

- The user explicitly wants agent transcripts **excluded** from the
  repo. Respect that; suggest a one-liner `.gitignore` addition and
  skip this skill entirely.
- The leak is already on a shared `main`/release branch. Do **not**
  offer to rewrite history — jump to `references/remediation.md` §5.
- The project genuinely has no agent session (no `.specstory/`, no
  `.claude/plans/`, etc.). Nothing to stage.
- Single-file, single-commit hygiene that the agent handles without any
  script (e.g., adding a missing trailing newline).

## Integration with existing infrastructure

This skill sits **on top of** any chezmoi-managed stack the user
already has. It does not duplicate:

- **chezmoi's global `core.hooksPath`** (`~/.config/git/hooks/pre-commit`)
  — that wrapper runs the repo's `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and then
  optionally `gitleaks git --staged`. The skill bootstraps the repo-level
  config the wrapper expects to find.
- **chezmoi's `.gitleaks.toml`** — the user's config already carries
  curated rules for common API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Supabase,
  Linear, WakaTime, Cursor, HuggingFace, Notion, Tailscale, Clash /
  V2Ray tokens). The skill's `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` ships the
  same rule IDs so `.gitleaksignore` / allowlist tweaks stay portable.
- **the pinned `redact-agent-secrets` hook** — the redactor ships as a
  pinned pre-commit hook from this repo
  (`.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`), so every consuming repo gets fixes via
  `pre-commit autoupdate` instead of a vendored copy that drifts. Details
  in [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md).

What this skill **adds**:

- Agent-facing discipline (this `SKILL.md` + `references/remediation.md`).
- A single-command project bootstrap (`bootstrap-project.sh`) for repos
  without chezmoi or where the user wants the stack in one go.
- Session-discovery heuristics (`find-session.sh`) for the "find my
  current transcript among many" problem.
- An exit-code wrapper (`scan-staged.sh`) agents can branch on before
  committing.

## Workflow A: commit-time hygiene

Default flow when the agent is about to commit feature changes plus
chat/plan artifacts.

```bash
# 1. Make sure the agent knows which session is "ours" — mostly
#    relevant when multiple Claude/SpecStory sessions run in the repo.
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/find-session.sh

# 2. Stage code the usual way, then auto-add agent artifacts.
git add path/to/feature/file.ts
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh
# Use --session-only if you want ONLY the current SpecStory + newest plan;
# default stages every dirty *.md in every configured agent dir.

# 3. Belt-and-suspenders secret scan before commit. Exit 0 = clean.
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh || {
  # Exit 10/20: leaks found. Jump to references/remediation.md.
  echo "Leaks detected — see references/remediation.md before committing." >&2
  exit 1
}

# 4. Commit. pre-commit (installed by bootstrap) runs redact-agent-secrets
#    then gitleaks again as a catch-all.
git commit -m "feat: ..."
```

## Workflow B: bootstrap a new project

For repos that don't yet have `.pre-commit-config.yaml` / `.gitleaks.toml`
installed. Runs once per repo.

```bash
cd /path/to/new/project
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh \
  --install-hook            # optional: auto-stage on every commit

# Verify: shake out any existing issues in the working tree.
pre-commit run --all-files
```

What `bootstrap-project.sh` does:

1. Drops `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the repo
   (skips if already present unless `--force`). The redactor is a pinned
   remote hook (`repo: …/agent-skills`, `rev: ahh-v1.1.0`), **not** a
   vendored `scripts/redact_secrets.py` — so `pre-commit autoupdate`
   keeps it current everywhere.
2. Runs `pre-commit install` (or `uvx pre-commit@4 install` if
   pre-commit isn't on `PATH`).
3. Audits `.gitignore` / `.git/info/exclude` for patterns that would
   silently hide an agent artifact dir — warns without editing.
4. Checks `~/.claude/settings.json` for `plansDirectory`; prints the
   one-line patch if missing.
5. With `--install-hook`: writes a `prepare-commit-msg` hook that calls
   `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only --allow-empty` so every
   `git commit` auto-attaches the current session file.

Migrating a repo off the **old vendored layout** (a committed
`scripts/redact_secrets.py` + a `- repo: local` redact hook):

```bash
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh --migrate
```

removes the vendored script and rewrites the local hook into the pinned
remote hook, leaving your other hooks and `.gitleaks.toml` untouched
(idempotent; safe to re-run).

## Workflow C: post-leak remediation

When `scan-staged.sh` reports exit `10`/`20`, or the user says "I
committed / pushed a secret":

1. **STOP** the user from running `git push --force` reflexively.
2. Read `references/remediation.md` end-to-end.
3. Walk the user through **step 1 (rotate)** regardless of blast
   radius. Only after rotation does the question of scrubbing history
   become worth discussing.
4. Use the decision tree in the runbook to pick the right git action.

## Gotchas

- **SpecStory >= 2.4.0 already redacts on write — plan around it, not
  against it.** Since
  [PR #235](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/235) shipped in
  v2.4.0 (2026-07-20), the CLI redacts secrets via the
  [Betterleaks](https://github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks) ruleset **by
  default**, covering both local markdown and cloud sync, writing
  `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`. Measured coverage is 36 of 54 class/context pairs;
  15 are ours alone (every webhook rule, plus every custom key in prose
  context — betterleaks catches many classes only in `KEY=value` form via its
  entropy-based `generic-api-key` rule). So: **keep this layer, but never
  rewrite what SpecStory already cleaned.** `redact_secrets.py` writes the
  same `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` sentinel and `.gitleaks.toml` allowlists it, so
  a cleaned transcript is left untouched and pre-commit stops demanding a
  re-`git add`. Full matrix + knobs in
  [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md).
  Only `[redaction] enabled` is configurable upstream — the PR's
  `extra_patterns` did not survive the Betterleaks rewrite, so repo-specific
  rules stay our job. For SpecStory older than 2.4.0 (or with redaction
  disabled), run `redact_secrets.py --fix --legacy`.
- **`plansDirectory` project-level sometimes ignored.** Claude Code
  issue [#19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537)
  reports project-level `plansDirectory` being ignored in some
  versions. After running a `/plan`, verify the file actually landed
  where you expected before relying on `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`
  picking it up. User-level config (`~/.claude/settings.json` with
  `"plansDirectory": "./.claude/plans"`) is the recommended default.
- **`gitleaks protect` is deprecated.** Since v8.19.0 use
  `gitleaks git --staged --redact` (pre-commit) and
  `gitleaks dir <path>` (working directory). The older commands still
  work but emit a deprecation notice. This skill uses the modern
  syntax everywhere.
- **`pre-commit install` is per-clone.** Each teammate must run
  `pre-commit install` in their own clone for hooks to fire. CI cannot
  be trusted as the single gate — it's second-chance, not last-chance.
- **Transcript files can be huge.** A long SpecStory session can exceed
  2 MB. The template bumps `check-added-large-files` to `--maxkb=2048`
  to avoid false positives, but a very long session can still overflow.
  If you hit the limit, rotate sessions (`specstory run claude`
  creates a fresh file) instead of raising the cap further.
- **Session-UUID divergence between SpecStory CLI and VS Code
  extension.** The extension autosaves into `.specstory/history/`
  continuously; the CLI (`specstory run claude`) creates one file per
  invocation. If both are active you can end up with two transcripts
  for what feels like "one session" — mtime-newest wins in
  `find-session.sh`.
- **Global `core.hooksPath` means bare repos aren't protected.** The
  chezmoi setup's global hook runs `.pre-commit-config.yaml` IF it
  exists — so a repo without `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has no
  protection. Run `bootstrap-project.sh` before the first commit with
  agent artifacts, not after.
- **Active SpecStory writer can defeat the redact loop.** The standard
  `git add → git commit → pre-commit auto-fixes → re-stage → re-commit`
  flow assumes the file is **quiescent** during the commit. SpecStory's
  `specstory_*_watch` daemon tails the agent transcript continuously,
  so if the chat captured `ps -axo args`-style output that contained an
  unrelated daemon's secret in argv (e.g. SpecStory's own
  `--cloud-token …` flag), every diagnostic command (`grep`, `sed -n
  '<line>p'`, `cat | head | tail`) prints the secret again, SpecStory
  appends it to the transcript, and the redact-then-restage cycle
  never converges. Symptom: pre-commit says "Successfully redacted N
  file(s)" but `gitleaks-system` immediately fails on the same line,
  re-running `git add && git commit` doesn't help, and `grep -c
  '<secret-prefix>' file` shows the count *increasing* over commit
  attempts. **Workaround**: a single atomic
  `python3 -c "<in-place re.sub>" && git add <file> && git commit -m
  "..."` pipeline so the index is frozen before any new specstory write
  lands. **Don't** print, grep, or diff the secret line during the
  recovery — every print echoes back into the transcript. Diagnose with
  `lsof <file>` (looking for `specstory_*` writers) instead. See
  `pitfalls/redact-secrets-loop-with-active-specstory-writer.md` in
  upstream chezmoi for the full debugging trail.
  **Fixed sub-case:** the *bare-phrase* variant of this loop — where the
  redactor's own `PRIVATE KEY` substring match kept flagging prose that
  merely *discusses* private keys (this skill's docs, or a chat about
  redaction) with **no real secret present** — no longer happens.
  `redact_secrets.py` now scopes to key *headers* (the
  `detect-private-key` BLACKLIST), so prose mentions are ignored and
  converge immediately. The atomic-commit workaround above is still
  needed for the harder case: a **real** secret an active writer keeps
  re-appending. When only the substring redactor (`redact-agent-secrets`)
  trips while `gitleaks` + `detect-private-key` pass, it's the false
  positive — verify with `gitleaks git --staged` and, if clean, commit
  with `SKIP=redact-agent-secrets` (keeps the real gates active).

## Available scripts

- **`scripts/find-session.sh [--format=specstory|claude|both] [--json]`**
  Discover the current agent session files for `$PWD`. TSV default,
  `--json` for structured callers. Never exits non-zero (always 0,
  empty fields signal absence).

- **`scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh [--session-only] [--include-all-plans] [--dry-run] [--allow-empty]`**
  `git add` the right agent artifacts before the next commit.
  `--session-only` stages only the current SpecStory + newest plan;
  default stages every dirty `*.md` in every configured artifact dir.
  Refuses to run if there are no code changes (prevents "commit just
  transcript"); override with `--allow-empty`.

- **`scripts/scan-staged.sh [--redact] [--verbose]`**
  Run `gitleaks git --staged` with agent-friendly exit codes
  (0 clean / 10 redacted / 20 leaks / 30 gitleaks missing). JSON lines
  on stdout, prose diagnostics on stderr.

- **`scripts/probe-specstory-redaction.py [--json] [--keep] [--dry-run]`**
  Measure which secret classes SpecStory's native redaction covers, by
  synthesizing a Claude Code session and rendering it twice (with and without
  `--no-redact-secrets`). Prints a coverage matrix and the residual set our
  layer must still handle. Exit 30 when specstory isn't installed.

- **`scripts/bootstrap-project.sh [--from-chezmoi] [--migrate] [--install-hook] [--force] [--dry-run]`**
  Install `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the current
  repo, wire the hook to the installed skill's redactor, then run
  `pre-commit install`. Audits
  `.gitignore` and `~/.claude/settings.json` for misconfigurations
  (warns, never silently edits).

## Bundled assets

- `assets/artifact-dirs.txt` — the canonical list of agent artifact
  directories (SpecStory, Claude plans, Cursor plans + rules, OpenCode
  plans, Spec-kit, Codex). Consumed by `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` and
  by `bootstrap-project.sh` when rendering the pre-commit `files:`
  regex.
- `assets/pre-commit-config.yaml.template` — minimal
  `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with `redact-agent-secrets` + gitleaks +
  standard hygiene hooks.
- `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` — portable subset of the chezmoi
  `.gitleaks.toml` with custom rule IDs + a path-scoped allowlist for
  agent artifact dirs.
- `assets/redact_secrets.py` — the redactor, published to consuming repos
  as the pinned `redact-agent-secrets` pre-commit hook (root
  `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`). Writes `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`, the sentinel
  SpecStory also writes natively; `--legacy` writes the pre-2.4.0
  placeholders instead. Release procedure in
  `references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`.

## Reference files

- [`references/transcript-session-discovery.md`](references/transcript-session-discovery.md)
  — SpecStory / Claude session layouts and the `$PWD → slug` algorithm.
  Read when `find-session.sh` returns empty or ambiguous results.
- [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md)
  — three-layer defense (redact → gitleaks → `scan-staged.sh`),
  allowlist design, sync procedure for the bundled redactor. Read
  when tuning rules or debugging unexpected pre-commit failures.
- [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md)
  — what SpecStory >= 2.4.0 redacts on its own, measured per secret class and
  per context, plus the upstream PRs, config knobs, and why our layer is still
  load-bearing. Read before changing anything about redaction placeholders.
- [`references/remediation.md`](references/remediation.md) —
  rotate-first runbook for "I committed / pushed a secret". Read
  **before** any `git filter-repo` / `git push --force` action.

## Tests

The skill ships with a three-level test suite under
[`tests/`](tests/README.md). Run from repo root:

```bash
make test-skill
```

- `test_redact_secrets.py` — pytest for pure redactor functions.
- `test_gitleaks_corpus.py` — golden-corpus fixtures staged in tmp git
  repos, asserting real-key shapes fire and example shapes are
  allowlisted only inside configured artifact dirs.
- `test_scan_staged.sh` — exit-code contract for
  `scripts/scan-staged.sh` (0 / 20 / 30 / 2).
- `test_specstory_coverage.py` — locks in that SpecStory still redacts by
  default and still writes `[REDACTED:<label>]`; skips without the CLI.

The corpus + shell tests skip gracefully when `gitleaks` isn't on
`PATH`. See [`tests/README.md`](tests/README.md) for what each
regression the suite locks in.

## Related skills

- [`project-knowledge-harness`](../project-knowledge-harness/SKILL.md)

12	// Status is the live git state of one checkout — everything dev's inventory
13	// shows about a task without persisting any of it.
14	type Status struct {
15		Branch   string `json:"branch,omitempty"`
16		Detached bool   `json:"detached"`
17		// Upstream is the tracking ref (e.g. "origin/feat/auth"), empty when the
18		// branch has never been published.
19		Upstream string `json:"upstream,omitempty"`
20		Ahead    int    `json:"ahead"`
21		Behind   int    `json:"behind"`
22		// Changed counts unique changed paths. Staged and Unstaged are index /
23		// working-tree views and can overlap when one path has both kinds of
24		// changes; Changed does not double-count it.
25		Changed   int `json:"changed"`
26		Staged    int `json:"staged"`
27		Unstaged  int `json:"unstaged"`
28		Untracked int `json:"untracked"`
29		// Added, Modified, Deleted and Renamed classify status letters. One path
30		// can contribute to two when its staged and unstaged states differ.
31		Added    int `json:"added"`
32		Modified int `json:"modified"`
33		Deleted  int `json:"deleted"`
34		Renamed  int `json:"renamed"`
35		// LatestChange is the newest mtime among changed files that still exist.
36		// Deleted paths fall back to the checkout's last commit time at the repo
37		// aggregation layer.
38		LatestChange time.Time `json:"latest_change,omitempty"`
39		// Conflicted counts unmerged paths; a non-zero value means the checkout is
40		// mid-merge or mid-rebase and must not be touched automatically.
41		Conflicted int `json:"conflicted"`
42	}
43	
44	// Dirty reports uncommitted work of any kind.
45	func (s Status) Dirty() bool { return s.Changed > 0 }
46	
47	// Published reports whether the branch has an upstream at all.
48	func (s Status) Published() bool { return s.Upstream != "" }
49	
50	// Synced reports a branch that is published and exactly level with upstream.
51	func (s Status) Synced() bool { return s.Published() && s.Ahead == 0 && s.Behind == 0 }
52	
53	// Summary renders the compact, starship-like column used throughout dev:
54	//
55	//	⇕⇡2⇣1 =1 +3 !2 ?4
56	//
57	// Divergence, conflicts, staged, unstaged and untracked paths remain separate
58	// so "dirty" says how and by how much, rather than collapsing to one ●.
59	func (s Status) Summary() string {
60		var parts []string
61		switch {
62		case s.Ahead > 0 && s.Behind > 0:
63			parts = append(parts, "⇕⇡"+strconv.Itoa(s.Ahead)+"⇣"+strconv.Itoa(s.Behind))
64		case s.Ahead > 0:
65			parts = append(parts, "⇡"+strconv.Itoa(s.Ahead))
66		case s.Behind > 0:
67			parts = append(parts, "⇣"+strconv.Itoa(s.Behind))
68		}
69		if s.Conflicted > 0 {
70			parts = append(parts, "="+strconv.Itoa(s.Conflicted))
71		}
72		if s.Staged > 0 {
73			parts = append(parts, "+"+strconv.Itoa(s.Staged))
74		}
75		if s.Unstaged > 0 {
76			parts = append(parts, "!"+strconv.Itoa(s.Unstaged))
77		}
78		if s.Untracked > 0 {
79			parts = append(parts, "?"+strconv.Itoa(s.Untracked))
80		}
81		if len(parts) == 0 {
82			if !s.Published() {
83				return "local"
84			}
85			return "clean"
86		}
87		return strings.Join(parts, " ")
88	}
89	
90	// Breakdown renders the detailed change count shown by `dev status` and the
91	// TUI detail pane. Changed is the unique-path total; staged and unstaged may
92	// overlap, which is stated by presenting them as categories rather than a sum.
93	func (s Status) Breakdown() string {
94		if s.Changed == 0 {
95			return "0 changed paths"
96		}
97		var parts []string
98		if s.Staged > 0 {
99			parts = append(parts, "+"+strconv.Itoa(s.Staged)+" staged")
100		}
101		if s.Unstaged > 0 {
102			parts = append(parts, "!"+strconv.Itoa(s.Unstaged)+" unstaged")
103		}
104		if s.Untracked > 0 {
105			parts = append(parts, "?"+strconv.Itoa(s.Untracked)+" untracked")
106		}
107		if s.Conflicted > 0 {
108			parts = append(parts, "="+strconv.Itoa(s.Conflicted)+" conflicted")
109		}
110		return strconv.Itoa(s.Changed) + " changed paths (" + strings.Join(parts, ", ") + ")"
111	}
112	
113	// TypeBreakdown classifies the status letters when that detail is available.
114	func (s Status) TypeBreakdown() string {
115		var parts []string
116		for _, item := range []struct {
117			n    int
118			name string
119		}{
120			{s.Added, "added"}, {s.Modified, "modified"}, {s.Deleted, "deleted"},
121			{s.Renamed, "renamed/copied"},
122		} {
123			if item.n > 0 {
124				parts = append(parts, strconv.Itoa(item.n)+" "+item.name)
125			}
126		}
127		return strings.Join(parts, ", ")
128	}
129	
130	// StatusOf reads the porcelain v2 status of the checkout at dir. Porcelain v2
131	// is the documented machine-readable format: it reports branch, upstream and
132	// ahead/behind in the same pass as the file states, so one process gives dev
133	// everything it needs.
134	func StatusOf(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Status, error) {
135		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "status", "--porcelain=v2", "--branch", "--untracked-files=normal", "-z")
136		if err != nil {
137			return Status{}, err
138		}
139		return statusFromOutput(dir, out), nil
140	}
141	
142	func statusFromOutput(dir, out string) Status {
143		var s Status
144		for _, rec := range nulLines(out) {
145			if rec == "" {
146				continue
147			}
148			switch rec[0] {
149			case '#':
150				parseBranchHeader(rec, &s)
151			case '1', '2':
152				// "1 XY ..." ordinary change, "2 XY ..." rename/copy. X is
153				// staged, Y unstaged. This record is one unique changed path even
154				// when both sides are non-dot.
155				f := strings.Fields(rec)
156				if len(f) < 2 || len(f[1]) < 2 {
157					continue
158				}
159				s.Changed++
160				x, y := f[1][0], f[1][1]
161				if x != '.' {
162					s.Staged++
163				}
164				if y != '.' {
165					s.Unstaged++
166				}
167				classifyChange(x, &s)
168				classifyChange(y, &s)
169				updateLatestChange(dir, statusPath(rec), &s)
170			case 'u':
171				s.Changed++
172				s.Conflicted++
173				updateLatestChange(dir, statusPath(rec), &s)
174			case '?':
175				s.Changed++
176				s.Untracked++
177				updateLatestChange(dir, strings.TrimPrefix(rec, "? "), &s)
178			}
179		}
180		return s
181	}
182	
183	// statusPath extracts the final pathname from a porcelain-v2 record while
184	// preserving spaces in it. Rename records have one extra score field; their
185	// old path arrives as the next NUL record and is intentionally ignored.
186	func statusPath(rec string) string {
187		if rec == "" {
188			return ""
189		}
190		var fields int
191		switch rec[0] {
192		case '1':
193			fields = 9
194		case '2':
195			fields = 10
196		case 'u':
197			fields = 11
198		default:
199			return ""
200		}
201		parts := strings.SplitN(rec, " ", fields)
202		if len(parts) != fields {
203			return ""
204		}
205		return parts[fields-1]
206	}
207	
208	func updateLatestChange(dir, path string, s *Status) {
209		if path == "" {
210			return
211		}
212		info, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, filepath.FromSlash(path)))
213		if err == nil && info.ModTime().After(s.LatestChange) {
214			s.LatestChange = info.ModTime()
215		}
216	}
217	
218	func classifyChange(code byte, s *Status) {
219		switch code {
220		case 'A':
221			s.Added++
222		case 'M', 'T':
223			s.Modified++
224		case 'D':
225			s.Deleted++
226		case 'R', 'C':
227			s.Renamed++
228		}
229	}
230	
231	func parseBranchHeader(rec string, s *Status) {
232		f := strings.Fields(rec)
233		if len(f) < 3 {
234			return
235		}
236		switch f[1] {
237		case "branch.head":
238			if f[2] == "(detached)" {
239				s.Detached = true
240			} else {
241				s.Branch = f[2]
242			}
243		case "branch.upstream":
244			s.Upstream = f[2]
245		case "branch.ab":
246			// "# branch.ab +2 -1"
247			if len(f) < 4 {
248				return
249			}
250			s.Ahead, _ = strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimPrefix(f[2], "+"))
251			s.Behind, _ = strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimPrefix(f[3], "-"))
252		}
253	}
254	
255	// LastCommit reports the author timestamp of HEAD as a Unix epoch, and the
256	// subject line. Used to age a task in `dev sweep`.
257	func LastCommit(ctx context.Context, dir string) (unix int64, subject string, err error) {
258		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "log", "-1", "--format=%at%x00%s")
259		if err != nil || out == "" {
260			return 0, "", err
261		}
262		ts, subj, _ := strings.Cut(out, "\x00")
263		unix, _ = strconv.ParseInt(ts, 10, 64)
264		return unix, subj, nil
265	}
266	
267	// WipCommit stages non-agent product work and records a checkpoint commit.
268	// Moving transcripts/plans are deliberately excluded: their exact final bytes
269	// belong to the post-writer artifact finalizer, never an in-process checkpoint.
270	func WipCommit(ctx context.Context, dir, message string) (bool, error) {
271		st, err := StatusOf(ctx, dir)
272		if err != nil {
273			return false, err
274		}
275		if !st.Dirty() {
276			return false, nil
277		}
278		if st.Conflicted > 0 {
279			return false, &Error{Args: []string{"commit"}, Dir: dir,
280				Stderr: "checkout has unmerged paths; resolve the conflict before parking"}
281		}
282		paths, err := ChangedPaths(ctx, dir)
283		if err != nil {
284			return false, err
285		}
286		hasProductWork := false
287		for _, path := range paths {
288			if !IsAgentArtifact(path) {
289				hasProductWork = true
290				break
291			}
292		}
293		if !hasProductWork {
294			return false, nil
295		}
296		args := []string{"add", "-A", "--", "."}
297		for _, pattern := range AgentArtifactPathspecs() {
298			args = append(args, ":(exclude)"+pattern)
299		}
300		if _, err := run(ctx, dir, args...); err != nil {
301			return false, err
302		}
303		if message == "" {
304			message = "wip: checkpoint"
305		}
306		if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "commit", "-m", message); err != nil {
307			return false, err
308		}
309		return true, nil
310	}
311

1	package gitx
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"os"
7		"strings"
8	
9		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/pathx"
10	)
11	
12	// Worktree is one entry of `git worktree list --porcelain`.
13	type Worktree struct {
14		Path string
15		// Head is the commit the worktree is checked out at.
16		Head string
17		// Branch is the short branch name, empty when detached.
18		Branch   string
19		Detached bool
20		Bare     bool
21		// Locked reports a `git worktree lock`; Prunable reports a checkout whose
22		// directory has gone missing. Both block a plain remove.
23		Locked         bool
24		LockedReason   string
25		Prunable       bool
26		PrunableReason string
27		// Main reports the primary (non-linked) checkout.
28		Main bool
29	}
30	
31	// Worktrees lists every worktree of the repository containing dir, in git's
32	// own order: the main checkout first, then linked worktrees.
33	func Worktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) ([]Worktree, error) {
34		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "list", "--porcelain")
35		if err != nil {
36			return nil, err
37		}
38		var (
39			list []Worktree
40			cur  *Worktree
41		)
42		flush := func() {
43			if cur != nil {
44				list = append(list, *cur)
45				cur = nil
46			}
47		}
48		for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
49			if line == "" { // records are blank-line separated
50				flush()
51				continue
52			}
53			key, val, _ := strings.Cut(line, " ")
54			switch key {
55			case "worktree":
56				flush()
57				cur = &Worktree{Path: val, Main: len(list) == 0}
58			case "HEAD":
59				if cur != nil {
60					cur.Head = val
61				}
62			case "branch":
63				if cur != nil {
64					cur.Branch = strings.TrimPrefix(val, "refs/heads/")
65				}
66			case "detached":
67				if cur != nil {
68					cur.Detached = true
69				}
70			case "bare":
71				if cur != nil {
72					cur.Bare = true
73				}
74			case "locked":
75				if cur != nil {
76					cur.Locked, cur.LockedReason = true, val
77				}
78			case "prunable":
79				if cur != nil {
80					cur.Prunable, cur.PrunableReason = true, val
81				}
82			}
83		}
84		flush()
85		return list, nil
86	}
87	
88	// WorktreeFor finds the worktree checked out on branch, if any. Git refuses to
89	// check the same branch out twice, so at most one can match.
90	func WorktreeFor(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) (Worktree, bool, error) {
91		list, err := Worktrees(ctx, dir)
92		if err != nil {
93			return Worktree{}, false, err
94		}
95		for _, w := range list {
96			if w.Branch == branch {
97				return w, true, nil
98			}
99		}
100		return Worktree{}, false, nil
101	}
102	
103	// AddWorktree creates a linked worktree at path.
104	//
105	// When branch already exists it is checked out; otherwise it is created from
106	// base. Passing an explicit base matters: without one git branches from the
107	// *current* HEAD, so a worktree created while standing on feature/A would
108	// silently inherit feature/A's commits.
109	func AddWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path, branch, base string) error {
110		exists := BranchExists(ctx, dir, branch)
111		args := []string{"worktree", "add"}
112		if exists {
113			args = append(args, path, branch)
114		} else {
115			args = append(args, "-b", branch, path)
116			if base != "" {
117				args = append(args, base)
118			}
119		}
120		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
121		return err
122	}
123	
124	// MoveWorktree relocates a linked worktree through Git so the shared
125	// administrative metadata keeps pointing at the checkout's new path. dir may
126	// be any checkout of the same repository.
127	func MoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, source, destination string) error {
128		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "move", source, destination)
129		return err
130	}
131	
132	// RemoveWorktree removes a linked worktree checkout. It never deletes the
133	// branch — that is a separate, explicit decision.
134	func RemoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path string, force bool) error {
135		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
136		if err != nil {
137			return fmt.Errorf("resolve current directory before removing worktree: %w", err)
138		}
139		inside, err := pathx.Contains(path, cwd)
140		if err != nil {
141			return fmt.Errorf("compare current directory with worktree %s: %w", path, err)
142		}
143		if inside {
144			return fmt.Errorf("refusing to remove worktree %s while the caller is inside it", path)
145		}
146		args := []string{"worktree", "remove"}
147		if force {
148			args = append(args, "--force")
149		}
150		args = append(args, path)
151		_, err = run(ctx, dir, args...)
152		return err
153	}
154	
155	// PruneWorktrees clears administrative entries for checkouts whose directories
156	// were deleted behind git's back.
157	func PruneWorktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) error {
158		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "prune")
159		return err
160	}
161	
162	// BranchExists reports whether a local branch of that name exists.
163	func BranchExists(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) bool {
164		if branch == "" {
165			return false
166		}
167		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+branch)
168		return err == nil
169	}
170	
171	// RefExists reports whether any ref or commit-ish resolves.
172	func RefExists(ctx context.Context, dir, ref string) bool {
173		if ref == "" {
174			return false
175		}
176		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", ref+"^{commit}")
177		return err == nil
178	}

146	func suggestFor(app *App, ctx context.Context, r inventory.Row, stale time.Duration, retireOptions sweepRetireOptions) []suggestion {
