1	package gitx
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"os"
7		"strings"
8	
9		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/pathx"
10	)
11	
12	// Worktree is one entry of `git worktree list --porcelain`.
13	type Worktree struct {
14		Path string
15		// Head is the commit the worktree is checked out at.
16		Head string
17		// Branch is the short branch name, empty when detached.
18		Branch   string
19		Detached bool
20		Bare     bool
21		// Locked reports a `git worktree lock`; Prunable reports a checkout whose
22		// directory has gone missing. Both block a plain remove.
23		Locked         bool
24		LockedReason   string
25		Prunable       bool
26		PrunableReason string
27		// Main reports the primary (non-linked) checkout.
28		Main bool
29	}
30	
31	// Worktrees lists every worktree of the repository containing dir, in git's
32	// own order: the main checkout first, then linked worktrees.
33	func Worktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) ([]Worktree, error) {
34		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "list", "--porcelain")
35		if err != nil {
36			return nil, err
37		}
38		var (
39			list []Worktree
40			cur  *Worktree
41		)
42		flush := func() {
43			if cur != nil {
44				list = append(list, *cur)
45				cur = nil
46			}
47		}
48		for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
49			if line == "" { // records are blank-line separated
50				flush()
51				continue
52			}
53			key, val, _ := strings.Cut(line, " ")
54			switch key {
55			case "worktree":
56				flush()
57				cur = &Worktree{Path: val, Main: len(list) == 0}
58			case "HEAD":
59				if cur != nil {
60					cur.Head = val
61				}
62			case "branch":
63				if cur != nil {
64					cur.Branch = strings.TrimPrefix(val, "refs/heads/")
65				}
66			case "detached":
67				if cur != nil {
68					cur.Detached = true
69				}
70			case "bare":
71				if cur != nil {
72					cur.Bare = true
73				}
74			case "locked":
75				if cur != nil {
76					cur.Locked, cur.LockedReason = true, val
77				}
78			case "prunable":
79				if cur != nil {
80					cur.Prunable, cur.PrunableReason = true, val
81				}
82			}
83		}
84		flush()
85		return list, nil
86	}
87	
88	// WorktreeFor finds the worktree checked out on branch, if any. Git refuses to
89	// check the same branch out twice, so at most one can match.
90	func WorktreeFor(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) (Worktree, bool, error) {
91		list, err := Worktrees(ctx, dir)
92		if err != nil {
93			return Worktree{}, false, err
94		}
95		for _, w := range list {
96			if w.Branch == branch {
97				return w, true, nil
98			}
99		}
100		return Worktree{}, false, nil
101	}
102	
103	// AddWorktree creates a linked worktree at path.
104	//
105	// When branch already exists it is checked out; otherwise it is created from
106	// base. Passing an explicit base matters: without one git branches from the
107	// *current* HEAD, so a worktree created while standing on feature/A would
108	// silently inherit feature/A's commits.
109	func AddWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path, branch, base string) error {
110		exists := BranchExists(ctx, dir, branch)
111		args := []string{"worktree", "add"}
112		if exists {
113			args = append(args, path, branch)
114		} else {
115			args = append(args, "-b", branch, path)
116			if base != "" {
117				args = append(args, base)
118			}
119		}
120		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
121		return err
122	}
123	
124	// MoveWorktree relocates a linked worktree through Git so the shared
125	// administrative metadata keeps pointing at the checkout's new path. dir may
126	// be any checkout of the same repository.
127	func MoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, source, destination string) error {
128		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "move", source, destination)
129		return err
130	}
131	
132	// RemoveWorktree removes a linked worktree checkout. It never deletes the
133	// branch — that is a separate, explicit decision.
134	func RemoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path string, force bool) error {
135		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
136		if err != nil {
137			return fmt.Errorf("resolve current directory before removing worktree: %w", err)
138		}
139		inside, err := pathx.Contains(path, cwd)
140		if err != nil {
141			return fmt.Errorf("compare current directory with worktree %s: %w", path, err)
142		}
143		if inside {
144			return fmt.Errorf("refusing to remove worktree %s while the caller is inside it", path)
145		}
146		args := []string{"worktree", "remove"}
147		if force {
148			args = append(args, "--force")
149		}
150		args = append(args, path)
151		_, err = run(ctx, dir, args...)
152		return err
153	}
154	
155	// PruneWorktrees clears administrative entries for checkouts whose directories
156	// were deleted behind git's back.
157	func PruneWorktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) error {
158		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "prune")
159		return err
160	}
161	
162	// BranchExists reports whether a local branch of that name exists.
163	func BranchExists(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) bool {
164		if branch == "" {
165			return false
166		}
167		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+branch)
168		return err == nil
169	}
170	
171	// RefExists reports whether any ref or commit-ish resolves.
172	func RefExists(ctx context.Context, dir, ref string) bool {
173		if ref == "" {
174			return false
175		}
176		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", ref+"^{commit}")
177		return err == nil
178	}

13		"strings"

15	
16	// BranchRelation describes committed history between a task branch and base.
17	type BranchRelation struct {
18		BaseOnly   int
19		BranchOnly int
20	}
21	
22	// Contained reports that every branch commit is already reachable from base.
23	func (r BranchRelation) Contained() bool { return r.BranchOnly == 0 }
24	
25	// CompareBranches reports committed history on each side without inspecting or
26	// changing a worktree. Finish analysis and read-only closeout audits share this
27	// implementation so provider errors remain unknown rather than looking like a
28	// known non-contained branch.
29	func CompareBranches(ctx context.Context, dir, base, branch string) (BranchRelation, error) {
30		return compareBranches(ctx, dir, base, branch)
31	}
32	
33	// DirtyPath is one staged, unstaged, conflicted, or untracked checkout path.
34	// BaseEquivalent is true only when neither its index snapshot nor the final
35	// git-add-all worktree snapshot contains content absent from base.
36	type DirtyPath struct {
37		Path           string
38		OldPath        string
39		Staged         bool
40		Unstaged       bool
41		Untracked      bool
42		Conflicted     bool
43		BaseEquivalent bool
44	}
45	
46	// DisplayPath renders a rename without losing either side.
47	func (p DirtyPath) DisplayPath() string {
48		if p.OldPath != "" && p.OldPath != p.Path {
49			return p.OldPath + " -> " + p.Path
50		}
51		return p.Path
52	}
53	
54	// FinishAnalysis is the immutable preflight for a done operation.
55	type FinishAnalysis struct {
56		Status      Status
57		Relation    BranchRelation
58		Changes     []DirtyPath
59		Fingerprint string
60	}
61	
62	// UniqueDirty counts paths with content not represented by the base tree.
63	func (a FinishAnalysis) UniqueDirty() int {
64		n := 0
65		for _, change := range a.Changes {
66			if !change.BaseEquivalent {
67				n++
68			}
69		}
70		return n
71	}
72	
73	// EquivalentDirty counts dirty paths whose index and worktree snapshots both
74	// agree with the base.
75	func (a FinishAnalysis) EquivalentDirty() int {
76		return len(a.Changes) - a.UniqueDirty()
77	}
78	
79	// AnalyzeFinish compares both committed history and every uncommitted layer
80	// without changing the real index. The alternate index models the exact tree
81	// produced by `git add -A`, including untracked files but excluding ignored
82	// files according to Git's normal rules.
83	func AnalyzeFinish(ctx context.Context, dir, base, branch string) (FinishAnalysis, error) {
84		relation, err := compareBranches(ctx, dir, base, branch)
85		if err != nil {
86			return FinishAnalysis{}, err
87		}
88		changes, status, rawStatus, err := finishDirtyPaths(ctx, dir)
89		if err != nil {
90			return FinishAnalysis{}, err
91		}
92		analysis := FinishAnalysis{Status: status, Relation: relation, Changes: changes}
93		if status.Conflicted > 0 {
94			analysis.Fingerprint = finishFingerprint(rawStatus, "conflicted", "conflicted")
95			return analysis, nil
96		}
97	
98		indexTree, worktreeTree, indexDiff, worktreeDiff, err := finishTrees(ctx, dir, base)
99		if err != nil {
100			return FinishAnalysis{}, err
101		}
102		for i := range analysis.Changes {
103			change := &analysis.Changes[i]
104			unique := worktreeDiff[change.Path]
105			if change.Staged {
106				unique = unique || indexDiff[change.Path]
107			}
108			if change.OldPath != "" {
109				unique = unique || worktreeDiff[change.OldPath]
110				if change.Staged {
111					unique = unique || indexDiff[change.OldPath]
112				}
113			}
114			change.BaseEquivalent = !unique
115		}
116		analysis.Fingerprint = finishFingerprint(rawStatus, indexTree, worktreeTree)
117		return analysis, nil
118	}
119	
120	func compareBranches(ctx context.Context, dir, base, branch string) (BranchRelation, error) {
121		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-list", "--left-right", "--count", base+"..."+branch)
122		if err != nil {
123			return BranchRelation{}, err
124		}
125		fields := strings.Fields(out)
126		if len(fields) != 2 {
127			return BranchRelation{}, fmt.Errorf("git rev-list returned %q, want two counts", out)
128		}
129		baseOnly, err := strconv.Atoi(fields[0])
130		if err != nil {
131			return BranchRelation{}, fmt.Errorf("parse base-only count %q: %w", fields[0], err)
132		}
133		branchOnly, err := strconv.Atoi(fields[1])
134		if err != nil {
135			return BranchRelation{}, fmt.Errorf("parse branch-only count %q: %w", fields[1], err)
136		}
137		return BranchRelation{BaseOnly: baseOnly, BranchOnly: branchOnly}, nil
138	}
139	
140	func finishDirtyPaths(ctx context.Context, dir string) ([]DirtyPath, Status, string, error) {
141		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "status", "--porcelain=v2", "--branch", "--untracked-files=all", "-z")
142		if err != nil {
143			return nil, Status{}, "", err
144		}
145		records := nulLines(out)
146		changes := make([]DirtyPath, 0, len(records))
147		for i := 0; i < len(records); i++ {
148			rec := records[i]
149			if rec == "" {
150				continue
151			}
152			var change DirtyPath
153			switch rec[0] {
154			case '1', '2':
155				fields := strings.Fields(rec)
156				if len(fields) < 2 || len(fields[1]) < 2 {
157					continue
158				}
159				change.Path = statusPath(rec)
160				change.Staged = fields[1][0] != '.'
161				change.Unstaged = fields[1][1] != '.'
162				if rec[0] == '2' && i+1 < len(records) {
163					i++
164					change.OldPath = records[i]
165				}
166			case 'u':
167				change.Path, change.Conflicted = statusPath(rec), true
168			case '?':
169				change.Path = strings.TrimPrefix(rec, "? ")
170				change.Untracked = true
171			default:
172				continue
173			}
174			if change.Path != "" {
175				changes = append(changes, change)
176			}
177		}
178		sort.Slice(changes, func(i, j int) bool { return changes[i].DisplayPath() < changes[j].DisplayPath() })
179		return changes, statusFromOutput(dir, out), out, nil
180	}
181	
182	func finishTrees(ctx context.Context, dir, base string) (string, string, map[string]bool, map[string]bool, error) {
183		tempDir, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "dev-finish-index-*")
184		if err != nil {
185			return "", "", nil, nil, err
186		}
187		defer os.RemoveAll(tempDir)
188		objectDir := filepath.Join(tempDir, "objects")
189		if err := os.MkdirAll(objectDir, 0o755); err != nil {
190			return "", "", nil, nil, err
191		}
192		commonDir, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir")
193		if err != nil {
194			return "", "", nil, nil, err
195		}
196		if !filepath.IsAbs(commonDir) {
197			commonDir = filepath.Join(dir, commonDir)
198		}
199		repoObjects := filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(commonDir, "objects"))
200		alternates := repoObjects
201		if inherited := os.Getenv("GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES"); inherited != "" {
202			alternates += string(os.PathListSeparator) + inherited
203		}
204		objectEnv := []string{
205			"GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY=" + objectDir,
206			"GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES=" + alternates,
207		}
208		indexSource, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--git-path", "index")
209		if err != nil {
210			return "", "", nil, nil, err
211		}
212		if !filepath.IsAbs(indexSource) {
213			indexSource = filepath.Join(dir, indexSource)
214		}
215		indexBytes, err := os.ReadFile(indexSource)
216		if err != nil {
217			return "", "", nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("read index snapshot: %w", err)
218		}
219		index := filepath.Join(tempDir, "index")
220		if err := os.WriteFile(index, indexBytes, 0o600); err != nil {
221			return "", "", nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("copy index snapshot: %w", err)
222		}
223		env := append(append([]string(nil), objectEnv...), "GIT_INDEX_FILE="+index)
224		indexTree, err := runEnv(ctx, dir, env, "write-tree")
225		if err != nil {
226			return "", "", nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("snapshot index: %w", err)
227		}
228		indexDiff, err := treeDiffPaths(ctx, dir, env, base, indexTree)
229		if err != nil {
230			return "", "", nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("compare index snapshot: %w", err)
231		}
232	
233		if _, err := runEnv(ctx, dir, env, "add", "--all"); err != nil {
234			return "", "", nil, nil, err
235		}
236		worktreeTree, err := runEnv(ctx, dir, env, "write-tree")
237		if err != nil {
238			return "", "", nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("snapshot worktree: %w", err)
239		}
240		worktreeDiff, err := treeDiffPaths(ctx, dir, env, base, worktreeTree)
241		if err != nil {
242			return "", "", nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("compare worktree snapshot: %w", err)
243		}
244		return indexTree, worktreeTree, indexDiff, worktreeDiff, nil
245	}
246	
247	func treeDiffPaths(ctx context.Context, dir string, env []string, base, tree string) (map[string]bool, error) {
248		out, err := runEnv(ctx, dir, env, "diff-tree", "--no-commit-id", "--name-only", "-r", "-z", base, tree)
249		if err != nil {
250			return nil, err
251		}
252		paths := make(map[string]bool)
253		for _, path := range nulLines(out) {
254			if path != "" {
255				paths[path] = true
256			}
257		}
258		return paths, nil
259	}
260	
261	func finishFingerprint(status, indexTree, worktreeTree string) string {
262		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(status + "\x00" + indexTree + "\x00" + worktreeTree))
263		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
264	}
265	
266	// CommitAllChanges creates a normal user commit, preserving configured hooks.
267	func CommitAllChanges(ctx context.Context, dir, message string) error {
268		if strings.TrimSpace(message) == "" {
269			return errors.New("commit message is required")
270		}
271		if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "add", "--all"); err != nil {
272			return err
273		}
274		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "commit", "-m", message)
275		return err
276	}
277	
278	// DiscardAllChanges restores tracked/index state and removes non-ignored
279	// untracked files. Callers must obtain explicit destructive confirmation.
280	func DiscardAllChanges(ctx context.Context, dir string) error {
281		if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "reset", "--hard", "HEAD"); err != nil {
282			return err
283		}
284		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "clean", "-fd")
285		return err
286	}
287

1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, catalog, experiment, diskusage, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can
4	// be tested without a terminal.
5	package cli
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"fmt"
10		"io"
11		"os"
12		"path/filepath"
13		"strconv"
14		"sync"
15		"time"
16	
17		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/catalog"
18		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
19		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/diskusage"
20		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/note"
21		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/perftrace"
22		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
23		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
24	)
25	
26	// App is the state shared by every command.
27	type App struct {
28		Cfg      config.Config
29		Tasks    *task.Store
30		Catalog  *catalog.Store
31		Registry *catalog.Registry
32		Notes    *note.Service
33		Sizes    *diskusage.Manager
34	
35		In  io.Reader
36		Out io.Writer
37		Err io.Writer
38	
39		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
40		configPath string
41		// remotesPath is the --remotes override; empty means dev/remotes.toml.
42		remotesPath string
43		// scaffoldsPath is the --scaffolds override; empty means dev/scaffolds.toml.
44		scaffoldsPath string
45		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
46		runtimeOverride string
47		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
48		noRuntime bool
49		// allowSharedCheckout is an explicit escape hatch for coordinated agents
50		// whose file ownership is known to be disjoint.
51		allowSharedCheckout bool
52		// colorMode controls styling of human-readable output.
53		colorMode string
54		// interactiveCheck is a test seam for commands that prompt only when a real
55		// terminal is attached. Production falls back to interactive().
56		interactiveCheck func() bool
57		// runtimeInstance and runtimesByName are injection seams used by focused
58		// command tests.
59		runtimeInstance runtime.Runtime
60		runtimesByName  map[string]runtime.Runtime
61		// trace is an opt-in, process-local performance recorder. It is deliberately
62		// separate from durable activity stats and ordinary command output.
63		trace                  *perftrace.Recorder
64		tracePath              string
65		traceOnce              *sync.Once
66		traceTUI               bool
67		deferredReleaseRefresh bool
68	}
69	
70	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
71	func (a *App) Load() error {
72		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
73		if err != nil {
74			return err
75		}
76		a.Cfg = cfg
77		if a.In == nil {
78			a.In = os.Stdin
79		}
80		if a.Out == nil {
81			a.Out = os.Stdout
82		}
83		if a.Err == nil {
84			a.Err = os.Stderr
85		}
86		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
87		a.Catalog = catalog.NewStore(cfg.AssetsDir(), catalog.WithDiagnosticSink(func(diagnostic catalog.Diagnostic) {
88			fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "%s %s\n", a.errStyle().warning("dev: warning:"), diagnostic.Error())
89		}))
90		a.Registry = catalog.NewRegistry(a.Catalog)
91		noteStore := note.NewStore(cfg.NotesDir(), note.WithDiagnosticSink(func(path string, err error) {
92			fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: warning: skipping note %s: %v\n", filepath.Base(path), err)
93		}))
94		a.Notes = note.NewService(noteStore, cfg.NotesIndexFile())
95		a.Notes.IndexDiagnostic = func(err error) {
96			fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: warning: note search index: %v\n", err)
97		}
98		if a.Sizes == nil {
99			cache := diskusage.NewCache(filepath.Join(config.CacheHome(), "dev", "sizes-v1.json"), 10*time.Minute)
100			a.Sizes = diskusage.NewManager(cache, 2)
101		}
102		return nil
103	}
104	
105	func (a *App) interactive() bool {
106		if a.interactiveCheck != nil {
107			return a.interactiveCheck()
108		}
109		return interactive()
110	}
111	
112	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
113	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
114	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
115		if a.runtimeInstance != nil {
116			return a.runtimeInstance
117		}
118		if a.noRuntime {
119			return runtime.None{}
120		}
121		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
122		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
123			backend = a.runtimeOverride
124		}
125		return a.runtimeNamed(backend)
126	}
127	
128	// runtimeNamed resolves the backend that owns a persisted opaque handle. It
129	// deliberately bypasses the current backend override: feeding a Herdr handle to
130	// tmux after a config change is never valid.
131	func (a *App) runtimeNamed(name string) runtime.Runtime {
132		if rt := a.runtimesByName[name]; rt != nil {
133			return rt
134		}
135		if a.runtimeInstance != nil && (name == "" || a.runtimeInstance.Name() == name) {
136			return a.runtimeInstance
137		}
138		rt := runtime.Select(name)
139		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
140			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
141		}
142		return rt
143	}
144	
145	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
146	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
147		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
148	}
149	
150	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
151	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
152		message := fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)
153		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "%s %s\n", a.errStyle().warning("dev:"), message)
154	}
155	
156	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
157	// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
158	// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
159	// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
160	// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
161	// integrations.
162	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
163		// Windows shells do not inherit an extra descriptor the way the POSIX
164		// wrapper's `3>file` redirection does, so the PowerShell wrapper names a
165		// temp file instead and reads it back after dev exits.
166		if path := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE"); path != "" {
167			return os.WriteFile(path, append([]byte(dir), 0), 0o600)
168		}
169		if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
170			fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
171			if err != nil || fd < 3 {
172				return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
173			}
174			file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
175			if file == nil {
176				return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
177			}
178			if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
179				return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
180			}
181			if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
182				return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
183			}
184			return nil
185		}
186		_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
187		return err
188	}
189	
190	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
191	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
192

1	package artifact
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"sort"
6	
7		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
8		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/pathx"
9	)
10	
11	// WorktreeInspection is the read-only aggregate of every artifact intent for a
12	// checkout. Ready means each intent was explicitly discarded or finalized to a
13	// commit still reachable from a recovery ref; it never changes an intent.
14	type WorktreeInspection struct {
15		IntentCount int      `json:"intent_count"`
16		Status      Status   `json:"status,omitempty"`
17		Ready       bool     `json:"ready"`
18		IntentIDs   []string `json:"intent_ids"`
19	}
20	
21	// InspectWorktrees groups all intents once and verifies finalized commit
22	// reachability without reconciling or writing state.
23	func InspectWorktrees(ctx context.Context, store *Store) (map[string]WorktreeInspection, error) {
24		intents, err := store.List()
25		if err != nil {
26			return nil, err
27		}
28		out := map[string]WorktreeInspection{}
29		for _, intent := range intents {
30			path, err := pathx.Canonical(intent.WorktreePath)
31			if err != nil {
32				continue
33			}
34			inspection, exists := out[path]
35			if !exists {
36				inspection.Ready = true
37			}
38			inspection.IntentCount++
39			inspection.IntentIDs = append(inspection.IntentIDs, intent.ID)
40			if statusPriority(intent.Status) >= statusPriority(inspection.Status) {
41				inspection.Status = intent.Status
42			}
43			ready := intent.Status == Discarded ||
44				(intent.Status == Finalized && intent.ArtifactCommit != "" && CommitReachable(ctx, intent))
45			inspection.Ready = inspection.Ready && ready
46			out[path] = inspection
47		}
48		for path, inspection := range out {
49			sort.Strings(inspection.IntentIDs)
50			out[path] = inspection
51		}
52		return out, nil
53	}
54	
55	// CommitReachable reports whether an intent's artifact commit is retained by
56	// its checkout HEAD, task branch, or base. It is read-only and shared by
57	// integration enforcement and closeout evidence.
58	func CommitReachable(ctx context.Context, intent Intent) bool {
59		refs := []struct {
60			dir string
61			ref string
62		}{
63			{intent.WorktreePath, "HEAD"},
64			{intent.RepoPath, intent.Branch},
65			{intent.RepoPath, intent.Base},
66		}
67		for _, candidate := range refs {
68			if candidate.dir == "" || candidate.ref == "" {
69				continue
70			}
71			if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, candidate.dir, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", intent.ArtifactCommit, candidate.ref); err == nil {
72				return true
73			}
74		}
75		return false
76	}
77	
78	func statusPriority(status Status) int {
79		switch status {
80		case Discarded, Finalized:
81			return 1
82		case Armed:
83			return 2
84		case Finalizing:
85			return 3
86		case Failed:
87			return 4
88		default:
89			return 0
90		}
91	}
92

1	// Package artifact finalizes agent transcripts only after their writer exits.
2	package artifact
3	
4	import (
5		"fmt"
6		"regexp"
7		"strings"
8		"time"
9	)
10	
11	const SchemaVersion = 1
12	
13	type Status string
14	
15	const (
16		Armed      Status = "armed"
17		Finalizing Status = "finalizing"
18		Finalized  Status = "finalized"
19		Failed     Status = "failed"
20		// Discarded records an operator's explicit decision that an intent can
21		// never be finalized — its transcript is gone, or its HEAD no longer
22		// exists. It is deliberately distinct from Finalized: nothing was
23		// committed, and the record survives to say so.
24		Discarded Status = "discarded"
25	)
26	
27	// Intent is a durable handoff from an active agent to an external finalizer.
28	type Intent struct {
29		SchemaVersion      int      `json:"schema_version"`
30		ID                 string   `json:"id"`
31		RunID              string   `json:"run_id"`
32		Provider           string   `json:"provider"`
33		SessionID          string   `json:"session_id"`
34		TaskID             string   `json:"task_id,omitempty"`
35		RepoPath           string   `json:"repo_path"`
36		GitCommonDir       string   `json:"git_common_dir"`
37		WorktreePath       string   `json:"worktree_path"`
38		Branch             string   `json:"branch"`
39		Base               string   `json:"base,omitempty"`
40		Head               string   `json:"head"`
41		PlanPaths          []string `json:"plan_paths,omitempty"`
42		UnrelatedArtifacts []string `json:"unrelated_artifacts,omitempty"`
43		AllowLarge         bool     `json:"allow_large,omitempty"`
44	
45		Status         Status    `json:"status"`
46		TranscriptPath string    `json:"transcript_path,omitempty"`
47		ArtifactCommit string    `json:"artifact_commit,omitempty"`
48		FailureCode    string    `json:"failure_code,omitempty"`
49		SessionEndedAt time.Time `json:"session_ended_at,omitempty"`
50		CreatedAt      time.Time `json:"created_at"`
51		UpdatedAt      time.Time `json:"updated_at"`
52	}
53	
54	var (
55		idPattern      = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$`)
56		sessionPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+:[0-9a-fA-F-]{16,}$`)
57	)
58	
59	func (i Intent) Validate() error {
60		switch {
61		case i.SchemaVersion != SchemaVersion:
62			return fmt.Errorf("unsupported artifact intent schema %d", i.SchemaVersion)
63		case !idPattern.MatchString(i.ID):
64			return fmt.Errorf("invalid artifact intent id %q", i.ID)
65		case i.RunID == "" || !idPattern.MatchString(i.RunID):
66			return fmt.Errorf("invalid artifact run id %q", i.RunID)
67		case i.Provider == "" || i.SessionID == "":
68			return fmt.Errorf("artifact intent needs provider and session id")
69		case i.RepoPath == "" || i.WorktreePath == "" || i.GitCommonDir == "":
70			return fmt.Errorf("artifact intent needs repository, worktree and git common-dir paths")
71		case i.Branch == "" || i.Head == "":
72			return fmt.Errorf("artifact intent needs branch and head")
73		}
74		if !sessionPattern.MatchString(i.Provider + ":" + i.SessionID) {
75			return fmt.Errorf("invalid agent session %q", i.Provider+":"+i.SessionID)
76		}
77		switch i.Status {
78		case Armed, Finalizing, Finalized, Failed, Discarded:
79			return nil
80		default:
81			return fmt.Errorf("invalid artifact intent status %q", i.Status)
82		}
83	}
84	
85	func ParseSession(value string) (provider, sessionID string, err error) {
86		provider, sessionID, ok := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(value), ":")
87		provider = strings.ToLower(provider)
88		if !ok || !sessionPattern.MatchString(provider+":"+sessionID) {
89			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("invalid session %q: want provider:uuid", value)
90		}
91		return provider, sessionID, nil
92	}
93

1	package task
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"

14		"github.com/BurntSushi/toml"
15	)
16	
17	// ErrNotFound is returned when no task matches an identifier.
18	var ErrNotFound = errors.New("no such task")
19	
20	// Store is a directory of one-TOML-file-per-task.
21	//
22	// One file per task, rather than a single registry document, is a deliberate
23	// choice: the state directory is meant to be syncable across machines (it can
24	// simply be a git repo), and a shared central file would conflict on every
25	// parallel edit while separate files merge cleanly.
26	type Store struct{ Dir string }
27	
28	// NewStore returns a store rooted at dir.
29	func NewStore(dir string) *Store { return &Store{Dir: dir} }
30	
31	var idUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
32	
33	// MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.
34	func MakeID(repo, branch string) string {
35		clean := func(s string) string {
36			s = idUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
37			for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
38				s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
39			}
40			return strings.Trim(s, "-._")
41		}
42		r, b := clean(repo), clean(branch)
43		if r == "" {
44			r = "repo"
45		}
46		if b == "" {
47			b = "branch"
48		}
49		return r + "__" + b
50	}
51	
52	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".toml") }
53	
54	// Save writes a task, stamping Updated (and Created on first write).
55	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {
56		if t.ID == "" {
57			t.ID = MakeID(t.Repo, t.Branch)
58		}
59		if err := t.Validate(); err != nil {
60			return err
61		}
62		now := time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
63		if t.Created.IsZero() {
64			t.Created = now
65		}
66		t.Updated = now
67	
68		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o755); err != nil {
69			return fmt.Errorf("create state dir: %w", err)
70		}
71		// Write to a temp file and rename, so an interrupted write can never leave
72		// a half-parsed task behind.
73		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+t.ID+".*.tmp")
74		if err != nil {
75			return err
76		}
77		defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())
78		enc := toml.NewEncoder(tmp)
79		if err := enc.Encode(t); err != nil {
80			tmp.Close()
81			return fmt.Errorf("encode task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
82		}
83		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
84			return err
85		}
86		if err := os.Chmod(tmp.Name(), 0o644); err != nil {
87			return err
88		}
89		return os.Rename(tmp.Name(), s.path(t.ID))
90	}
91	
92	// Get loads one task by its exact id.
93	func (s *Store) Get(id string) (*Task, error) {
94		var t Task
95		if _, err := toml.DecodeFile(s.path(id), &t); err != nil {
96			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
97				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
98			}
99			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read task %s: %w", id, err)
100		}
101		t.ID = id
102		return &t, nil
103	}
104	
105	// List loads every task, sorted by state (hot first) then most recent.
106	func (s *Store) List() ([]*Task, error) {
107		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
108		if err != nil {
109			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
110				return nil, nil // no state yet is a normal, empty inventory
111			}
112			return nil, err
113		}
114		var out []*Task
115		for _, e := range entries {
116			name := e.Name()
117			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") {
118				continue
119			}
120			id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")
121			t, err := s.Get(id)
122			if err != nil {
123				// One corrupt file must not hide the rest of the inventory.
124				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: skipping %s: %v\n", name, err)
125				continue
126			}
127			out = append(out, t)
128		}
129		Sort(out)
130		return out, nil
131	}
132	
133	// Delete removes a task entry. It never touches git state.
134	func (s *Store) Delete(id string) error {
135		err := os.Remove(s.path(id))
136		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
137			return fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
138		}
139		return err
140	}
141	
142	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
143	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
144	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
145	// than a silent pick.
146	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
147		if ref == "" {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
149		}
150		all, err := s.List()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		for _, t := range all {
155			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
156				return t, nil
157			}
158		}
159		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
160		var hits []*Task
161		for _, t := range all {
162			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
163			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
164				hits = append(hits, t)
165			}
166		}
167		switch len(hits) {
168		case 1:
169			return hits[0], nil
170		case 0:
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
172		default:
173			names := make([]string, len(hits))
174			for i, t := range hits {
175				names[i] = t.ID
176			}
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
178		}
179	}
180	
181	// FindByWorktree returns the task whose checkout contains dir.
182	//
183	// A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
184	// the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
185	// claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
186	// every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
187	// match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
188	func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
189		all, err := s.List()
190		if err != nil {
191			return nil, err
192		}
193		under := func(dir, root string) bool {
194			return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
195		}
196		var best *Task
197		var bestLen int
198		for _, t := range all {
199			root := t.WorktreePath
200			if root == "" {
201				root = t.RepoPath
202			}
203			if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
204				best, bestLen = t, len(root)
205			}
206		}
207		if best == nil {
208			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
209		}
210		return best, nil
211	}
212	
213	// stateRank orders states so the inventory reads as an attention queue.
214	func stateRank(s State) int {
215		switch s {
216		case Hot:
217			return 0
218		case Warm:
219			return 1
220		case Cold:
221			return 2
222		case Done:
223			return 3
224		}
225		return 4
226	}
227	
228	// Sort orders tasks hot-first, then by most recently updated.
229	func Sort(ts []*Task) {
230		sort.SliceStable(ts, func(i, j int) bool {
231			ri, rj := stateRank(ts[i].State), stateRank(ts[j].State)
232			if ri != rj {
233				return ri < rj
234			}
235			if !ts[i].Updated.Equal(ts[j].Updated) {
236				return ts[i].Updated.After(ts[j].Updated)
237			}
238			return ts[i].ID < ts[j].ID
239		})
240	}

1	// Package task stores the small amount of state git cannot answer: which
2	// change streams exist, what state each is in, which machine owns it, and what
3	// the next action is. Everything else — branch, dirty, ahead/behind, whether a
4	// worktree exists — is derived live and deliberately not stored here.
5	package task
6	
7	import (
8		"fmt"
9		"strings"
10		"time"
11	)
12	
13	// State is where a change stream sits in its lifecycle.
14	type State string
15	
16	const (
17		// Hot: worktree and branch exist, a runtime session is open, actively worked on.
18		Hot State = "hot"
19		// Warm: worktree and branch kept, runtime closed. Back within days.
20		Warm State = "warm"
21		// Cold: committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstructible anywhere.
22		Cold State = "cold"
23		// Done: merged. Kept only until the entry is reaped.
24		Done State = "done"
25	)
26	
27	// States lists the lifecycle in order, for help text and validation.
28	var States = []State{Hot, Warm, Cold, Done}
29	
30	// ParseState validates a user-supplied state name.
31	func ParseState(s string) (State, error) {
32		got := State(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)))
33		for _, valid := range States {
34			if got == valid {
35				return got, nil
36			}
37		}
38		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown state %q: want one of %s", s, JoinStates(", "))
39	}
40	
41	// JoinStates renders the valid state names.
42	func JoinStates(sep string) string {
43		parts := make([]string, len(States))
44		for i, s := range States {
45			parts[i] = string(s)
46		}
47		return strings.Join(parts, sep)
48	}
49	
50	// Icon is the glyph shown in the inventory.
51	func (s State) Icon() string {
52		switch s {
53		case Hot:
54			return "🔥"
55		case Warm:
56			return "🌤"
57		case Cold:
58			return "❄️"
59		case Done:
60			return "✅"
61		}
62		return "?"
63	}
64	
65	// Label is the uppercase column form.
66	func (s State) Label() string { return strings.ToUpper(string(s)) }
67	
68	// CheckoutMode is how a task occupies the repository filesystem.
69	type CheckoutMode string
70	
71	const (
72		// ModeWorktree owns a linked worktree and branch.
73		ModeWorktree CheckoutMode = "worktree"
74		// ModeBranch uses a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout.
75		ModeBranch CheckoutMode = "branch"
76		// ModeDirect tracks ad-hoc work on the branch already checked out in the
77		// canonical repo — usually main — without creating a branch or worktree.
78		ModeDirect CheckoutMode = "direct"
79	)
80	
81	// Task is one change stream. Field names are the TOML keys.
82	type Task struct {
83		// ID is derived from repo and branch; it is the filename stem and is not
84		// stored inside the file.
85		ID string `toml:"-"`
86	
87		// Name is the human label ("atp security recovery").
88		Name string `toml:"name"`
89		// Repo is the repository's display name.
90		Repo string `toml:"repo"`
91		// RepoPath is the main checkout, the directory git commands run in.
92		RepoPath string `toml:"repo_path"`
93		// Branch is the change stream's identity — the one durable handle that
94		// survives every machine, worktree and runtime.
95		Branch string `toml:"branch"`
96		// Base is the ref the branch was created from, recorded so `dev done` can
97		// integrate without re-guessing.
98		Base string `toml:"base"`
99		// WorktreePath is the linked checkout, empty when the task works directly
100		// in the main checkout or has gone cold.
101		WorktreePath string `toml:"worktree_path"`
102		// Mode says whether this task uses a worktree, a branch in the canonical
103		// checkout, or the current branch directly. Older entries infer it.
104		Mode CheckoutMode `toml:"mode"`
105	
106		State State `toml:"state"`
107		// Owner is the hostname that last held this task hot. One writer per
108		// branch at a time avoids two machines diverging the same history.
109		Owner string `toml:"owner"`
110		// Next is the single most valuable field in the file: what to do when you
111		// come back. Without it, parking a task still loses the thread.
112		Next string   `toml:"next"`
113		Note string   `toml:"note"`
114		Tags []string `toml:"tags"`
115	
116		// AgentSession reserves a resumable agent context ("claude:<uuid>"). The
117		// production start/park/resume flow does not yet capture or attach it.
118		AgentSession string `toml:"agent_session"`
119		// RuntimeHandle is the last known runtime session id (e.g. a Herdr
120		// workspace id). RuntimeName records which backend owns that opaque handle.
121		// Both are advisory and must be revalidated against live checkout coverage.
122		RuntimeHandle string `toml:"runtime_handle"`
123		RuntimeName   string `toml:"runtime_name"`
124	
125		Created time.Time `toml:"created"`
126		Updated time.Time `toml:"updated"`
127	}
128	
129	// EffectiveMode returns the explicit mode, or infers a legacy task. Before
130	// modes were recorded, a path meant worktree and no path meant a canonical
131	// branch task; direct mode is never guessed because it changes integration
132	// semantics and must be explicit.
133	func (t Task) EffectiveMode() CheckoutMode {
134		if t.Mode != "" {
135			return t.Mode
136		}
137		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
138			return ModeWorktree
139		}
140		return ModeBranch
141	}
142	
143	// Title is the display name, falling back to the branch when unnamed.
144	func (t Task) Title() string {
145		if t.Name != "" {
146			return t.Name
147		}
148		return t.Branch
149	}
150	
151	// OwnedBy reports whether host is this task's owner. An empty owner means
152	// unclaimed, which counts as owned by anyone.
153	func (t Task) OwnedBy(host string) bool { return t.Owner == "" || t.Owner == host }
154	
155	// Validate rejects a task that could not be acted on later.
156	func (t Task) Validate() error {
157		switch {
158		case t.Repo == "":
159			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo is required", t.ID)
160		case t.Branch == "":
161			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: branch is required", t.ID)
162		case t.RepoPath == "":
163			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo_path is required", t.ID)
164		}
165		if _, err := ParseState(string(t.State)); err != nil {
166			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
167		}
168		switch t.Mode {
169		case "", ModeWorktree, ModeBranch, ModeDirect:
170		default:
171			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: unknown mode %q", t.ID, t.Mode)
172		}
173		return nil
174	}
175

1	// Package runtime abstracts the terminal multiplexer that hosts a checkout.
2	//
3	// dev deliberately owns no terminal state of its own. A runtime is where a
4	// task is *live*; the durable facts live in git and in the task registry. That
5	// separation is the whole point: closing a runtime session must never feel
6	// like abandoning a task, so every adapter here is expected to be lossy and
7	// re-derivable.
8	package runtime
9	
10	import (
11		"context"
12		"fmt"
13		"os"
14		"os/exec"
15		"strings"
16	
17		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/pathx"
18	)
19	
20	// Pane is one terminal surface inside a runtime session.
21	type Pane struct {
22		ID           string
23		CWD          string
24		ShellCWD     string
25		Agent        string
26		AgentStatus  string
27		AgentSession string
28	}
29	
30	// Session is one live workspace/session of a runtime backend.
31	type Session struct {
32		// Handle is the backend's own identifier (a herdr workspace id, a tmux
33		// session name). Opaque to the rest of dev.
34		Handle string
35		Label  string
36		// Dirs lists the working directories observed in this session. A session
37		// can span several (multiple panes), which is why this is not a single
38		// value.
39		Dirs []string
40		// AgentStatus is the backend's view of agent activity, when it has one:
41		// "working", "idle", "done", "waiting". Empty when unsupported.
42		AgentStatus string
43		// AgentSessions lists resumable agent context ids, e.g. "claude:<uuid>".
44		AgentSessions []string
45		// Panes retain the exact runtime IDs and cwd values used for caller and
46		// mixed-workspace retirement checks.
47		Panes   []Pane
48		Focused bool
49	}
50	
51	// Covers reports whether the session has a pane rooted at or under dir.
52	func (s Session) Covers(dir string) bool {
53		for _, d := range s.Dirs {
54			// A pane inside the repository makes it live. The inverse is not
55			// true: a generic pane at $HOME does not make every repository below
56			// $HOME active.
57			if inside, err := pathx.Contains(dir, d); err == nil && inside {
58				return true
59			}
60		}
61		return false
62	}
63	
64	// OpenResult is the transient result of making a checkout live. Handle may be
65	// persisted by callers, but the pane belongs to this one creation response and
66	// must never be treated as durable state.
67	type OpenResult struct {
68		Handle     string
69		Surface    string
70		Opened     bool
71		Created    bool
72		RootPaneID string
73	}
74	
75	// AgentActivity is one recognized live coding agent occupying a runtime pane.
76	// Every activity returned by a backend is occupied regardless of Status; idle,
77	// done and unknown describe lifecycle state, not permission to share a checkout.
78	type AgentActivity struct {
79		PaneID      string
80		WorkspaceID string
81		Agent       string
82		Name        string
83		Status      string
84		CWD         string
85	}
86	
87	// AgentActivityLister is an optional runtime capability. Core runtimes need not
88	// know about agents; Herdr implements it because its pane model can identify the
89	// exact process and checkout involved.
90	type AgentActivityLister interface {
91		AgentActivities(ctx context.Context) ([]AgentActivity, error)
92	}
93	
94	// CurrentPaneResolver is an optional runtime capability for resolving the live
95	// pane behind inherited caller context. Herdr pane IDs can change after a move,
96	// so collision exclusions must not trust HERDR_PANE_ID alone.
97	type CurrentPaneResolver interface {
98		CurrentPaneID(ctx context.Context) (string, error)
99	}
100	
101	// Activator is the optional interactive half of opening a runtime surface.
102	// Open deliberately remains detached so creation commands can run in the
103	// background. Navigation commands call Activate after their own terminal UI
104	// has been torn down: inside a multiplexer this switches the current client;
105	// outside it attaches a new client and blocks until the user detaches.
106	type Activator interface {
107		Activate(ctx context.Context, handle string) error
108	}
109	
110	// PaneRunner is the optional exact-pane command surface. The command is shell
111	// text for the pane's existing interactive shell, not argv for a child process
112	// started by dev. Implementations must not include command text in errors.
113	type PaneRunner interface {
114		RunInPane(ctx context.Context, paneID, command string) error
115	}
116	
117	// Runtime is the contract every backend satisfies. Adapters must degrade
118	// gracefully: an unavailable backend returns errors rather than panicking, and
119	// List on an idle backend returns an empty slice, not an error.
120	type Runtime interface {
121		// Name is the backend identifier used in config and in `dev doctor`.
122		Name() string
123		// Available reports whether this backend can be used on this machine right
124		// now (binary installed and, where relevant, a server reachable).
125		Available() bool
126		// Open makes dir live. Its result distinguishes a newly created surface from
127		// a reused one and may carry a root pane proven by that same create response.
128		Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (OpenResult, error)
129		// Close ends the session without touching the checkout, the branch or the
130		// task entry.
131		Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error
132		// List enumerates live sessions.
133		List(ctx context.Context) ([]Session, error)
134		// Annotate attaches display-only metadata to a session (state, next
135		// action). Backends without a metadata channel implement this as a no-op.
136		Annotate(ctx context.Context, handle string, kv map[string]string) error
137	}
138	
139	// WorktreeOpener is implemented by backends that understand git worktrees and
140	// can present one as a first-class session grouped under its parent repo.
141	// dev always creates the worktree itself — this only surfaces it.
142	type WorktreeOpener interface {
143		OpenWorktree(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (OpenResult, error)
144	}
145	
146	// ErrUnavailable reports a backend that is not usable on this machine.
147	type ErrUnavailable struct{ Backend, Reason string }
148	
149	func (e *ErrUnavailable) Error() string {
150		return fmt.Sprintf("runtime %s unavailable: %s", e.Backend, e.Reason)
151	}
152	
153	// Select resolves a configured backend name to a Runtime.
154	//
155	// "auto" prefers the richest backend that is actually available: herdr (which
156	// models workspaces, worktrees and agent sessions), then tmux, then zellij,
157	// then None.
158	// None is always available so dev never hard-fails for lack of a multiplexer.
159	func Select(backend string) Runtime {
160		herdr, tmux, zellij, none := NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), NewZellij(), None{}
161		switch backend {
162		case "herdr":
163			return herdr
164		case "tmux":
165			return tmux
166		case "zellij":
167			return zellij

185	// All returns every backend, for `dev doctor` to report on.

188	// haveBinary reports whether name is on PATH.
189	func haveBinary(name string) bool {
190		_, err := exec.LookPath(name)
191		return err == nil
192	}
193	
194	// runInteractive connects a multiplexer client directly to dev's terminal.
195	// Runtime protocol calls use captured stdout/stderr; attach clients must not,
196	// because they own the terminal until the user detaches.
197	func runInteractive(ctx context.Context, bin string, args ...string) error {
198		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, bin, args...)
199		cmd.Stdin, cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = os.Stdin, os.Stdout, os.Stderr
200		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
201			return fmt.Errorf("%s %s: %w", bin, strings.Join(args, " "), err)
202		}
203		return nil
204	}

1	// Package lockx provides a cross-platform advisory lock over a directory.
2	//
3	// It is a leaf package on purpose. Both the catalog store and Git transaction
4	// code need to serialize mutations, and neither should have to depend on the
5	// other to get a lock.
6	package lockx
7	
8	import (
9		"context"
10		"errors"
11		"fmt"
12		"os"
13		"path/filepath"
14	)
15	
16	// WithDir runs operation while holding an exclusive lock for dir. The lock file
17	// lives beside dir rather than inside it, so locking never adds a file to the
18	// directory being protected. label names the caller in wrapped errors.
19	func WithDir(ctx context.Context, dir, label string, operation func() error) (err error) {
20		if operation == nil {
21			return fmt.Errorf("%s lock requires an operation", label)
22		}
23		if ctx == nil {
24			ctx = context.Background()
25		}
26		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
27			return fmt.Errorf("create %s directory for lock: %w", label, err)
28		}
29		absoluteDir, err := filepath.Abs(dir)
30		if err != nil {
31			return fmt.Errorf("make %s directory absolute for lock: %w", label, err)
32		}
33		canonicalDir, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(absoluteDir)
34		if err != nil {
35			return fmt.Errorf("canonicalize %s directory for lock: %w", label, err)
36		}
37		lockPath := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(canonicalDir), "."+filepath.Base(canonicalDir)+".lock")
38		lock, err := acquire(ctx, lockPath)
39		if err != nil {
40			return fmt.Errorf("acquire %s lock: %w", label, err)
41		}
42		defer func() {
43			if releaseErr := lock.Close(); releaseErr != nil {
44				err = errors.Join(err, fmt.Errorf("release %s lock: %w", label, releaseErr))
45			}
46		}()
47		return operation()
48	}
49

1	// Package pathx provides the path-safety checks shared by filesystem lifecycle
2	// operations. The checks are strict: a destination must be below its root, not
3	// merely share a string prefix with it, and symlinks are resolved before that
4	// decision is made.
5	package pathx
6	
7	import (
8		"errors"
9		"fmt"
10		"io/fs"
11		"os"
12		"path/filepath"
13		"slices"
14		"strings"
15	)
16	
17	var (
18		// ErrOutsideRoot reports a path that does not resolve below the requested root.
19		ErrOutsideRoot = errors.New("path is outside root")
20		// ErrRoot reports an operation that named the root itself rather than a child.
21		ErrRoot = errors.New("path is the root itself")
22		// ErrTraversal reports an explicit .. component in an unclean input path.
23		ErrTraversal = errors.New("path contains parent traversal")
24		// ErrInvalidComponent reports a value that is not one filesystem component.
25		ErrInvalidComponent = errors.New("invalid path component")
26	)
27	
28	// Canonical returns an absolute, clean path with symlinks resolved. If the final
29	// path does not exist yet, it resolves the nearest existing ancestor and then
30	// appends the missing suffix. This is the form needed to validate a destination
31	// before creating or moving anything into it.
32	func Canonical(path string) (string, error) {
33		if path == "" {
34			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonical path: empty path")
35		}
36		absolute, err := filepath.Abs(path)
37		if err != nil {
38			return "", fmt.Errorf("make %q absolute: %w", path, err)
39		}
40		absolute = filepath.Clean(absolute)
41	
42		probe := absolute
43		var missing []string
44		for {
45			resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(probe)
46			if err == nil {
47				slices.Reverse(missing)
48				parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
49				return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
50			}
51			if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
52				return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: %w", path, err)
53			}
54			// EvalSymlinks reports ErrNotExist both for a genuinely missing component
55			// and for a symlink whose target is missing. Treating the latter as an
56			// ordinary lexical suffix would make an escape look as though it remained
57			// below its root. Resolve the link target explicitly before appending the
58			// still-missing suffix.
59			if info, lstatErr := os.Lstat(probe); lstatErr == nil && info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
60				target, readErr := os.Readlink(probe)
61				if readErr != nil {
62					return "", fmt.Errorf("read unresolved symlink %q: %w", probe, readErr)
63				}
64				if hasParentTraversal(target) {
65					return "", fmt.Errorf("unresolved symlink %q target %q: %w", probe, target, ErrTraversal)
66				}
67				if !filepath.IsAbs(target) {
68					target = filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(probe), target)
69				}
70				resolved, resolveErr := Canonical(target)
71				if resolveErr != nil {
72					return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve target of %q: %w", probe, resolveErr)
73				}
74				slices.Reverse(missing)
75				parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
76				return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
77			} else if lstatErr != nil && !errors.Is(lstatErr, fs.ErrNotExist) {
78				return "", fmt.Errorf("inspect unresolved path %q: %w", probe, lstatErr)
79			}
80			parent := filepath.Dir(probe)
81			if parent == probe {
82				return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: no existing ancestor: %w", path, err)
83			}
84			missing = append(missing, filepath.Base(probe))
85			probe = parent
86		}
87	}
88	
89	// CanonicalChild returns candidate in canonical form when it resolves strictly
90	// below root. It rejects root itself, lexical .. traversal, sibling-prefix
91	// confusion, and paths that escape through a symlink.
92	func CanonicalChild(root, candidate string) (string, error) {
93		if hasParentTraversal(candidate) {
94			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", candidate, ErrTraversal)
95		}
96		canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
97		if err != nil {
98			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize root: %w", err)
99		}
100		canonicalCandidate, err := Canonical(candidate)
101		if err != nil {
102			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize candidate: %w", err)
103		}
104	
105		rel, err := filepath.Rel(canonicalRoot, canonicalCandidate)
106		if err != nil {
107			// Rel only fails when the two paths cannot be expressed relative to one
108			// another — most often different Windows volumes. That is a definitive
109			// "not below root", not a filesystem error to surface.
110			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q is not below %q: %w", candidate, root, ErrOutsideRoot)
111		}
112		switch {
113		case rel == ".":
114			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", candidate, ErrRoot)
115		case filepath.IsAbs(rel), rel == "..", strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator)):
116			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q is not below %q: %w", candidate, root, ErrOutsideRoot)
117		default:
118			return canonicalCandidate, nil
119		}
120	}
121	
122	// IsChild reports whether candidate resolves strictly below root. Policy
123	// rejections are returned as false without hiding filesystem errors.
124	func IsChild(root, candidate string) (bool, error) {
125		_, err := CanonicalChild(root, candidate)
126		if err == nil {
127			return true, nil
128		}
129		if errors.Is(err, ErrOutsideRoot) || errors.Is(err, ErrRoot) || errors.Is(err, ErrTraversal) {
130			return false, nil
131		}
132		return false, err
133	}
134	
135	// Contains reports whether candidate is root itself or resolves below it.
136	func Contains(root, candidate string) (bool, error) {
137		canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
138		if err != nil {
139			return false, err
140		}
141		canonicalCandidate, err := Canonical(candidate)
142		if err != nil {
143			return false, err
144		}
145		if canonicalRoot == canonicalCandidate {
146			return true, nil
147		}
148		return IsChild(canonicalRoot, canonicalCandidate)
149	}
150	
151	// ValidateComponent requires a non-empty relative value containing exactly one
152	// path component. Both slash styles are rejected so state synced between Unix
153	// and Windows cannot acquire a different meaning on another host.
154	func ValidateComponent(component string) error {
155		switch {
156		case strings.TrimSpace(component) == "":
157			return fmt.Errorf("empty component: %w", ErrInvalidComponent)
158		case strings.ContainsRune(component, '\x00'):
159			return fmt.Errorf("component contains NUL: %w", ErrInvalidComponent)
160		case component == "." || component == "..":
161			return fmt.Errorf("component %q is reserved: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
162		case filepath.IsAbs(component) || filepath.VolumeName(component) != "" || driveQualified(component):
163			return fmt.Errorf("component %q is absolute or drive-qualified: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
164		case strings.ContainsAny(component, `/\\`):
165			return fmt.Errorf("component %q contains a path separator: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
166		case filepath.Clean(component) != component || filepath.Base(component) != component:
167			return fmt.Errorf("component %q is not a single clean name: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
168		default:
169			return nil
170		}
171	}
172	
173	// JoinChild validates every component, joins it below root, and returns the
174	// canonical destination. It is suitable for paths such as
175	// <project-root>/<category>/<name>, where each user-supplied value must remain a
176	// single component.
177	func JoinChild(root string, components ...string) (string, error) {
178		if len(components) == 0 {
179			return "", fmt.Errorf("join child: no components: %w", ErrRoot)
180		}
181		for i, component := range components {
182			if err := ValidateComponent(component); err != nil {
183				return "", fmt.Errorf("component %d: %w", i, err)
184			}
185		}
186		canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
187		if err != nil {
188			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize root: %w", err)
189		}
190		return CanonicalChild(canonicalRoot, filepath.Join(append([]string{canonicalRoot}, components...)...))
191	}
192	
193	func driveQualified(component string) bool {
194		if len(component) < 2 || component[1] != ':' {
195			return false
196		}
197		letter := component[0]
198		return letter >= 'a' && letter <= 'z' || letter >= 'A' && letter <= 'Z'
199	}
200	
201	func hasParentTraversal(path string) bool {
202		for _, component := range strings.FieldsFunc(path, func(r rune) bool {
203			return r == '/' || r == '\\'
204		}) {
205			if component == ".." {
206				return true
207			}
208		}
209		return false
210	}

20	
21	var ErrIntentNotFound = errors.New("artifact intent not found")
22	
23	// Store keeps one strict JSON intent per finalization handoff.
24	type Store struct {
25		Dir   string
26		clock func() time.Time
27		newID func() string
28	}
29	
30	func NewStore(dir string) *Store {
31		return &Store{Dir: dir, clock: time.Now, newID: randomID}
32	}
33	
34	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".json") }
35	
36	func (s *Store) Create(ctx context.Context, intent *Intent) error {
37		if intent == nil {
38			return fmt.Errorf("create nil artifact intent")
39		}
40		return lockx.WithDir(ctx, s.Dir, "artifact intent", func() error {
41			candidate := *intent
42			if candidate.ID == "" {
43				candidate.ID = s.newID()
44			}
45			candidate.SchemaVersion = SchemaVersion
46			candidate.Status = Armed
47			now := s.clock().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
48			candidate.CreatedAt, candidate.UpdatedAt = now, now
49			if err := candidate.Validate(); err != nil {
50				return err
51			}
52			if _, err := os.Stat(s.path(candidate.ID)); err == nil {
53				return fmt.Errorf("artifact intent %s already exists", candidate.ID)
54			} else if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
55				return err
56			}
57			if err := s.write(candidate); err != nil {
58				return err
59			}
60			*intent = candidate
61			return nil
62		})
63	}
64	
65	func (s *Store) Get(id string) (*Intent, error) {
66		if !idPattern.MatchString(id) {
67			return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid artifact intent id %q", id)
68		}
69		file, err := os.Open(s.path(id))
70		if err != nil {
71			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
72				return nil, fmt.Errorf("artifact intent %s: %w", id, ErrIntentNotFound)
73			}
74			return nil, err
75		}
76		defer file.Close()
77		decoder := json.NewDecoder(file)
78		decoder.DisallowUnknownFields()
79		var intent Intent
80		if err := decoder.Decode(&intent); err != nil {
81			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode artifact intent %s: %w", id, err)
82		}
83		if err := ensureJSONEOF(decoder); err != nil {
84			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode artifact intent %s: %w", id, err)
85		}
86		if intent.ID != id {
87			return nil, fmt.Errorf("artifact intent filename %s disagrees with id %s", id, intent.ID)
88		}
89		if err := intent.Validate(); err != nil {
90			return nil, err
91		}
92		return &intent, nil
93	}
94	
95	func (s *Store) List() ([]Intent, error) {
96		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
97		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
98			return nil, nil
99		}
100		if err != nil {
101			return nil, err
102		}
103		var intents []Intent
104		for _, entry := range entries {
105			if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(entry.Name(), ".json") {
106				continue
107			}
108			intent, err := s.Get(strings.TrimSuffix(entry.Name(), ".json"))
109			if err != nil {
110				return nil, err
111			}
112			intents = append(intents, *intent)
113		}
114		sort.Slice(intents, func(i, j int) bool { return intents[i].CreatedAt.Before(intents[j].CreatedAt) })
115		return intents, nil
116	}
117	
118	func (s *Store) FindByRunID(runID string) (*Intent, error) {
119		intents, err := s.List()
120		if err != nil {
121			return nil, err
122		}
123		for i := range intents {
124			if intents[i].RunID == runID {
125				return &intents[i], nil
126			}
127		}
128		return nil, fmt.Errorf("artifact run %s: %w", runID, ErrIntentNotFound)
129	}
130	
131	func (s *Store) Update(ctx context.Context, id string, mutate func(*Intent) error) error {
132		if mutate == nil {
133			return fmt.Errorf("artifact update needs a mutation")
134		}
135		return lockx.WithDir(ctx, s.Dir, "artifact intent", func() error {
136			intent, err := s.Get(id)
137			if err != nil {
138				return err
139			}
140			if err := mutate(intent); err != nil {
141				return err
142			}
143			intent.UpdatedAt = s.clock().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
144			if err := intent.Validate(); err != nil {
145				return err
146			}
147			return s.write(*intent)
148		})
149	}
150	
151	func (s *Store) write(intent Intent) error {
152		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o700); err != nil {
153			return err
154		}
155		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, ".intent-*.tmp")
156		if err != nil {
157			return err
158		}
159		name := tmp.Name()
160		defer os.Remove(name)
161		if err := tmp.Chmod(0o600); err != nil {
162			tmp.Close()
163			return err
164		}
165		encoder := json.NewEncoder(tmp)
166		encoder.SetIndent("", "  ")
167		if err := encoder.Encode(intent); err != nil {
168			tmp.Close()
169			return err
170		}
171		if err := tmp.Sync(); err != nil {
172			tmp.Close()
173			return err
174		}
175		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
176			return err
177		}
178		return os.Rename(name, s.path(intent.ID))
179	}
180	
181	func ensureJSONEOF(decoder *json.Decoder) error {
182		var extra any
183		if err := decoder.Decode(&extra); errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
184			return nil
185		} else if err != nil {
186			return err
187		}
188		return fmt.Errorf("multiple JSON values")
189	}
190	
191	func randomID() string {
192		var raw [12]byte
193		if _, err := rand.Read(raw[:]); err != nil {
194			return fmt.Sprintf("intent-%d", time.Now().UnixNano())
195		}
196		return "intent-" + hex.EncodeToString(raw[:])
197	}

34	func newHarness(t *testing.T) *harness {

44		// real use rather than via an absolute path.

48			t.Fatal(err)
49		}
50		r.Root = dest
51	
52		// Isolate every path dev touches from the developer's real machine.
53		t.Setenv("HOME", home)
54		t.Setenv("XDG_DATA_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".local", "share"))
55		t.Setenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".config"))
56		t.Setenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".cache"))

65		// normalizes them back to the OS separator on use.

1	package gitx
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"os"
6		"path/filepath"
7		"strings"
8	)
9	
10	// Repo identifies one repository, independent of which worktree you are
11	// standing in. Two linked worktrees of the same clone share a Key.
12	type Repo struct {
13		// Root is the working-tree root of the checkout that was probed.
14		Root string
15		// GitDir is this checkout's administrative directory. A linked worktree has
16		// its own entry below the shared common directory.
17		GitDir string
18		// GitCommonDir is the shared .git directory — the same value for every
19		// worktree of a clone, which makes it the natural identity.
20		GitCommonDir string
21		// Name is the basename users recognise the repo by.
22		Name string
23		// IsLinkedWorktree reports whether Root is a linked worktree rather than
24		// the main checkout.
25		IsLinkedWorktree bool
26		// MainRoot is the main (non-linked) checkout of this clone.
27		MainRoot string
28		// Bare reports whether the main checkout is a bare repository.
29		Bare bool
30	}
31	
32	// Key is the stable identity of the clone, shared by all its worktrees.
33	func (r Repo) Key() string { return r.GitCommonDir }
34	
35	// Discover probes dir and reports the repository containing it.
36	func Discover(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Repo, error) {
37		// A single rev-parse call answers everything: batching avoids four
38		// process spawns per repo, which matters when scanning 39 of them.
39		out, err := run(ctx, dir,
40			"rev-parse",
41			"--path-format=absolute",
42			"--show-toplevel",
43			"--git-dir",
44			"--git-common-dir",
45			"--is-bare-repository",
46		)
47		if err != nil {
48			return Repo{}, err
49		}
50		f := lines(out)
51		r := Repo{}
52		// A bare repo has no toplevel, so git prints one fewer line.
53		switch len(f) {
54		case 4:
55			r.Root = f[0]
56			r.GitDir = f[1]
57			r.GitCommonDir = f[2]
58			r.Bare = f[3] == "true"
59		case 3:
60			r.GitDir = f[0]
61			r.GitCommonDir = f[1]
62			r.Bare = f[2] == "true"
63		default:
64			return Repo{}, ErrNotARepo
65		}
66	
67		// The main checkout is the parent of the common .git dir, except for a
68		// bare repo (where the common dir *is* the repo).
69		if r.Bare {
70			r.MainRoot = strings.TrimSuffix(r.GitCommonDir, string(filepath.Separator))
71		} else if r.GitDir == r.GitCommonDir {
72			// A normal checkout may use --separate-git-dir, so the common directory's
73			// parent is not necessarily the working-tree root.
74			r.MainRoot = r.Root
75		} else {
76			r.MainRoot = filepath.Dir(r.GitCommonDir)
77		}
78		r.IsLinkedWorktree = r.Root != "" && r.GitDir != r.GitCommonDir
79		r.Name = filepath.Base(r.MainRoot)
80		if r.Bare {
81			// ".../foo/.bare" or ".../foo.git" should both read as "foo".
82			r.Name = strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(r.MainRoot), ".git")
83			if strings.HasPrefix(r.Name, ".") {
84				r.Name = filepath.Base(filepath.Dir(r.MainRoot))
85			}
86		}
87		return r, nil
88	}
89	
90	// IsRepo reports whether dir is inside a git working tree, without the cost of
91	// a full Discover.
92	func IsRepo(ctx context.Context, dir string) bool {
93		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--git-dir")
94		return err == nil
95	}
96	
97	// DefaultBranch resolves the repository's default branch — origin/HEAD when the
98	// remote advertises it, else the first of main/master that exists locally.
99	// Returns "" when nothing can be determined, which callers must treat as
100	// "ask the user" rather than guessing.
101	func DefaultBranch(ctx context.Context, dir string) string {
102		if out, err := run(ctx, dir, "symbolic-ref", "--short", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD"); err == nil {
103			if _, b, ok := strings.Cut(out, "/"); ok {
104				return b
105			}
106		}
107		for _, cand := range []string{"main", "master", "trunk", "develop"} {

115	// Remote returns the push URL of the named remote ("origin" when empty).
116	func Remote(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) string {
117		if name == "" {
118			name = "origin"
119		}
120		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "remote", "get-url", name)
121		if err != nil {
122			return ""
123		}
124		return out
125	}
126	
127	// RemoteFromConfig reads one remote URL directly from a Git common directory.
128	// It is the zero-process path used by whole-machine inventory, where spawning
129	// `git remote get-url` once per repo dominated startup. Includes and URL
130	// rewriting are deliberately not evaluated; callers that need Git's complete
131	// semantics should use Remote instead.
132	func RemoteFromConfig(commonDir, name string) string {
133		if commonDir == "" {
134			return ""
135		}
136		if name == "" {
137			name = "origin"
138		}
139		b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(commonDir, "config"))
140		if err != nil {
141			return ""
142		}
143		want := `remote "` + name + `"`
144		section := ""
145		for _, raw := range strings.Split(string(b), "\n") {
146			line := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
147			if line == "" || strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") || strings.HasPrefix(line, ";") {
148				continue
149			}
150			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "[") && strings.HasSuffix(line, "]") {
151				section = strings.TrimSpace(line[1 : len(line)-1])
152				continue
153			}
154			if section != want {
155				continue
156			}
157			key, value, ok := strings.Cut(line, "=")
158			if ok && strings.TrimSpace(key) == "url" {
159				return strings.Trim(strings.TrimSpace(value), `"`)
160			}
161		}
162		return ""
163	}

35	func InProgress(dir string) (string, bool, error) {
36		repository, err := Discover(context.Background(), dir)
37		if err != nil {
38			return "", false, err
39		}
40		// REBASE_HEAD is deliberately absent: Git leaves it behind after a rebase
41		// *completes*, so treating it as evidence would permanently block every
42		// worktree that was ever rebased. Only the rebase state directories prove
43		// a rebase is still running.
44		for _, candidate := range []string{
45			"MERGE_HEAD", "CHERRY_PICK_HEAD", "REVERT_HEAD",
46			"rebase-merge", "rebase-apply", "sequencer",
47		} {
48			for _, root := range []string{repository.GitDir, repository.GitCommonDir} {
49				if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(root, candidate)); err == nil {
50					return candidate, true, nil
51				} else if !errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
52					return "", false, err
53				}
54			}
55		}
56		return "", false, nil
57	}

59	func Uncommit(ctx context.Context, dir string, rewritePublished bool) (*UncommitReceipt, error) {
60		repository, status, err := transactionPreflight(ctx, dir, rewritePublished)
61		if err != nil {
62			return nil, err
63		}
64		if status.Staged > 0 {
65			return nil, fmt.Errorf("uncommit requires an empty index so existing staged work is not mixed")
66		}
67		line, err := Run(ctx, repository.Root, "rev-list", "--parents", "-n", "1", "HEAD")
68		if err != nil {
69			return nil, err
70		}
71		fields := strings.Fields(line)
72		if len(fields) != 2 {
73			if len(fields) == 1 {
74				return nil, fmt.Errorf("cannot uncommit the root commit")
75			}
76			return nil, fmt.Errorf("cannot uncommit a merge commit; parent topology would be lost")
77		}
78		receipt := &UncommitReceipt{OldOID: fields[0], Parent: fields[1], Branch: status.Branch, Created: time.Now().UTC()}
79		path := uncommitReceiptPath(repository.GitDir)
80		if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
81			return nil, fmt.Errorf("an uncommit receipt already exists; run dev git recommit first")
82		} else if !errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
83			return nil, err
84		}
85		if err := writeJSONAtomic(path, receipt); err != nil {
86			return nil, err
87		}
88		if _, err := Run(ctx, repository.Root, "reset", "--soft", receipt.Parent); err != nil {
89			_ = os.Remove(path)
90			return nil, err
91		}
92		return receipt, nil
93	}

95	func Recommit(ctx context.Context, dir string) (string, error) {
96		repository, err := Discover(ctx, dir)
97		if err != nil {
98			return "", err
99		}
100		if operation, active, err := InProgress(repository.Root); err != nil {
101			return "", err
102		} else if active {
103			return "", fmt.Errorf("Git operation %s is in progress", operation)
104		}
105		path := uncommitReceiptPath(repository.GitDir)
106		receipt, err := readReceipt(path)
107		if err != nil {
108			return "", err
109		}
110		status, err := StatusOf(ctx, repository.Root)
111		if err != nil {
112			return "", err
113		}
114		if status.Detached || status.Branch != receipt.Branch {
115			return "", fmt.Errorf("branch changed from %s to %s", receipt.Branch, status.Branch)
116		}
117		if status.Staged == 0 {
118			return "", fmt.Errorf("nothing is staged to recommit")
119		}
120		head, err := Run(ctx, repository.Root, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
121		if err != nil {
122			return "", err
123		}
124		if head != receipt.Parent {
125			return "", fmt.Errorf("HEAD changed since uncommit: expected %s, got %s", receipt.Parent, head)
126		}
127		if !RefExists(ctx, repository.Root, receipt.OldOID) {
128			return "", fmt.Errorf("original commit %s is no longer available", receipt.OldOID)
129		}
130		if _, err := Run(ctx, repository.Root, "commit", "-C", receipt.OldOID); err != nil {
131			return "", err
132		}
133		commit, err := Run(ctx, repository.Root, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
134		if err != nil {
135			return "", err
136		}
137		if err := os.Remove(path); err != nil {
138			return "", fmt.Errorf("commit created, but remove uncommit receipt: %w", err)
139		}
140		return commit, nil
141	}

175			if result.StashOID == "" {

177			}
178			if _, err := Run(ctx, repository.Root, "stash", "apply", "--index", result.StashOID); err != nil {
179				return fmt.Errorf("restore local work from stash %s failed; stash retained: %w", result.StashOID, err)
180			}
181			result.Restored = true

195			if path == "" {

197			}
198			if root, seen := rootCache[path]; seen {
199				return root, root != ""
200			}
201			root, ok := canonicalWorktreeRoot(ctx, path)
202			if !ok {
203				root = ""
204			}
205			rootCache[path] = root
206			return root, ok
207		}
208		for _, pane := range session.Panes {
209			for _, path := range []string{pane.CWD, pane.ShellCWD} {
210				if root, ok := rootFor(path); ok {
211					rootSet[root] = true
212				}
213			}
214		}
215		for _, dir := range session.Dirs {

15	// AuditStatus is the read-only result of one retirement check or a complete
16	// audit. Audit eligibility is advisory; Service.Retire remains authoritative
17	// and revalidates every destructive step.
18	type AuditStatus string
19	
20	const (
21		AuditEligible      AuditStatus = "eligible"
22		AuditBlocked       AuditStatus = "blocked"
23		AuditUnknown       AuditStatus = "unknown"
24		AuditNotApplicable AuditStatus = "not-applicable"
25	)

32		CheckTaskIdentity      = "task-identity"

46	// Fact represents a boolean observation that may not have been collected.

53	// KnownFact constructs a collected boolean fact.
54	func KnownFact(value bool) Fact { return Fact{Known: true, Value: value} }

96	// Audit classifies already-collected retirement facts without changing any
97	// runtime, worktree, branch, task, or artifact state.
98	func Audit(input AuditInput) AuditResult {
99		if input.TargetKind == AuditTargetCanonical {
100			return notApplicableAudit("canonical checkout retirement is not applicable")
101		}
102		if input.TargetKind == AuditTargetEphemeral {
103			return notApplicableAudit("ephemeral checkout retirement is not managed here")
104		}
105	
106		checks := []AuditCheck{
107			targetKindCheck(input.TargetKind),
108			registrationCheck(input),
109			unlockedCheck(input.Unlocked),
110			branchNamedCheck(input.BranchNamed),
111			identityCheck(input.IdentityMatches),
112			pathCheck(input.PathExists),
113			statusCheck(input),
114			cleanCheck(input),
115			operationCheck(input),
116			baseCheck(input.BaseKnown),
117			containmentCheck(input),
118			taskCheck(input),
119			artifactKnownCheck(input.ArtifactKnown),
120			artifactFinalizedCheck(input),
121			runtimeKnownCheck(input.RuntimeKnown),
122			runtimeReadyCheck(input),
123		}
124		return AuditResult{Status: aggregateAuditStatus(checks), Checks: checks}
125	}
126	
127	func targetKindCheck(kind AuditTargetKind) AuditCheck {
128		switch kind {
129		case AuditTargetDev, AuditTargetExternal:
130			return check(CheckTargetKind, AuditEligible, "target is a non-canonical, non-ephemeral checkout")
131		case "":
132			return check(CheckTargetKind, AuditUnknown, "checkout ownership is unknown")
133		default:
134			return check(CheckTargetKind, AuditUnknown, "checkout ownership is unrecognized")
135		}
136	}

138	func registrationCheck(input AuditInput) AuditCheck {
139		if !input.Registered.Known {
140			return check(CheckRegistered, AuditUnknown, "worktree registration was not inspected")
141		}
142		if input.Registered.Value {
143			return check(CheckRegistered, AuditEligible, "checkout is registered as a linked worktree")
144		}
145		if !input.PathExists.Known {
146			return check(CheckRegistered, AuditUnknown, "checkout is unregistered but path existence is unknown")
147		}
148		if input.PathExists.Value {
149			return check(CheckRegistered, AuditBlocked, "checkout path exists but is not registered as a linked worktree")
150		}
151		return check(CheckRegistered, AuditEligible, "checkout is already absent from the worktree registry")
152	}
