func writeWorkflowFixture(t *testing.T, home, worktree, workflowState, agentState string, result, resumed bool, at time.Time) {
	t.Helper()
	session := filepath.Join(home, ".claude", "projects", "project-1", "session-1")
	workflowDir := filepath.Join(session, "workflows")
	mappingDir := filepath.Join(session, "subagents", "workflows", "wf_run-1")
	for _, dir := range []string{workflowDir, mappingDir} {
		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o700); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	workflow := `{"id":"wf_run-1","status":"` + workflowState + `","updatedAt":"` + at.Add(3*time.Minute).Format(time.RFC3339) + `","prompt":"TOP SECRET PROMPT"}`
	meta := `{"workflowId":"wf_run-1","runId":"wf_run-1","agentId":"agent-1","worktreePath":` + jsonQuote(worktree) + `,"spawnedWithWorktree":true,"isolation":"worktree","state":"` + agentState + `","updatedAt":"` + at.Add(2*time.Minute).Format(time.RFC3339) + `","script":"TOP SECRET SCRIPT"}`
	journal := `{"type":"started","workflowId":"wf_run-1","runId":"wf_run-1","agentId":"agent-1","timestamp":"` + at.Format(time.RFC3339) + `"}` + "\n"
	if result {
		journal += `{"type":"result","workflowId":"wf_run-1","runId":"wf_run-1","agentId":"agent-1","timestamp":"` + at.Add(time.Minute).Format(time.RFC3339) + `","result":{"body":"TOP SECRET RESULT"}}` + "\n"
	}
	paths := map[string]string{
		filepath.Join(workflowDir, "wf_run-1.json"): workflow,
		filepath.Join(mappingDir, "agent-agent-1.meta.json"): meta,
		filepath.Join(mappingDir, "journal.jsonl"): journal,
	}
	if resumed {
		paths[filepath.Join(session, "subagents", "agent-agent-1.jsonl")] = "TOP SECRET TRANSCRIPT"
	}
	for path, content := range paths {
		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o700); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(content), 0o600); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if err := os.Chtimes(path, at, at); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
}

func workflowFixtureFiles(t *testing.T, home string) []string {
	t.Helper()
	root := filepath.Join(home, ".claude", "projects")
	var paths []string
	err := filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, entry os.DirEntry, err error) error {
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if !entry.IsDir() {
			paths = append(paths, path)
		}
		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return paths
}

func snapshotFiles(t *testing.T, paths []string) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	var snapshot bytes.Buffer
	for _, path := range paths {
		content, err := os.ReadFile(path)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		snapshot.WriteString(path)
		snapshot.WriteByte(0)
		snapshot.Write(content)
		snapshot.WriteByte(0)
	}
	return snapshot.Bytes()
}

func jsonQuote(value string) string {
	encoded, _ := json.Marshal(value)
	return string(encoded)
}

371			}
372		}
373		list := make([]string, 0, len(shapes))
374		for shape := range shapes {
375			list = append(list, shape)
376		}
377		sort.Strings(list)
378		t.Logf("safe structural JSON shapes=%v", list)
379	}

381	func structuralJSONShape(raw []byte, prefix string, depth int) []string {
382		if depth > 5 {
383			return nil
384		}
385		trimmed := bytes.TrimSpace(raw)
386		if len(trimmed) == 0 {
387			return nil
388		}
389		switch trimmed[0] {
390		case '{':
391			var object map[string]json.RawMessage
392			if json.Unmarshal(trimmed, &object) != nil {
393				return []string{prefix + "<invalid-object>"}
394			}
395			keys := make([]string, 0, len(object))
396			for key := range object {
397				keys = append(keys, key)
398			}
399			sort.Strings(keys)
400			var out []string
401			for _, key := range keys {
402				lower := strings.ToLower(key)
403				if strings.Contains(lower, "prompt") || strings.Contains(lower, "script") || strings.Contains(lower, "log") ||
404					strings.Contains(lower, "result") || strings.Contains(lower, "transcript") {
405					continue
406				}
407				path := key
408				if prefix != "" {
409					path = prefix + "." + key
410				}
411				out = append(out, path+":"+jsonKind(object[key]))
412				out = append(out, structuralJSONShape(object[key], path, depth+1)...)
413			}
414			return out
415		case '[':
416			var values []json.RawMessage
417			if json.Unmarshal(trimmed, &values) != nil {
418				return []string{prefix + "[]:<invalid-array>"}
419			}
420			var out []string
421			for i, value := range values {
422				if i >= 16 {
423					break
424				}
425				out = append(out, structuralJSONShape(value, prefix+"[]", depth+1)...)
426			}
427			return out
428		default:
429			return nil
430		}
431	}
432	
433	func jsonKind(raw []byte) string {
434		trimmed := bytes.TrimSpace(raw)
435		if len(trimmed) == 0 {
436			return "empty"
437		}
438		switch trimmed[0] {
439		case '{':
440			return "object"
441		case '[':
442			return "array"
443		case '"':
444			return "string"
445		case 't', 'f':
446			return "bool"
447		case 'n':
448			return "null"
449		default:
450			return "number"
451		}
452	}

390	func decodeProgress(raw json.RawMessage) (map[string]progressRecord, []time.Time, bool, error) {
391		if len(raw) == 0 {
392			return map[string]progressRecord{}, nil, true, nil
393		}
394		var entries []json.RawMessage
395		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &entries); err != nil {
396			return nil, nil, false, failure("invalid-workflow-progress")
397		}
398		byID := make(map[string]progressRecord, len(entries))
399		var allActivity []time.Time
400		allKnown := true
401		for _, entry := range entries {
402			object, err := decodeObject(entry)
403			if err != nil {
404				return nil, nil, false, failure("invalid-workflow-progress")
405			}
406			agentID, okAgent := requiredString(object, "agentId")
407			isolation, okIsolation := requiredString(object, "isolation")
408			state, okState := requiredString(object, "state")
409			if !okAgent || !okIsolation || !okState || validateID(agentID, "") != nil {
410				return nil, nil, false, failure("invalid-workflow-progress")
411			}
412			if _, duplicate := byID[agentID]; duplicate {
413				return nil, nil, false, failure("duplicate-agent-progress")
414			}
415			queued, queuedKnown := optionalEpochMillis(object, "queuedAt")
416			started, startedKnown := optionalEpochMillis(object, "startedAt")
417			last, lastKnown := optionalEpochMillis(object, "lastProgressAt")
418			known := queuedKnown && startedKnown && lastKnown
419			if !queued.IsZero() && !started.IsZero() && started.Before(queued) {
420				known = false
421			}
422			if !started.IsZero() && !last.IsZero() && last.Before(started) {
423				known = false
424			}
425			activity := nonZeroTimes(queued, started, last)
426			byID[agentID] = progressRecord{
427				agentID: agentID, isolation: strings.ToLower(isolation), state: strings.ToLower(state),
428				activity: activity, timeKnown: known,
429			}
430			allActivity = append(allActivity, activity...)
431			allKnown = allKnown && known
432		}
433		return byID, allActivity, allKnown, nil
434	}
435	
436	func timestampFields(object map[string]json.RawMessage, stringKeys, millisKeys []string) ([]time.Time, bool) {
437		known := true
438		var values []time.Time
439		for _, key := range stringKeys {
440			value, ok := optionalTimestamp(object, key)
441			known = known && ok
442			if !value.IsZero() {
443				values = append(values, value)
444			}
445		}
446		for _, key := range millisKeys {
447			value, ok := optionalEpochMillis(object, key)
448			known = known && ok
449			if !value.IsZero() {
450				values = append(values, value)
451			}
452		}
453		return values, known
454	}
```
</details></tool-use>

package gitx

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"strings"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/pathx"
)

// EphemeralCheckout is the read-only Git cleanliness evidence needed by the
// ephemeral cleanup service. It retains counts and a digest, never pathnames.
type EphemeralCheckout struct {
	Status          Status
	Ignored         int
	DirtySubmodules int
	Fingerprint     string
}

// InspectEphemeralCheckout reads full porcelain status, including all
// untracked files and non-ignored submodule state, plus Git's ignored-file
// inventory. Initialized submodules are inspected recursively so ignored files
// cannot hide behind the parent repository boundary. No command changes an
// index or worktree.
func InspectEphemeralCheckout(ctx context.Context, dir string) (EphemeralCheckout, error) {
	return inspectEphemeralCheckout(ctx, dir, make(map[string]bool))
}

func inspectEphemeralCheckout(ctx context.Context, dir string, seen map[string]bool) (EphemeralCheckout, error) {
	canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(dir)
	if err != nil {
		return EphemeralCheckout{}, err
	}
	if seen[canonical] {
		return EphemeralCheckout{}, fmt.Errorf("recursive submodule checkout path %s", canonical)
	}
	seen[canonical] = true
	defer delete(seen, canonical)

	statusOutput, err := run(ctx, canonical,
		"status", "--porcelain=v2", "--branch", "--untracked-files=all", "--ignore-submodules=none", "-z")
	if err != nil {
		return EphemeralCheckout{}, err
	}
	ignoredOutput, err := run(ctx, canonical,
		"ls-files", "--others", "--ignored", "--exclude-standard", "-z")
	if err != nil {
		return EphemeralCheckout{}, err
	}
	gitlinksOutput, err := run(ctx, canonical, "ls-files", "--stage", "-z")
	if err != nil {
		return EphemeralCheckout{}, err
	}

	ignored := nonEmptyNULRecords(ignoredOutput)
	dirtyPaths := submoduleDirtyPaths(statusOutput)
	dirtySubmodules := 0
	var childFingerprints []string
	for _, submodulePath := range gitlinkPaths(gitlinksOutput) {
		joined := filepath.Join(canonical, filepath.FromSlash(submodulePath))
		child, err := pathx.CanonicalChild(canonical, joined)
		if err != nil {
			return EphemeralCheckout{}, fmt.Errorf("validate submodule path: %w", err)
		}
		info, err := os.Lstat(child)
		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
			dirtySubmodules++
			childFingerprints = append(childFingerprints, digestEphemeral(submodulePath, "missing"))
			continue
		}
		if err != nil || info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 || !info.IsDir() {
			return EphemeralCheckout{}, fmt.Errorf("inspect submodule checkout")
		}
		childInspection, err := inspectEphemeralCheckout(ctx, child, seen)
		if err != nil {
			return EphemeralCheckout{}, err
		}
		ignored += childInspection.Ignored
		childDirty := dirtyPaths[submodulePath] || childInspection.Status.Dirty() ||
			childInspection.Ignored > 0 || childInspection.DirtySubmodules > 0
		if childDirty {
			dirtySubmodules++
		}
		dirtySubmodules += childInspection.DirtySubmodules
		childFingerprints = append(childFingerprints, digestEphemeral(submodulePath, childInspection.Fingerprint))
	}
	sort.Strings(childFingerprints)
	fingerprintParts := []string{statusOutput, ignoredOutput, gitlinksOutput}
	fingerprintParts = append(fingerprintParts, childFingerprints...)
	return EphemeralCheckout{
		Status:          statusFromOutput(canonical, statusOutput),
		Ignored:         ignored,
		DirtySubmodules: dirtySubmodules,
		Fingerprint:     digestEphemeral(fingerprintParts...),
	}, nil
}

func nonEmptyNULRecords(output string) int {
	count := 0
	for _, record := range nulLines(output) {
		if record != "" {
			count++
		}
	}
	return count
}

func submoduleDirtyCount(output string) int { return len(submoduleDirtyPaths(output)) }

func submoduleDirtyPaths(output string) map[string]bool {
	paths := make(map[string]bool)
	for _, record := range nulLines(output) {
		if record == "" || (record[0] != '1' && record[0] != '2') {
			continue
		}
		fields := strings.Fields(record)
		if len(fields) > 2 && strings.HasPrefix(fields[2], "S") {
			if path := statusPath(record); path != "" {
				paths[filepath.ToSlash(path)] = true
			}
		}
	}
	return paths
}

func gitlinkPaths(output string) []string {
	var paths []string
	for _, record := range nulLines(output) {
		metadata, path, ok := strings.Cut(record, "\t")
		if !ok || path == "" {
			continue
		}
		fields := strings.Fields(metadata)
		if len(fields) == 3 && fields[0] == "160000" && fields[2] == "0" {
			paths = append(paths, filepath.ToSlash(path))
		}
	}
	sort.Strings(paths)
	return paths
}

func digestEphemeral(parts ...string) string {
	hash := sha256.New()
	for _, part := range parts {
		hash.Write([]byte(part))
		hash.Write([]byte{0})
	}
	return hex.EncodeToString(hash.Sum(nil))
}

22	  foreground conversation in the current terminal with no default timeout.

24	  reply, loops, mutates lifecycle state, or changes permissions.

33	  output form reveals argv, shell source, executable directories, environment,

42	
43	- Pull-request `--repo` selectors now constrain both account rows and local
44	  query targets, and JSON reports the effective scope after non-open account
45	  requests narrow to local collection. Schema version 1 local joins distinguish
46	  `expected_branch` from `live_branch`, report checkout existence, worktree
47	  registration and status availability/errors independently, and include Git
48	  status only when the expected branch is actually checked out. Fork pull

50	  IDs when needed), canonical/unmanaged/external worktrees join without a task,
51	  duplicate local clones no longer suppress the remote query, and ambiguous
52	  same-branch local evidence fails closed instead of choosing a clone. Provider
53	  host identity is preserved so an enterprise remote is never queried against
54	  the public forge, partial failures appear in JSON `warnings`, and stale GitHub
55	  checks are not reported as passing.
56	- The Zellij runtime no longer fails every session listing when an exited
57	  session is left in Zellij's namespace. Zellij keeps exited sessions
58	  resurrectable, and `dump-layout` against one errors with `There is no active
59	  session!`, which previously turned `dev ls`, `dev doctor` and the TUI runtime
60	  join into an error. Exited sessions are now excluded from the live view, and
61	  `dev start` refuses to create over a name an exited session still owns
62	  instead of silently resurrecting its old layout at the old directory. If a
63	  live session exits between listing and layout inspection, creation now also
64	  fails closed rather than falling through to resurrection. Only Zellij's exact
65	  exited marker is recognized; a live session name containing `EXITED` remains live.

```text
600	follow-up rather than treating "has a remote" as proof.
601	
602	The catalog also exposes personal repository tags/notes (`dev repo mark`). To
603	find local Git state at risk before any future cleanup:
604	
605	```bash
606	dev repo list --no-remote              # no configured remotes at all
607	dev repo list --local-only             # at least one branch lacks remote upstream
608	dev repo list --multiple-remotes
609	dev repo list --multiple-upstreams     # branches track more than one remote
610	dev repo list --sizes --json           # full remotes/branches/size contract
611	```
612	
613	`no remote`, `local-only branch`, and `multiple upstreams` are distinct facts.
614	They do not claim whether commit objects are present remotely; a future reclaim
615	preflight must compare every local head/tag/note/stash against actual remote
616	refs immediately before removal.
617	
618	Going cold is safe because **the branch is the identity and the directory is a
619	cache**. `dev park --cold` refuses unless the branch is pushed, and `dev resume`
620	rebuilds the checkout from `origin/<branch>`. Once that holds, the local
621	filesystem stops being a graveyard of half-finished worktrees.
622	
623	## Rich Git state
624	
625	Every inventory surface uses the same compact, starship-like status:
626	
627	```text
628	⇕⇡3⇣2 =1 +4 !2 ?3
629	```
630	
631	- `⇡` / `⇣` / `⇕` — ahead, behind, diverged
632	- `=` — conflicted paths
633	- `+` — staged paths
634	- `!` — unstaged paths
635	- `?` — untracked paths
636	
637	`dev status` and the TUI detail pane also show the unique changed-path total
638	and type breakdown (added / modified / deleted / renamed). A path staged and
639	then modified again is one changed path, while correctly appearing in both the
640	staged and unstaged categories. JSON output exposes all counts separately.
641	
642	## Worktree ownership
643	
644	Three mechanisms create git worktrees. `dev` takes one position so nobody has
645	to improvise:
646	
647	| Kind | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
648	|---|---|---|---|
649	| Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff | **`dev`** | `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<slug>` | until external `dev retire` |
650	| Harness-owned turn-scoped subagent isolation | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` (gitignored) | owned by that harness; no history-relocation guarantee |
651	| `herdr worktree create` | **not used** — `dev` runs `git worktree add`, then `herdr worktree open --path …` | — | — |
652	
653	**If code, history, or plans must remain reviewable—or you may return tomorrow—
654	use `dev`.**
655	
656	`dev` does not delegate placement to herdr because the path policy has to hold
657	on machines without herdr. It creates the checkout with plain git and asks
658	herdr only to *open* it — which still surfaces it in the sidebar grouped under
659	its parent repo with its own branch and ahead/behind row.
660	
661	`dev` refuses to create a worktree inside a repository: a checkout nested in
662	another checkout makes every indexer, file watcher and `rg` run see a second
663	copy of the tree.
664	
665	### Provisioning
666	
667	A worktree is a clean checkout — no `node_modules`, no `.venv`, no `.env`.
668	Without provisioning, every new one starts broken. `dev` copies the gitignored
669	files you list, optionally symlinks heavy directories, and runs a setup
670	command detected from the lockfiles. Included files must remain the same
671	regular file through open; source swaps and symlinked destination parents are
672	refused, existing destinations are reported as skipped, and contents are never
673	logged:
674	
675	```toml
676	[worktree]
677	include     = [".env", ".env.local"]   # only files that are ALSO gitignored
678	link        = []                       # opt-in; sharing node_modules is risky
679	post_create = "auto"                   # uv.lock → uv sync, package-lock.json → npm ci, …
680	```
681	
682	`.claude/settings.local.json` is not a universal include. Add that exact path
683	only for an explicitly selected sticky/plain-Claude launcher and verify it
684	arrives. `claude-copilot-once` preserves an existing Copilot pin and creates/
685	removes only one it added when absent; its proxy must already run.
686	`codex-copilot-once` injects backend via CLI and may auto-start its proxy path,
687	so neither wrapper needs the copied file.
688	
689	**Copy or reinstall?** Reinstalling is always correct but can take minutes;
690	copying is fast but only sound for dependency trees carrying no absolute paths.
691	That is a per-ecosystem fact, not a preference, so dev knows it:
692	
693	```toml
694	[worktree]
695	strategy = "reinstall"      # reinstall | copy | link | skip
696	
697	[worktree.strategies]
698	node = "copy"               # node_modules copies soundly
699	```
700	
701	Asking to copy a virtualenv is refused with the reason — it bakes its own
702	absolute path into `pyvenv.cfg` and `bin/activate` — and narrowed back to
703	reinstalling rather than silently producing a broken checkout.
704	
705	`dev wt plan` shows exactly what a new worktree of a repository would get:
706	which project types were detected, which tools are missing, and every file and
707	command involved. `dev wt plan --write` seeds
708	`<repo>/.dev-cli/config.toml` from it, so
709	a project can commit its own setup and every machine provisions the same way.
710	
711	```
712	$ dev wt plan
713	PROJECT  MANAGER  FROM               DEPENDENCIES  TOOL
714	node     npm      package-lock.json  node_modules  installed
715	python   uv       uv.lock            .venv         installed
716	
717	   ACTION    WHAT          WHY
718	✓  copy      .env          gitignored, so the checkout would not have it
719	✓  copy-dir  node_modules  npm dependencies, copied instead of reinstalling
720	✓  run       uv sync       uv.lock detected
721	```
722

1	# Agent-safe retirement
2	
3	A process must not delete the worktree that contains its own current directory.
4	The terminal can remain visible after Unix unlinks the path, but config reloads,
5	relative files and new subprocesses then fail. Herdr still showing a pane does
6	not mean the Git checkout is healthy.
7	
8	Use three separate milestones:
9	
10	1. **READY** — commit product work, run `dev prepare`, then exit normally so the
11	   post-SpecStory finalizer can commit the exact final transcript. A manual
12	   external finalizer must pass `--writer-stopped`; a Claude SessionEnd observer
13	   can provide the same durable proof without staging during teardown.
14	2. **MERGED** — an external coordinator runs `dev done --ff`, or verifies an
15	   external merge with `dev done --merged --base-ref <ref>`. Runtime and
16	   worktree remain intact.
17	3. **RETIRED** — from outside the target workspace run `dev retire`. It closes
18	   eligible runtime sessions, waits until they disappear, revalidates Git, and
19	   removes the worktree without force.
20	
21	Retirement never overrides `working`, `blocked`, or `waiting` agents. Unknown
22	status needs external `--close-unknown`. A workspace containing panes outside
23	the target is mixed-purpose and must be reorganized or closed manually.
24	
25	Raw `git worktree remove --force` bypasses these protections. Do not use it on
26	an agent-owned checkout.
27	
28	From the canonical main checkout, `dev sweep --merged-worktrees` reports both
29	tracked and unmanaged linked worktrees whose named branches are contained in
30	main. Review the exact candidates and blockers first; apply only after user
31	confirmation. Worktree retirement keeps branches unless `--delete-branches`
32	was separately requested.
33
```
</details></tool-use>

1	---
2	name: dev-cli
3	description: 'Manage repositories and work-in-progress with the dev CLI: create/clone/setup agent-ready repos, bootstrap and organise them safely, own worktree/task lifecycle, safely prepare/finalize/retire agent sessions, render or hand off deterministic prompt recipes, run guarded Git transactions, capture sidecar repo notes, track HOT/WARM/COLD tasks, navigate via TUI, and bridge gh/glab/Azure DevOps/herdr/tmux/zellij. Use when creating, starting, parking, resuming or retiring work; preserving agent transcripts; triaging pull requests or closeout context; scanning or organising repos; capturing/searching repo thoughts; choosing worktree isolation; or cleaning stale branches, checkouts and sessions.'
4	---
5	
6	# dev-cli
7	
8	The `dev` command is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent
9	runtimes. It exists to stop four different things collapsing into one:
10	
11	```
12	git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
13	git worktree    a disposable local checkout
14	herdr / tmux / zellij
15	                a per-host live runtime
16	dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
17	```
18	
19	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. `dev` persists
20	human/task facts such as identity, checkout mode, **state**, **owner** and **next
21	action** in one TOML file per task under configured `paths.state_dir/tasks`
22	(default `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/tasks`); transient pane data is not persisted.
23	
24	**The problem it solves:** when a terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only
25	record of what you are working on, nothing can ever be closed. `dev` gives that
26	record a home outside the runtime, so closing a session stops meaning
27	abandoning a task.
28	
29	## Check it is there first
30	
31	`dev` is not installed everywhere. Before using it:
32	
33	```bash
34	command -v dev || echo "not installed"
35	dev doctor          # version/install owner/path, PATH collisions, and capabilities
36	```
37	
38	Only **git** is required. `herdr`, `tmux`, `zellij`, `gh`, `glab` and Azure CLI
39	each enable more and degrade cleanly when absent — never make a step
40	hard-depend on one.
41	
42	## Worktree ownership — read this before creating any worktree
43	
44	There are three mechanisms that create git worktrees, and picking the wrong one
45	is the most common source of confusion. The rule:
46	
47	| Kind of worktree | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
48	|---|---|---|---|
49	| Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff — anything you might return to | **`dev`** | `paths.worktree_path`, default `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<branch-slug>` | until `dev done` or `dev sweep` |
50	| Harness-owned turn-scoped isolation (`isolation: worktree`, `/batch`, `EnterWorktree`) | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` (keep gitignored) | owned by that harness; not a transcript-relocation guarantee |
51	| `herdr worktree create` | **not used** — `dev` runs `git worktree add` itself, then `herdr worktree open --path …` | — | — |
52	
53	**Rule of thumb: if code/history/plan must remain reviewable or a human may
54	return tomorrow, use `dev`. Use native isolation only when the harness owns the
55	entire turn-scoped lifecycle.**
56	
57	Why `dev` does not delegate to `herdr worktree create`: the path policy has to
58	hold on machines where herdr is not installed. `dev` creates the checkout with
59	plain git and asks herdr only to *open* it — which still makes it appear in the
60	sidebar grouped under its parent repo with its own branch and ahead/behind row.
61	
62	Never nest a `dev` worktree inside a repository. A checkout inside another
63	checkout makes every indexer, file watcher and `rg` run see a second copy of
64	the tree. `dev` refuses to do it.
65	
66	Full detail: `references/worktree-ownership.md`.
67	
68	## The task lifecycle
69	
70	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
71	|---|---|---|---|
72	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
73	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | normally closed | back within days |
74	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
75	| ✅ `done` | merged | may remain open | MERGED; external retirement pending |
76	
77	```bash
78	dev repo open api                                  # ad hoc; no task/worktree
79	dev start api --task "typo" --direct                # track current/main directly
80	dev start api --task "small" --branch-only --base main
81	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # isolated worktree → hot
82	dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
83	dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
84	dev resume "token refresh"                         # → hot, rebuilt if needed
85	dev prepare --session claude:<uuid>                # arm final transcript handoff
86	dev done                                           # TTY wizard: inspect dirty state, then FF/PR/merged
87	dev done --ff                                      # → done/MERGED; resources kept
88	dev retire "token refresh"                         # external-only cleanup → RETIRED
89	```
90	
91	**Parking is the move that matters.** `dev park --next "…"` is what makes it
92	safe to close a session, and the `--next` text is what makes resuming cheap.
93	Always suggest a `--next` when parking.
94	
95	Full detail: `references/task-lifecycle.md`. Before integrating or deleting an
96	agent-owned checkout, read `references/agent-retirement.md`.
97	
98	## Pick the task's checkout mode
99	
100	A task does not imply a worktree. Use the lightest explicit boundary:
101	
102	- `dev repo open <repo>` / REPOS Enter — ad-hoc open, no task at all.
103	- `dev start … --direct` / REPOS `d` — track current branch (usually main),
104	  create no branch/worktree. HOT ↔ WARM only; `dev done` needs no merge mode.
105	- `dev start … --branch-only` — create and switch a branch in the canonical
106	  checkout. No concurrent branch there.
107	- `dev start …` / REPOS `s` — default isolated branch + worktree. Use once work
108	  may be interrupted, experimental, or parallel.
109	
110	Do not create isolation before it has a job, but do not carry dirty main changes
111	into a parallel task implicitly either: a worktree starts from committed HEAD.
112	Checkpoint first when the new task depends on that work.
113	
114	## Parallel background work
115	
116	Read `references/parallel-agents.md` before spawning an independent agent while
117	another remains live. The fail-closed workflow uses `dev start --json`, requires
118	a newly created first-class Herdr worktree and its exact returned root pane,
119	then launches an explicit SpecStory/profile command there. Reused, fallback,
120	non-Herdr, missing or unverified panes are never launch targets.
121	
122	For a human one-liner, `dev start --run '<shell command>'` uses the same exact
123	new-worktree/root-pane proof and `--focus` independently switches afterward.
124	It does not choose a launcher profile, permission mode, agent name, or wait
125	policy; use the full JSON workflow when those require separate validation.
126	
127	`dev` guards writer-claiming direct/branch starts and resume when another
128	recognized Herdr agent occupies the same canonical Git worktree. Every state,
129	including `idle`, `done`, and `unknown`, is occupied; Herdr resolves the current
130	pane before excluding it. Pure repo/worktree/TUI open is navigation to the live

```text
1	# Agent-safe worktree retirement
2	
3	## The rule
4	
5	A feature agent may prepare and integrate work, but it must not destroy the
6	runtime or checkout containing its own process. Completion has three milestones:
7	
8	```text
9	READY     exact final transcript committed after the writer exits
10	MERGED    branch integrated; runtime/worktree may still exist
11	RETIRED   runtime absent, worktree removed, optional branch deleted, task reaped
12	```
13	
14	`hot/warm/cold/done` remain the persisted task states. `done` now means MERGED,
15	not "everything has already been deleted".
16	
17	## Normal local flow
18	
19	From the feature worktree:
20	
21	```bash
22	# Commit product changes first. Do not stage the moving transcript.
23	dev prepare --session claude:<uuid> --plan .claude/plans/task.md
24	# Exit the agent normally so SpecStory can write its final Markdown.
25	```
26	
27	The outer `specstory run` wrapper calls:
28	
29	```bash
30	dev artifact finalize --run-id "$DEV_AGENT_RUN_ID" --if-pending --writer-stopped
31	```
32	
33	Then an external main/integration workspace runs:
34	
35	```bash
36	dev done <task> --ff
37	dev retire <task> --delete-branch
38	```
39	
40	`done` only integrates and records MERGED. `retire` re-resolves every runtime
41	pane, closes eligible sessions, waits for them to disappear, revalidates Git,
42	and removes the worktree without force.
43	
44	For periodic cleanup from the canonical main checkout:
45	
46	```bash
47	dev sweep --merged-worktrees
48	# Present the exact candidates/blockers to the user and ask for approval.
49	dev sweep --merged-worktrees --apply --yes
50	```
51	
52	This includes unmanaged linked worktrees whose named branches are already
53	contained in main. It never treats containment alone as permission: dirty Git,
54	pending artifacts and runtime blockers still stop cleanup. Branches remain by
55	default; add `--delete-branches` only when the user approved that separately.
56	
57	## Pull-request flow
58	
59	```bash
60	dev done <task> --pr
61	# after CI/review and a commit-preserving merge
62	git fetch origin
63	dev done <task> --merged --base-ref origin/main
64	dev retire <task> --delete-branch
65	```
66	
67	A squash merge is not ancestry-equivalent. It requires an explicit operator
68	attestation:
69	
70	```bash
71	dev done <task> --merged --base-ref origin/main --confirm-squash <merge-commit>
72	```
73	
74	This proves only that the named squash commit is in the base; the operator is
75	asserting that it represents the feature.
76	
77	## Safety policy
78	
79	Retirement always refuses when:
80	
81	- the caller cwd is the target or below it;
82	- the caller Herdr workspace/pane or tmux pane covers the target;
83	- a workspace contains panes outside the target;
84	- an agent is `working`, `blocked`, or `waiting`;
85	- runtime enumeration fails;
86	- the checkout is dirty, on the wrong branch, or not contained in its base;
87	- artifact finalization is armed/finalizing/failed.
88	
89	`unknown` or empty agent status requires `--close-unknown` from outside the
90	target. Runtime enumeration failure requires external `--assume-no-runtime`.
91	Neither flag bypasses caller containment or active-agent states.
92	
93	Raw `git worktree remove --force` can bypass dev. Never run it from an agent that
94	occupies the target. dev's guarantee is that no dev-mediated path does so.
95	
96	## What self-deletion looks like
97	
98	A real Codex session deleted its own registered worktree and branch from another
99	checkout. Herdr kept the workspace and terminal alive because Unix processes can
100	hold an open cwd inode after the path is unlinked. SpecStory then recreated the
101	same path with only `.specstory/` content.
102	
103	The resulting shell looked alive but was no longer a Git checkout:
104	
105	```text
106	failed to reload config: No such file or directory
107	fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
108	```
109	
110	Config/skill reloads and new subprocesses failed while Herdr still displayed an
111	idle agent. Treat `runtime alive + Git registration absent + artifact-only path`
112	as an orphan requiring transcript salvage and external reconciliation, never as
113	RETIRED.
114	
115	## Artifact rules
116	
117	- Match SpecStory Markdown by the exact UUID in its fixed preamble, not filename
118	  or newest mtime.
119	- Finalize only after SessionEnd was observed or the outer wrapper supplies
120	  `--writer-stopped`; byte stability remains a second, independent check.
121	- Stage only that transcript and explicitly named plans.
122	- Never stage another provider/session implicitly.
123	- `.specstory/statistics.json` is derived and ignored.
124	- New untracked transcripts above 2 MiB need `--allow-large`.
125	- Scanner/redactor failure commits nothing and leaves a retryable intent.
126	- Artifact commits are on the same feature branch, not necessarily the same
127	  product commit; they carry `Agent-Artifact-Session` and
128	  `Dev-Artifact-Intent` trailers.
129
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Worktree ownership
2	
3	Read this before creating a worktree, sharing a checkout between agents, or when
4	a new checkout lacks dependencies, env files, or launcher backend state.
5	
6	## The rule
7	
8	| Change boundary | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
9	|---|---|---|---|
10	| Durable feature/fix/experiment/handoff | **`dev`** | `paths.worktree_path` | until external `dev retire` |
11	| Harness-owned turn-scoped isolation | Claude Code | `.claude/worktrees/` | managed by that harness; do not assume artifact relocation |
12	| Runtime workspace/panes | Herdr | per-host runtime | until explicitly closed |
13	| Rendered agent history | SpecStory | process launch checkout | until committed/removed with that checkout |
14	
15	Use a `dev` worktree for independent approaches or any change stream whose code,
16	history, or plan must remain reviewable. Agents with explicitly disjoint file
17	ownership may share one checkout, but `--allow-shared-checkout` is a deliberate
18	coordination override—not a default.
19	
20	`EnterWorktree` changes an agent's working location; it does not prove an
21	existing SpecStory wrapper/watcher rebound its source/output paths. Start the
22	new process from the target worktree root.
23	
24	## Why dev creates the checkout
25	
26	`dev` runs `git worktree add`, then asks Herdr to run
27	`worktree open --path <path> --no-focus`. Path policy therefore remains stable
28	on machines without Herdr, while Herdr still displays repo/branch provenance.
29	A fallback plain workspace is reported as such and is not an exact agent launch
30	target.
31	
32	Never nest a durable worktree inside another checkout. Every watcher, language
33	server, backup tool and search then sees a second copy of the repository.
34	
35	Herdr's native **New worktree** action is still valid for an external,
36	unmanaged checkout. When the canonical repository is under a configured scan
37	root, Git registration lets dev discover the checkout without scanning
38	`~/.herdr/worktrees`; dev does not auto-adopt, relocate, or provision it. Run
39	`dev wt provision <path>` if it needs the project environment and `dev adopt`
40	followed by `dev adopt --apply` only when it should enter the durable task
41	lifecycle.
42	
43	## Paths
44	
45	Default:
46	
47	```text
48	~/Worktrees/<repo>/<branch-slug>
49	```
50	
51	Configurable through `paths.worktree_root` and `paths.worktree_path`, with
52	`worktree_root`, `repo`, `repo_path`, `branch`, `category`, `host`, and `date`
53	variables plus `slug`, `lower`, and `base` filters.
54	
55	Always pass `--base` for unattended creation. A new branch otherwise inherits
56	the current HEAD, which may be an unrelated feature.
57	
58	## Provisioning
59	
60	A worktree is a clean checkout. `dev wt create` and `dev start` build and apply
61	an inspectable plan:
62	
63	```bash
64	dev wt plan
65	dev wt plan --write
66	dev wt provision --dry-run
67	```
68	
69	Effective settings come from global config or committed repo
70	`.dev-cli/config.toml` (legacy `.dev.toml` remains readable):
71	
72	```toml
73	[worktree]
74	include = [".env", ".env.local"]
75	link = []
76	post_create = "auto"
77	strategy = "reinstall"
78	```
79	
80	An executable `post_create` from `.dev-cli/config.toml` requires approval of its
81	exact content hash with `dev config trust <repo> --yes`. Legacy `.dev.toml`
82	retains its compatibility behavior.
83	
84	Only paths that are both explicitly included and genuinely gitignored are
85	copied. Tracked files already have the branch-correct version. Included files
86	must remain the same regular file from validation through open; source swaps and
87	symlinked destination parents are refused. Existing destinations are reported
88	as skipped, never falsely as copied, and file contents are never logged.
89	
90	### Project-local Claude backend state
91	
92	`.claude/settings.local.json` stays gitignored and is **not** a universal default
93	include. The verified `claude-copilot-once` wrapper preserves an existing
94	Copilot pin and creates/removes only its own pin when one was absent;
95	`codex-copilot-once` injects its backend via CLI. Neither needs a copied project
96	file. Claude's Copilot proxy must already be running; the Codex path may
97	self-start its proxy flow.
98	
99	An explicitly selected sticky/plain-Claude profile may opt in exactly:
100	
101	```toml
102	[worktree]
103	include = [".env", ".env.local", ".claude/settings.local.json"]
104	```
105	
106	Verify the file arrived before launch. If absent, stop instead of allowing the
107	launcher to fall back silently to another backend. `dev` logs the relative path
108	only, never its contents.
109	
110	## Dependency strategies
111	
112	- `reinstall`: safe default; run lockfile-derived installer.
113	- `copy`: duplicate path-independent dependency trees.
114	- `link`: explicit and usually unsafe for mutable dependencies.
115	- `skip`: for external/container-managed environments.
116	
117	`dev` refuses unsound choices, such as copied/linked Python virtualenvs, and
118	reports missing tools or failed setup without deleting the usable checkout.
119	
120	## Cleanup
121	
122	- `dev wt rm <branch>` removes only the checkout after external runtime safety checks; branch survives.
123	- `dev park` records WARM; when called from its own runtime it leaves that runtime alive for normal exit.
124	- `dev park --cold --push` closes eligible runtime state and removes the pushed worktree only from outside.
125	- `dev done --ff` integrates and records MERGED; runtime/worktree/branch survive.
126	- `dev done --pr` leaves everything active for review.
127	- `dev retire` is the only complete close/wait/remove/reap path.
128	- `dev sweep` reports first; `--apply` routes cleanup through retire.
129	- From canonical main, `dev sweep --merged-worktrees` also audits unmanaged
130	  linked worktrees whose branches are contained in main. Agents must present
131	  that report for user confirmation before applying; branches are retained
132	  unless `--delete-branches` was separately approved.
133	
134	Bare `dev done` on a TTY classifies dirty content against the base before
135	offering commit-all or discard-all; unique discard requires `DROP`. Dirty
136	checkout removal may require explicit force, but caller/runtime safety is never
137	bypassable. Herdr `done` is not a cleanup signal, and `--cold --keep-session` is
138	rejected. Never raw-force-remove an agent's cwd.
139
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	---
2	description: Retire an integrated dev-cli worktree and runtime safely, from outside the workspace being removed.
3	authority: project
4	status: stable
5	verified_on: 2026-09-02
6	---
7	
8	# Agent-safe retirement
9	
10	A `dev` change stream reaches full retirement only after an external caller closes its runtime and removes its worktree — a feature agent must never destroy the checkout or runtime containing its own process.
11	
12	## Three milestones, not one
13	
14	Completion is three separate milestones, and the persisted task state `done` now means the middle one, not the last:
15	
16	```text
17	READY     exact final transcript committed after the writer exits
18	MERGED    branch integrated; runtime/worktree may still exist
19	RETIRED   runtime absent, worktree removed, optional branch deleted, task reaped
20	```
21	
22	`hot`, `warm`, `cold`, and `done` remain the only persisted task states — `done` means MERGED, with cleanup possibly still pending. It does **not** mean the runtime or worktree has already been deleted.
23	
24	## Commands
25	
26	| Command | What it does |
27	|---|---|
28	| `dev prepare --session <provider:uuid> --plan <path>` | Arms post-writer artifact finalization without closing the running agent. Product changes must already be committed; the transcript itself is deliberately not staged yet. |
29	| `dev artifact finalize --run-id "$DEV_AGENT_RUN_ID" --if-pending --writer-stopped` | Commits the one exact, stable transcript after its writer has stopped. `--if-pending` no-ops silently when no armed intent matches the run id; `--writer-stopped` confirms the outer wrapper has returned. |
30	| `dev done --ff` | Rebases the task branch onto its base and fast-forwards it locally. Records MERGED; never closes the runtime, removes a worktree, or deletes a branch. |
31	| `dev done --pr` | Pushes the branch and opens a pull/merge request through an available forge CLI. The task stays under review, not MERGED. |
32	| `dev done --merged --base-ref <ref>` | Verifies an externally merged branch is contained in `<ref>` and records MERGED. |
33	| `dev done --merged --base-ref <ref> --confirm-squash <merge-commit>` | Same, but for a squash merge: attests that the named commit, already proven contained in `<ref>`, represents the feature branch. This is an operator assertion dev cannot verify on its own. |
34	| `dev artifact discard <intent> --yes` | Records that an intent can never be finalized — its transcript was never written, or its HEAD is gone after a rebase — so it stops blocking integration and retirement. It commits and recovers nothing, prints exactly what is being abandoned, and refuses an intent that is still `armed`, because finalization is the path that preserves a transcript. |
35	| `dev retire [task-or-worktree] [--close-unknown] [--assume-no-runtime] [--delete-branch] [--timeout <duration>]` | Re-resolves every covering runtime session, refuses active agents and mixed-purpose workspaces, waits for closure, revalidates Git state, and only then removes the linked worktree without force. Deletes the task record only after every requested step succeeds. |
36	| `dev sweep --merged-worktrees [--base <ref>] [--apply] [--yes] [--close-unknown] [--assume-no-runtime] [--delete-branches]` | From the canonical checkout, reports (and, with `--apply`, retires) both task-tracked and unmanaged linked worktrees whose branches are already contained in the base. |
37	
38	A dirty checkout does not fail here: `dev done` classifies it against the base
39	first, offering commit or discard interactively, or taking an explicit
40	`--dirty` policy from a script. See
41	[Change-stream workflow](change-stream-workflow.md) for that wizard. The
42	`--keep-worktree` and `--delete-branch` flags remain accepted on `dev done`
43	only to fail loudly and point at `dev retire`.
44	
45	For a read-only explanation before acting, render or open the generic
46	`workspace-closeout` recipe from the exact checkout:
47	
48	```bash
49	dev prompt render workspace-closeout .
50	dev prompt open workspace-closeout . --agent my-agent
51	```
52	
53	The recipe includes the full retirement audit, but its result is advisory.
54	`eligible` and a merged PR never authorize cleanup; an external `dev retire`
55	still recollects and revalidates every gate. If `dev done --ff` or
56	`dev git pull-rebase` stops at a conflict, use `prompt open` only to discuss the
57	semantic resolution, then explicitly continue/abort Git and rerun the lifecycle
58	command. See [Prompt handoffs](prompt-handoffs.md).
59	
60	## Normal local flow
61	
62	From the feature worktree:
63	
64	```bash
65	# Commit product changes first. Do not stage the moving transcript.
66	dev prepare --session claude:<uuid> --plan .claude/plans/task.md
67	# Exit the agent normally so SpecStory can write its final Markdown.
68	```
69	
70	The outer `specstory run` wrapper then calls:
71	
72	```bash
73	dev artifact finalize --run-id "$DEV_AGENT_RUN_ID" --if-pending --writer-stopped
74	```
75	
76	An external main/integration workspace finishes the job:
77	
78	```bash
79	dev done <task> --ff
80	dev retire <task> --delete-branch
81	```
82	
83	`dev done` only integrates and records MERGED. `dev retire` re-resolves every runtime pane, closes eligible sessions, waits for them to disappear, revalidates Git, and removes the worktree without force.
84	
85	## Pull-request flow
86	
87	```bash
88	dev done <task> --pr
89	# after CI/review and a commit-preserving merge
90	git fetch origin
91	dev done <task> --merged --base-ref origin/main
92	dev retire <task> --delete-branch
93	```
94	
95	A squash merge is not ancestry-equivalent, so it needs an explicit operator attestation:
96	
97	```bash
98	dev done <task> --merged --base-ref origin/main --confirm-squash <merge-commit>
99	```
100	
101	This proves only that the named squash commit is contained in the base; the operator is asserting that it actually represents the feature branch.
102	
103	## Refusal conditions
104	
105	`retire.Inspect` refuses to proceed whenever any of the following hold, and it re-checks after closing sessions rather than trusting a stale view:
106	
107	- the caller's current directory is the target checkout or below it;
108	- the caller's `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`, or `TMUX_PANE` identifies a runtime session that covers the target;
109	- a covering runtime workspace also contains panes outside the target (mixed-purpose workspace);
110	- any covering agent status is `working`, `running`, `busy`, `blocked`, or `waiting` — **never overridable, by any flag**;
111	- agent status is empty or `unknown`, **unless** the caller passes `--close-unknown` from outside the target;
112	- agent status is unrecognized (anything outside the known set) — always blocks;
113	- runtime enumeration itself fails, **unless** the caller passes `--assume-no-runtime`.
114	
115	`--close-unknown` and `--assume-no-runtime` only relax fail-closed *observations* (an unreadable status, a runtime list that could not be enumerated). Neither flag ever bypasses caller containment or an active-agent state. `retirement.Service.Retire` also revalidates the target's identity, Git ancestry, in-progress Git operations (`gitx.InProgress`, checking `MERGE_HEAD`, `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`, `REVERT_HEAD`, `rebase-merge`, `rebase-apply`, `sequencer` — not `REBASE_HEAD`, which Git leaves behind after a rebase completes), and worktree cleanliness after runtime sessions close — reality may have changed while a runtime was draining, so no earlier proof carries across that boundary.
116	
117	## Periodic cleanup with sweep
118	
119	```bash
120	dev sweep --merged-worktrees
121	# Present the exact candidates/blockers to the user and ask for approval.
122	dev sweep --merged-worktrees --apply --yes
123	```
124	
125	This surfaces both task-tracked DONE worktrees and unmanaged linked worktrees whose named branches are already contained in the base — run it from the canonical checkout. It reports before applying: containment alone is never permission. Dirty Git state, a pending or unreachable artifact, a locked or prunable worktree registration, an in-progress Git operation, and the same runtime refusal conditions as `dev retire` all still block cleanup. Branches remain after retirement by default; pass `--delete-branches` only when the user separately approved deleting them.
126	
127	## Safety boundaries
128	
129	Raw `git worktree remove --force` bypasses dev entirely — never run it from an agent that occupies the target. dev's guarantee is only that no dev-mediated path performs a forced removal; it cannot stop an operator or script from calling Git directly.
130	
131	A real Codex session once deleted its own registered worktree and branch from another checkout. Herdr kept the workspace and terminal alive because a Unix process can hold an open cwd inode after the path is unlinked, and SpecStory then recreated the same path containing only `.specstory/` content. The shell looked alive but was no longer a Git checkout:
132	
133	```text
134	failed to reload config: No such file or directory
135	fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
136	```
137	
138	Treat `runtime alive + Git registration absent + artifact-only path` as an orphan that needs transcript salvage and external reconciliation — **never** as RETIRED.
139	
140	`dev sweep` now recognises that shape rather than leaving it to be spotted by eye. When a task records a checkout that exists but Git does not register, and the directory holds nothing but agent artifact folders, sweep reports it as an abandoned agent workspace. It offers to remove it only when every file inside is byte-identical to one the repository already has; anything that differs is listed as salvage work and left untouched, including by `--apply`.
141	
142	Byte equality rather than mere presence is the point. A transcript writer that outlives its worktree usually flushes a longer final version than the copy committed earlier, so a same-named file in the repository is not evidence that the tail was saved.
143	
144	## Sources
145	
146	- [`internal/skill/dev-cli/references/agent-retirement.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/skill/dev-cli/references/agent-retirement.md)
147	- [`internal/help/topics/retirement.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/help/topics/retirement.md)
148	- [`internal/cli/retire.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/cli/retire.go)
149	- [`internal/cli/artifact.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/cli/artifact.go)
150	- [`internal/cli/sweep.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/cli/sweep.go)
151	- [`internal/cli/done.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/cli/done.go)
152	- [`internal/retire/safety.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/retire/safety.go)
153	- [`internal/retire/service.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/retire/service.go)
154	- [`internal/retire/audit.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/retire/audit.go)

```text
1	---
2	description: 安全地從外部 retire dev-cli 已整合的 worktree 與 runtime，而非在被移除的 workspace 內部執行。
3	authority: project
4	status: stable
5	verified_on: 2026-09-02
6	lang: zh-TW
7	---
8	
9	# Agent-safe retirement
10	
11	!!! note "術語規則"
12	    有公認中文譯名且本文使用中文時，首次以「中文 (English original)」呈現。產品名稱與 Git／CLI／agent domain terms 可直接保留英文；沒有公認譯名不得自創。程式碼、API／tool 名稱、CLI flag、套件名與路徑一律不翻譯。
13	
14	一條 `dev` change stream 只有在外部呼叫者關閉其 runtime、移除其 worktree 之後，才算真正完成 retirement——feature agent 絕不能自行摧毀自己所在的 checkout 或 runtime。
15	
16	## 三個里程碑，不是一個
17	
18	Completion 分成三個獨立里程碑，且目前 persisted task state 的 `done` 對應的是中間那個，不是最後一個：
19	
20	```text
21	READY     writer 離開後，commit 了 exact final transcript
22	MERGED    branch 已整合；runtime/worktree 可能仍存在
23	RETIRED   runtime 已消失、worktree 已移除、可選擇刪除 branch、task 已 reap
24	```
25	
26	`hot`、`warm`、`cold`、`done` 仍是唯一的 persisted task state——`done` 代表 MERGED，cleanup 可能仍待執行，**不代表** runtime 或 worktree 已經被刪除。
27	
28	## 命令
29	
30	| 命令 | 作用 |
31	|---|---|
32	| `dev prepare --session <provider:uuid> --plan <path>` | 在不關閉目前執行中 agent 的情況下，arm post-writer artifact finalization。Product changes 必須已先 commit；transcript 本身刻意尚未 stage。 |
33	| `dev artifact finalize --run-id "$DEV_AGENT_RUN_ID" --if-pending --writer-stopped` | 在 writer 停止後，commit 唯一 exact、stable 的 transcript。`--if-pending` 在沒有對應 armed intent 時靜默 no-op；`--writer-stopped` 確認外層 wrapper 已 return。 |
34	| `dev done --ff` | 把 task branch rebase 到其 base 上並在本機 fast-forward。記錄為 MERGED；不會關閉 runtime、移除 worktree 或刪除 branch。 |
35	| `dev done --pr` | Push branch，並透過可用的 forge CLI 開啟 pull/merge request。Task 保持在 review 狀態，不是 MERGED。 |
36	| `dev done --merged --base-ref <ref>` | 驗證某個已在外部 merge 的 branch 是否被 `<ref>` 包含，並記錄為 MERGED。 |
37	| `dev done --merged --base-ref <ref> --confirm-squash <merge-commit>` | 同上，但用於 squash merge：attest（斷言）已證明被 `<ref>` 包含的該 commit 代表這條 feature branch。這是 dev 無法自行驗證的 operator assertion。 |
38	| `dev artifact discard <intent> --yes` | 記錄某個 intent 永遠無法 finalize——transcript 從未被寫出，或 rebase 之後 HEAD 已不存在——使它不再阻擋 integration 與 retirement。它不會 commit 也不會復原任何東西，會先印出確切將被放棄的內容，並拒絕仍為 `armed` 的 intent，因為 finalize 才是保存 transcript 的路徑。 |
39	| `dev retire [task-or-worktree] [--close-unknown] [--assume-no-runtime] [--delete-branch] [--timeout <duration>]` | 重新解析每一個 covering runtime session，拒絕 active agent 與 mixed-purpose workspace，等待其關閉，重新驗證 Git state，才移除 linked worktree（不使用 force）。只有在所有要求的步驟都成功後，才刪除 task record。 |
40	| `dev sweep --merged-worktrees [--base <ref>] [--apply] [--yes] [--close-unknown] [--assume-no-runtime] [--delete-branches]` | 從 canonical checkout 執行，回報（加上 `--apply` 時則 retire）branch 已被 base 包含的 task-tracked 與 unmanaged linked worktree。 |
41	
42	Dirty checkout 在這裡不會直接失敗：`dev done` 會先把它與 base 比對分類，在
43	interactive 時提供 commit 或 discard，在 script 中則接受明確的 `--dirty`
44	policy。該 wizard 詳見[變更流工作流程](change-stream-workflow.zh-TW.md)。
45	`dev done` 上的 `--keep-worktree` 與 `--delete-branch` 之所以仍被接受，只是為了
46	明確報錯並指向 `dev retire`。
47	
48	Action 前若需要 read-only explanation，從 exact checkout render 或 open generic
49	`workspace-closeout` recipe：
50	
51	```bash
52	dev prompt render workspace-closeout .
53	dev prompt open workspace-closeout . --agent my-agent
54	```
55	
56	Recipe 內含完整 retirement audit，但結果只是 advisory。`eligible` 與 merged PR 都不
57	授權 cleanup；外部 `dev retire` 仍會重新收集並驗證所有 gate。若 `dev done --ff` 或
58	`dev git pull-rebase` 停在 conflict，只用 `prompt open` 討論 semantic resolution，
59	接著明確 continue/abort Git，再重新執行 lifecycle command。詳見
60	[Prompt handoff](prompt-handoffs.zh-TW.md)。
61	
62	## 一般 local flow
63	
64	在 feature worktree 中：
65	
66	```bash
67	# 先 commit product changes，不要 stage 仍在變動中的 transcript。
68	dev prepare --session claude:<uuid> --plan .claude/plans/task.md
69	# 正常結束 agent，讓 SpecStory 寫出最終 Markdown。
70	```
71	
72	外層 `specstory run` wrapper 接著呼叫：
73	
74	```bash
75	dev artifact finalize --run-id "$DEV_AGENT_RUN_ID" --if-pending --writer-stopped
76	```
77	
78	外部的 main/integration workspace 完成剩下的工作：
79	
80	```bash
81	dev done <task> --ff
82	dev retire <task> --delete-branch
83	```
84	
85	`dev done` 只負責整合並記錄為 MERGED。`dev retire` 會重新解析每個 runtime pane、關閉符合條件的 session、等待它們消失、重新驗證 Git，再移除 worktree（不使用 force）。
86	
87	## Pull-request 流程
88	
89	```bash
90	dev done <task> --pr
91	# CI/review 完成，且以保留 commit 的方式 merge 之後
92	git fetch origin
93	dev done <task> --merged --base-ref origin/main
94	dev retire <task> --delete-branch
95	```
96	
97	Squash merge 並不等同於 ancestry-equivalent，因此需要明確的 operator attestation：
98	
99	```bash
100	dev done <task> --merged --base-ref origin/main --confirm-squash <merge-commit>
101	```
102	
103	這只證明所指名的 squash commit 被包含在 base 中；operator 是在斷言它確實代表這條 feature branch。
104	
105	## 拒絕條件
106	
107	只要符合以下任一條件，`retire.Inspect` 就會拒絕繼續執行；且它會在關閉 session 後重新檢查，而不是信任過期的視圖：
108	
109	- 呼叫者目前所在目錄就是 target checkout 或其下層；
110	- 呼叫者的 `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`、`HERDR_PANE_ID` 或 `TMUX_PANE` 對應到一個涵蓋 target 的 runtime session；
111	- 某個涵蓋 target 的 runtime workspace 同時也包含 target 以外的 pane（mixed-purpose workspace）；
112	- 任何涵蓋中的 agent status 為 `working`、`running`、`busy`、`blocked` 或 `waiting`——**任何 flag 都無法 override**；
113	- Agent status 為空或 `unknown`，**除非**呼叫者從 target 外部傳入 `--close-unknown`；
114	- Agent status 無法辨識（不在已知集合內）——一律阻擋；
115	- Runtime enumeration 本身失敗，**除非**呼叫者傳入 `--assume-no-runtime`。
116	
117	`--close-unknown` 與 `--assume-no-runtime` 只放寬 fail-closed 的*觀測結果*（無法讀取的 status、無法列舉的 runtime list）。這兩個 flag 都絕不會 bypass caller containment 或 active-agent state。`retirement.Service.Retire` 在 runtime session 關閉後，也會重新驗證 target identity、Git ancestry、進行中的 Git operation（`gitx.InProgress`，檢查 `MERGE_HEAD`、`CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`、`REVERT_HEAD`、`rebase-merge`、`rebase-apply`、`sequencer`；不含 `REBASE_HEAD`，因為 Git 在 rebase 完成後仍會保留它）以及 worktree 是否 clean——因為 runtime draining 期間現實可能已改變，先前的驗證結果不會跨越這個邊界沿用。
118	
119	## 用 sweep 做定期 cleanup
120	
121	```bash
122	dev sweep --merged-worktrees
123	# 把確切的 candidates/blockers 呈現給使用者，並徵求核可。
124	dev sweep --merged-worktrees --apply --yes
125	```
126	
127	這會同時列出 task-tracked 的 DONE worktree，以及 named branch 已被 base 包含的 unmanaged linked worktree——請從 canonical checkout 執行。它會先回報再套用：containment 本身絕不等於許可。Dirty 的 Git state、pending 或無法到達的 artifact、locked 或 prunable 的 worktree registration、進行中的 Git operation，以及與 `dev retire` 相同的 runtime 拒絕條件，都仍會阻擋 cleanup。Retirement 完成後預設保留 branch；只有在使用者另外核可刪除時，才加上 `--delete-branches`。
128	
129	## 安全邊界
130	
131	原始的 `git worktree remove --force` 會完全繞過 dev——絕不要在佔用 target 的 agent 中執行它。dev 的保證僅止於：沒有任何 dev-mediated 路徑會執行 forced removal；它無法阻止 operator 或 script 直接呼叫 Git。
132	
133	曾經真實發生過：一個 Codex session 從另一個 checkout 刪除了自己已註冊的 worktree 與 branch。Herdr 仍讓該 workspace 與 terminal 保持存活，因為 Unix process 在路徑被 unlink 之後仍可持有開啟中的 cwd inode；接著 SpecStory 又在同一路徑重新建立、但內容只剩 `.specstory/`。這個 shell 看起來還活著，但已經不再是一個 Git checkout：
134	
135	```text
136	failed to reload config: No such file or directory
137	fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
138	```
139	
140	請把「runtime 存活 + Git registration 不存在 + artifact-only path」視為需要 transcript salvage 與外部 reconciliation 的 orphan——**絕不能**視為 RETIRED。
141	
142	`dev sweep` 現在會自行辨識這個形狀，不再只能靠人眼察覺。當某個 task 記錄的 checkout 存在、但 Git 並未註冊它，且該目錄裡只有 agent artifact 資料夾時，sweep 會將它回報為 abandoned agent workspace。只有在其中每個檔案都與 repository 已有的檔案 byte-identical 時，sweep 才會提議移除；任何內容不同的檔案都會被列為 salvage 工作並保持原狀，`--apply` 也不會動它。
143	
144	這裡採用 byte equality 而非僅檢查檔案是否存在，正是重點所在。比 worktree 活得更久的 transcript writer，通常會 flush 出比先前 commit 版本更長的最終稿，因此 repository 中存在同名檔案並不能證明結尾內容已被保存。
145
