8	
9	# Compatibility and known limitations
10	
11	This page separates graceful degradation from real limitations. Reverify it whenever command/runtime code or version-sensitive Claude Code documentation changes.
12	
13	## dev-cli capability matrix
14	
15	| Capability | Dependency | Without it |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| core repository/task/worktree operations | Git | unavailable; Git is the only hard runtime dependency |
18	| rich grouped runtime and agent activity | Herdr server + CLI | `auto` tries tmux, then Zellij, then none |
19	| named terminal session | tmux or compatible Zellij | `none` preserves core behavior and shell navigation |
20	| GitHub pull requests/remotes | `gh` authenticated | branch still pushes when Git works; browser/manual flow may be needed |
21	| GitLab merge requests/remotes | `glab` authenticated | same graceful fallback |
22	| repository bootstrap publishing | authenticated `gh` or `glab` | local repository/scaffold still works; the wizard explains how to log in |
23	| remote repository snapshot template | Git plus network/authentication for the source | validation fails before the destination is created and rendered URL userinfo is redacted; local templates still work |
24	| setup-capable project skills | skills provider plus the entrypoint interpreter | unselected skills are skipped; selected required setup fails before scaffold mutation when its interpreter is unavailable; a clone acquired first is retained |
25	| staged lazygit message prefill | a lazygit version that reads `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT` | files remain staged and dev prints the suggested message; normal Git commit remains available |
26	| worktree dependency setup | ecosystem manager (`uv`, npm, Cargo, etc.) | plan reports the missing tool and keeps the checkout |
27	| interactive dashboard | terminal input/output | bare `dev` prints the plain task list when piped |
28	| repository-note search | linked `modernc.org/sqlite` with FTS5 | no external `sqlite3` executable is required |
29	| terminal multiplexing on Windows | tmux/Zellij/Herdr (POSIX only) | Windows always uses the `none` backend; `dev shell-init powershell` still moves the shell |
30	| in-place self-update | standalone install (not Homebrew/Scoop/`go install`) | `dev upgrade` delegates to the package manager's upgrade command instead |
31	
32	## Confirmed project limitations
33	
34	### Note search and filesystem durability vary by text and platform
35	
36	Latin note queries use term-wise prefix FTS and SQLite ranking. Non-ASCII queries use literal term-wise substring matching because SQLite's `unicode61` tokenizer does not segment arbitrary CJK substrings; those results do not use the same FTS ranking.
37	
38	Note writes sync the file and atomically rename it on every supported platform. Unix also syncs the containing directory after rename/delete. The Windows implementation cannot provide that directory-fsync step, so a sudden power loss has a narrower durability guarantee there. Concurrent mutations by cooperating `dev` processes are serialized and each Markdown replacement is atomic; arbitrary external writers do not participate in that lock.
39	
40	### A merged pull request does not retire its worktree
41	
42	`dev done --pr` pushes and opens a pull/merge request, then leaves the task, runtime, and worktree unchanged because review owns integration.
43	
44	`dev pr list --scope local --state merged` now reports which requests the forge considers merged, and which local checkout each belongs to. `dev sweep` still does not consult it, and that is deliberate: a squashed merge produces a commit that is not an ancestor of the local branch, so a forge saying "merged" cannot prove the work is recoverable from the remote. `dev sweep --merged-worktrees` proves containment locally with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, and `dev done --merged` requires an explicit `--confirm-squash` attestation. Treat the pull-request list as a prompt to look, not as permission to delete.
45	
46	### Pull-request inventory is limited by the provider surfaces
47	
48	GitHub's `gh search prs` account surface cannot report a head branch, review decision, or check status, so those rows are `detail: "summary"` and cannot be joined to a worktree. An absent field on a summary row means the surface could not report it, not that the value is empty. GitLab's account list does carry branch/merge detail and therefore returns full rows, but its list surfaces report neither pipeline checks nor a normalized review decision.
49	
50	Personal per-repository inventory may make one paginated query per requested role for each repository (author and reviewer by default). It covers repositories `dev` has a task for unless `--all-repos` widens the scan. `--repo` filters both account rows and local targets. Account search cannot distinguish merged from closed, so requesting merged/closed/all narrows an account/all request to local collection; JSON reports that effective scope.
51	
52	The schema-version-1 local join reports expected and live branches, checkout existence, worktree registration, status availability/error, and whether the expected branch is actually checked out. Git details are omitted unless those live checks succeed. Azure DevOps pull requests are not listed at all; a configured target is reported as unsupported rather than failing the command.
53	
54	### Prompt open uses the current terminal, not runtime placement
55	
56	`dev prompt open <recipe>` runs one configured child in the foreground of the
57	terminal/TTY that invoked it. It does not create, focus, reuse, or inject into a
58	Herdr, tmux, or Zellij pane. Inside Herdr it naturally remains in the current
59	pane. To use another Herdr pane, create or focus it manually, enter the exact
60	checkout, and run `prompt open` there.
61	
62	This is intentionally separate from `dev start --run`, whose dispatch target is
63	only the exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree.
64	`prompt open` neither supplies a fresh runtime surface nor weakens that
65	exact-pane proof. `run` is the non-interactive alternative; it receives no user
66	stdin and defaults to a 10-minute timeout, while `open` reserves stdin for the
67	conversation and has no default timeout.
68	
69	The configured child retains its own permission policy. Recipe instructions are
70	read-only guidance, not a sandbox; `dev` does not add permission flags, answer
71	approval prompts, or parse the response into an action.
72	
73	### Prompt closeout reports do not authorize cleanup
74	
75	`session-close` computes runtime-closure evidence only. An `idle` or `done`
76	covering agent can satisfy that one activity gate, but does not prove that work
77	is committed, artifacts are finalized, review is complete, or task intent is
78	done. Caller-contained, mixed-purpose, active, unknown, and unrecognized
79	sessions remain blocked or unknown as their evidence requires.
80	
81	`workspace-closeout` performs the broader read-only audit: target kind,
82	registration/path, status availability, clean Git state, no in-progress Git
83	operation, known base and containment, task completion, artifact
84	reachability/finalization, and runtime eligibility. A merged pull request is only
85	evidence. Even an `eligible` audit is advisory; `dev retire` recollects and
86	revalidates fresh state before any mutation. Neither recipe closes a runtime,
87	changes Git/task state, deletes a branch/worktree, or grants permission to do so.
88	
89	### Zellij exited sessions are closed but keep their names
90	
91	Zellij keeps exited sessions available for resurrection. `dev` recognizes only
92	the exact `(EXITED - attach to resurrect)` marker, omits those sessions from live
93	coverage, and refuses to create over their names; reclaim one with
94	`zellij delete-session <name>`. A live session name containing `EXITED` is not an
95	exit marker. If a session exits between native listing and layout inspection,
96	open fails closed and asks for a retry rather than resurrecting an old layout at
97	the requested checkout.
98	
99	### Forge CLI sign-in is reported, never retried
100	
101	`gh` and `glab` are optional and independent, and `dev` never authenticates on your behalf. When a provider's stored credential is missing or rejected, `dev` reports which provider and the exact login command — for example ``glab is signed out — run `glab auth login --hostname gitlab.com` `` — and continues with whatever the other provider returned. `dev repo remote` and the TUI REMOTE view render the partial result and warn; `dev pr` fails only when no provider is authenticated at all. `dev doctor` probes sign-in state, so an installed but signed-out CLI is visible before a command needs it.
102	
103	Only a missing or rejected credential is reported this way. A rate limit, a permissions or scope failure, and a network error keep their full diagnostic text including the command that failed, because signing in again would not fix them. The original command and provider output remain in the wrapped error in every case.
104	
105	### Agent session capture is reserved, not wired
106	
107	The task schema has an `AgentSession` field and Herdr inventory can expose live agent session IDs. The production start/park/resume path does not yet capture or attach that ID. Treat the field and live inventory as observability/future integration, not a promise that `dev resume` restores the coding-agent conversation.
108	
109	### Built-in forge cache TTL differs from generated config
110	
111	`dev config init` writes `forge.cache_ttl = "15m"`. With no config file, the current built-in `Forge.CacheTTL` zero value means an existing valid cache is not rejected by age; explicit `r` refresh still replaces it. Freshness also requires a source fingerprint matching the configured GH/GL hosts and Azure targets, so an endpoint change is never hidden by the zero TTL. Legacy source-less caches remain available only through explicit `--cached` and are reported stale. Run `config init` or set the TTL when freshness matters.
112	
113	Older generated configs may contain `forge.remote_limit = 100`. The field is
114	still accepted, but complete forge inventories are now paginated and it no
115	longer caps synchronization. `dev config init` no longer writes it. The
116	`--limit` flag on `dev repo remote` limits rendered matches after the complete
117	inventory has been searched.
118	
119	### Lazygit staged-message prefill is best effort
120	
121	`repo --check-in=stage` writes a pending message in the exact worktree Git
122	directory. [Lazygit v0.59.0 uses that file for lowercase
123	`c`](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/v0.59.0/pkg/gui/controllers/helpers/working_tree_helper.go#L191-L216), but it is a
124	lazygit implementation detail rather than a Git interface; uppercase `C` and
125	plain `git commit` do not consume it. Dev never overwrites a different existing
126	draft. A draft-write failure is warning-only: staging remains successful and
127	is never rolled back. If the integration changes upstream, the staged index
128	and printed message remain the recovery path.
129	
130	### Windows is a build target, not a full-feature platform
131	
132	`dev` compiles and runs on `windows/amd64` and `windows/arm64`, and every release ships a `.zip` for each. Core repository, task and worktree operations work. What differs:
133	
134	- There is no tmux, Zellij or Herdr, so the runtime backend is always `none`. Grouped runtime/agent activity and named sessions are unavailable; the `cd` directive and PowerShell wrapper still work.
135	- Shell integration is `dev shell-init powershell`. POSIX shells hand the directory back on file descriptor 3; PowerShell cannot inherit it, so the wrapper passes a temp-file path in `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` instead.
136	- `dev fleet open` starts a child shell (`%COMSPEC%`) rather than replacing the process, because Windows has no `exec(2)`.
137	- The domain test suites still assume a POSIX filesystem in places, so Windows CI runs the tests advisory-only while compilation, `go vet` and the build are enforced.
138	
139	### Direct mode has a smaller lifecycle
140	
141	A direct task uses the canonical checkout and cannot go COLD, because cold cleanup would remove a directory the repository needs. Use branch-only or worktree mode for cross-machine reconstruction.
142	
143	## Current behaviors that are implemented
144	
145	These were historical gaps and should not be reintroduced as limitations:
146	
147	- `dev repo new|create`, `repo clone`, and `repo setup` share a preset-driven bootstrap pipeline. A plain explicit `repo new NAME` remains minimal, while a clear Git URL, local Git path, or owner/name routes through clone acquisition and preserves source history/remote. The no-argument wizard detects the same reference in its first field; for a new repository, a default-no customization gate keeps the normal `agent-ready` flow concise. Text fields use a TTY inline editor, so cursor keys edit rather than inserting raw escape bytes; non-TTY readers retain line-oriented behavior.
148	- `repo new` can snapshot a local directory/repository or Git source at an optional branch, tag, or commit and confined subdirectory into a fresh history. An unpinned local Git tree includes tracked plus untracked non-ignored files; a non-Git directory includes its full current tree. Source `.git` metadata is excluded, URL userinfo is redacted, unsafe file types/paths fail before destination creation, and held root/file handles confine mutable-path races. Human plans preview paths and warn when the snapshot is live; presets can select catalog-repository subfolders.
149	- Repository setup supports `--check-in=commit|stage|none` (`auto` for preset compatibility). Staged setup runs before-commit setup and `git add -A` without an `after_commit` phase, cannot publish or hand off to `start`, and may prefill lazygit lowercase `c` as described above.
150	- Selected skills with matching source and agent targets share one installer invocation. The `agent-history-hygiene` initializer writes pre-commit/gitleaks policy and merges missing machine-local `.project.json`/`statistics.json` rules into `.specstory/.gitignore`; custom content and transcript history remain trackable.
151	- Project `.dev-cli/config.toml` and `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml` are constrained to portable setup policy. Executable project configuration is keyed to the canonical Git common directory and an exact content hash; a changed hash is untrusted until approved again.
152	
153	- `dev start --focus` activates the runtime after non-JSON creation.
154	- `dev start --run '<shell command>'` dispatches only to an exact root pane from
155	  a newly created first-class Herdr worktree. It is incompatible with `--json`,
156	  non-worktree modes, and non-Herdr runtimes, and does not wait for command exit.
157	- TUI navigation refuses to open a missing COLD checkout and directs the user to `dev resume`.
158	- `DEV_TUI_TRACE` starts at `cli.Execute`; it cannot include OS process loading. `tui.initial_view_returned` measures model construction, not renderer flush or physical terminal paint. Use it for same-profile comparisons rather than universal hardware/network guarantees.
159	- Runtime handles now record backend provenance and are revalidated before cleanup.
160	- `auto` runtime selection includes Zellij between tmux and none.
161	
162	- `dev done` opens an interactive finish wizard on a TTY when `--ff`/`--pr` are both omitted, analyzing a dirty checkout against the base (commit, discard, or cancel) instead of rejecting any uncommitted change outright; a non-interactive caller still passes an explicit `--dirty` policy and `--yes` for a destructive discard.
163	- Human-readable output now carries semantic color (`--color auto|always|never`), automatically disabled when `NO_COLOR` is set, `TERM=dumb`, or stdout/stderr is not a terminal.
164	- `dev done` records MERGED only: it never closes the invoking runtime, removes a worktree, or deletes a branch. Cleanup moved to `dev retire`, which runs from outside the target workspace, refuses active agents and mixed-purpose workspaces, and revalidates Git state after every runtime closure. `dev done --delete-branch` is now an error pointing at `dev retire --delete-branch`, and `--keep-worktree` warns as a no-op.
165	- `dev sweep --merged-worktrees` enumerates linked worktrees from Git rather than from the task registry, so unmanaged worktrees whose branches are contained in the base become retirable. Containment alone is never permission; dirty state, unfinalized artifacts, in-progress Git operations, and runtime refusals all still block it, and branches survive unless `--delete-branches` is passed.
166	- `dev sweep` reports a branch-backed task whose branch Git no longer has as dead and offers to reap the record. Such a task cannot be finished, resumed, or retired, because every one of those paths resolves the branch first; the suggestion stays report-only until `--apply`.
167	- An unknown command is reported instead of discarded. `dev` silences cobra's own error printing and previously also skipped printing anything whose message began with `unknown command`, so a mistyped command produced no output at all on either stream. The message, cobra's "Did you mean this?" suggestions, and a pointer to `--help` are now printed to stderr with exit status 1.
168	- A stray argument to a command family is an error rather than a silent help render. `dev wt bogus` used to print `dev wt` help and exit 0 because a family has no `Run` of its own; every family node now reports the unknown subcommand and exits 1, while a bare family still prints its help and exits 0.
169	- Argument-count and flag errors print the failing command's usage block. `--color` still governs whether that block is colorized.
170	- Each command family's help carries an ASCII orientation diagram and a `See also: dev help <topic>` pointer, and `dev help <command>` resolves a command name or alias to its topic, so `dev help wt` reaches the worktrees page.
171	- Semantic color covers every human-readable surface, including the interactive dashboard: `dev --color never`, `NO_COLOR` and `TERM=dumb` now disable dashboard color too, which they previously did not.
172	- `dev sweep` reaps a task whose repository directory no longer exists. Such a record was unreachable by every command in the binary: `done`, `resume`, `park` and `retire` all resolve the repository first, the dead-branch rule excludes direct mode, and the stale-worktree rule requires a recorded worktree path. A live runtime session rules the suggestion out, and reaping removes only dev's record of intent.
173	- `dev sweep` reports a task-recorded checkout that exists but Git does not register and that holds nothing but agent artifact directories. Removal is offered only when every file inside is byte-identical to one already in the repository; anything else is reported as salvage work and is never removed, including under `--apply`.
174	- `dev sweep` acts on a cold task whose worktree is still on disk. Inventory has always computed that drift for `dev ls` and the dashboard, but sweep never consulted it, so it was displayed and not actionable.
175	- `dev retire <path>` reaps the matching task record. Only the by-task form set the task identity, so retiring the same checkout by path left the record behind; the DONE-state and identity checks are unchanged.
176	- `dev version` reports whether the running build is a published release, and `dev doctor` carries the same line plus the install owner, invoked/resolved executable path, and warnings for distinct `dev` copies on `PATH`. Nothing in the tool answered "am I current?" before, and `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so an untagged feature was invisible to anyone installing it.
177	- A release publishes platform archives and `SHA256SUMS` and takes its notes from `CHANGELOG.md`. Earlier releases published a GitHub release object and nothing else, so their assets are absent by construction.
178	- A release publishes Windows `.zip` archives alongside the Unix `.tar.gz` set, refreshes an in-repo Scoop manifest attached to the release (and pushed to the bucket when a token is configured), and publishes the matching source formula to `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`. Homebrew publication is a required release step and fails visibly when its repository token is missing or rejected. A manual workflow can retry or backfill the formula for an existing stable release without creating or moving a tag.
179	- `dev upgrade` downloads the current release for this platform, verifies it against the release `SHA256SUMS`, and replaces the running binary with an atomic rename (Windows moves the live `.exe` aside and sweeps it on the next run). It detects and runs Homebrew, Scoop or `go install` when one of them owns the file; Homebrew users receive releases through the automatically advanced tap instead of an in-place Cellar overwrite.
180	- An interactive `dev` command prints one dim "newer release available" line at most once a day, read from the day-old release cache; it never blocks on the network. For the TUI, a stale-cache background refresh starts only after the initial view returns. `[update] check = false` or `DEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` disables it.

17	## dev-cli capability matrix
18	
19	| Capability | Dependency | 缺少時 |

25	| GitLab merge requests/remotes | authenticated `glab` | 同樣 graceful fallback |
26	| repository bootstrap publishing | authenticated `gh` 或 `glab` | local repository/scaffold 仍可使用；wizard 會說明如何 login |

30	| worktree dependency setup | ecosystem manager（`uv`、npm、Cargo 等） | plan 回報 missing tool 並保留 checkout |
31	| interactive dashboard | terminal input/output | 透過 pipe 執行 bare `dev` 時輸出 plain task list |

33	| Windows 上的 terminal multiplexing | tmux/Zellij/Herdr（僅 POSIX） | Windows 一律使用 `none` backend；`dev shell-init powershell` 仍能移動 shell |

36	## 已確認的專案限制
37	
38	### Note search 與 filesystem durability 依文字及平台而異
39	
40	Latin note query 使用 term-wise prefix FTS 與 SQLite ranking。Non-ASCII query 改用 literal term-wise substring matching，因為 SQLite 的 `unicode61` tokenizer 不會切分任意 CJK substrings；這些結果不使用相同的 FTS ranking。
41	
42	所有支援平台的 note write 都會 sync file 並 atomic rename。Unix 也會在 rename/delete 後 sync containing directory。Windows implementation 無法提供 directory-fsync 步驟，因此 sudden power loss 時的 durability guarantee 較窄。Cooperating `dev` processes 的 concurrent mutations 會被 serialized，且每次 Markdown replacement 都是 atomic；任意 external writer 不會參與這個 lock。
43	
44	### 已 merge 的 pull request 不會自動收掉它的 worktree
45	
46	`dev done --pr` push 並建立 pull/merge request，之後保留 task、runtime 與 worktree，因為 integration 由 review 負責。
47	
48	`dev pr list --scope local --state merged` 現在會報告 forge 認定已 merge 的 request，以及各自對應到哪一個本地 checkout。`dev sweep` 仍然不會去查它，這是刻意的：squash merge 產生的 commit 並不是本地 branch 的 ancestor，所以 forge 說「merged」無法證明這份工作能從 remote 復原。`dev sweep --merged-worktrees` 用 `git merge-base --is-ancestor` 在本地證明 containment，而 `dev done --merged` 需要明確的 `--confirm-squash` attestation。把 pull request 清單當成「該去看一下」的提示，而不是「可以刪」的許可。
49	
50	### Pull request inventory 受限於 provider surface
51	
52	GitHub 的 `gh search prs` account surface 無法回報 head branch、review decision 或 check status，因此這些 rows 是 `detail: "summary"`，也無法 join 到 worktree。Summary row 的 absent field 表示 surface 無法回報，不是 value 為空。GitLab account list 帶有 branch/merge detail，因此回傳 full row；但 GitLab list surfaces 都不回報 pipeline checks 或 normalized review decision。
53	
54	Personal per-repository inventory 對每個 repository 的每個 requested role（預設 author 與 reviewer）可能各發一個 paginated query。預設只涵蓋 `dev` 有 task 的 repository；`--all-repos` 擴大 scan。`--repo` 同時 filter account rows 與 local targets。Account search 無法區分 merged 與 closed，所以 merged/closed/all 會將 account/all request narrow 到 local collection；JSON 回報該 effective scope。
55	
56	Schema-version-1 local join 回報 expected/live branch、checkout existence、worktree registration、status availability/error，以及 expected branch 是否確實 checked out。只有這些 live checks 成功時才出現 Git detail。Azure DevOps pull request 完全不列出；configured target 會被報告為 unsupported，而不是讓 command 失敗。
57	
58	### Prompt open 使用 current terminal，不負責 runtime placement
59	
60	`dev prompt open <recipe>` 在呼叫它的 terminal/TTY foreground 執行一個
61	configured child。它不會建立、focus、reuse 或 inject Herdr、tmux 或 Zellij pane。
62	在 Herdr 裡自然會留在 current pane。若要用另一個 Herdr pane，請手動建立或 focus、
63	進入 exact checkout，再從那裡執行 `prompt open`。
64	
65	這與 `dev start --run` 刻意分開；後者唯一可 dispatch 的 target，是本次新建
66	first-class Herdr worktree 回傳的 exact root pane。`prompt open` 不會提供 fresh runtime
67	surface，也不會放寬 exact-pane proof。`run` 是 non-interactive alternative：沒有 user
68	stdin，default timeout 為 10 分鐘；`open` 保留 stdin 給 conversation，沒有 default timeout。
69	
70	Configured child 保留自己的 permission policy。Recipe instruction 是 read-only
71	guidance，不是 sandbox；`dev` 不會加入 permission flag、代答 approval prompt，或把
72	response parse 成 action。
73	
74	### Prompt closeout report 不授權 cleanup
75	
76	`session-close` 只計算 runtime-closure evidence。Covering agent 為 `idle` 或 `done`
77	時可以通過這一項 activity gate，但不證明 work 已 commit、artifact 已 finalize、review
78	完成或 task intent done。Caller-contained、mixed-purpose、active、unknown 與
79	unrecognized session 仍依 evidence 維持 blocked/unknown。
80	
81	`workspace-closeout` 執行較廣的 read-only audit：target kind、registration/path、
82	status availability、clean Git state、沒有 in-progress Git operation、known base 與
83	containment、task completion、artifact reachability/finalization、runtime eligibility。
84	Merged pull request 只是 evidence。即使 audit 為 `eligible` 也只是 advisory；
85	`dev retire` 在 mutation 前會重新收集與驗證 fresh state。兩個 recipe 都不會關閉
86	runtime、改變 Git/task state、刪除 branch/worktree 或授予 permission。
87	
88	### Zellij exited session 已關閉，但仍保留 name
89	
90	Zellij 會保留可 resurrect 的 exited session。`dev` 只辨識 exact
91	`(EXITED - attach to resurrect)` marker、從 live coverage 省略這些 session，並拒絕用其
92	name 建立新 session；可用 `zellij delete-session <name>` 回收。Live session name 只是含
93	`EXITED` 並不是 exit marker。若 session 在 native listing 與 layout inspection 之間退出，
94	open 會 fail closed 並要求 retry，不會在 requested checkout resurrect 舊 layout。
95	
96	### Forge CLI 登入狀態只會被報告，不會自動重試
97	
98	`gh` 與 `glab` 是選用且彼此獨立的，`dev` 永遠不會代替你認證。當某個 provider 的憑證缺少或被拒絕時，`dev` 會報告是哪一個 provider 以及確切的登入指令 — 例如 ``glab is signed out — run `glab auth login --hostname gitlab.com` `` — 並繼續使用另一個 provider 傳回的結果。`dev repo remote` 與 TUI REMOTE view 會呈現部分結果並發出 warning；`dev pr` 只有在完全沒有任何 provider 通過認證時才會失敗。`dev doctor` 會探測登入狀態，所以「已安裝但未登入」的 CLI 在某個指令需要它之前就看得到。
99	
100	只有缺少或被拒絕的憑證會用這種方式報告。Rate limit、權限或 scope 失敗，以及網路錯誤，都會保留完整的診斷文字（含失敗的指令），因為重新登入並不能解決它們。無論哪一種情況，原始指令與 provider 輸出都保留在被包裝的 error 之中。
101	
102	### Agent session capture 只有保留欄位，尚未接線
103	
104	Task schema 有 `AgentSession`，Herdr inventory 也能顯示 live agent session ID；production start/park/resume path 尚未 capture 或 attach 該 ID。這個欄位與 live inventory 只能視為 observability/future integration，不能承諾 `dev resume` 會恢復 coding-agent conversation。
105	
106	### Built-in forge cache TTL 與 generated config 不同
107	
108	`dev config init` 會寫 `forge.cache_ttl = "15m"`。沒有 config file 時，目前 built-in `Forge.CacheTTL` 的 zero value 代表既有 valid cache 不會因 age 被拒絕；explicit `r` 仍會 refresh。Freshness 也要求 source fingerprint 符合 configured GH/GL hosts 與 Azure targets，因此 endpoint change 不會被 zero TTL 隱藏。Legacy source-less cache 只能透過 explicit `--cached` 使用，並會標為 stale。Freshness 重要時請執行 `config init` 或設定 TTL。
109	
110	較舊的 generated config 可能包含 `forge.remote_limit = 100`。此欄位仍可解析，
111	但 forge inventory 現在會完整 pagination，因此不再限制 synchronization。
112	`dev config init` 不再寫入它；`dev repo remote --limit` 只在完整 inventory 搜尋
113	完成後限制 rendered matches。
114	
115	### Lazygit staged-message prefill 是 best effort
116	
117	`repo --check-in=stage` 會在正確的 worktree Git directory 寫入 pending message。
118	[Lazygit v0.59.0 的小寫 `c` 會使用該
119	檔案](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/v0.59.0/pkg/gui/controllers/helpers/working_tree_helper.go#L191-L216)，但這是 lazygit implementation detail，不是 Git
120	interface；大寫 `C` 與一般 `git commit` 不會讀取它。Dev 不會覆寫內容不同的既有
121	draft。Draft write failure 只會產生 warning；staging 仍視為成功且不會 rollback。若
122	upstream integration 日後改變，staged index 與已印出的 message 仍是 recovery path。
123	
124	### Windows 是 build target，不是 full-feature 平台
125	
126	`dev` 可在 `windows/amd64` 與 `windows/arm64` 編譯並執行，每個 release 都會附各自的 `.zip`。核心的 repository、task 與 worktree 操作可用。差異：
127	
128	- 沒有 tmux、Zellij 或 Herdr，因此 runtime backend 一律是 `none`。Grouped runtime/agent activity 與 named session 無法使用；`cd` 指令與 PowerShell wrapper 仍可運作。
129	- Shell integration 是 `dev shell-init powershell`。POSIX shell 透過 file descriptor 3 回傳目錄；PowerShell 無法繼承它，wrapper 改用 `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` 傳入 temp-file path。
130	- `dev fleet open` 會啟動子 shell（`%COMSPEC%`），而非取代 process，因為 Windows 沒有 `exec(2)`。
131	- Domain test suites 仍有部分假設 POSIX filesystem，因此 Windows CI 的 test 僅供參考，compilation、`go vet` 與 build 則為強制項。
132	
133	### Direct mode 的 lifecycle 較小
134	
135	Direct task 使用 canonical checkout，不能進入 COLD，因為 cold cleanup 會移除 repository 必需的 directory。需要跨機器 reconstruction 時使用 branch-only 或 worktree mode。
136	
137	## 已實作、不能再列為 limitation 的 behavior
138	
139	以下是歷史缺口，現行版本已實作：
140	
141	- `dev repo new|create`、`repo clone` 與 `repo setup` 共用 preset-driven bootstrap pipeline。Plain explicit `repo new NAME` 仍維持 minimal；清楚的 Git URL、local Git path 或 owner/name 會改走 clone acquisition，保留 source history/remote。無參數 wizard 的第一個欄位也會偵測同樣 reference；建立新 repository 時，預設為 no 的 customization gate 讓正常 `agent-ready` flow 保持精簡。Text fields 使用 TTY inline editor，因此 cursor keys 會編輯內容，不會插入 raw escape bytes；non-TTY reader 維持 line-oriented behavior。
142	- `repo new` 可從 local directory/repository 或 Git source 的 optional branch、tag、commit 與 confined subdirectory 建立 fresh-history snapshot。未 pin 的 local Git tree 包含 tracked 加 untracked non-ignored files；non-Git directory 包含完整 current tree。Source `.git` metadata 會排除、URL userinfo 會 redact，不安全的 file types/paths 會在 destination 建立前失敗，held root/file handles 會限制 mutable-path races。Human plan 會預覽 paths 並警告 live snapshot，preset 也可選擇 catalog-repository subfolder。
143	- Repository setup 支援 `--check-in=commit|stage|none`（`auto` 用於 preset compatibility）。Staged setup 會執行 before-commit setup 與 `git add -A`，但不執行 `after_commit` phase；它不能 publish 或 handoff 到 `start`，並可依前述方式預填 lazygit 小寫 `c`。
144	- Source 與 agent targets 相同的 selected skills 會共用一次 installer invocation。`agent-history-hygiene` initializer 會寫入 pre-commit/gitleaks policy，並將缺少的 machine-local `.project.json`／`statistics.json` 規則 merge 進 `.specstory/.gitignore`；custom content 與 transcript history 都保持可追蹤。
145	- Project `.dev-cli/config.toml` 與 `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml` 僅能保存 portable setup policy。Executable project configuration 會綁定 canonical Git common directory 與 exact content hash；hash 改變後必須重新信任。
146	
147	- `dev start --focus` 會在 non-JSON creation 後 activate runtime。
148	- `dev start --run '<shell command>'` 只會 dispatch 到本次新建 first-class Herdr
149	  worktree 的 exact root pane。它不能與 `--json`、non-worktree modes 或 non-Herdr
150	  runtimes 併用，也不等待 command exit。
151	- TUI navigation 會拒絕開啟 checkout 不存在的 COLD task，並要求使用 `dev resume`。
152	- `DEV_TUI_TRACE` 從 `cli.Execute` 起算，無法涵蓋 OS process loading。`tui.initial_view_returned` 量測 model construction，不是 renderer flush 或 physical terminal paint；它適合同 profile 比較，不是跨硬體／network 的 universal guarantee。
153	- Runtime handle 現在保存 backend provenance，cleanup 前會重新驗證。

156	- `dev done` 在省略 `--ff`/`--pr` 且為 TTY 時會開啟 interactive finish wizard，把 dirty checkout 拿去跟 base 比較（commit、discard 或 cancel），不再直接拒絕任何 uncommitted change；non-interactive caller 仍須明確傳入 `--dirty` policy，且 destructive discard 需要 `--yes`。
157	- Human-readable output 現在具備 semantic color（`--color auto|always|never`），在 `NO_COLOR` 已設定、`TERM=dumb`，或 stdout/stderr 不是 terminal 時會自動停用。
158	- `dev done` 只記錄 MERGED：它不會關閉呼叫端 runtime、移除 worktree 或刪除 branch。Cleanup 已移交 `dev retire`，後者必須從目標 workspace 之外執行，會拒絕 active agent 與 mixed-purpose workspace，並在每次關閉 runtime 之後重新驗證 Git state。`dev done --delete-branch` 現在會直接報錯並指向 `dev retire --delete-branch`，`--keep-worktree` 則以 no-op 警告。

170	- `dev version` 會回報目前執行的 build 是否為已發布的 release，`dev doctor` 也帶有同一行資訊，並顯示 install owner、呼叫／解析後的 executable 路徑，以及 `PATH` 上不同 `dev` 副本的警告。先前工具中沒有任何地方能回答「我是不是最新的？」，而 `go install ...@latest` 只會解析到最新的 tag，因此未 tag 的 feature 對安裝者而言等同不存在。

172	- Release 會在 Unix `.tar.gz` 之外一併發布 Windows `.zip`、更新附在 release 上的 in-repo Scoop manifest（設定 token 時也會 push 到 bucket），並把對應的 source formula 發布到 `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`。Homebrew 發布是必要的 release step；repository token 缺失或被拒絕時會明確讓 job 失敗。Manual workflow 可為既有 stable release retry 或 backfill formula，不會建立或移動 tag。
173	- `dev upgrade` 會下載此平台目前的 release、以 release `SHA256SUMS` 驗證，再以 atomic rename 取代執行中的 binary（Windows 會把 live `.exe` 移到旁邊，下次執行時清除）。若 Homebrew、Scoop 或 `go install` 擁有該檔案，則偵測並執行對應指令；Homebrew 使用者透過自動推進的 tap 收到 release，不會就地覆寫 Cellar binary。
174	- Interactive `dev` command 每天最多印一行 dim 的「有新版」提示，來源是一天內的 release cache，永不因網路而 block。TUI 的 stale-cache background refresh 只會在 initial view return 後啟動。`[update] check = false` 或 `DEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` 可停用。

36	## High-value structured interfaces
37	
38	```bash
39	dev ls --json
40	dev repo list --json
41	dev repo context [repo]
42	dev repo remote --json
43	dev repo new NAME --json
44	dev repo clone <ref> --json
45	dev repo setup [repo-or-path] --preset PRESET --json
46	dev note list [repo] --json
47	dev note search <query> --json
48	dev note show <note-id> --json
49	dev pr list --json
50	dev prompt list --json
51	dev prompt render <pr-triage|session-close|workspace-closeout>
52	dev bootstrap --json
53	```
54	
55	Prefer JSON or the agent-ready Markdown context over parsing human tables. Tables are optimized for terminals and may change columns/width without changing the structured contract.
56	
57	Every `dev repo list --json` row includes `notes.count`. When a latest note exists, the same object adds `notes.latest_id`, `notes.latest_preview`, and `notes.latest_updated`; these optional fields are omitted when the count is zero. `dev note list --json` and `dev note search --json` return arrays of complete note records, while `dev note show --json` returns one complete record.
58	
59	### Pull-request schema and effective scope
60	
61	`dev pr list --json` emits an object with `schema_version: 1`, `generated_at`,
62	`scope`, `state`, `roles`, optional normalized `repositories`, provider readiness,
63	`warnings`, and `pull_requests`. Partial role/provider failures appear in
64	`warnings` even when useful rows are still returned. `scope` is the surface that actually ran: requesting
65	merged/closed/all from account or all narrows collection to local, and JSON says
66	`"local"`. `--repo` filters account rows as well as local query targets.
67	Personal local inventory may make one paginated query per repository for each
68	requested role (author and reviewer by default). Every row carries its provider
69	`host`; a local enterprise remote whose host differs from `GH_HOST`/`GITLAB_HOST`
70	is reported rather than queried against the wrong endpoint. Full GitHub rows also carry
71	optional `head_repo` and `is_cross_repository`; local evidence joins against the
72	source repository, and a deleted/unknown source never falls back to an unrelated
73	target-repository branch with the same name.
74	
75	A request's optional `local` object distinguishes task intent from live checkout
76	health. It carries `expected_branch`, observed `live_branch`, and independent
77	`branch_checked_out`, `checkout_exists`, `worktree_registered`, and
78	`status_available` booleans, plus optional `status_error`. Optional `git` appears
79	only when the expected branch was actually proven checked out and status was
80	available; it contains `dirty`, `ahead`, `behind`, and optional `upstream`.
81	Missing/cold/unregistered status therefore cannot look clean through zero values.
82	Schema 1 is add-only.
83	
84	### Prompt recipes and structured behavior
85	
86	`dev prompt list --json` returns sorted recipe metadata (`name`, `summary`,
87	`scope`, optional `target_usage`, and `context_version`). The three recipes are
88	`pr-triage`, `session-close`, and `workspace-closeout`.
89	
90	`dev prompt render <recipe>` prints a Markdown prompt whose JSON envelope has
91	`schema_version: 1`, recipe/context versions, generation time, host, scope,
92	optional target, capabilities, warnings, and recipe context. Collection is
93	read-only and missing evidence stays explicit.
94	
95	`dev prompt agents [--json]` is the sorted, redacted profile inventory. Human
96	output has `PROFILE DEFAULT RUN OPEN DESCRIPTION`; direct launchers expose only
97	the executable basename, shell launchers say `shell`, and unavailable modes say
98	`—`. Every JSON object has `name`, `description`, `default`, and nested
99	`run`/`open` objects containing `configured`, `kind` (`command|shell|none`), and
100	`executable`. Neither form emits argv, shell source, executable directories,
101	environment, prompt text, or config path.
102	
103	| Command | Process contract |
104	|---|---|
105	| `dev prompt run <recipe> [--agent NAME] [--dry-run]` | Resolve the global profile and its run launcher before collection; then run one batch process with no user stdin, stdin/file/argv prompt transport, and a 10-minute default timeout. |
106	| `dev prompt open <recipe> [--agent NAME] [--dry-run]` | Resolve the global profile/open launcher and check the non-dry TTY before collection; then run one foreground process with file/argv prompt transport and no default timeout. |
107	
108	`--agent` wins, otherwise the unique configured default wins, otherwise the sole
109	agent wins. Multiple agents with no default fail as ambiguous. Selection is not
110	mode-local: a selected profile missing the requested mode fails without using a
111	different profile. Diagnostics list sorted mode-capable profiles and point to
112	`dev prompt agents`. Dynamic completion loads parsed `--config`, filters names by
113	run/open capability, sanitizes descriptions through the shared completion
114	format, and degrades invalid config to no candidates plus no file completion.
115	Dry-run shows the resolved mode, cwd, transport, timeout, safe command markers,
116	and complete prompt, and starts nothing. Real launches in a checkout remain
117	subject to the writer-occupancy guard after collection supplies the cwd. `dev`
118	never parses a reply, starts an agent loop, changes permissions, or treats advice
119	as lifecycle authorization. `open` never creates, focuses, or reuses a
120	Herdr/tmux/Zellij surface; inside Herdr it remains in the current pane. See
121	[Prompt handoffs](../guides/prompt-handoffs.md).

123	## Repository bootstrap
124	
125	Repository setup remains separate from acquisition. For acquisition,
126	`new`/`create` distinguishes a plain repository name from a clear clone
127	reference:
128	
129	| Command | Behavior |
130	|---|---|
131	| `dev repo new` | interactive wizard; its first field accepts either a new name or a clone reference |
132	| `dev repo new NAME` / `dev repo create NAME` | create a new local repository; a clear Git URL, local Git path, or owner/name instead routes to clone and preserves history/remote |
133	| `dev repo clone [owner/name\|url]` | clone into the configured destination, then optionally apply a preset; setup defaults off |
134	| `dev repo setup [repo-or-path]` | repeat-safely merge native initializers and preset files into an existing clean checkout; defaults to the current repository and does not commit unless requested |
135	
136	A clone-routed `new` retains the source `origin`; it therefore rejects
137	new-upstream creation flags. It also rejects `--template*`, whose explicit
138	meaning is “copy content into a fresh history.”
139	
140	Across these commands, controls include `--preset`, `--path`, typed input values through
141	`--set`, item selection through `--enable`/`--disable`, `--check-in
142	<auto|commit|stage|none>`, `--dry-run`, `--yes`, `--json`, and `--handoff
143	<stay|cd|open|start>`. `repo new` additionally accepts `--template`,
144	`--template-ref`, and `--template-subdir`. JSON mode is non-interactive and
145	never changes directory or opens a runtime. Dry-run performs no target
146	repository mutation; clone setup can only be planned in detail after the clone
147	exists. Use the generated reference below for each command's exact flag
148	availability.
149	
150	The wizard renders the selected scaffold and workflow summary before target
151	repository mutation. The built-in presets are:
152	
153	- `minimal`: `main`, README, and an initial commit; this preserves existing
154	  scripted `repo new NAME` behavior.
155	- `agent-ready`: extends `minimal` with common ignores, starter `AGENTS.md`,
156	  and project-scoped `.claude/settings.json` plus `.claude/plans/`.
157	  `agent-history-hygiene` and `project-knowledge-harness` are offered but are
158	  not selected silently. When selected, dev installs them and runs reviewed
159	  built-in initializers for their project surfaces before the initial commit;
160	  downloaded skill scripts are not executed for these built-ins. Matching
161	  skills with the same source and identical agent targets share one installer
162	  invocation, while their setup phases still run per skill. The history
163	  initializer creates `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and `.gitleaks.toml`, then
164	  ensures `.specstory/.gitignore` contains rules for SpecStory's `.project.json`
165	  and `statistics.json`, never the trackable `.specstory/history/` directory.
166	  Existing custom ignore content and its mode are preserved; only missing
167	  managed rules are appended.
168	
169	After preset selection, the new-repository wizard asks “Customize preset and
170	template options?” with a default of no. The ordinary `agent-ready` flow uses
171	its reviewed template, file, input, and skill defaults without presenting each
172	question. Answer yes—or provide customization flags—to expand those controls.
173	
174	Presets can add typed `string`, `bool`, and `choice` inputs, text templates,
175	hooks, and project skills. Hooks run in fixed `before_commit`, `after_commit`,
176	and `after_remote` phases. The safe hook form is an argv `command`; a shell
177	`run` is explicit, and only `interactive = true` loads an interactive shell.
178	Required failures stop later commit/remote steps; optional failures are
179	reported as warnings. Produced local files are retained for recovery. Native
180	initializers and preset files are repeat-safe; custom hooks and skill setup are
181	responsible for their own idempotency.
182	
183	### Snapshot templates
184	
185	`dev repo new NAME --template SOURCE` seeds a fresh repository from a content
186	snapshot. `SOURCE` may be a local directory/repository, Git URL, or owner/name.
187	For a Git source, `--template-ref` selects an arbitrary branch, tag, or commit;
188	`--template-subdir` selects a clean relative directory as the new repository
189	root. Without a ref, a local Git working tree includes existing tracked files
190	plus untracked files that are not ignored by Git; ignored build/cache content
191	is omitted. A non-Git directory snapshots its complete current tree.
192	
193	The new repository does not inherit source history or remotes. Dev excludes
194	every source `.git` entry, rejects traversal, symlinks and special files,
195	preserves regular-file modes, and validates the complete snapshot before
196	creating the destination. Snapshot files take precedence when the selected
197	scaffold would write the same path; the scaffold still fills missing files and
198	runs the selected initializers. Source and destination traversal is performed
199	relative to held `os.Root` handles, and file bytes come from the already-open
200	validated source handle rather than a second mutable pathname lookup.
201	
202	Confirmation and human dry-run output show a bounded preview of selected paths
203	and warn when a local source is a live working-tree/directory snapshot rather
204	than a commit. Credential-bearing URL userinfo is removed from summaries,
205	structured output, and clone/template errors.
206	
207	Presets expose the same operation through scalar `template`, `template_ref`,
208	and `template_subdir` fields. They inherit normally and explicit CLI flags win,
209	which supports one starter catalog repository plus a child preset for each
210	subfolder.
211	
212	### Check-in policy
213	
214	The interactive wizard offers `commit`, `stage`, and `none`; scripts may also
215	pass `auto`. The behavior is:
216	
217	| Value | Behavior |
218	|---|---|
219	| `commit` | `git add -A`, commit with `--message`/the preset message, then run `after_commit` setup |
220	| `stage` | run `before_commit` setup, then `git add -A`; leave the checkout staged and do not run `after_commit` |
```

173	
174	`dev repo new NAME --template SOURCE` 會用 content snapshot 建立全新 repository。

181	新 repository 不會繼承 source history 或 remotes。Dev 會排除每個 source `.git`
182	entry、拒絕 traversal、symlink 與 special files、保留 regular-file modes，並在建立

184	snapshot 優先；scaffold 仍會補齊缺少的 files 並執行 selected initializers。
185	Source 與 destination traversal 都相對於 held `os.Root` handles 進行；file bytes 來自

188	Confirmation 與 human dry-run output 會顯示 bounded selected-path preview；local source
189	若是 live working-tree/directory snapshot 而非 commit，也會明確 warning。含 credential

196	### Check-in policy
197	
198	Interactive wizard 提供 `commit`、`stage`、`none`；script 也可傳 `auto`：
199	
200	| 值 | 行為 |
201	|---|---|
202	| `commit` | `git add -A`，以 `--message`／preset message commit，再執行 `after_commit` setup |
203	| `stage` | 執行 `before_commit` setup 後 `git add -A`；保留 staged checkout，不執行 `after_commit` |
204	| `none` | generated changes 保持 unstaged、uncommitted |
205	| `auto` | `repo new` 使用 `initial_check_in` 與相容的 `initial_commit`；clone/setup 則不自動 check-in |
206	
207	`stage` mode 會 best-effort 在正確的 worktree Git directory 寫入
208	`LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT`。[Lazygit v0.59.0 會讀取此
209	file](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/v0.59.0/pkg/gui/controllers/helpers/working_tree_helper.go#L191-L216)，並將它作為小寫 `c` 的 initial message；大寫
210	`C` 與 Git 本身不使用此 integration。不同內容的既有 draft 會保留並回報 warning，
211	不會被覆寫。這是 implementation-detail adapter，不是 `commit.template`。
212	
213	Staging 才是 durable outcome：optional lazygit draft 若無法寫入，dev 會發出 warning
214	並保留 staged index，不會 rollback。
215	
216	Staged setup 不能建立 upstream；`handoff=start` 也要求已 commit 的 setup，因為新
217	worktree 會漏掉 staged files。`stay`、`cd`、`open` 仍可供 review。`repo setup
218	--commit` 保留為 `--check-in=commit` 的 compatibility alias；`--message` 同時適用於
219	commit 與 stage。Structured result 保留 `committed`，並在適用時加入 `staged`、
220	`staged_paths`、`commit_message`、`commit_draft_provider` 與不含 file content 的
221	`template` summary。

225	提供 publishing 選項前，dev 會以 read-only 方式 probe `gh` 與 `glab`。只有 CLI 已

227	指引。預設 local-only，新 publish 的 repository 預設 private。
228	
229	Publishing 會沿用 local repository name 與 configured description，再詢問 provider
230	namespace/owner、visibility，以及是否 push initial/current branch。Dev 會在必要的

commit 694cb70120bf475a790e926afdeff02d3bf26851
Author: Da-Wei Lee <daviddwlee84@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Sep 2 01:03:30 2026 +0800

    feat: add a pull-request inbox and agent handoff
    
    Opening a PR ends a worktree's useful life, but nothing told you that.
    `dev pr list` combines the requests you opened with the ones awaiting your
    review and joins each to the local worktree for its head branch, so a
    checkout that is done becomes visible instead of accumulating.
    
    The two provider surfaces are kept distinct because they answer different
    questions: an account-wide search costs two calls regardless of repository
    count but cannot report a head branch, review decision or checks, while a
    per-repository listing can. `--scope` selects between them, `detail` on
    each row records which produced it, and per-repository queries stay
    limited to repositories dev has a task for unless `--all-repos` widens
    them. `--actions` and `--json` emit the gh/glab commands; dev prints them
    and never runs them.
    
    `dev pr prompt [triage|review|retire]` renders a prompt around the live
    queue and, with `--agent`, hands it to a command from the new `[[agent]]`
    section. There is no built-in agent and no default entry: dev starts a
    command you define, streams its output, and neither reads the reply nor
    iterates. `[[agent]]` is host configuration and is rejected in a
    repository's `.dev-cli/config.toml`.
    
    `forge.PRLister` is an optional capability following the RepoPublisher
    precedent, implemented for gh and glab; the az adapter declines it by
    omission so Azure targets report as unsupported rather than failing.
    
    Signed-out provider CLIs no longer leak their full command line into the
    TUI REMOTE footer, `dev repo remote` warnings or the cached provider
    status; a rejected credential now names the login command instead. Rate
    limits, permission and network failures keep their diagnostic text,
    because signing in again would not fix them. `dev doctor` reports whether
    gh and glab are signed in, not only whether they are installed.
    
    TODO.md records what deliberately stayed out: persisting PR identity and
    squash proof, forge-derived retirement suggestions, Azure inventory,
    GitLab pipeline status, and date-range filtering for aged requests.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011Biw72AjYU94SyosaNCrts

commit 4167d17df4a38359d6451c223f4d755e17383093
Author: Da-Wei Lee <daviddwlee84@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Sep 2 00:57:43 2026 +0800

    fix: skip exited zellij sessions
    
    Zellij keeps an exited session resurrectable in its namespace, and
    `list-sessions --short` still prints it. The Zellij adapter dumped each
    listed session's layout to read its cwd, and `action dump-layout` against
    an exited session fails with "There is no active session!", which aborted
    the entire listing. Every consumer of runtime.List under the zellij
    backend inherited that error: `dev ls`, `dev doctor`, sweep, retire
    safety checks and the TUI runtime join.
    
    List now parses the long `list-sessions --no-formatting` output, splits
    live sessions from EXITED ones, and describes only the live ones, so a
    dead session neither errors nor inflates the runtime view. A dump-layout
    that reports no active session is tolerated as a session dying mid-listing
    rather than failing the listing.
    
    Open had a latent hole this exposed: an exited session still owns its
    name, so `attach --create-background` would resurrect its old layout at
    the old cwd while reporting a fresh session at the requested directory.
    It now fails closed with the delete-session/attach recovery commands.
    Close reads live names directly, so a stale handle is a no-op.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011Biw72AjYU94SyosaNCrts

OBJECTIVE:
Perform a security-focused code review to identify HIGH-CONFIDENCE security vulnerabilities that could have real exploitation potential. This is not a general code review - focus ONLY on security implications newly added by this PR. Do not comment on existing security concerns.

CRITICAL INSTRUCTIONS:
1. MINIMIZE FALSE POSITIVES: Only flag issues where you're >80% confident of actual exploitability
2. AVOID NOISE: Skip theoretical issues, style concerns, or low-impact findings
3. FOCUS ON IMPACT: Prioritize vulnerabilities that could lead to unauthorized access, data breaches, or system compromise
4. EXCLUSIONS: Do NOT report the following issue types:
   - Denial of Service (DOS) vulnerabilities, even if they allow service disruption
   - Secrets or sensitive data stored on disk (these are handled by other processes)
   - Rate limiting or resource exhaustion issues

SECURITY CATEGORIES TO EXAMINE:

**Input Validation Vulnerabilities:**
- SQL injection via unsanitized user input
- Command injection in system calls or subprocesses
- XXE injection in XML parsing
- Template injection in templating engines
- NoSQL injection in database queries
- Path traversal in file operations

**Authentication & Authorization Issues:**
- Authentication bypass logic
- Privilege escalation paths
- Session management flaws
- JWT token vulnerabilities
- Authorization logic bypasses

**Crypto & Secrets Management:**
- Hardcoded API keys, passwords, or tokens
- Weak cryptographic algorithms or implementations
- Improper key storage or management
- Cryptographic randomness issues
- Certificate validation bypasses

**Injection & Code Execution:**
- Remote code execution via deseralization
- Pickle injection in Python
- YAML deserialization vulnerabilities
- Eval injection in dynamic code execution
- XSS vulnerabilities in web applications (reflected, stored, DOM-based)

**Data Exposure:**
- Sensitive data logging or storage
- PII handling violations
- API endpoint data leakage
- Debug information exposure

Additional notes:
- Even if something is only exploitable from the local network, it can still be a HIGH severity issue

ANALYSIS METHODOLOGY:

Phase 1 - Repository Context Research (Use file search tools):
- Identify existing security frameworks and libraries in use
- Look for established secure coding patterns in the codebase
- Examine existing sanitization and validation patterns
- Understand the project's security model and threat model

Phase 2 - Comparative Analysis:
- Compare new code changes against existing security patterns
- Identify deviations from established secure practices
- Look for inconsistent security implementations
- Flag code that introduces new attack surfaces

Phase 3 - Vulnerability Assessment:
- Examine each modified file for security implications
- Trace data flow from user inputs to sensitive operations
- Look for privilege boundaries being crossed unsafely
- Identify injection points and unsafe deserialization

REQUIRED OUTPUT FORMAT:

You MUST output your findings in markdown. The markdown output should contain the file, line number, severity, category (e.g. `sql_injection` or `xss`), description, exploit scenario, and fix recommendation.

For example:

# Vuln 1: XSS: `foo.py:42`

* Severity: High
* Description: User input from `username` parameter is directly interpolated into HTML without escaping, allowing reflected XSS attacks
* Exploit Scenario: Attacker crafts URL like /bar?q=<script>alert(document.cookie)</script> to execute JavaScript in victim's browser, enabling session hijacking or data theft
* Recommendation: Use Flask's escape() function or Jinja2 templates with auto-escaping enabled for all user inputs rendered in HTML

SEVERITY GUIDELINES:
- **HIGH**: Directly exploitable vulnerabilities leading to RCE, data breach, or authentication bypass
- **MEDIUM**: Vulnerabilities requiring specific conditions but with significant impact
- **LOW**: Defense-in-depth issues or lower-impact vulnerabilities

CONFIDENCE SCORING:
- 0.9-1.0: Certain exploit path identified, tested if possible
- 0.8-0.9: Clear vulnerability pattern with known exploitation methods
- 0.7-0.8: Suspicious pattern requiring specific conditions to exploit
- Below 0.7: Don't report (too speculative)

FINAL REMINDER:
Focus on HIGH and MEDIUM findings only. Better to miss some theoretical issues than flood the report with false positives. Each finding should be something a security engineer would confidently raise in a PR review.

FALSE POSITIVE FILTERING:

> You do not need to run commands to reproduce the vulnerability, just read the code to determine if it is a real vulnerability. Do not use the bash tool or write to any files.
>
> HARD EXCLUSIONS - Automatically exclude findings matching these patterns:
> 1. Denial of Service (DOS) vulnerabilities or resource exhaustion attacks.
> 2. Secrets or credentials stored on disk if they are otherwise secured.
> 3. Rate limiting concerns or service overload scenarios.
> 4. Memory consumption or CPU exhaustion issues.
> 5. Lack of input validation on non-security-critical fields without proven security impact.
> 6. Input sanitization concerns for GitHub Action workflows unless they are clearly triggerable via untrusted input.
> 7. A lack of hardening measures. Code is not expected to implement all security best practices, only flag concrete vulnerabilities.
> 8. Race conditions or timing attacks that are theoretical rather than practical issues. Only report a race condition if it is concretely problematic.
> 9. Vulnerabilities related to outdated third-party libraries. These are managed separately and should not be reported here.
> 10. Memory safety issues such as buffer overflows or use-after-free-vulnerabilities are impossible in rust. Do not report memory safety issues in rust or any other memory safe languages.
> 11. Files that are only unit tests or only used as part of running tests.
> 12. Log spoofing concerns. Outputting un-sanitized user input to logs is not a vulnerability.
> 13. SSRF vulnerabilities that only control the path. SSRF is only a concern if it can control the host or protocol.
> 14. Including user-controlled content in AI system prompts is not a vulnerability.
> 15. Regex injection. Injecting untrusted content into a regex is not a vulnerability.
> 16. Regex DOS concerns.
> 16. Insecure documentation. Do not report any findings in documentation files such as markdown files.
> 17. A lack of audit logs is not a vulnerability.
>
> PRECEDENTS -
> 1. Logging high value secrets in plaintext is a vulnerability. Logging URLs is assumed to be safe.
> 2. UUIDs can be assumed to be unguessable and do not need to be validated.
> 3. Environment variables and CLI flags are trusted values. Attackers are generally not able to modify them in a secure environment. Any attack that relies on controlling an environment variable is invalid.
> 4. Resource management issues such as memory or file descriptor leaks are not valid.
> 5. Subtle or low impact web vulnerabilities such as tabnabbing, XS-Leaks, prototype pollution, and open redirects should not be reported unless they are extremely high confidence.
> 6. React and Angular are generally secure against XSS. These frameworks do not need to sanitize or escape user input unless it is using dangerouslySetInnerHTML, bypassSecurityTrustHtml, or similar methods. Do not report XSS vulnerabilities in React or Angular components or tsx files unless they are using unsafe methods.
> 7. Most vulnerabilities in github action workflows are not exploitable in practice. Before validating a github action workflow vulnerability ensure it is concrete and has a very specific attack path.
> 8. A lack of permission checking or authentication in client-side JS/TS code is not a vulnerability. Client-side code is not trusted and does not need to implement these checks, they are handled on the server-side. The same applies to all flows that send untrusted data to the backend, the backend is responsible for validating and sanitizing all inputs.
> 9. Only include MEDIUM findings if they are obvious and concrete issues.
> 10. Most vulnerabilities in ipython notebooks (*.ipynb files) are not exploitable in practice. Before validating a notebook vulnerability ensure it is concrete and has a very specific attack path where untrusted input can trigger the vulnerability.
> 11. Logging non-PII data is not a vulnerability even if the data may be sensitive. Only report logging vulnerabilities if they expose sensitive information such as secrets, passwords, or personally identifiable information (PII).
> 12. Command injection vulnerabilities in shell scripts are generally not exploitable in practice since shell scripts generally do not run with untrusted user input. Only report command injection vulnerabilities in shell scripts if they are concrete and have a very specific attack path for untrusted input.
>
> SIGNAL QUALITY CRITERIA - For remaining findings, assess:
> 1. Is there a concrete, exploitable vulnerability with a clear attack path?
> 2. Does this represent a real security risk vs theoretical best practice?
> 3. Are there specific code locations and reproduction steps?
> 4. Would this finding be actionable for a security team?
>
> For each finding, assign a confidence score from 1-10:
> - 1-3: Low confidence, likely false positive or noise
> - 4-6: Medium confidence, needs investigation
> - 7-10: High confidence, likely true vulnerability

START ANALYSIS:

Begin your analysis now. Do this in 3 steps:

1. Use a sub-task to identify vulnerabilities. Use the repository exploration tools to understand the codebase context, then analyze the PR changes for security implications. In the prompt for this sub-task, include all of the above.
2. Then for each vulnerability identified by the above sub-task, create a new sub-task to filter out false-positives. Launch these sub-tasks as parallel sub-tasks. In the prompt for these sub-tasks, include everything in the "FALSE POSITIVE FILTERING" instructions.
3. Filter out any vulnerabilities where the sub-task reported a confidence less than 8.

Your final reply must contain the markdown report and nothing else.

commit 694cb70120bf475a790e926afdeff02d3bf26851
Author: Da-Wei Lee <daviddwlee84@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Sep 2 01:03:30 2026 +0800

    feat: add a pull-request inbox and agent handoff
    
    Opening a PR ends a worktree's useful life, but nothing told you that.
    `dev pr list` combines the requests you opened with the ones awaiting your
    review and joins each to the local worktree for its head branch, so a
    checkout that is done becomes visible instead of accumulating.
    
    The two provider surfaces are kept distinct because they answer different
    questions: an account-wide search costs two calls regardless of repository
    count but cannot report a head branch, review decision or checks, while a
    per-repository listing can. `--scope` selects between them, `detail` on
    each row records which produced it, and per-repository queries stay
    limited to repositories dev has a task for unless `--all-repos` widens
    them. `--actions` and `--json` emit the gh/glab commands; dev prints them
    and never runs them.
    
    `dev pr prompt [triage|review|retire]` renders a prompt around the live
    queue and, with `--agent`, hands it to a command from the new `[[agent]]`
    section. There is no built-in agent and no default entry: dev starts a
    command you define, streams its output, and neither reads the reply nor
    iterates. `[[agent]]` is host configuration and is rejected in a
    repository's `.dev-cli/config.toml`.
    
    `forge.PRLister` is an optional capability following the RepoPublisher
    precedent, implemented for gh and glab; the az adapter declines it by
    omission so Azure targets report as unsupported rather than failing.
    
    Signed-out provider CLIs no longer leak their full command line into the
    TUI REMOTE footer, `dev repo remote` warnings or the cached provider
    status; a rejected credential now names the login command instead. Rate
    limits, permission and network failures keep their diagnostic text,
    because signing in again would not fix them. `dev doctor` reports whether
    gh and glab are signed in, not only whether they are installed.
    
    TODO.md records what deliberately stayed out: persisting PR identity and
    squash proof, forge-derived retirement suggestions, Azure inventory,
    GitLab pipeline status, and date-range filtering for aged requests.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011Biw72AjYU94SyosaNCrts

commit 4167d17df4a38359d6451c223f4d755e17383093
Author: Da-Wei Lee <daviddwlee84@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Sep 2 00:57:43 2026 +0800

    fix: skip exited zellij sessions
    
    Zellij keeps an exited session resurrectable in its namespace, and
    `list-sessions --short` still prints it. The Zellij adapter dumped each
    listed session's layout to read its cwd, and `action dump-layout` against
    an exited session fails with "There is no active session!", which aborted
    the entire listing. Every consumer of runtime.List under the zellij
    backend inherited that error: `dev ls`, `dev doctor`, sweep, retire
    safety checks and the TUI runtime join.
    
    List now parses the long `list-sessions --no-formatting` output, splits
    live sessions from EXITED ones, and describes only the live ones, so a
    dead session neither errors nor inflates the runtime view. A dump-layout
    that reports no active session is tolerated as a session dying mid-listing
    rather than failing the listing.
    
    Open had a latent hole this exposed: an exited session still owns its
    name, so `attach --create-background` would resurrect its old layout at
    the old cwd while reporting a fresh session at the requested directory.
    It now fails closed with the delete-session/attach recovery commands.
    Close reads live names directly, so a stale handle is a no-op.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011Biw72AjYU94SyosaNCrts

OBJECTIVE:
Perform a security-focused code review to identify HIGH-CONFIDENCE security vulnerabilities that could have real exploitation potential. This is not a general code review - focus ONLY on security implications newly added by this PR. Do not comment on existing security concerns.

CRITICAL INSTRUCTIONS:
1. MINIMIZE FALSE POSITIVES: Only flag issues where you're >80% confident of actual exploitability
2. AVOID NOISE: Skip theoretical issues, style concerns, or low-impact findings
3. FOCUS ON IMPACT: Prioritize vulnerabilities that could lead to unauthorized access, data breaches, or system compromise
4. EXCLUSIONS: Do NOT report the following issue types:
   - Denial of Service (DOS) vulnerabilities, even if they allow service disruption
   - Secrets or sensitive data stored on disk (these are handled by other processes)
   - Rate limiting or resource exhaustion issues

SECURITY CATEGORIES TO EXAMINE:

**Input Validation Vulnerabilities:**
- SQL injection via unsanitized user input
- Command injection in system calls or subprocesses
- XXE injection in XML parsing
- Template injection in templating engines
- NoSQL injection in database queries
- Path traversal in file operations

**Authentication & Authorization Issues:**
- Authentication bypass logic
- Privilege escalation paths
- Session management flaws
- JWT token vulnerabilities
- Authorization logic bypasses

**Crypto & Secrets Management:**
- Hardcoded API keys, passwords, or tokens
- Weak cryptographic algorithms or implementations
- Improper key storage or management
- Cryptographic randomness issues
- Certificate validation bypasses

**Injection & Code Execution:**
- Remote code execution via deseralization
- Pickle injection in Python
- YAML deserialization vulnerabilities
- Eval injection in dynamic code execution
- XSS vulnerabilities in web applications (reflected, stored, DOM-based)

**Data Exposure:**
- Sensitive data logging or storage
- PII handling violations
- API endpoint data leakage
- Debug information exposure

Additional notes:
- Even if something is only exploitable from the local network, it can still be a HIGH severity issue

ANALYSIS METHODOLOGY:

Phase 1 - Repository Context Research (Use file search tools):
- Identify existing security frameworks and libraries in use
- Look for established secure coding patterns in the codebase
- Examine existing sanitization and validation patterns
- Understand the project's security model and threat model

Phase 2 - Comparative Analysis:
- Compare new code changes against existing security patterns
- Identify deviations from established secure practices
- Look for inconsistent security implementations
- Flag code that introduces new attack surfaces

Phase 3 - Vulnerability Assessment:
- Examine each modified file for security implications
- Trace data flow from user inputs to sensitive operations
- Look for privilege boundaries being crossed unsafely
- Identify injection points and unsafe deserialization

REQUIRED OUTPUT FORMAT:

You MUST output your findings in markdown. The markdown output should contain the file, line number, severity, category (e.g. `sql_injection` or `xss`), description, exploit scenario, and fix recommendation.

For example:

# Vuln 1: XSS: `foo.py:42`

* Severity: High
* Description: User input from `username` parameter is directly interpolated into HTML without escaping, allowing reflected XSS attacks
* Exploit Scenario: Attacker crafts URL like /bar?q=<script>alert(document.cookie)</script> to execute JavaScript in victim's browser, enabling session hijacking or data theft
* Recommendation: Use Flask's escape() function or Jinja2 templates with auto-escaping enabled for all user inputs rendered in HTML

SEVERITY GUIDELINES:
- **HIGH**: Directly exploitable vulnerabilities leading to RCE, data breach, or authentication bypass
- **MEDIUM**: Vulnerabilities requiring specific conditions but with significant impact
- **LOW**: Defense-in-depth issues or lower-impact vulnerabilities

CONFIDENCE SCORING:
- 0.9-1.0: Certain exploit path identified, tested if possible
- 0.8-0.9: Clear vulnerability pattern with known exploitation methods
- 0.7-0.8: Suspicious pattern requiring specific conditions to exploit
- Below 0.7: Don't report (too speculative)

FINAL REMINDER:
Focus on HIGH and MEDIUM findings only. Better to miss some theoretical issues than flood the report with false positives. Each finding should be something a security engineer would confidently raise in a PR review.

FALSE POSITIVE FILTERING:

> You do not need to run commands to reproduce the vulnerability, just read the code to determine if it is a real vulnerability. Do not use the bash tool or write to any files.
>
> HARD EXCLUSIONS - Automatically exclude findings matching these patterns:
> 1. Denial of Service (DOS) vulnerabilities or resource exhaustion attacks.
> 2. Secrets or credentials stored on disk if they are otherwise secured.
> 3. Rate limiting concerns or service overload scenarios.
> 4. Memory consumption or CPU exhaustion issues.
> 5. Lack of input validation on non-security-critical fields without proven security impact.
> 6. Input sanitization concerns for GitHub Action workflows unless they are clearly triggerable via untrusted input.
> 7. A lack of hardening measures. Code is not expected to implement all security best practices, only flag concrete vulnerabilities.
> 8. Race conditions or timing attacks that are theoretical rather than practical issues. Only report a race condition if it is concretely problematic.
> 9. Vulnerabilities related to outdated third-party libraries. These are managed separately and should not be reported here.
> 10. Memory safety issues such as buffer overflows or use-after-free-vulnerabilities are impossible in rust. Do not report memory safety issues in rust or any other memory safe languages.
> 11. Files that are only unit tests or only used as part of running tests.
> 12. Log spoofing concerns. Outputting un-sanitized user input to logs is not a vulnerability.
> 13. SSRF vulnerabilities that only control the path. SSRF is only a concern if it can control the host or protocol.
> 14. Including user-controlled content in AI system prompts is not a vulnerability.
> 15. Regex injection. Injecting untrusted content into a regex is not a vulnerability.
> 16. Regex DOS concerns.
> 16. Insecure documentation. Do not report any findings in documentation files such as markdown files.
> 17. A lack of audit logs is not a vulnerability.
>
> PRECEDENTS -
> 1. Logging high value secrets in plaintext is a vulnerability. Logging URLs is assumed to be safe.
> 2. UUIDs can be assumed to be unguessable and do not need to be validated.
> 3. Environment variables and CLI flags are trusted values. Attackers are generally not able to modify them in a secure environment. Any attack that relies on controlling an environment variable is invalid.
> 4. Resource management issues such as memory or file descriptor leaks are not valid.
> 5. Subtle or low impact web vulnerabilities such as tabnabbing, XS-Leaks, prototype pollution, and open redirects should not be reported unless they are extremely high confidence.
> 6. React and Angular are generally secure against XSS. These frameworks do not need to sanitize or escape user input unless it is using dangerouslySetInnerHTML, bypassSecurityTrustHtml, or similar methods. Do not report XSS vulnerabilities in React or Angular components or tsx files unless they are using unsafe methods.
> 7. Most vulnerabilities in github action workflows are not exploitable in practice. Before validating a github action workflow vulnerability ensure it is concrete and has a very specific attack path.
> 8. A lack of permission checking or authentication in client-side JS/TS code is not a vulnerability. Client-side code is not trusted and does not need to implement these checks, they are handled on the server-side. The same applies to all flows that send untrusted data to the backend, the backend is responsible for validating and sanitizing all inputs.
> 9. Only include MEDIUM findings if they are obvious and concrete issues.
> 10. Most vulnerabilities in ipython notebooks (*.ipynb files) are not exploitable in practice. Before validating a notebook vulnerability ensure it is concrete and has a very specific attack path where untrusted input can trigger the vulnerability.
> 11. Logging non-PII data is not a vulnerability even if the data may be sensitive. Only report logging vulnerabilities if they expose sensitive information such as secrets, passwords, or personally identifiable information (PII).
> 12. Command injection vulnerabilities in shell scripts are generally not exploitable in practice since shell scripts generally do not run with untrusted user input. Only report command injection vulnerabilities in shell scripts if they are concrete and have a very specific attack path for untrusted input.

> - 4-6: Medium confidence, needs investigation
> - 7-10: High confidence, likely true vulnerability

170	func suggestFor(app *App, ctx context.Context, r inventory.Row, stale time.Duration, retireOptions sweepRetireOptions) []suggestion {
171		t := r.Task
172		var out []suggestion
173	
174		// A task whose repository is gone cannot be finished, resumed, parked or
175		// retired: every one of those resolves the repository first, and `dev done`
176		// refuses outright once the checkout is missing. Nothing else in this
177		// function reaches it either — the dead-branch rule below excludes direct
178		// mode, and the stale-worktree rule needs a recorded worktree path. Left
179		// alone, the record is unreachable by any command in the binary.
180		//
181		// Reaping removes dev's record of intent and nothing else; the branch, the
182		// commits and the remote are untouched. A live session proves the directory
183		// is there, so it is the one condition that rules this out.
184		if t.RepoPath != "" && !r.Live() && !dirExists(t.RepoPath) {
185			out = append(out, suggestion{
186				row:    r,
187				reason: fmt.Sprintf("repository %s no longer exists", config.Contract(t.RepoPath)),
188				action: fmt.Sprintf("reap the task entry %s (Git keeps any work; this drops only dev's record)", t.ID),
189				apply:  func() error { return app.Tasks.Delete(t.ID) },
190			})
191			return out
192		}
193	
194		out = append(out, orphanSuggestions(app, r)...)
195	
196		switch {
197		// A hot task with no live session is the commonest drift: the session was
198		// closed (or the machine rebooted) without parking.
199		case t.State == task.Hot && !r.Live():
200			out = append(out, suggestion{
201				row:    r,
202				reason: fmt.Sprintf("hot but no live session, idle %s", humanAge(r.Age())),
203				action: fmt.Sprintf("mark %s warm", t.ID),
204				apply: func() error {
205					t.State = task.Warm
206					return app.Tasks.Save(t)
207				},
208			})
209	
210		// A warm task nobody has touched in weeks is a candidate for cold: keeping
211		// the worktree costs disk and clutters every listing.
212		case t.State == task.Warm && r.Age() > stale:
213			reason := fmt.Sprintf("warm and untouched for %s", humanAge(r.Age()))
214			if r.Status.Dirty() {
215				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + ", but has uncommitted work",
216					action: "commit or `dev park --wip` before going cold — not changed automatically"})
217				break
218			}
219			if !r.Status.Synced() {
220				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + fmt.Sprintf(", not pushed (%s)", r.Status.Summary()),

222				break
223			}
224			out = append(out, suggestion{
225				row:    r,
226				reason: reason + ", clean and pushed",
227				action: fmt.Sprintf("go cold: remove %s (branch and remote keep the work)", config.Contract(r.Checkout)),
228				apply: func() error {
229					if t.WorktreePath != "" {
230						if err := ensureArtifactsFinalized(app, t.WorktreePath); err != nil {
231							return err
232						}
233						if err := safeRemoveWorktree(ctx, runtimeForTask(app, t), t.RepoPath, t.WorktreePath,
234							false, false, false, 5*time.Second); err != nil {
235							return err
236						}
237						t.WorktreePath = ""
238					}
239					t.State = task.Cold
240					clearTaskRuntime(t)
241					return app.Tasks.Save(t)
242				},
243			})
244	
245		// DONE means integrated; runtime/worktree cleanup is a separate,
246		// externally coordinated retirement step.
247		case t.State == task.Done:
248			action := fmt.Sprintf("retire runtime/worktree for %s", t.ID)
249			if retireOptions.deleteBranches && t.Branch != "" && t.Branch != t.Base {
250				action += fmt.Sprintf(" and delete %s", t.Branch)
251			}
252			out = append(out, suggestion{
253				row:    r,
254				reason: "merged, cleanup pending",
255				action: action,
256				apply: func() error {
257					if err := ensureArtifactsFinalized(app, checkoutOf(t)); err != nil {
258						return err
259					}
260					target, rt, err := retirementTargetForTask(ctx, app, t)
261					if err != nil {
262						return err
263					}
264					service := &retirement.Service{Runtime: rt, Tasks: app.Tasks}
265					_, err = service.Retire(ctx, retirement.Request{
266						Target: target,

269						},
270						DeleteBranch: retireOptions.deleteBranches,

273				},
274			})
275		}
276	
277		// A branch-backed task whose branch git no longer has is dead: the branch
278		// was deleted after integration, so the record holds intent for work that
279		// no longer exists anywhere. It cannot be finished, resumed, or retired,
280		// because every one of those paths resolves the branch first.

305					}

308						return err
309					}
310					t.WorktreePath = ""
311					clearTaskRuntime(t)

313				},
314			})
315		}
316	
317		// Drift that is independent of the lifecycle stage.
318		if r.WorktreeMissing && t.WorktreePath != "" {
319			wtPath := t.WorktreePath
320			out = append(out, suggestion{
321				row:    r,
322				reason: "records a worktree that git no longer knows about",
323				action: fmt.Sprintf("clear the stale worktree path %s", config.Contract(wtPath)),
324				apply: func() error {
325					if err := gitx.PruneWorktrees(ctx, t.RepoPath); err != nil {
326						return err
327					}
328					t.WorktreePath = ""

331					}

333				},
334			})
335		}
336		return out
337	}

339	// dirExists reports whether path is a directory that can be read right now.
340	func dirExists(path string) bool {
341		info, err := os.Stat(path)
342		return err == nil && info.IsDir()
343	}
