```text
1	---
2	description: Find the dev-cli command groups, generated exact flags, configuration layers, and stable automation surfaces.
3	authority: project
4	status: generated-plus-authored
5	verified_on: 2026-09-03
6	---
7	
8	# Commands and configuration
9	
10	Use the authored map for intent and the embedded generated reference for exact flags. The generated block comes from the binary's Cobra command tree and is checked by `dev skill sync --check`.
11	
12	## Command map
13	
14	| Goal | Commands |
15	|---|---|
16	| task lifecycle | `start`, `park`, `resume`, `done`, `retire`, `sweep`, `ls`, `status` |
17	| agent artifacts | `prepare`, `artifact finalize`, `artifact list`, `artifact discard` |
18	| guarded Git transactions | `git uncommit`, `git recommit`, `git pull-rebase`, `git amend-all`, `git setup` |
19	| linked worktrees | `wt list`, `wt create`, `wt open`, `wt rm`, `wt plan`, `wt provision` |
20	| repositories/remotes | `repo list`, `repo context`, `repo new`/`repo create`, `repo clone`, `repo setup`, `repo open`, `repo sync`, `repo remote`, `repo mark` |
21	| repository quick notes | `note add`, `note list`, `note show`, `note search`, `note edit`, `note delete`, `note path`, `note reindex` |
22	| machine inventory | `bootstrap`, `adopt`, `doctor` |
23	| experiments | `try`, `tries …`, `graduate` |
24	| terminal UI | `tui`, `tui tools` |
25	| configuration/shell | `config init/show/path/edit/trust`, `config scaffolds init/show/path/edit`, `shell-init`, completion |
26	| remote fleet | `fleet list`, `fleet status`, `fleet sync`, `fleet open`, `fleet config …` |
27	| pull-request inventory | `pr list` |
28	| prompt handoff | `prompt list`, `prompt agents`, `prompt render`, `prompt run`, `prompt open` |
29	| agent skills | `skill list`, `skill add`, `skill update`, `skill install`, `skill sync`, `skill print` |
30	| generated policy/assets | `gitignore`, `skill install/sync` |
31	| activity/data | `summary`, `journal`, `stats …`, `cache …` |
32	| help | `help [topic]` |
33	
34	Run `dev <command> --help` for the installed binary; this site describes the repository version identified in its freshness metadata.
35	
36	## High-value structured interfaces
37	
38	```bash
39	dev ls --json
40	dev repo list --json
41	dev repo context [repo]
42	dev repo remote --json
43	dev repo new NAME --json
44	dev repo clone <ref> --json
45	dev repo setup [repo-or-path] --preset PRESET --json
46	dev note list [repo] --json
47	dev note search <query> --json
48	dev note show <note-id> --json
49	dev pr list --json
50	dev prompt list --json
51	dev prompt render <pr-triage|session-close|workspace-closeout>
52	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --json
53	dev bootstrap --json
54	```
55	
56	Prefer JSON or the agent-ready Markdown context over parsing human tables. Tables are optimized for terminals and may change columns/width without changing the structured contract.
57	
58	Every `dev repo list --json` row includes `notes.count`. When a latest note exists, the same object adds `notes.latest_id`, `notes.latest_preview`, and `notes.latest_updated`; these optional fields are omitted when the count is zero. `dev note list --json` and `dev note search --json` return arrays of complete note records, while `dev note show --json` returns one complete record.
59	
60	### Pull-request schema and effective scope
61	
62	`dev pr list --json` emits an object with `schema_version: 1`, `generated_at`,
63	`scope`, `state`, `roles`, optional normalized `repositories`, provider readiness,
64	`warnings`, and `pull_requests`. Partial role/provider failures appear in
65	`warnings` even when useful rows are still returned. `scope` is the surface that actually ran: requesting
66	merged/closed/all from account or all narrows collection to local, and JSON says
67	`"local"`. `--repo` filters account rows as well as local query targets.
68	Personal local inventory may make one paginated query per repository for each
69	requested role (author and reviewer by default). Every row carries its provider
70	`host`; a local enterprise remote whose host differs from `GH_HOST`/`GITLAB_HOST`
71	is reported rather than queried against the wrong endpoint. Full GitHub rows also carry
72	optional `head_repo` and `is_cross_repository`; local evidence joins against the
73	source repository, and a deleted/unknown source never falls back to an unrelated
74	target-repository branch with the same name.
75	
76	A request's optional `local` object distinguishes task intent from live checkout
77	health. It carries `expected_branch`, observed `live_branch`, and independent
78	`branch_checked_out`, `checkout_exists`, `worktree_registered`, and
79	`status_available` booleans, plus optional `status_error`. Optional `git` appears
80	only when the expected branch was actually proven checked out and status was
81	available; it contains `dirty`, `ahead`, `behind`, and optional `upstream`.
82	Missing/cold/unregistered status therefore cannot look clean through zero values.
83	Schema 1 is add-only.
84	
85	### Ephemeral-worktree report and apply contract
86	
87	`dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --json` emits one object with
88	`schema_version: 1`, generation time, canonical repository/common-dir identity,
89	provider inactivity threshold, explicit-base/branch-deletion request, sorted
90	capabilities/diagnostics/candidates, and summary counts. Candidates contain only
91	validated provider/run/agent IDs, normalized states/times, worktree path/branch/
92	registry HEAD, live Git facts and counts, task/artifact/caller/runtime facts,
93	stable checks/classification, a separate branch-deletion audit, planned actions,
94	and one stable fingerprint. It never includes metadata filenames or prompt,
95	script, log, result-body, or transcript content. Empty collections are arrays and
96	schema 1 is add-only.
97	
98	The JSON form is report-only; `--json --apply` is rejected. Human apply requires
99	an interactive terminal and one confirmation per eligible candidate. It rejects
100	`--yes`, `--close-unknown`, `--assume-no-runtime`, and apply with `--no-runtime`.
101	`--stale-days` is provider inactivity (default 14, minimum 1), not commit age.
102	`--ephemeral-worktrees` and `--merged-worktrees` are mutually exclusive.
103	
104	Branches are retained by default, including branches with commits unique from a
105	base. `--delete-branches` requires `--apply` plus an explicit `--base`; the
106	candidate's branch action remains unsafe unless both tips resolve unchanged, the
107	branch is contained, and it has zero unique commits. Apply recollects all proof
108	under a common-dir lock and accepts only the same fingerprint. Results are
109	versioned internally as removed, partial, skipped-changed, or failed; branch
110	failure after worktree removal is partial and retains the branch.
111	
112	### Prompt recipes and structured behavior
113	
114	`dev prompt list --json` returns sorted recipe metadata (`name`, `summary`,
115	`scope`, optional `target_usage`, and `context_version`). The three recipes are
116	`pr-triage`, `session-close`, and `workspace-closeout`.
117	
118	`dev prompt render <recipe>` prints a Markdown prompt whose JSON envelope has
119	`schema_version: 1`, recipe/context versions, generation time, host, scope,
120	optional target, capabilities, warnings, and recipe context. Collection is
121	read-only and missing evidence stays explicit.
122	
123	`dev prompt agents [--json]` is the sorted, redacted profile inventory. Human
124	output has `PROFILE DEFAULT RUN OPEN DESCRIPTION`; direct launchers expose only
125	the executable basename, shell launchers say `shell`, and unavailable modes say
126	`—`. Every JSON object has `name`, `description`, `default`, and nested
127	`run`/`open` objects containing `configured`, `kind` (`command|shell|none`), and
128	`executable`. Neither form emits argv, shell source, executable directories,
129	environment, prompt text, or config path.
130	
131	| Command | Process contract |
132	|---|---|
133	| `dev prompt run <recipe> [--agent NAME] [--dry-run]` | Resolve the global profile and its run launcher before collection; then run one batch process with no user stdin, stdin/file/argv prompt transport, and a 10-minute default timeout. |
134	| `dev prompt open <recipe> [--agent NAME] [--dry-run]` | Resolve the global profile/open launcher and check the non-dry TTY before collection; then run one foreground process with file/argv prompt transport and no default timeout. |
135	
136	`--agent` wins, otherwise the unique configured default wins, otherwise the sole
137	agent wins. Multiple agents with no default fail as ambiguous. Selection is not
138	mode-local: a selected profile missing the requested mode fails without using a
139	different profile. Diagnostics list sorted mode-capable profiles and point to
140	`dev prompt agents`. Dynamic completion loads parsed `--config`, filters names by
141	run/open capability, sanitizes descriptions through the shared completion
142	format, and degrades invalid config to no candidates plus no file completion.
143	Dry-run shows the resolved mode, cwd, transport, timeout, safe command markers,
144	and complete prompt, and starts nothing. Real launches in a checkout remain
145	subject to the writer-occupancy guard after collection supplies the cwd. `dev`
146	never parses a reply, starts an agent loop, changes permissions, or treats advice
147	as lifecycle authorization. `open` never creates, focuses, or reuses a
148	Herdr/tmux/Zellij surface; inside Herdr it remains in the current pane. See
149	[Prompt handoffs](../guides/prompt-handoffs.md).
150	
151	## Repository bootstrap
152	
153	Repository setup remains separate from acquisition. For acquisition,
154	`new`/`create` distinguishes a plain repository name from a clear clone
155	reference:
156	
157	| Command | Behavior |
158	|---|---|
159	| `dev repo new` | interactive wizard; its first field accepts either a new name or a clone reference |
160	| `dev repo new NAME` / `dev repo create NAME` | create a new local repository; a clear Git URL, local Git path, or owner/name instead routes to clone and preserves history/remote |
161	| `dev repo clone [owner/name\|url]` | clone into the configured destination, then optionally apply a preset; setup defaults off |
162	| `dev repo setup [repo-or-path]` | repeat-safely merge native initializers and preset files into an existing clean checkout; defaults to the current repository and does not commit unless requested |
163	
164	A clone-routed `new` retains the source `origin`; it therefore rejects
165	new-upstream creation flags. It also rejects `--template*`, whose explicit
166	meaning is “copy content into a fresh history.”
167	
168	Across these commands, controls include `--preset`, `--path`, typed input values through
169	`--set`, item selection through `--enable`/`--disable`, `--check-in
170	<auto|commit|stage|none>`, `--dry-run`, `--yes`, `--json`, and `--handoff
171	<stay|cd|open|start>`. `repo new` additionally accepts `--template`,
172	`--template-ref`, and `--template-subdir`. JSON mode is non-interactive and
173	never changes directory or opens a runtime. Dry-run performs no target
174	repository mutation; clone setup can only be planned in detail after the clone
175	exists. Use the generated reference below for each command's exact flag
176	availability.
177	
178	The wizard renders the selected scaffold and workflow summary before target
179	repository mutation. The built-in presets are:
180	
181	- `minimal`: `main`, README, and an initial commit; this preserves existing
182	  scripted `repo new NAME` behavior.
183	- `agent-ready`: extends `minimal` with common ignores, starter `AGENTS.md`,
184	  and project-scoped `.claude/settings.json` plus `.claude/plans/`.
185	  `agent-history-hygiene` and `project-knowledge-harness` are offered but are
186	  not selected silently. When selected, dev installs them and runs reviewed
187	  built-in initializers for their project surfaces before the initial commit;
188	  downloaded skill scripts are not executed for these built-ins. Matching
189	  skills with the same source and identical agent targets share one installer
190	  invocation, while their setup phases still run per skill. The history
191	  initializer creates `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and `.gitleaks.toml`, then
192	  ensures `.specstory/.gitignore` contains rules for SpecStory's `.project.json`
193	  and `statistics.json`, never the trackable `.specstory/history/` directory.
194	  Existing custom ignore content and its mode are preserved; only missing
195	  managed rules are appended.
196	
197	After preset selection, the new-repository wizard asks “Customize preset and
198	template options?” with a default of no. The ordinary `agent-ready` flow uses
199	its reviewed template, file, input, and skill defaults without presenting each
200	question. Answer yes—or provide customization flags—to expand those controls.
201	
202	Presets can add typed `string`, `bool`, and `choice` inputs, text templates,
203	hooks, and project skills. Hooks run in fixed `before_commit`, `after_commit`,
204	and `after_remote` phases. The safe hook form is an argv `command`; a shell
205	`run` is explicit, and only `interactive = true` loads an interactive shell.
206	Required failures stop later commit/remote steps; optional failures are
207	reported as warnings. Produced local files are retained for recovery. Native
208	initializers and preset files are repeat-safe; custom hooks and skill setup are
209	responsible for their own idempotency.
210	
211	### Snapshot templates
212	
213	`dev repo new NAME --template SOURCE` seeds a fresh repository from a content
214	snapshot. `SOURCE` may be a local directory/repository, Git URL, or owner/name.
215	For a Git source, `--template-ref` selects an arbitrary branch, tag, or commit;
216	`--template-subdir` selects a clean relative directory as the new repository
217	root. Without a ref, a local Git working tree includes existing tracked files
218	plus untracked files that are not ignored by Git; ignored build/cache content
219	is omitted. A non-Git directory snapshots its complete current tree.
220	
221	The new repository does not inherit source history or remotes. Dev excludes
222	every source `.git` entry, rejects traversal, symlinks and special files,
223	preserves regular-file modes, and validates the complete snapshot before
224	creating the destination. Snapshot files take precedence when the selected
225	scaffold would write the same path; the scaffold still fills missing files and
226	runs the selected initializers. Source and destination traversal is performed
227	relative to held `os.Root` handles, and file bytes come from the already-open
228	validated source handle rather than a second mutable pathname lookup.
229	
230	Confirmation and human dry-run output show a bounded preview of selected paths
231	and warn when a local source is a live working-tree/directory snapshot rather
232	than a commit. Credential-bearing URL userinfo is removed from summaries,
233	structured output, and clone/template errors.
234	
235	Presets expose the same operation through scalar `template`, `template_ref`,
236	and `template_subdir` fields. They inherit normally and explicit CLI flags win,
237	which supports one starter catalog repository plus a child preset for each
238	subfolder.
239	
240	### Check-in policy
241	
242	The interactive wizard offers `commit`, `stage`, and `none`; scripts may also
243	pass `auto`. The behavior is:
244	
245	| Value | Behavior |
246	|---|---|
247	| `commit` | `git add -A`, commit with `--message`/the preset message, then run `after_commit` setup |
248	| `stage` | run `before_commit` setup, then `git add -A`; leave the checkout staged and do not run `after_commit` |
249	| `none` | leave generated changes unstaged and uncommitted |
250	| `auto` | for `repo new`, use `initial_check_in` and compatible `initial_commit`; clone/setup otherwise perform no automatic check-in |
251	
252	In `stage` mode, dev best-effort writes `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT` in the exact
253	worktree Git directory. [Lazygit v0.59.0 reads this
254	file](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/v0.59.0/pkg/gui/controllers/helpers/working_tree_helper.go#L191-L216)
255	as the initial message for lowercase `c`; uppercase `C` and Git itself do not use this integration. An
256	existing different draft is preserved and reported rather than overwritten.
257	This is an implementation-detail adapter, not `commit.template`.
258	
259	Staging is the durable outcome: if the optional lazygit draft cannot be
260	written, dev emits a warning and retains the staged index instead of rolling it
261	back.
262	
263	Staged setup cannot create an upstream, and `handoff=start` requires committed
264	setup because a new worktree would omit the staged files. `stay`, `cd`, and
265	`open` remain available for review. `repo setup --commit` is retained as a
266	compatibility alias for `--check-in=commit`; `--message` applies to both commit
267	and stage. Structured results retain `committed` and add `staged`,
268	`staged_paths`, `commit_message`, `commit_draft_provider`, and a content-free
269	`template` summary where applicable.
270	
271	### Upstream publishing
272	
273	Before offering publication, dev probes `gh` and `glab` without changing
274	state. A provider is offered only when its CLI is installed and authenticated;
275	otherwise the wizard gives the relevant installation or login guidance.
276	Local-only is the default, and a newly published repository defaults private.
277	
278	Publishing uses the local repository name and configured description, then asks
279	for the provider namespace/owner, visibility, and whether to push the
280	initial/current branch. Dev creates the empty GitHub or GitLab repository after
281	required local setup and commit steps succeed, then adds/verifies `origin` and
282	optionally pushes with upstream tracking. A
283	provider, name-conflict, or push failure never deletes the local checkout or
284	an upstream that was already created.
285	
286	Publishing from `repo setup` requires `--check-in=commit` (or the compatible
287	`--commit` flag), so the newly created upstream cannot omit the generated setup
288	changes. `--check-in=stage` is incompatible with any new upstream; for a new
289	repository, `none` may create an intentionally empty upstream only with
290	`--push=false`.
291	
292	### Handoff
293	
294	`stay` prints the result only. `cd` uses the trusted `shell-init` wrapper to
295	change the parent shell. `open` opens the configured Herdr/tmux/Zellij runtime
296	and falls back to `cd` when runtime is `none`. `start` continues into the
297	existing task wizard with the repository fixed, and is unavailable when setup
298	leaves uncommitted files that a new worktree would omit. Neither repository
299	bootstrap nor a default `dev start` launches a coding agent. Explicit
300	worktree-mode `dev start --run '<shell command>'` dispatches one command only
301	when a newly created first-class Herdr worktree returns its exact root pane;
302	`--focus` independently controls navigation afterward.
303	
304	All shared TTY text fields in the repository, task-start, and finish wizards
305	use an inline editor: Left/Right, Home/End, Delete/Backspace, insertion at the
306	cursor, and Esc/Ctrl-C cancellation work as terminal actions rather than being
307	inserted as raw escape bytes. Buffered and piped non-TTY input retains its
308	line-oriented behavior.
309	
310	## `dev done` finish flags
311	
312	`dev done` for branch/worktree tasks integrates through exactly one of `--ff` (rebase onto the base, then fast-forward it) or `--pr` (push and open a pull/merge request). Omitting both opens the interactive finish wizard on a TTY — see [Change-stream workflow](../guides/change-stream-workflow.md) for the prompts.
313	
314	A dirty checkout is handled by `--dirty <auto|fail|commit|discard>` (default `auto`):
315	
316	| Value | Behavior |
317	|---|---|
318	| `auto` | interactive: prompts to commit or discard; non-interactive: fails, same as `fail` |
319	| `fail` | refuses to finish with a dirty checkout |
320	| `commit` | commits everything with `--message`/`-m` (prompted interactively if omitted) |
321	| `discard` | resets tracked changes and removes untracked files; destructive, requires `--yes` outside a TTY |
322	
323	`--yes`/`-y` confirms the selected finish plan; it is mandatory for a non-interactive `--dirty discard` and otherwise skips the interactive confirmation step. `--keep-worktree` keeps the worktree after `--ff` integration (default: removed once merged), `--push` also pushes the resulting branch, and `--delete-branch` deletes the branch once its commits are contained in the base — never a branch with unpushed commits.
324	
325	## Configuration
326	
327	```bash
328	dev config init
329	dev config show
330	dev config path
331	dev config scaffolds init
332	dev config scaffolds show
333	dev config scaffolds path
334	dev config scaffolds edit
335	```
336	
337	`config init` detects local roots and writes explicit defaults. A missing config file is allowed; the built-in defaults keep core Git behavior usable, but generated config is recommended because it makes machine policy reviewable.
338	
339	Key sections:
340	
341	| Section | Controls |
342	|---|---|
343	| `[paths]` | scan roots, project/tries/worktree roots, worktree template, state path |
344	| `[runtime]` | `auto`, Herdr, tmux, Zellij, or none plus metadata settings |
345	| `[worktree]` | ignored includes, linked dirs, setup commands, strategies, timeout |
346	| `[forge]` / `[[forge.azure_devops]]` | complete remote inventory cache TTL and opt-in Azure organization/project targets |
347	| `[bootstrap]` | recursion, symlink handling, index/layout policy |
348	| `[tui]` / `[[tui.tools]]` | columns, sorting, and external-tool bindings |
349	| `[stats]` | sampler and optional WakaTime import |
350	| `[update]` | `check` (default `true`) — allow the once-a-day "newer release available" hint and its background cache refresh; `DEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` overrides it |
351	| `[[agent]]`, `[agent.run]`, `[agent.open]` | host-only names, optional descriptions, global default selection, and independent batch/foreground prompt launchers; no built-in entries |
352	
353	`DEV_TUI_TRACE=/absolute/new-file.json` enables a one-run TUI startup/readiness
354	trace. The target must be absolute and must not exist; dev never overwrites it.
355	The private bounded document is written after TUI teardown and contains relative
356	categorical timings plus aggregate row counts rather than names, paths, or raw
357	payloads. It is not configuration,
358	cache, durable stats, stdout, or network telemetry. For TUI invocations, the
359	optional update-cache network refresh is also deferred until the initial view
360	has returned.
361	
362	Repository quick-note Markdown is durable under configured `paths.state_dir/notes`, which defaults to `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes`. The full-text index at `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db` is disposable and rebuilds from those files; changing `paths.state_dir` does not move the cache.
363	
364	### Agent prompt launchers
365	
366	There are no built-in agent entries. Launchers are host-only policy in the user
367	config; the `agent` section is denied in repository `.dev-cli/config.toml`.
368	
369	```toml
370	[[agent]]
371	name = "my-agent"
372	description = "Local review and implementation agent"
373	default = true
374	
375	[agent.run]
376	command = ["my-agent", "--batch"]
377	input = "stdin"
378	timeout = "10m"
379	
380	[agent.open]
381	command = ["my-agent", "{{prompt_file}}"]
382	input = "file"
383	```
384	
385	`[[agent]]` has required `name`, optional `description` and `default`, and nested
386	`run`/`open` launchers. Names cannot have surrounding whitespace, compare
387	case-insensitively, and must be unique; at most one entry may be default. An
388	entry must configure at least one mode. Selection remains explicit/default/sole
389	across all profiles, then the requested mode is required on that exact profile;
390	the other mode remains unavailable rather than inheriting or falling back.
391	
392	Each launcher sets exactly one of `command` (direct argv) or `shell` (static
393	shell text), a required `input`, and optional `load_shell_rc` for `shell` only.
394	Only `run` accepts an optional non-negative `timeout`; `open` rejects one. `load_shell_rc = true` uses `$SHELL -lic`;
395	otherwise shell launch uses `$SHELL -c`. Shell text cannot contain prompt
396	placeholders, so prompt data is never interpolated into a command string.
397	
398	Transport constraints are exact:
399	
400	- `stdin`: `run` only; no placeholder; the finite prompt replaces child stdin.
401	- `file`: a `command` needs exactly one whole `{{prompt_file}}` element; a
402	  `shell` must reference `$DEV_PROMPT_FILE`/`${DEV_PROMPT_FILE}`. The temporary
403	  directory/file modes are 0700/0600 and cleanup follows process exit.
404	- `argv`: `command` only, with exactly one whole `{{prompt}}` element; maximum
405	  rendered prompt size is 100 KiB.
406	
407	Embedded placeholder forms are rejected. Omitted/zero timeout resolves to 10
408	minutes for `run`; `open` has no deadline and rejects a timeout. See
409	[Prompt handoffs](../guides/prompt-handoffs.md) for recipe and runtime safety.
410	
411	### Scaffold presets
412	
413	Global repository recipes live at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/scaffolds.toml` (or
414	the root `--scaffolds` override). Every authored file declares `version = 1`.
415	A compact preset looks like:
416	
417	```toml
418	version = 1
419	default_preset = "team"
420	default_agents = ["claude-code", "codex"]
421	
422	[presets.team]
423	extends = "agent-ready"
424	handoff = "cd"
425	initial_check_in = "stage"
426	template = "acme/starter-catalog"
427	template_ref = "v2"
428	template_subdir = "services/go"
429	
430	[[presets.team.inputs]]
431	id = "deployment"
432	type = "choice"
433	choices = ["none", "docker"]
434	default = "none"
435	
436	[[presets.team.files]]
437	id = "service-readme"
438	source = "service/README.md" # templates/service/README.md beside this file
439	destination = "docs/service.md"
440	
441	[[presets.team.hooks]]
442	id = "verify"
443	phase = "before_commit"
444	command = ["make", "test"]
445	required = true
446	
447	[[presets.team.skills]]
448	id = "knowledge"
449	source = "daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills"
450	name = "project-knowledge-harness"
451	agents = ["claude-code", "codex"]
452	default = true
453	
454	[presets.team.skills.setup]
455	phase = "before_commit"
456	interpreter = "bash"
457	script = "scripts/init.sh"
458	args = ["--target", "{{path}}", "--project-name", "{{name}}"]
459	required = true
460	```
461	
462	Skill setup normally names a project-local script inside the installed skill.
463	The shipped recommendations instead use `builtin = "agent-history-hygiene"` or
464	`builtin = "project-knowledge-harness"`; these fixed reviewed initializers do
465	not execute downloaded skill code.
466	
467	A preset may extend one parent. Scalars override; simple lists replace; files,
468	hooks, and skills merge by `id`, and an inherited item can be disabled with
469	`enabled = false`. A `[[presets.*.files]]` rendering source must remain in the
470	`templates/` tree next to its config source; that file-level mechanism is
471	separate from the repository snapshot `template` scalar above. Destinations
472	must remain inside the repository, and a skill setup script must remain inside
473	the installed skill directory. `initial_check_in` accepts `commit`, `stage`, or
474	`none`; the legacy `initial_commit` boolean remains readable, but a preset must
475	not set both.
476	
477	### Safe project overlays
478	
479	A repository may commit these fixed files:
480	
481	- `.dev-cli/config.toml`: allowlisted worktree provisioning and repository
482	  setup wizard defaults.
483	- `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml`: project presets, templates, hooks, and skill
484	  setup using the same versioned schema.
485	
486	```toml
487	# .dev-cli/config.toml
488	version = 1
489	
490	[worktree]
491	include = [".env.example"]
492	strategy = "reinstall"
493	
494	[repo.setup]
495	preset = "team"
496	handoff = "cd"
497	check_in = "stage"
498	```
499	
500	Effective precedence, lowest to highest, is built-ins, global config/scaffolds,
501	legacy `.dev.toml`, the target repository's `.dev-cli/*`, then explicit CLI or
502	wizard choices. `.dev.toml` remains readable for compatibility; new project
503	configuration should use `.dev-cli/config.toml`. Global `default_preset` and the
504	project `[repo.setup]` preset, handoff, and check-in fields seed interactive
505	wizard choices; they do not change scripted defaults, which are controlled by
506	the corresponding flags. The legacy `commit` boolean remains readable, but may
507	not be combined with `check_in` in the same layer.
508	
509	Project files cannot override host paths, state location, runtime backend,
510	forge inventory or credentials, stats, update, bootstrap, or TUI policy. They
511	also cannot silently publish a repository. Before a post-create command from
512	`.dev-cli/config.toml`, or a hook or skill setup from project
513	`.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml`, executes, dev asks to trust the canonical repository
514	plus an execution-content hash. Changed executable content requires new
515	consent; non-interactive use without a matching trust record fails closed.
516	Legacy `.dev.toml` retains its compatibility behavior. Keep credentials and
517	host-specific paths in user config or ignored environment files, never in a
518	committed project overlay.
519	
520	Project-authored skill setup must use a local source so its bytes can be bound
521	to the trust hash. Remote project skills may still be installed, but cannot
522	declare executable setup; global presets remain host-owned policy.
523	
524	## Colored output
525	
526	Every human-readable surface applies semantic ANSI color through a small set of roles: `title`/`header`/`prompt` (bold cyan), `label`/`dim` (dim), `success` (green), `warning` (yellow), `danger` (bold red), `review` (magenta, for a PR/review handoff), and `strong`/`code` for Markdown. Values that carry their own meaning are colored by that meaning rather than by a fixed role:
527	
528	| Value | Green | Yellow | Red |
529	|---|---|---|---|
530	| Git status | `clean` | `dirty`, `ahead`, `behind`, `no checkout` | `conflict`, `error` |
531	| Task state | `hot`, `done` | `warm`, `cold`, `parked` | — |
532	| Fleet host | `ok` | `stale`, `no-dev` | `unreachable`, `timeout`, `incompatible` |
533	| Skill update | `current` | `update` | `missing`, `failed` |
534	| Artifact intent | `finalized` | `armed`, `finalizing` | `failed` |
535	
536	`dev journal` and `dev summary` emit Markdown, so their headings and fenced code blocks are styled the same way `dev help <topic>` styles a quick-reference page. In command help, only the names you can type — command names and flag specs — are colored; descriptions stay plain, and the column alignment cobra computes is unaffected because a terminal gives an escape sequence no width.
537	
538	Control it with the global `--color <auto|always|never>` flag (default `auto`). `auto` disables color when output is not attached to a terminal, when `NO_COLOR` is set to any non-empty value, or when `TERM=dumb`. The setting reaches the interactive dashboard as well, so `dev --color never` renders it without color. `--json` output is never colored regardless of mode. There is no config-file field for color — `--color` and the environment are the only controls, so piping `dev` never requires `--color never` to stay clean.
539	
540	## Shell integration
541	
542	```bash
543	eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"
544	dev shell-init fish | source
545	```
546	
547	The trusted `shell-init` output defines a wrapper because a child process cannot change its parent's working directory. For navigation commands, that wrapper reads a NUL-terminated path from a private child-only file descriptor and calls `builtin cd`; it does not evaluate ordinary `dev` command output as shell code.
548

9	# Compatibility and known limitations
10	
11	This page separates graceful degradation from real limitations. Reverify it whenever command/runtime code or version-sensitive Claude Code documentation changes.
12	
13	## dev-cli capability matrix
14	
15	| Capability | Dependency | Without it |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| core repository/task/worktree operations | Git | unavailable; Git is the only hard runtime dependency |
18	| rich grouped runtime and agent activity | Herdr server + CLI | `auto` tries tmux, then Zellij, then none |
19	| named terminal session | tmux or compatible Zellij | `none` preserves core behavior and shell navigation |
20	| GitHub pull requests/remotes | `gh` authenticated | branch still pushes when Git works; browser/manual flow may be needed |
21	| GitLab merge requests/remotes | `glab` authenticated | same graceful fallback |
22	| repository bootstrap publishing | authenticated `gh` or `glab` | local repository/scaffold still works; the wizard explains how to log in |
23	| remote repository snapshot template | Git plus network/authentication for the source | validation fails before the destination is created and rendered URL userinfo is redacted; local templates still work |
24	| setup-capable project skills | skills provider plus the entrypoint interpreter | unselected skills are skipped; selected required setup fails before scaffold mutation when its interpreter is unavailable; a clone acquired first is retained |
25	| staged lazygit message prefill | a lazygit version that reads `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT` | files remain staged and dev prints the suggested message; normal Git commit remains available |
26	| worktree dependency setup | ecosystem manager (`uv`, npm, Cargo, etc.) | plan reports the missing tool and keeps the checkout |
27	| interactive dashboard | terminal input/output | bare `dev` prints the plain task list when piped |
28	| repository-note search | linked `modernc.org/sqlite` with FTS5 | no external `sqlite3` executable is required |
29	| terminal multiplexing on Windows | tmux/Zellij/Herdr (POSIX only) | Windows always uses the `none` backend; `dev shell-init powershell` still moves the shell |
30	| in-place self-update | standalone install (not Homebrew/Scoop/`go install`) | `dev upgrade` delegates to the package manager's upgrade command instead |
31	| verified ephemeral worktree apply | Git, compatible bounded Claude Workflow metadata, known task/artifact state, and every available runtime inventory | report remains available, but missing/unknown proof is never apply-eligible |
32	
33	## Confirmed project limitations
34	
35	### Note search and filesystem durability vary by text and platform
36	
37	Latin note queries use term-wise prefix FTS and SQLite ranking. Non-ASCII queries use literal term-wise substring matching because SQLite's `unicode61` tokenizer does not segment arbitrary CJK substrings; those results do not use the same FTS ranking.
38	
39	Note writes sync the file and atomically rename it on every supported platform. Unix also syncs the containing directory after rename/delete. The Windows implementation cannot provide that directory-fsync step, so a sudden power loss has a narrower durability guarantee there. Concurrent mutations by cooperating `dev` processes are serialized and each Markdown replacement is atomic; arbitrary external writers do not participate in that lock.
40	
41	### A merged pull request does not retire its worktree
42	
43	`dev done --pr` pushes and opens a pull/merge request, then leaves the task, runtime, and worktree unchanged because review owns integration.
44	
45	`dev pr list --scope local --state merged` now reports which requests the forge considers merged, and which local checkout each belongs to. `dev sweep` still does not consult it, and that is deliberate: a squashed merge produces a commit that is not an ancestor of the local branch, so a forge saying "merged" cannot prove the work is recoverable from the remote. `dev sweep --merged-worktrees` proves containment locally with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, and `dev done --merged` requires an explicit `--confirm-squash` attestation. Treat the pull-request list as a prompt to look, not as permission to delete.
46	
47	### Claude Workflow ephemeral cleanup is strict and version-sensitive
48	
49	`dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees` supports the private layout verified with
50	Claude Code 2.1.259: validated fixed-depth `wf_*.json`, matching worktree meta and
51	journal paths, `runId`, `status`, `workflowProgress` agent state/isolation,
52	`worktreePath`, `spawnedWithWorktree`, journal `started`/`result`, and same-ID
53	resume existence. Unknown add-only JSON fields are tolerated because upstream has
54	no metadata schema version. A missing/wrong required type, changed or unsafe
55	source file, duplicate/path mismatch, exhausted bound, or uncertain timestamp
56	makes the affected evidence unknown or unavailable; dev does not guess another
57	layout or decode payload fields.
58	
59	V1 has no operator attestation. `killed` without a matching child result,
60	progress, or any same-ID resumed transcript remains `unknown` regardless of age.
61	Apply is available only when provider inactivity and every Git/task/artifact/
62	caller/runtime fact are known and safe. `--no-runtime` may produce a report but
63	cannot apply. Missing, prunable, unregistered, and orphan paths are report-only.
64	The command never closes runtimes, prunes worktree registrations, deletes Claude
65	metadata, or force-removes/rescues/stashes/commits dirty or ignored work.
66	
67	This adapter is provider-specific behind a provider-neutral audit/service; no
68	other agent harness is inferred from a path or branch name. If Claude changes the
69	private layout, the safe behavior is an unavailable capability plus unknown
70	candidates until the adapter, fixtures, tested version, and both documentation
71	locales are updated.
72	
73	### Pull-request inventory is limited by the provider surfaces
74	
75	GitHub's `gh search prs` account surface cannot report a head branch, review decision, or check status, so those rows are `detail: "summary"` and cannot be joined to a worktree. An absent field on a summary row means the surface could not report it, not that the value is empty. GitLab's account list does carry branch/merge detail and therefore returns full rows, but its list surfaces report neither pipeline checks nor a normalized review decision.
76	
77	Personal per-repository inventory may make one paginated query per requested role for each repository (author and reviewer by default). It covers repositories `dev` has a task for unless `--all-repos` widens the scan. `--repo` filters both account rows and local targets. Account search cannot distinguish merged from closed, so requesting merged/closed/all narrows an account/all request to local collection; JSON reports that effective scope.
78	
79	The schema-version-1 local join reports expected and live branches, checkout existence, worktree registration, status availability/error, and whether the expected branch is actually checked out. Git details are omitted unless those live checks succeed. Azure DevOps pull requests are not listed at all; a configured target is reported as unsupported rather than failing the command.
80	
81	### Prompt open uses the current terminal, not runtime placement
82	
83	`dev prompt open <recipe>` runs one configured child in the foreground of the
84	terminal/TTY that invoked it. It does not create, focus, reuse, or inject into a
85	Herdr, tmux, or Zellij pane. Inside Herdr it naturally remains in the current
86	pane. To use another Herdr pane, create or focus it manually, enter the exact
87	checkout, and run `prompt open` there.
88	
89	This is intentionally separate from `dev start --run`, whose dispatch target is
90	only the exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree.
91	`prompt open` neither supplies a fresh runtime surface nor weakens that
92	exact-pane proof. `run` is the non-interactive alternative; it receives no user
93	stdin and defaults to a 10-minute timeout, while `open` reserves stdin for the
94	conversation and has no default timeout.
95	
96	The configured child retains its own permission policy. Recipe instructions are
97	read-only guidance, not a sandbox; `dev` does not add permission flags, answer
98	approval prompts, or parse the response into an action.
99	
100	### Prompt closeout reports do not authorize cleanup
101	
102	`session-close` computes runtime-closure evidence only. An `idle` or `done`
103	covering agent can satisfy that one activity gate, but does not prove that work
104	is committed, artifacts are finalized, review is complete, or task intent is
105	done. Caller-contained, mixed-purpose, active, unknown, and unrecognized
106	sessions remain blocked or unknown as their evidence requires.
107	
108	`workspace-closeout` performs the broader read-only audit: target kind,
109	registration/path, status availability, clean Git state, no in-progress Git
110	operation, known base and containment, task completion, artifact
111	reachability/finalization, and runtime eligibility. A merged pull request is only
112	evidence. Even an `eligible` audit is advisory; `dev retire` recollects and
113	revalidates fresh state before any mutation. Neither recipe closes a runtime,
114	changes Git/task state, deletes a branch/worktree, or grants permission to do so.
115	
116	### Zellij exited sessions are closed but keep their names
117	
118	Zellij keeps exited sessions available for resurrection. `dev` recognizes only
119	the exact `(EXITED - attach to resurrect)` marker, omits those sessions from live
120	coverage, and refuses to create over their names; reclaim one with
121	`zellij delete-session <name>`. A live session name containing `EXITED` is not an
122	exit marker. If a session exits between native listing and layout inspection,
123	open fails closed and asks for a retry rather than resurrecting an old layout at
124	the requested checkout.
125	
126	### Forge CLI sign-in is reported, never retried
127	
128	`gh` and `glab` are optional and independent, and `dev` never authenticates on your behalf. When a provider's stored credential is missing or rejected, `dev` reports which provider and the exact login command — for example ``glab is signed out — run `glab auth login --hostname gitlab.com` `` — and continues with whatever the other provider returned. `dev repo remote` and the TUI REMOTE view render the partial result and warn; `dev pr` fails only when no provider is authenticated at all. `dev doctor` probes sign-in state, so an installed but signed-out CLI is visible before a command needs it.
129	
130	Only a missing or rejected credential is reported this way. A rate limit, a permissions or scope failure, and a network error keep their full diagnostic text including the command that failed, because signing in again would not fix them. The original command and provider output remain in the wrapped error in every case.
131	
132	### Agent session capture is reserved, not wired
133	
134	The task schema has an `AgentSession` field and Herdr inventory can expose live agent session IDs. The production start/park/resume path does not yet capture or attach that ID. Treat the field and live inventory as observability/future integration, not a promise that `dev resume` restores the coding-agent conversation.
135	
136	### Built-in forge cache TTL differs from generated config
137	
138	`dev config init` writes `forge.cache_ttl = "15m"`. With no config file, the current built-in `Forge.CacheTTL` zero value means an existing valid cache is not rejected by age; explicit `r` refresh still replaces it. Freshness also requires a source fingerprint matching the configured GH/GL hosts and Azure targets, so an endpoint change is never hidden by the zero TTL. Legacy source-less caches remain available only through explicit `--cached` and are reported stale. Run `config init` or set the TTL when freshness matters.
139	
140	Older generated configs may contain `forge.remote_limit = 100`. The field is
141	still accepted, but complete forge inventories are now paginated and it no
142	longer caps synchronization. `dev config init` no longer writes it. The
143	`--limit` flag on `dev repo remote` limits rendered matches after the complete
144	inventory has been searched.
145	
146	### Lazygit staged-message prefill is best effort
147	
148	`repo --check-in=stage` writes a pending message in the exact worktree Git
149	directory. [Lazygit v0.59.0 uses that file for lowercase
150	`c`](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/v0.59.0/pkg/gui/controllers/helpers/working_tree_helper.go#L191-L216), but it is a
151	lazygit implementation detail rather than a Git interface; uppercase `C` and
152	plain `git commit` do not consume it. Dev never overwrites a different existing
153	draft. A draft-write failure is warning-only: staging remains successful and
154	is never rolled back. If the integration changes upstream, the staged index
155	and printed message remain the recovery path.
156	
157	### Windows is a build target, not a full-feature platform
158	
159	`dev` compiles and runs on `windows/amd64` and `windows/arm64`, and every release ships a `.zip` for each. Core repository, task and worktree operations work. What differs:
160	
161	- There is no tmux, Zellij or Herdr, so the runtime backend is always `none`. Grouped runtime/agent activity and named sessions are unavailable; the `cd` directive and PowerShell wrapper still work.
162	- Shell integration is `dev shell-init powershell`. POSIX shells hand the directory back on file descriptor 3; PowerShell cannot inherit it, so the wrapper passes a temp-file path in `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` instead.
163	- `dev fleet open` starts a child shell (`%COMSPEC%`) rather than replacing the process, because Windows has no `exec(2)`.
164	- The domain test suites still assume a POSIX filesystem in places, so Windows CI runs the tests advisory-only while compilation, `go vet` and the build are enforced.
165	
166	### Direct mode has a smaller lifecycle
167	
168	A direct task uses the canonical checkout and cannot go COLD, because cold cleanup would remove a directory the repository needs. Use branch-only or worktree mode for cross-machine reconstruction.
169	
170	## Current behaviors that are implemented
171	
172	These were historical gaps and should not be reintroduced as limitations:
173	
174	- `dev repo new|create`, `repo clone`, and `repo setup` share a preset-driven bootstrap pipeline. A plain explicit `repo new NAME` remains minimal, while a clear Git URL, local Git path, or owner/name routes through clone acquisition and preserves source history/remote. The no-argument wizard detects the same reference in its first field; for a new repository, a default-no customization gate keeps the normal `agent-ready` flow concise. Text fields use a TTY inline editor, so cursor keys edit rather than inserting raw escape bytes; non-TTY readers retain line-oriented behavior.
175	- `repo new` can snapshot a local directory/repository or Git source at an optional branch, tag, or commit and confined subdirectory into a fresh history. An unpinned local Git tree includes tracked plus untracked non-ignored files; a non-Git directory includes its full current tree. Source `.git` metadata is excluded, URL userinfo is redacted, unsafe file types/paths fail before destination creation, and held root/file handles confine mutable-path races. Human plans preview paths and warn when the snapshot is live; presets can select catalog-repository subfolders.
176	- Repository setup supports `--check-in=commit|stage|none` (`auto` for preset compatibility). Staged setup runs before-commit setup and `git add -A` without an `after_commit` phase, cannot publish or hand off to `start`, and may prefill lazygit lowercase `c` as described above.
177	- Selected skills with matching source and agent targets share one installer invocation. The `agent-history-hygiene` initializer writes pre-commit/gitleaks policy and merges missing machine-local `.project.json`/`statistics.json` rules into `.specstory/.gitignore`; custom content and transcript history remain trackable.
178	- Project `.dev-cli/config.toml` and `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml` are constrained to portable setup policy. Executable project configuration is keyed to the canonical Git common directory and an exact content hash; a changed hash is untrusted until approved again.
179	
180	- `dev start --focus` activates the runtime after non-JSON creation.
181	- `dev start --run '<shell command>'` dispatches only to an exact root pane from
182	  a newly created first-class Herdr worktree. It is incompatible with `--json`,
183	  non-worktree modes, and non-Herdr runtimes, and does not wait for command exit.
184	- TUI navigation refuses to open a missing COLD checkout and directs the user to `dev resume`.
185	- `DEV_TUI_TRACE` starts at `cli.Execute`; it cannot include OS process loading. `tui.initial_view_returned` measures model construction, not renderer flush or physical terminal paint. Use it for same-profile comparisons rather than universal hardware/network guarantees.
186	- Runtime handles now record backend provenance and are revalidated before cleanup.
187	- `auto` runtime selection includes Zellij between tmux and none.
188	
189	- `dev done` opens an interactive finish wizard on a TTY when `--ff`/`--pr` are both omitted, analyzing a dirty checkout against the base (commit, discard, or cancel) instead of rejecting any uncommitted change outright; a non-interactive caller still passes an explicit `--dirty` policy and `--yes` for a destructive discard.
190	- Human-readable output now carries semantic color (`--color auto|always|never`), automatically disabled when `NO_COLOR` is set, `TERM=dumb`, or stdout/stderr is not a terminal.
191	- `dev done` records MERGED only: it never closes the invoking runtime, removes a worktree, or deletes a branch. Cleanup moved to `dev retire`, which runs from outside the target workspace, refuses active agents and mixed-purpose workspaces, and revalidates Git state after every runtime closure. `dev done --delete-branch` is now an error pointing at `dev retire --delete-branch`, and `--keep-worktree` warns as a no-op.
192	- `dev sweep --merged-worktrees` enumerates linked worktrees from Git rather than from the task registry, so unmanaged worktrees whose branches are contained in the base become retirable. Containment alone is never permission; dirty state, unfinalized artifacts, in-progress Git operations, and runtime refusals all still block it, and branches survive unless `--delete-branches` is passed.
193	- `dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees` adds a separate schema-v1 Claude Workflow report. The path/branch convention is only discovery; exact bounded provider linkage plus fresh Git/task/artifact/caller/runtime evidence authorizes TTY/per-item apply. Apply locks and re-fingerprints, removes without force, retains branches by default, and allows only explicit-base unchanged/contained/zero-unique `branch -d`.
194	- `dev sweep` reports a branch-backed task whose branch Git no longer has as dead and offers to reap the record. Such a task cannot be finished, resumed, or retired, because every one of those paths resolves the branch first; the suggestion stays report-only until `--apply`.
195	- An unknown command is reported instead of discarded. `dev` silences cobra's own error printing and previously also skipped printing anything whose message began with `unknown command`, so a mistyped command produced no output at all on either stream. The message, cobra's "Did you mean this?" suggestions, and a pointer to `--help` are now printed to stderr with exit status 1.
196	- A stray argument to a command family is an error rather than a silent help render. `dev wt bogus` used to print `dev wt` help and exit 0 because a family has no `Run` of its own; every family node now reports the unknown subcommand and exits 1, while a bare family still prints its help and exits 0.
197	- Argument-count and flag errors print the failing command's usage block. `--color` still governs whether that block is colorized.
198	- Each command family's help carries an ASCII orientation diagram and a `See also: dev help <topic>` pointer, and `dev help <command>` resolves a command name or alias to its topic, so `dev help wt` reaches the worktrees page.
199	- Semantic color covers every human-readable surface, including the interactive dashboard: `dev --color never`, `NO_COLOR` and `TERM=dumb` now disable dashboard color too, which they previously did not.
200	- `dev sweep` reaps a task whose repository directory no longer exists. Such a record was unreachable by every command in the binary: `done`, `resume`, `park` and `retire` all resolve the repository first, the dead-branch rule excludes direct mode, and the stale-worktree rule requires a recorded worktree path. A live runtime session rules the suggestion out, and reaping removes only dev's record of intent.
201	- `dev sweep` reports a task-recorded checkout that exists but Git does not register and that holds nothing but agent artifact directories. Removal is offered only when every file inside is byte-identical to one already in the repository; anything else is reported as salvage work and is never removed, including under `--apply`.
202	- `dev sweep` acts on a cold task whose worktree is still on disk. Inventory has always computed that drift for `dev ls` and the dashboard, but sweep never consulted it, so it was displayed and not actionable.
203	- `dev retire <path>` reaps the matching task record. Only the by-task form set the task identity, so retiring the same checkout by path left the record behind; the DONE-state and identity checks are unchanged.
204	- `dev version` reports whether the running build is a published release, and `dev doctor` carries the same line plus the install owner, invoked/resolved executable path, and warnings for distinct `dev` copies on `PATH`. Nothing in the tool answered "am I current?" before, and `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so an untagged feature was invisible to anyone installing it.
205	- A release publishes platform archives and `SHA256SUMS` and takes its notes from `CHANGELOG.md`. Earlier releases published a GitHub release object and nothing else, so their assets are absent by construction.
206	- A release publishes Windows `.zip` archives alongside the Unix `.tar.gz` set, refreshes an in-repo Scoop manifest attached to the release (and pushed to the bucket when a token is configured), and publishes the matching source formula to `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`. Homebrew publication is a required release step and fails visibly when its repository token is missing or rejected. A manual workflow can retry or backfill the formula for an existing stable release without creating or moving a tag.
207	- `dev upgrade` downloads the current release for this platform, verifies it against the release `SHA256SUMS`, and replaces the running binary with an atomic rename (Windows moves the live `.exe` aside and sweeps it on the next run). It detects and runs Homebrew, Scoop or `go install` when one of them owns the file; Homebrew users receive releases through the automatically advanced tap instead of an in-place Cellar overwrite.
208	- An interactive `dev` command prints one dim "newer release available" line at most once a day, read from the day-old release cache; it never blocks on the network. For the TUI, a stale-cache background refresh starts only after the initial view returns. `[update] check = false` or `DEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` disables it.
209	
210	## Claude Code status matrix
211	
212	| Surface | Status on 2026-08-28 | Compatibility note |
213	|---|---|---|
214	| core agentic loop/tools | official | exact tools depend on surface/model/policy |
215	| worktree isolation | official, rapidly evolving | cleanup, baseRef, resume, and safety details are version-sensitive |
216	| subagents | official | fork/background defaults and naming changed across 2.1.x |
217	| Agent view | research preview | retain manual sessions/worktrees fallback |
218	| agent teams | experimental, disabled by default | no automatic worktree isolation; resumption/task/shutdown limitations |
219	| Dynamic Workflows | versioned feature | requires v2.1.154+; availability/config and limits vary by release |
220	| Agent SDK | official SDK | language SDK parity and event availability can differ |
221	
222	`TeamCreate` and `TeamDelete` are historical tools removed in v2.1.178. The old `Task` worker tool name was replaced by `Agent`; do not confuse either with Task-list metadata tools.
223	
224	## Documentation-stack limitations
225	
226	- `mkdocs-static-i18n` reports that `zh-TW` is not a Lunr language, so Chinese search does not receive a dedicated Lunr stemmer/segmenter. Navigation and pages still build.
227	- `mkdocs-llmstxt` skips pages after static-i18n remaps them. This project replaces that empty output with a deterministic local generator and runs strict builds again.
228	- The copy-to-LLM plugin's button labels remain English on zh-TW pages; this is cosmetic.
229	- MkDocs and Material are pinned below their next major versions because the selected plugin stack targets MkDocs 1.x/Material 9.x.
230	
231	## Reporting a compatibility change
232	
233	Update the owning guide, both languages, this matrix, and [Sources and freshness](sources-freshness.md). Include the tested binary/version and a code/test or official-source link. Never preserve a known false statement for backward documentation compatibility.

28	  batch timeout/shell-RC policy. `open` rejects stdin and timeout, prompts are never interpolated
29	  into shell text, and repository `.dev-cli/config.toml` cannot define agents.

33	  output form reveals argv, shell source, executable directories, environment,

37	  verifies exact workflow/agent/path/journal linkage without decoding prompts,
38	  scripts, logs, result bodies, or transcripts; strict V1 liveness, Git/task/
39	  artifact/runtime/caller checks, ignored-file and recursive-submodule checks,
40	  and locked fingerprint revalidation all fail closed. Apply is TTY-only with
41	  per-item confirmation and plain non-force removal. Branches survive by default;
42	  separately requested deletion needs an explicit unchanged base and safe `-d`.

54	  `expected_branch` from `live_branch`, report checkout existence, worktree
55	  registration and status availability/errors independently, and include Git
56	  status only when the expected branch is actually checked out. Fork pull
57	  requests join against their source repository (resolving GitLab source project
58	  IDs when needed), canonical/unmanaged/external worktrees join without a task,
59	  duplicate local clones no longer suppress the remote query, and ambiguous
60	  same-branch local evidence fails closed instead of choosing a clone. Provider
61	  host identity is preserved so an enterprise remote is never queried against
62	  the public forge, partial failures appear in JSON `warnings`, and stale GitHub
63	  checks are not reported as passing.
64	- The Zellij runtime no longer fails every session listing when an exited
65	  session is left in Zellij's namespace. Zellij keeps exited sessions
66	  resurrectable, and `dump-layout` against one errors with `There is no active
67	  session!`, which previously turned `dev ls`, `dev doctor` and the TUI runtime
68	  join into an error. Exited sessions are now excluded from the live view, and
69	  `dev start` refuses to create over a name an exited session still owns

72	  fails closed rather than falling through to resurrection. Only Zellij's exact

78	  the original command and provider output preserved in the wrapped error.

95	- Session and workspace prompts now reuse retirement's pane/mixed-workspace and
96	  agent-status policy, Git branch relation logic, and read-only artifact
97	  reachability inspection. Missing or failed evidence remains unknown instead
