18	// EphemeralCheckout is the read-only Git cleanliness evidence needed by the
19	// ephemeral cleanup service. It retains counts and a digest, never pathnames.
20	type EphemeralCheckout struct {
21		Status          Status
22		Ignored         int
23		DirtySubmodules int
24		Fingerprint     string
25	}
26	
27	// InspectEphemeralCheckout reads full porcelain status, including all
28	// untracked files and non-ignored submodule state, plus Git's ignored-file
29	// inventory. Initialized submodules are inspected recursively so ignored files
30	// cannot hide behind the parent repository boundary. No command changes an
31	// index or worktree.
32	func InspectEphemeralCheckout(ctx context.Context, dir string) (EphemeralCheckout, error) {
33		return inspectEphemeralCheckout(ctx, dir, make(map[string]bool))
34	}
35	
36	func inspectEphemeralCheckout(ctx context.Context, dir string, seen map[string]bool) (EphemeralCheckout, error) {
37		canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(dir)
38		if err != nil {
39			return EphemeralCheckout{}, err
40		}
41		if seen[canonical] {
42			return EphemeralCheckout{}, fmt.Errorf("recursive submodule checkout path %s", canonical)
43		}
44		seen[canonical] = true
45		defer delete(seen, canonical)
46	
47		statusOutput, err := run(ctx, canonical,
48			"status", "--porcelain=v2", "--branch", "--untracked-files=all", "--ignore-submodules=none", "-z")
49		if err != nil {
50			return EphemeralCheckout{}, err
51		}
52		ignoredOutput, err := run(ctx, canonical,
53			"ls-files", "--others", "--ignored", "--exclude-standard", "-z")
54		if err != nil {
55			return EphemeralCheckout{}, err
56		}
57		gitlinksOutput, err := run(ctx, canonical, "ls-files", "--stage", "-z")
58		if err != nil {
59			return EphemeralCheckout{}, err
60		}
61	
62		ignored := nonEmptyNULRecords(ignoredOutput)
63		dirtyPaths := submoduleDirtyPaths(statusOutput)
64		dirtySubmodules := 0
65		var childFingerprints []string
66		for _, submodulePath := range gitlinkPaths(gitlinksOutput) {
67			joined := filepath.Join(canonical, filepath.FromSlash(submodulePath))
68			child, err := pathx.CanonicalChild(canonical, joined)
69			if err != nil {
70				return EphemeralCheckout{}, fmt.Errorf("validate submodule path: %w", err)
71			}
72			info, err := os.Lstat(child)
73			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
74				dirtySubmodules++
75				childFingerprints = append(childFingerprints, digestEphemeral(submodulePath, "missing"))
76				continue
77			}
78			if err != nil || info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 || !info.IsDir() {
79				return EphemeralCheckout{}, fmt.Errorf("inspect submodule checkout")
80			}
81			childInspection, err := inspectEphemeralCheckout(ctx, child, seen)
82			if err != nil {
83				return EphemeralCheckout{}, err
84			}
85			ignored += childInspection.Ignored
86			childDirty := dirtyPaths[submodulePath] || childInspection.Status.Dirty() ||
87				childInspection.Ignored > 0 || childInspection.DirtySubmodules > 0
88			if childDirty {
89				dirtySubmodules++
90			}
91			dirtySubmodules += childInspection.DirtySubmodules
92			childFingerprints = append(childFingerprints, digestEphemeral(submodulePath, childInspection.Fingerprint))
93		}
94		sort.Strings(childFingerprints)
95		fingerprintParts := []string{statusOutput, ignoredOutput, gitlinksOutput}
96		fingerprintParts = append(fingerprintParts, childFingerprints...)
97		return EphemeralCheckout{
98			Status:          statusFromOutput(canonical, statusOutput),
99			Ignored:         ignored,
100			DirtySubmodules: dirtySubmodules,
101			Fingerprint:     digestEphemeral(fingerprintParts...),
102		}, nil
103	}
104	
105	func nonEmptyNULRecords(output string) int {
106		count := 0
107		for _, record := range nulLines(output) {
108			if record != "" {
109				count++
110			}
111		}
112		return count
113	}
114	
115	func submoduleDirtyCount(output string) int { return len(submoduleDirtyPaths(output)) }
116	
117	func submoduleDirtyPaths(output string) map[string]bool {
118		paths := make(map[string]bool)
119		for _, record := range nulLines(output) {
120			if record == "" || (record[0] != '1' && record[0] != '2') {
121				continue
122			}
123			fields := strings.Fields(record)
124			if len(fields) > 2 && strings.HasPrefix(fields[2], "S") {
125				if path := statusPath(record); path != "" {
126					paths[filepath.ToSlash(path)] = true
127				}
128			}
129		}
130		return paths
131	}
132	
133	func gitlinkPaths(output string) []string {
134		var paths []string
135		for _, record := range nulLines(output) {
136			metadata, path, ok := strings.Cut(record, "\t")
137			if !ok || path == "" {
138				continue
139			}
140			fields := strings.Fields(metadata)
141			if len(fields) == 3 && fields[0] == "160000" && fields[2] == "0" {
142				paths = append(paths, filepath.ToSlash(path))
143			}
144		}
145		sort.Strings(paths)
146		return paths
147	}
148	
149	func digestEphemeral(parts ...string) string {
150		hash := sha256.New()
151		for _, part := range parts {
152			hash.Write([]byte(part))
153			hash.Write([]byte{0})
154		}
155		return hex.EncodeToString(hash.Sum(nil))
156	}

170	func suggestFor(app *App, ctx context.Context, r inventory.Row, stale time.Duration, retireOptions sweepRetireOptions) []suggestion {
171		t := r.Task
172		var out []suggestion
173	
174		// A task whose repository is gone cannot be finished, resumed, parked or
175		// retired: every one of those resolves the repository first, and `dev done`
176		// refuses outright once the checkout is missing. Nothing else in this
177		// function reaches it either — the dead-branch rule below excludes direct
178		// mode, and the stale-worktree rule needs a recorded worktree path. Left
179		// alone, the record is unreachable by any command in the binary.
180		//
181		// Reaping removes dev's record of intent and nothing else; the branch, the
182		// commits and the remote are untouched. A live session proves the directory
183		// is there, so it is the one condition that rules this out.
184		if t.RepoPath != "" && !r.Live() && !dirExists(t.RepoPath) {
185			out = append(out, suggestion{
186				row:    r,
187				reason: fmt.Sprintf("repository %s no longer exists", config.Contract(t.RepoPath)),
188				action: fmt.Sprintf("reap the task entry %s (Git keeps any work; this drops only dev's record)", t.ID),
189				apply:  func() error { return app.Tasks.Delete(t.ID) },
190			})
191			return out
192		}
193	
194		out = append(out, orphanSuggestions(app, r)...)
195	
196		switch {
197		// A hot task with no live session is the commonest drift: the session was
198		// closed (or the machine rebooted) without parking.
199		case t.State == task.Hot && !r.Live():
200			out = append(out, suggestion{
201				row:    r,
202				reason: fmt.Sprintf("hot but no live session, idle %s", humanAge(r.Age())),
203				action: fmt.Sprintf("mark %s warm", t.ID),
204				apply: func() error {
205					t.State = task.Warm
206					return app.Tasks.Save(t)
207				},
208			})
209	
210		// A warm task nobody has touched in weeks is a candidate for cold: keeping
211		// the worktree costs disk and clutters every listing.
212		case t.State == task.Warm && r.Age() > stale:
213			reason := fmt.Sprintf("warm and untouched for %s", humanAge(r.Age()))
214			if r.Status.Dirty() {
215				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + ", but has uncommitted work",
216					action: "commit or `dev park --wip` before going cold — not changed automatically"})
217				break
218			}
219			if !r.Status.Synced() {
220				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + fmt.Sprintf(", not pushed (%s)", r.Status.Summary()),
221					action: fmt.Sprintf("push %s so it can go cold: dev park %s --cold --push", t.Branch, t.ID)})
222				break
223			}
224			out = append(out, suggestion{
225				row:    r,
226				reason: reason + ", clean and pushed",
227				action: fmt.Sprintf("go cold: remove %s (branch and remote keep the work)", config.Contract(r.Checkout)),
228				apply: func() error {
229					if t.WorktreePath != "" {
230						if err := ensureArtifactsFinalized(app, t.WorktreePath); err != nil {
231							return err
232						}
233						if err := safeRemoveWorktree(ctx, runtimeForTask(app, t), t.RepoPath, t.WorktreePath,
234							false, false, false, 5*time.Second); err != nil {
235							return err
236						}
237						t.WorktreePath = ""
238					}
239					t.State = task.Cold
240					clearTaskRuntime(t)
241					return app.Tasks.Save(t)
242				},
243			})
244	
245		// DONE means integrated; runtime/worktree cleanup is a separate,
246		// externally coordinated retirement step.
247		case t.State == task.Done:
248			action := fmt.Sprintf("retire runtime/worktree for %s", t.ID)
249			if retireOptions.deleteBranches && t.Branch != "" && t.Branch != t.Base {
250				action += fmt.Sprintf(" and delete %s", t.Branch)
251			}
252			out = append(out, suggestion{
253				row:    r,
254				reason: "merged, cleanup pending",
255				action: action,
256				apply: func() error {
257					if err := ensureArtifactsFinalized(app, checkoutOf(t)); err != nil {
258						return err
259					}
260					target, rt, err := retirementTargetForTask(ctx, app, t)
261					if err != nil {
262						return err
263					}
264					service := &retirement.Service{Runtime: rt, Tasks: app.Tasks}
265					_, err = service.Retire(ctx, retirement.Request{
266						Target: target,
267						Safety: retirement.Options{
268							CloseUnknown: retireOptions.closeUnknown, AssumeNoRuntime: retireOptions.assumeNoRuntime,
269						},
270						DeleteBranch: retireOptions.deleteBranches,
271					})
272					return err
273				},
274			})
275		}
276	
277		// A branch-backed task whose branch git no longer has is dead: the branch
278		// was deleted after integration, so the record holds intent for work that
279		// no longer exists anywhere. It cannot be finished, resumed, or retired,
280		// because every one of those paths resolves the branch first.

529	func confirm(app *App, in *bufio.Reader, action string) bool {
530		s := app.outStyle()
531		prompt := s.prompt(action + "?")
532		lower := strings.ToLower(action)
533		if strings.Contains(lower, "delete") || strings.Contains(lower, "remove") ||
534			strings.Contains(lower, "discard") || strings.Contains(lower, "drop") {
535			prompt = s.danger(action + "?")
536		}
537		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s %s ", prompt, s.dim("[y/N]"))
538		line, err := in.ReadString('\n')
539		if err != nil {
540			return false
541		}
542		answer := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(line))
543		return answer == "y" || answer == "yes"
544	}

546	type ephemeralSweepOptions struct {

549		json                   bool

551		baseExplicit           bool
552		yesChanged             bool
553		closeUnknownChanged    bool

555		deleteBranches         bool

557	
558	func runEphemeralSweep(ctx context.Context, app *App, _ *cobra.Command, options ephemeralSweepOptions) error {
559		switch {
560		case options.staleDays < 1:
561			return fmt.Errorf("--stale-days must be at least 1 for --ephemeral-worktrees")
562		case options.json && options.apply:
563			return fmt.Errorf("--json is report-only and cannot be combined with --apply")
564		case options.yesChanged:
565			return fmt.Errorf("--ephemeral-worktrees does not accept --yes; each item requires confirmation")
566		case options.closeUnknownChanged:
567			return fmt.Errorf("--ephemeral-worktrees does not accept --close-unknown")
568		case options.assumeNoRuntimeChanged:
569			return fmt.Errorf("--ephemeral-worktrees does not accept --assume-no-runtime")
570		case options.apply && app.noRuntime:
571			return fmt.Errorf("--ephemeral-worktrees cannot apply with --no-runtime")
572		case options.deleteBranches && !options.apply:
573			return fmt.Errorf("--delete-branches with --ephemeral-worktrees requires --apply")
574		case options.deleteBranches && (!options.baseExplicit || strings.TrimSpace(options.baseRef) == ""):
575			return fmt.Errorf("--delete-branches with --ephemeral-worktrees requires an explicit --base")
576		case options.apply && !app.interactive():
577			return fmt.Errorf("--ephemeral-worktrees --apply requires an interactive terminal")
578		}
579	
580		home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
581		if err != nil || home == "" {
582			return fmt.Errorf("resolve home directory for Claude Workflow metadata")
583		}
584		service := ephemeral.NewService(
585			claudeworkflow.New(filepath.Join(home, ".claude", "projects")),
586			ephemeral.ServiceOptions{
587				Tasks: app.Tasks, Artifacts: artifactStore(app), Runtimes: ephemeralSweepRuntimes(app),
588				RuntimeDisabled: app.noRuntime,
589			},
590		)
591		report, err := service.Report(ctx, ephemeral.ReportRequest{
592			RepoPath: mustGetwd(), StaleDays: options.staleDays,
593			BaseRef: options.baseRef, BaseExplicit: options.baseExplicit, DeleteBranches: options.deleteBranches,
594		})
595		if err != nil {
596			return err
597		}
598		if options.json {
599			encoder := json.NewEncoder(app.Out)
600			encoder.SetIndent("", "  ")
601			return encoder.Encode(report)
602		}
603		renderEphemeralReport(app, report)
604		if !options.apply {
605			return nil
606		}
607	
608		reader := bufio.NewReader(app.In)
609		var approved []string
610		for _, candidate := range report.Candidates {
611			if candidate.Classification != ephemeral.Eligible {
612				continue
613			}
614			action := "remove ephemeral worktree " + config.Contract(candidate.Path) + " (branch retained)"
615			if candidate.BranchDeletion.Requested && candidate.BranchDeletion.Safe {
616				action = "remove ephemeral worktree " + config.Contract(candidate.Path) + " and delete branch " + candidate.Branch
617			}
618			if confirm(app, reader, action) {
619				approved = append(approved, candidate.Fingerprint)
620			}
621		}
622		if len(approved) == 0 {
623			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, app.outStyle().dim("No eligible worktree was approved; nothing changed."))
624			return nil
625		}
626		result, err := service.Apply(ctx, ephemeral.ApplyRequest{Report: report, Fingerprints: approved})
627		if err != nil {
628			return err
629		}
630		renderEphemeralApply(app, result)
631		return nil
632	}
633	
634	func ephemeralSweepRuntimes(app *App) []runtime.Runtime {
635		if app.runtimeInstance != nil {
636			return []runtime.Runtime{app.runtimeInstance}
637		}
638		out := make([]runtime.Runtime, 0, 3)
639		for _, name := range []string{"herdr", "tmux", "zellij"} {
640			out = append(out, app.runtimeNamed(name))
641		}
642		return out
643	}
644	
645	func renderEphemeralReport(app *App, report ephemeral.Report) {
646		style := app.outStyle()
647		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%s\n", style.title("Verified ephemeral worktree report (schema v1)"))
648		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "Repository: %s\n", config.Contract(report.Repository.Root))
649		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "Candidates: %d (%d eligible, %d blocked, %d unknown, %d report-only)\n",
650			report.Summary.Total, report.Summary.Eligible, report.Summary.Blocked,
651			report.Summary.Unknown, report.Summary.NotApplicable)
652		for _, capability := range report.Capabilities {
653			if !capability.Available {
654				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  capability unavailable: %s\n", capability.Name)
655			}
656		}
657		for _, candidate := range report.Candidates {
658			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n  %-14s %s\n", strings.ToUpper(string(candidate.Classification)), config.Contract(candidate.Path))
659			if candidate.Provider != "" {
660				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "    provider=%s run=%s agent=%s workflow=%s agent-state=%s\n",
661					candidate.Provider, candidate.RunID, candidate.AgentID, candidate.WorkflowState, candidate.AgentState)
662			}
663			if candidate.LastActivityKnown {
664				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "    last activity: %s\n", candidate.LastActivity.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339))
665			} else {
666				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "    last activity: unknown")
667			}
668			for _, check := range candidate.Checks {
669				if check.Classification != ephemeral.Eligible {
670					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "    %s: %s — %s\n", check.ID, check.Classification, check.Detail)
671				}
672			}
673			for _, action := range candidate.PlannedActions {
674				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "    %s: %s (%s)\n", action.Kind, action.Status, action.Detail)
675			}
676		}
677		if report.Summary.Eligible == 0 {
678			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, style.dim("\nNo eligible ephemeral worktree was found; report-only entries were not changed."))
679		} else {
680			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, style.dim("\nRe-run with --apply from an interactive terminal; every eligible item is confirmed separately."))
681		}
682	}
683	
684	func renderEphemeralApply(app *App, result ephemeral.ApplyResult) {
685		style := app.outStyle()
686		for _, item := range result.Results {
687			switch item.Status {
688			case ephemeral.ApplyRemoved:
689				branch := "branch retained"
690				if item.DeletedBranch {
691					branch = "branch deleted"
692				}
693				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s %s (%s)\n", style.success("removed:"), config.Contract(item.Path), branch)
694			case ephemeral.ApplyPartial:
695				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s %s — %s\n", style.warning("partial:"), config.Contract(item.Path), item.Detail)
696			case ephemeral.ApplySkippedChanged:
697				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s %s — %s\n", style.warning("skipped-changed:"), config.Contract(item.Path), item.Detail)
698			default:
699				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s %s — %s\n", style.warning("failed:"), config.Contract(item.Path), item.Detail)
700			}
701		}
702	}
703

132		if rt := a.runtimesByName[name]; rt != nil {
133			return rt
134		}
135		if a.runtimeInstance != nil && (name == "" || a.runtimeInstance.Name() == name) {
136			return a.runtimeInstance

138		rt := runtime.Select(name)
139		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
140			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
141		}
142		return rt
143	}

385		progressByID, progressActivity, progressTimeKnown, err := decodeProgress(object["workflowProgress"])

396	func decodeProgress(raw json.RawMessage) (map[string]progressRecord, []time.Time, bool, error) {
397		if len(raw) == 0 {
398			return map[string]progressRecord{}, nil, true, nil
399		}
400		var entries []json.RawMessage
401		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &entries); err != nil {
402			return nil, nil, false, failure("invalid-workflow-progress")
403		}
404		byID := make(map[string]progressRecord, len(entries))
405		var allActivity []time.Time
406		allKnown := true
407		for _, entry := range entries {
408			object, err := decodeObject(entry)
409			if err != nil {
410				allKnown = false
411				continue
412			}
413			agentID, okAgent := requiredString(object, "agentId")
414			if !okAgent || validateID(agentID, "") != nil {
415				allKnown = false
416				continue
417			}
418			isolation, okIsolation := requiredString(object, "isolation")
419			state, okState := requiredString(object, "state")
420			valid := okIsolation && okState
421			if _, duplicate := byID[agentID]; duplicate {
422				return nil, nil, false, failure("duplicate-agent-progress")
423			}
424			queued, queuedKnown := optionalEpochMillis(object, "queuedAt")
425			started, startedKnown := optionalEpochMillis(object, "startedAt")
426			last, lastKnown := optionalEpochMillis(object, "lastProgressAt")
427			known := queuedKnown && startedKnown && lastKnown
428			if !queued.IsZero() && !started.IsZero() && started.Before(queued) {
429				known = false
430			}
431			if !started.IsZero() && !last.IsZero() && last.Before(started) {
432				known = false
433			}
434			activity := nonZeroTimes(queued, started, last)
435			byID[agentID] = progressRecord{
436				agentID: agentID, isolation: strings.ToLower(isolation), state: strings.ToLower(state), valid: valid,
437				activity: activity, timeKnown: known,
438			}
439			allActivity = append(allActivity, activity...)
440			allKnown = allKnown && known
441		}
442		return byID, allActivity, allKnown, nil
443	}

445	func timestampFields(object map[string]json.RawMessage, stringKeys, millisKeys []string) ([]time.Time, bool) {
446		known := true
447		var values []time.Time
448		for _, key := range stringKeys {
449			value, ok := optionalTimestamp(object, key)
450			known = known && ok
451			if !value.IsZero() {

465	func optionalEpochMillis(object map[string]json.RawMessage, key string) (time.Time, bool) {
466		raw, present := object[key]

477		}
478		return time.UnixMilli(millis).UTC(), true
479	}

617	func journalFacts(events []journalEvent, workflowID, runID, agentID string) (started, result bool, startedAt, resultAt time.Time, timesKnown bool) {
618		timesKnown = true
619		startedCount, resultCount := 0, 0
620		for _, event := range events {
621			if event.workflowID != workflowID || event.runID != runID || event.agentID != agentID {
622				continue
623			}
624			switch event.kind {
625			case "started":
626				startedCount++
627				startedAt = event.at
628			case "result":
629				resultCount++
630				resultAt = event.at
631			}
632			timesKnown = timesKnown && event.timeKnown
633		}
634		started, result = startedCount == 1, resultCount == 1
635		if startedCount > 1 || resultCount > 1 || (started && result && resultAt.Before(startedAt)) {
636			timesKnown = false
637		}
638		return
639	}

676	func (a *Adapter) readStable(path string, limit int64) ([]byte, fs.FileInfo, error) {
677		info, err := os.Lstat(path)

684	func (a *Adapter) readStableWithInfo(path string, before fs.FileInfo, limit int64) ([]byte, fs.FileInfo, error) {
685		if !safeMetadataInfo(path, before, false) {
686			return nil, nil, failure("unsafe-metadata")
687		}
688		first, opened, err := readBounded(path, limit)
689		if err != nil {
690			return nil, nil, err
691		}
692		if a.afterRead != nil {
693			a.afterRead(path)
694		}
695		after, err := os.Lstat(path)
696		if err != nil || !safeMetadataInfo(path, after, false) || !os.SameFile(before, after) ||
697			before.Size() != after.Size() || !before.ModTime().Equal(after.ModTime()) ||
698			!os.SameFile(before, opened) {
699			return nil, nil, failure("metadata-mutated")
700		}
701		second, reopened, err := readBounded(path, limit)
702		if err != nil {
703			return nil, nil, err
704		}
705		if !os.SameFile(before, reopened) || !bytes.Equal(first, second) {
706			return nil, nil, failure("metadata-mutated")
707		}
708		return first, after, nil
709	}

711	func readBounded(path string, limit int64) ([]byte, fs.FileInfo, error) {
712		file, err := os.Open(path)
713		if err != nil {
714			return nil, nil, failure("unsafe-metadata")
715		}
716		defer file.Close()
717		info, err := file.Stat()
718		if err != nil || !info.Mode().IsRegular() || info.Size() > limit {
719			if err == nil && info.Size() > limit {
720				return nil, nil, failure("metadata-bound")
721			}
722			return nil, nil, failure("unsafe-metadata")
723		}
724		data, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(file, limit+1))
725		if err != nil {
726			return nil, nil, failure("unsafe-metadata")
727		}
728		if int64(len(data)) > limit {
729			return nil, nil, failure("metadata-bound")
730		}
731		return data, info, nil
732	}

734	func (a *Adapter) directories(path string, total *int, maximum int) ([]string, error) {
735		entries, err := os.ReadDir(path)
736		if err != nil {
737			return nil, failure("unsafe-metadata")
738		}
739		var names []string
740		for _, entry := range entries {
741			if !entry.IsDir() {
742				if entry.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
743					return nil, failure("unsafe-metadata")
744				}
745				continue
746			}
747			name := entry.Name()
748			if err := pathx.ValidateComponent(name); err != nil {
749				return nil, failure("invalid-id")
750			}
751			child, err := fixedChild(path, name)
752			if err != nil {
753				return nil, failure("invalid-id")
754			}
755			info, err := os.Lstat(child)
756			if err != nil || !safeMetadataInfo(child, info, true) {
757				return nil, failure("unsafe-metadata")
758			}
759			*total++
760			if *total > maximum {
761				return nil, failure("metadata-bound")
762			}
763			names = append(names, name)
764		}
765		sort.Strings(names)
766		return names, nil
767	}
768	
769	func safeOptionalDirectory(path string) (bool, error) {
770		info, err := os.Lstat(path)
771		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
772			return false, nil
773		}
774		if err != nil || !safeMetadataInfo(path, info, true) {
775			return false, failure("unsafe-metadata")
776		}
777		return true, nil
778	}

821	func validateWorktreePath(query ephemeral.SourceQuery, raw string) (string, bool, error) {
822		if raw == "" || strings.ContainsRune(raw, '\x00') || !filepath.IsAbs(raw) || filepath.Clean(raw) != raw {
823			return "", false, failure("invalid-worktree-path")
824		}
825		canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(raw)
826		if err != nil {
827			return "", false, failure("invalid-worktree-path")
828		}
829		insideRepository, err := pathx.Contains(query.Repository.Root, canonical)
830		if err != nil {
831			return "", false, failure("invalid-worktree-path")
832		}
833		if !insideRepository {
834			return canonical, false, nil
835		}
836		harnessRoot := filepath.Join(query.Repository.Root, ".claude", "worktrees")
837		insideHarness, err := pathx.IsChild(harnessRoot, canonical)
838		if err != nil || !insideHarness {
839			return "", false, failure("invalid-worktree-path")
840		}
841		for _, target := range query.Targets {
842			candidate, candidateErr := pathx.Canonical(target.Path)
843			if candidateErr == nil && candidate == canonical {
844				return canonical, true, nil
845			}
846		}
847		return canonical, true, nil

850	func decodeObject(data []byte) (map[string]json.RawMessage, error) {
851		decoder := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(data))
852		opening, err := decoder.Token()
853		if err != nil || opening != json.Delim('{') {
854			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode object")
855		}
856		object := make(map[string]json.RawMessage)
857		for decoder.More() {
858			token, err := decoder.Token()
859			if err != nil {
860				return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode object key")
861			}
862			key, ok := token.(string)
863			if !ok {
864				return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode object key")
865			}
866			if _, duplicate := object[key]; duplicate {
867				return nil, fmt.Errorf("duplicate JSON field")
868			}
869			var raw json.RawMessage
870			if err := decoder.Decode(&raw); err != nil {
871				return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode object value")
872			}
873			object[key] = raw
874		}
875		closing, err := decoder.Token()
876		if err != nil || closing != json.Delim('}') {
877			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode object close")
878		}
879		var extra any
880		if err := decoder.Decode(&extra); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
881			return nil, fmt.Errorf("extra JSON value")
882		}
883		return object, nil
884	}

886	func requiredString(object map[string]json.RawMessage, key string) (string, bool) {
887		raw, ok := object[key]
888		if !ok {
889			return "", false
890		}
891		var value string
892		if json.Unmarshal(raw, &value) != nil || value == "" {
893			return "", false
894		}
895		return value, true
896	}

903				continue
904			}

906			if !ok || (found && candidate != value) {

908			}
909			value, found = candidate, true
910		}
911		return value, found
912	}

969	func (a *Adapter) rejectDuplicateClaims(result *ephemeral.SourceResult) {
970		byPath := make(map[string][]int)
971		byIdentity := make(map[string][]int)
972		for i, claim := range result.Claims {
973			byPath[claim.WorktreePath] = append(byPath[claim.WorktreePath], i)
974			identity := strings.Join([]string{claim.Provider, claim.SessionID, claim.RunID, claim.AgentID}, "\x00")
975			byIdentity[identity] = append(byIdentity[identity], i)
976		}
977		mark := func(groups map[string][]int, code, message string) {
978			for _, indices := range groups {
979				if len(indices) < 2 {
980					continue
981				}
982				for _, index := range indices {
983					result.Claims[index].Unique = ephemeral.KnownFact(false)
984				}
985				result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ephemeral.Diagnostic{
986					Source: providerName, Code: code, Message: message,
987				})
988			}
989		}
990		mark(byPath, "duplicate-worktree-claim", "multiple provider claims name one worktree path")
991		mark(byIdentity, "duplicate-provider-identity", "one provider run and agent identity names multiple worktree paths")
992	}

120	func (a *Adapter) Collect(ctx context.Context, query ephemeral.SourceQuery) ephemeral.SourceResult {
121		result := ephemeral.SourceResult{Provider: providerName, Complete: true}
122		capability := ephemeral.Capability{Name: "claude-workflow-metadata", Available: true, Detail: "bounded local metadata"}
123		result.Capabilities = []ephemeral.Capability{capability}
124		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
125			return a.failed(result, "canceled")
126		}
127		if err := a.validateLimits(); err != nil {
128			return a.failed(result, "metadata-bound")
129		}
130		rootInfo, err := os.Lstat(a.root)
131		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
132			result.Capabilities[0].Detail = "metadata root absent"
133			return result
134		}
135		if err != nil || !safeMetadataInfo(a.root, rootInfo, true) {
136			return a.failed(result, "unsafe-metadata")
137		}
138	
139		var used counts
140		projects, err := a.directories(a.root, &used.projects, a.limits.MaxProjects)
141		if err != nil {
142			return a.failed(result, failureCode(err))
143		}
144		for _, project := range projects {
145			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
146				return a.failed(result, "canceled")
147			}
148			projectPath, err := fixedChild(a.root, project)
149			if err != nil {
150				return a.failed(result, "invalid-id")
151			}
152			sessions, err := a.directories(projectPath, &used.sessions, a.limits.MaxSessions)
153			if err != nil {
154				return a.failed(result, failureCode(err))
155			}

161				result.Claims = append(result.Claims, claims...)

165		a.rejectDuplicateClaims(&result)

168			if left.WorktreePath != right.WorktreePath {

173			}

179	func (a *Adapter) failed(result ephemeral.SourceResult, code string) ephemeral.SourceResult {
180		result.Complete = false
181		result.Claims = nil
182		result.Capabilities[0].Available = false
183		result.Capabilities[0].Detail = "metadata could not be safely verified"
184		result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ephemeral.Diagnostic{
185			Source: providerName, Code: code, Message: diagnosticMessage(code),
186		})
187		return result
188	}

190	func diagnosticMessage(code string) string {
191		switch code {
192		case "metadata-bound":
193			return "provider metadata exceeded a fixed V1 bound"
194		case "metadata-mutated":
195			return "provider metadata changed while it was inspected"
196		case "unsafe-metadata":
197			return "provider metadata was not a private regular non-link path"
198		case "invalid-workflow":
199			return "workflow metadata has an invalid required field"
200		case "invalid-agent-mapping":
201			return "agent mapping metadata has an invalid required field"
202		case "invalid-journal":
203			return "workflow journal has an invalid required record"
204		case "invalid-worktree-path":
205			return "agent mapping contains an invalid or unrelated worktree path"
206		case "invalid-id":
207			return "provider metadata contains an invalid identifier"
208		case "canceled":
209			return "provider metadata inspection was canceled"
210		default:
211			return "provider metadata could not be safely verified"
212		}
213	}

215	func (a *Adapter) validateLimits() error {
216		values := []int{a.limits.MaxProjects, a.limits.MaxSessions, a.limits.MaxWorkflows, a.limits.MaxAgents, a.limits.MaxJournalRecords}
217		for _, value := range values {
218			if value < 0 {
219				return failure("metadata-bound")
220			}
221		}
222		if a.limits.MaxJSONBytes <= 0 || a.limits.MaxJournalBytes <= 0 {
223			return failure("metadata-bound")
224		}
225		return nil
226	}

617	func journalFacts(events []journalEvent, workflowID, runID, agentID string) (started, result bool, startedAt, resultAt time.Time, timesKnown bool) {
618		timesKnown = true
619		startedCount, resultCount := 0, 0
620		for _, event := range events {
621			if event.workflowID != workflowID || event.runID != runID || event.agentID != agentID {
622				continue
623			}
624			switch event.kind {
625			case "started":
626				startedCount++
627				startedAt = event.at
628			case "result":
629				resultCount++
630				resultAt = event.at
631			}
632			timesKnown = timesKnown && event.timeKnown
633		}
634		started, result = startedCount == 1, resultCount == 1
635		if startedCount > 1 || resultCount > 1 || (started && result && resultAt.Before(startedAt)) {
636			timesKnown = false
637		}
638		return
639	}

684	func (a *Adapter) readStableWithInfo(path string, before fs.FileInfo, limit int64) ([]byte, fs.FileInfo, error) {
685		if !safeMetadataInfo(path, before, false) {
686			return nil, nil, failure("unsafe-metadata")
687		}
688		first, opened, err := readBounded(path, limit)
689		if err != nil {

691		}
692		if a.afterRead != nil {
693			a.afterRead(path)

695		after, err := os.Lstat(path)
696		if err != nil || !safeMetadataInfo(path, after, false) || !os.SameFile(before, after) ||
697			before.Size() != after.Size() || !before.ModTime().Equal(after.ModTime()) ||
698			!os.SameFile(before, opened) {
699			return nil, nil, failure("metadata-mutated")
700		}
701		second, reopened, err := readBounded(path, limit)
702		if err != nil {
703			return nil, nil, err
704		}
705		if !os.SameFile(before, reopened) || !bytes.Equal(first, second) {
706			return nil, nil, failure("metadata-mutated")
707		}
708		return first, after, nil
709	}

711	func readBounded(path string, limit int64) ([]byte, fs.FileInfo, error) {
712		file, err := os.Open(path)
713		if err != nil {
714			return nil, nil, failure("unsafe-metadata")
715		}
716		defer file.Close()
717		info, err := file.Stat()
718		if err != nil || !info.Mode().IsRegular() || info.Size() > limit {
719			if err == nil && info.Size() > limit {
720				return nil, nil, failure("metadata-bound")
721			}
722			return nil, nil, failure("unsafe-metadata")
723		}
724		data, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(file, limit+1))
725		if err != nil {
726			return nil, nil, failure("unsafe-metadata")
727		}
728		if int64(len(data)) > limit {
729			return nil, nil, failure("metadata-bound")
730		}
731		return data, info, nil

830		if err != nil {

851		decoder := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(data))
852		opening, err := decoder.Token()
853		if err != nil || opening != json.Delim('{') {
854			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode object")
855		}
856		object := make(map[string]json.RawMessage)
857		for decoder.More() {
858			token, err := decoder.Token()
859			if err != nil {
860				return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode object key")
861			}
862			key, ok := token.(string)

866			if _, duplicate := object[key]; duplicate {

868			}

870			if err := decoder.Decode(&raw); err != nil {
871				return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode object value")
872			}
873			object[key] = raw
874		}
875		closing, err := decoder.Token()

1	package artifact

3	import (
4		"context"
5		"sort"

8		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/pathx"

11	// WorktreeInspection is the read-only aggregate of every artifact intent for a
12	// checkout. Ready means each intent was explicitly discarded or finalized to a
13	// commit still reachable from a recovery ref; it never changes an intent.
14	type WorktreeInspection struct {
15		IntentCount int      `json:"intent_count"`
16		Status      Status   `json:"status,omitempty"`
17		Ready       bool     `json:"ready"`
18		IntentIDs   []string `json:"intent_ids"`
19	}
20	
21	// InspectWorktrees groups all intents once and verifies finalized commit
22	// reachability without reconciling or writing state.
23	func InspectWorktrees(ctx context.Context, store *Store) (map[string]WorktreeInspection, error) {
24		intents, err := store.List()
25		if err != nil {
26			return nil, err
27		}
28		out := map[string]WorktreeInspection{}
29		for _, intent := range intents {
30			path, err := pathx.Canonical(intent.WorktreePath)
31			if err != nil {
32				continue
33			}
34			inspection, exists := out[path]
35			if !exists {
36				inspection.Ready = true
37			}
38			inspection.IntentCount++
39			inspection.IntentIDs = append(inspection.IntentIDs, intent.ID)
40			if statusPriority(intent.Status) >= statusPriority(inspection.Status) {
41				inspection.Status = intent.Status
42			}
43			ready := intent.Status == Discarded ||
44				(intent.Status == Finalized && intent.ArtifactCommit != "" && CommitReachable(ctx, intent))
45			inspection.Ready = inspection.Ready && ready
46			out[path] = inspection
47		}
48		for path, inspection := range out {
49			sort.Strings(inspection.IntentIDs)
50			out[path] = inspection
51		}
52		return out, nil
53	}
54	
55	// CommitReachable reports whether an intent's artifact commit is retained by
56	// its checkout HEAD, task branch, or base. It is read-only and shared by
57	// integration enforcement and closeout evidence.
58	func CommitReachable(ctx context.Context, intent Intent) bool {
59		refs := []struct {
60			dir string
61			ref string
62		}{
63			{intent.WorktreePath, "HEAD"},
64			{intent.RepoPath, intent.Branch},
65			{intent.RepoPath, intent.Base},
66		}
67		for _, candidate := range refs {
68			if candidate.dir == "" || candidate.ref == "" {
69				continue
70			}
71			if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, candidate.dir, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", intent.ArtifactCommit, candidate.ref); err == nil {
72				return true
73			}
74		}
75		return false
76	}
77	
78	func statusPriority(status Status) int {
79		switch status {
80		case Discarded, Finalized:
81			return 1
82		case Armed:
83			return 2
84		case Finalizing:
85			return 3
86		case Failed:
87			return 4
88		default:
89			return 0
90		}
91	}
92

9		"strings"

11	)

13	// State is where a change stream sits in its lifecycle.
14	type State string
15	
16	const (
17		// Hot: worktree and branch exist, a runtime session is open, actively worked on.
18		Hot State = "hot"
19		// Warm: worktree and branch kept, runtime closed. Back within days.
20		Warm State = "warm"
21		// Cold: committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstructible anywhere.
22		Cold State = "cold"
23		// Done: merged. Kept only until the entry is reaped.
24		Done State = "done"
25	)
26	
27	// States lists the lifecycle in order, for help text and validation.
28	var States = []State{Hot, Warm, Cold, Done}
29	
30	// ParseState validates a user-supplied state name.
31	func ParseState(s string) (State, error) {
32		got := State(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)))
33		for _, valid := range States {
34			if got == valid {
35				return got, nil
36			}
37		}
38		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown state %q: want one of %s", s, JoinStates(", "))
39	}
40	
41	// JoinStates renders the valid state names.
42	func JoinStates(sep string) string {
43		parts := make([]string, len(States))
44		for i, s := range States {
45			parts[i] = string(s)
46		}
47		return strings.Join(parts, sep)
48	}
49	
50	// Icon is the glyph shown in the inventory.
51	func (s State) Icon() string {
52		switch s {
53		case Hot:
54			return "🔥"
55		case Warm:
56			return "🌤"
57		case Cold:
58			return "❄️"
59		case Done:
60			return "✅"
61		}
62		return "?"
63	}
64	
65	// Label is the uppercase column form.
66	func (s State) Label() string { return strings.ToUpper(string(s)) }
67	
68	// CheckoutMode is how a task occupies the repository filesystem.
69	type CheckoutMode string
70	
71	const (
72		// ModeWorktree owns a linked worktree and branch.
73		ModeWorktree CheckoutMode = "worktree"
74		// ModeBranch uses a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout.
75		ModeBranch CheckoutMode = "branch"
76		// ModeDirect tracks ad-hoc work on the branch already checked out in the
77		// canonical repo — usually main — without creating a branch or worktree.
78		ModeDirect CheckoutMode = "direct"
79	)
80	
81	// Task is one change stream. Field names are the TOML keys.
82	type Task struct {
83		// ID is derived from repo and branch; it is the filename stem and is not
84		// stored inside the file.
85		ID string `toml:"-"`
86	
87		// Name is the human label ("atp security recovery").
88		Name string `toml:"name"`
89		// Repo is the repository's display name.
90		Repo string `toml:"repo"`
91		// RepoPath is the main checkout, the directory git commands run in.
92		RepoPath string `toml:"repo_path"`
93		// Branch is the change stream's identity — the one durable handle that
94		// survives every machine, worktree and runtime.
95		Branch string `toml:"branch"`
96		// Base is the ref the branch was created from, recorded so `dev done` can
97		// integrate without re-guessing.
98		Base string `toml:"base"`
99		// WorktreePath is the linked checkout, empty when the task works directly
100		// in the main checkout or has gone cold.
101		WorktreePath string `toml:"worktree_path"`
102		// Mode says whether this task uses a worktree, a branch in the canonical
103		// checkout, or the current branch directly. Older entries infer it.
104		Mode CheckoutMode `toml:"mode"`
105	
106		State State `toml:"state"`
107		// Owner is the hostname that last held this task hot. One writer per
108		// branch at a time avoids two machines diverging the same history.
109		Owner string `toml:"owner"`
110		// Next is the single most valuable field in the file: what to do when you
111		// come back. Without it, parking a task still loses the thread.
112		Next string   `toml:"next"`
113		Note string   `toml:"note"`
114		Tags []string `toml:"tags"`
115	
116		// AgentSession reserves a resumable agent context ("claude:<uuid>"). The
117		// production start/park/resume flow does not yet capture or attach it.
118		AgentSession string `toml:"agent_session"`
119		// RuntimeHandle is the last known runtime session id (e.g. a Herdr
120		// workspace id). RuntimeName records which backend owns that opaque handle.
121		// Both are advisory and must be revalidated against live checkout coverage.
122		RuntimeHandle string `toml:"runtime_handle"`
123		RuntimeName   string `toml:"runtime_name"`
124	
125		Created time.Time `toml:"created"`
126		Updated time.Time `toml:"updated"`
127	}
128	
129	// EffectiveMode returns the explicit mode, or infers a legacy task. Before
130	// modes were recorded, a path meant worktree and no path meant a canonical
131	// branch task; direct mode is never guessed because it changes integration
132	// semantics and must be explicit.
133	func (t Task) EffectiveMode() CheckoutMode {
134		if t.Mode != "" {
135			return t.Mode
136		}
137		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
138			return ModeWorktree
139		}
140		return ModeBranch
141	}
142	
143	// Title is the display name, falling back to the branch when unnamed.
144	func (t Task) Title() string {
145		if t.Name != "" {
146			return t.Name
147		}
148		return t.Branch
149	}
150	
151	// OwnedBy reports whether host is this task's owner. An empty owner means
152	// unclaimed, which counts as owned by anyone.
153	func (t Task) OwnedBy(host string) bool { return t.Owner == "" || t.Owner == host }
154	
155	// Validate rejects a task that could not be acted on later.
156	func (t Task) Validate() error {
157		switch {
158		case t.Repo == "":
159			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo is required", t.ID)
160		case t.Branch == "":
161			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: branch is required", t.ID)
162		case t.RepoPath == "":
163			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo_path is required", t.ID)
164		}
165		if _, err := ParseState(string(t.State)); err != nil {
166			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
167		}
168		switch t.Mode {
169		case "", ModeWorktree, ModeBranch, ModeDirect:
170		default:
171			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: unknown mode %q", t.ID, t.Mode)
172		}
173		return nil
174	}

1	// Package pathx provides the path-safety checks shared by filesystem lifecycle
2	// operations. The checks are strict: a destination must be below its root, not
3	// merely share a string prefix with it, and symlinks are resolved before that
4	// decision is made.
5	package pathx
6	
7	import (
8		"errors"
9		"fmt"
10		"io/fs"
11		"os"
12		"path/filepath"
13		"slices"
14		"strings"
15	)
16	
17	var (
18		// ErrOutsideRoot reports a path that does not resolve below the requested root.
19		ErrOutsideRoot = errors.New("path is outside root")
20		// ErrRoot reports an operation that named the root itself rather than a child.
21		ErrRoot = errors.New("path is the root itself")
22		// ErrTraversal reports an explicit .. component in an unclean input path.
23		ErrTraversal = errors.New("path contains parent traversal")
24		// ErrInvalidComponent reports a value that is not one filesystem component.
25		ErrInvalidComponent = errors.New("invalid path component")
26	)
27	
28	// Canonical returns an absolute, clean path with symlinks resolved. If the final
29	// path does not exist yet, it resolves the nearest existing ancestor and then
30	// appends the missing suffix. This is the form needed to validate a destination
31	// before creating or moving anything into it.
32	func Canonical(path string) (string, error) {
33		if path == "" {
34			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonical path: empty path")
35		}
36		absolute, err := filepath.Abs(path)
37		if err != nil {
38			return "", fmt.Errorf("make %q absolute: %w", path, err)
39		}
40		absolute = filepath.Clean(absolute)
41	
42		probe := absolute
43		var missing []string
44		for {
45			resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(probe)
46			if err == nil {
47				slices.Reverse(missing)
48				parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
49				return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
50			}
51			if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
52				return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: %w", path, err)
53			}
54			// EvalSymlinks reports ErrNotExist both for a genuinely missing component
55			// and for a symlink whose target is missing. Treating the latter as an
56			// ordinary lexical suffix would make an escape look as though it remained
57			// below its root. Resolve the link target explicitly before appending the
58			// still-missing suffix.
59			if info, lstatErr := os.Lstat(probe); lstatErr == nil && info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
60				target, readErr := os.Readlink(probe)
61				if readErr != nil {
62					return "", fmt.Errorf("read unresolved symlink %q: %w", probe, readErr)
63				}
64				if hasParentTraversal(target) {
65					return "", fmt.Errorf("unresolved symlink %q target %q: %w", probe, target, ErrTraversal)
66				}
67				if !filepath.IsAbs(target) {
68					target = filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(probe), target)
69				}
70				resolved, resolveErr := Canonical(target)
71				if resolveErr != nil {
72					return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve target of %q: %w", probe, resolveErr)
73				}
74				slices.Reverse(missing)
75				parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
76				return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
77			} else if lstatErr != nil && !errors.Is(lstatErr, fs.ErrNotExist) {
78				return "", fmt.Errorf("inspect unresolved path %q: %w", probe, lstatErr)
79			}
80			parent := filepath.Dir(probe)
81			if parent == probe {
82				return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: no existing ancestor: %w", path, err)
83			}
84			missing = append(missing, filepath.Base(probe))
85			probe = parent
86		}
87	}
88	
89	// CanonicalChild returns candidate in canonical form when it resolves strictly
90	// below root. It rejects root itself, lexical .. traversal, sibling-prefix
91	// confusion, and paths that escape through a symlink.
92	func CanonicalChild(root, candidate string) (string, error) {
93		if hasParentTraversal(candidate) {
94			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", candidate, ErrTraversal)
95		}
96		canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
97		if err != nil {
98			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize root: %w", err)
99		}
100		canonicalCandidate, err := Canonical(candidate)
101		if err != nil {
102			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize candidate: %w", err)
103		}
104	
105		rel, err := filepath.Rel(canonicalRoot, canonicalCandidate)
106		if err != nil {
107			// Rel only fails when the two paths cannot be expressed relative to one
108			// another — most often different Windows volumes. That is a definitive
109			// "not below root", not a filesystem error to surface.
110			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q is not below %q: %w", candidate, root, ErrOutsideRoot)
111		}
112		switch {
113		case rel == ".":
114			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", candidate, ErrRoot)
115		case filepath.IsAbs(rel), rel == "..", strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator)):
116			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q is not below %q: %w", candidate, root, ErrOutsideRoot)
117		default:
118			return canonicalCandidate, nil
119		}
120	}
121	
122	// IsChild reports whether candidate resolves strictly below root. Policy
123	// rejections are returned as false without hiding filesystem errors.
124	func IsChild(root, candidate string) (bool, error) {
125		_, err := CanonicalChild(root, candidate)
126		if err == nil {
127			return true, nil
128		}
129		if errors.Is(err, ErrOutsideRoot) || errors.Is(err, ErrRoot) || errors.Is(err, ErrTraversal) {
130			return false, nil
131		}
132		return false, err
133	}
134	
135	// Contains reports whether candidate is root itself or resolves below it.
136	func Contains(root, candidate string) (bool, error) {
137		canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
138		if err != nil {
139			return false, err
140		}
141		canonicalCandidate, err := Canonical(candidate)
142		if err != nil {
143			return false, err
144		}
145		if canonicalRoot == canonicalCandidate {
146			return true, nil
147		}
148		return IsChild(canonicalRoot, canonicalCandidate)
149	}
150	
151	// ValidateComponent requires a non-empty relative value containing exactly one
152	// path component. Both slash styles are rejected so state synced between Unix
153	// and Windows cannot acquire a different meaning on another host.
154	func ValidateComponent(component string) error {
155		switch {
156		case strings.TrimSpace(component) == "":
157			return fmt.Errorf("empty component: %w", ErrInvalidComponent)
158		case strings.ContainsRune(component, '\x00'):
159			return fmt.Errorf("component contains NUL: %w", ErrInvalidComponent)
160		case component == "." || component == "..":
161			return fmt.Errorf("component %q is reserved: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
162		case filepath.IsAbs(component) || filepath.VolumeName(component) != "" || driveQualified(component):
163			return fmt.Errorf("component %q is absolute or drive-qualified: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
164		case strings.ContainsAny(component, `/\\`):
165			return fmt.Errorf("component %q contains a path separator: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
166		case filepath.Clean(component) != component || filepath.Base(component) != component:
167			return fmt.Errorf("component %q is not a single clean name: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
168		default:
169			return nil
170		}
171	}
172

176	// single component.
177	func JoinChild(root string, components ...string) (string, error) {

768			a.afterRead(path)
769		}
770		after, err := os.Lstat(path)
771		if err != nil || !stableDirectoryInfo(path, before, opened, after) {
772			return nil, failure("metadata-mutated")
773		}
774		second, reopened, err := readDirectorySnapshot(path, maximum)
775		if err != nil {
776			return nil, err
777		}
778		if !os.SameFile(before, reopened) || !directoryEntriesEqual(first, second) {
779			return nil, failure("metadata-mutated")
780		}
781		for _, entry := range second {
782			if err := pathx.ValidateComponent(entry.Name()); err != nil {
783				return nil, failure("invalid-id")
784			}
785			child := filepath.Join(path, entry.Name())
786			info, err := os.Lstat(child)
787			if err != nil || !safeMetadataInfo(child, info, info.IsDir()) {
788				return nil, failure("unsafe-metadata")
789			}
790		}
791		final, err := os.Lstat(path)
792		if err != nil || !stableDirectoryInfo(path, before, reopened, final) {
793			return nil, failure("metadata-mutated")
794		}
795		third, finalOpened, err := readDirectorySnapshot(path, maximum)
796		if err != nil {
797			return nil, err
798		}
799		if !stableDirectoryInfo(path, before, finalOpened, finalOpened) || !directoryEntriesEqual(second, third) {
800			return nil, failure("metadata-mutated")
801		}
802		return third, nil
803	}
804	
805	func readDirectorySnapshot(path string, maximum int) ([]fs.DirEntry, fs.FileInfo, error) {
806		readLimit, err := boundPlusOne(maximum)
807		if err != nil {
808			return nil, nil, err
809		}
810		directory, err := os.Open(path)
811		if err != nil {
812			return nil, nil, failure("unsafe-metadata")
813		}
814		defer directory.Close()
815		info, err := directory.Stat()
816		if err != nil || !safeMetadataInfo(path, info, true) {
817			return nil, nil, failure("unsafe-metadata")
818		}
819		entries, readErr := directory.ReadDir(readLimit)
820		if readErr != nil && !errors.Is(readErr, io.EOF) {
821			return nil, nil, failure("unsafe-metadata")
822		}
823		if len(entries) > maximum {
824			return nil, nil, failure("metadata-bound")
825		}
826		sort.Slice(entries, func(i, j int) bool { return entries[i].Name() < entries[j].Name() })
827		return entries, info, nil
828	}
829	
830	func boundPlusOne(value int) (int, error) {
831		if value < 0 || value == int(^uint(0)>>1) {
832			return 0, failure("metadata-bound")
833		}
834		return value + 1, nil
835	}
836	
837	func stableDirectoryInfo(path string, expected, opened, current fs.FileInfo) bool {
838		return safeMetadataInfo(path, current, true) && os.SameFile(expected, opened) && os.SameFile(expected, current) &&
839			expected.Size() == current.Size() && expected.ModTime().Equal(current.ModTime())
840	}
841	
842	func directoryEntriesEqual(left, right []fs.DirEntry) bool {
843		if len(left) != len(right) {
844			return false
845		}
846		for i := range left {
847			if left[i].Name() != right[i].Name() || left[i].Type() != right[i].Type() || left[i].IsDir() != right[i].IsDir() {
848				return false
849			}
850		}
851		return true
852	}
853	
854	func (a *Adapter) directories(path string, total *int, maximum int) ([]string, error) {
855		entries, err := a.readDirectory(path, maximum)
856		if err != nil {
857			return nil, err
858		}
859		var names []string
860		for _, entry := range entries {
861			if !entry.IsDir() {
862				if entry.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
863					return nil, failure("unsafe-metadata")
864				}
865				continue
866			}
867			name := entry.Name()
868			if err := pathx.ValidateComponent(name); err != nil {
869				return nil, failure("invalid-id")
870			}
871			child, err := fixedChild(path, name)
872			if err != nil {
873				return nil, failure("invalid-id")
874			}
875			info, err := os.Lstat(child)
876			if err != nil || !safeMetadataInfo(child, info, true) {
877				return nil, failure("unsafe-metadata")
878			}
879			*total++
880			if *total > maximum {
881				return nil, failure("metadata-bound")
882			}
883			names = append(names, name)
884		}
885		sort.Strings(names)
886		return names, nil
887	}

244		type coveringSession struct {
245			Runtime string

252			if rt == nil || rt.Name() == "none" || seenRuntimes[rt.Name()] {
253				continue
254			}
255			seenRuntimes[rt.Name()] = true
256			if !rt.Available() {
257				continue
258			}
259			sessions, err := rt.List(ctx)

261				return runtimeEvidence{}, err
262			}
263			for _, session := range sessions {

265				covers := false

267					inside, err := pathx.Contains(target.Path, path)
268					if err != nil {

270					}
271					if inside {
272						covers = true
273					}
274				}
275				if covers {
276					sort.Strings(paths)
277					covering = append(covering, coveringSession{Runtime: rt.Name(), Handle: session.Handle, Paths: paths})
278				}
279			}
280		}
281		sort.Slice(covering, func(i, j int) bool {
282			if covering[i].Runtime != covering[j].Runtime {

284			}
285			return covering[i].Handle < covering[j].Handle
286		})
287		return runtimeEvidence{

289		}, nil

        for x in v.values(): walk(x)
    elif isinstance(v,list):
        for x in v: walk(x)
walk(report)
print('schema',report['schema_version'],'summary',report['summary'],'diagnostics',[d['code'] for d in report['diagnostics']])
PY

# agent-history-hygiene

Keep agent chat transcripts and plan files committed together with the
code they produced, without leaking secrets. Pairs with the
`redact-agent-secrets` + `gitleaks` pre-commit hooks the skill installs.

Three surfaces, separated by purpose:

| Surface                          | Question it answers                                          |
|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| `find-session.sh`                | "Which transcript / plan file is *my* current session?"      |
| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`       | "Which agent files belong in the next commit?"               |
| `bootstrap-project.sh`           | "How do I get pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor into a repo?" |
| `scan-staged.sh`                 | "Is there a leaked secret in what I'm about to commit?"      |
| `probe-specstory-redaction.py`   | "What does SpecStory already redact, so we don't redo it?"   |
| `references/remediation.md`      | "I already pushed a secret — now what?"                      |

## Core invariants

1. **Agent transcripts and plan files are committed alongside the diff
   that produced them.** Never add them to `.gitignore`. An agent that
   drops these from a commit has broken the user's review trail.
2. **Rotate at the provider before any git rewrite.** The only act
   that revokes a leaked credential is rotation. History rewriting
   scrubs bytes on one clone and leaves them on every other.
3. **`git push --force` against a shared branch is never the fix for a
   leak.** At best it's useless; at worst it destroys teammate work and
   silently re-introduces the secret when someone merges their old
   history back.

## When to use this skill

Use it when the user (or you) surface any of:

- "Commit my chat" / "save the specstory session" / "include the plan
  file in this commit" / "把 plan 跟 specstory 一起 commit 進去".
- You see dirty `.specstory/history/*.md`, `.claude/plans/*.md`,
  `.cursor/plans/*.md`, or any other configured agent artifact during
  `git status` and you're about to commit a feature.
- "Scrub this transcript" / "redact my key" / "gitleaks flagged my
  chat history".
- "Set up pre-commit for this repo" / "I'm starting a new project — how
  do I get the hook stack?" / "bootstrap secret scanning here".
- "I pushed a `.env`" / "a secret went to main" / "do I need to force
  push?" — the agent must steer to `references/remediation.md` and
  stop the user from force-pushing reflexively.

## When NOT to use

- The user explicitly wants agent transcripts **excluded** from the
  repo. Respect that; suggest a one-liner `.gitignore` addition and
  skip this skill entirely.
- The leak is already on a shared `main`/release branch. Do **not**
  offer to rewrite history — jump to `references/remediation.md` §5.
- The project genuinely has no agent session (no `.specstory/`, no
  `.claude/plans/`, etc.). Nothing to stage.
- Single-file, single-commit hygiene that the agent handles without any
  script (e.g., adding a missing trailing newline).

## Integration with existing infrastructure

This skill sits **on top of** any chezmoi-managed stack the user
already has. It does not duplicate:

- **chezmoi's global `core.hooksPath`** (`~/.config/git/hooks/pre-commit`)
  — that wrapper runs the repo's `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and then
  optionally `gitleaks git --staged`. The skill bootstraps the repo-level
  config the wrapper expects to find.
- **chezmoi's `.gitleaks.toml`** — the user's config already carries
  curated rules for common API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Supabase,
  Linear, WakaTime, Cursor, HuggingFace, Notion, Tailscale, Clash /
  V2Ray tokens). The skill's `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` ships the
  same rule IDs so `.gitleaksignore` / allowlist tweaks stay portable.
- **the pinned `redact-agent-secrets` hook** — the redactor ships as a
  pinned pre-commit hook from this repo
  (`.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`), so every consuming repo gets fixes via
  `pre-commit autoupdate` instead of a vendored copy that drifts. Details
  in [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md).

What this skill **adds**:

- Agent-facing discipline (this `SKILL.md` + `references/remediation.md`).
- A single-command project bootstrap (`bootstrap-project.sh`) for repos
  without chezmoi or where the user wants the stack in one go.
- Session-discovery heuristics (`find-session.sh`) for the "find my
  current transcript among many" problem.
- An exit-code wrapper (`scan-staged.sh`) agents can branch on before
  committing.

## Workflow A: commit-time hygiene

Default flow when the agent is about to commit feature changes plus
chat/plan artifacts.

```bash
# 1. Make sure the agent knows which session is "ours" — mostly
#    relevant when multiple Claude/SpecStory sessions run in the repo.
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/find-session.sh

# 2. Stage code the usual way, then auto-add agent artifacts.
git add path/to/feature/file.ts
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh
# Use --session-only if you want ONLY the current SpecStory + newest plan;
# default stages every dirty *.md in every configured agent dir.

# 3. Belt-and-suspenders secret scan before commit. Exit 0 = clean.
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh || {
  # Exit 10/20: leaks found. Jump to references/remediation.md.
  echo "Leaks detected — see references/remediation.md before committing." >&2
  exit 1
}

# 4. Commit. pre-commit (installed by bootstrap) runs redact-agent-secrets
#    then gitleaks again as a catch-all.
git commit -m "feat: ..."
```

## Workflow B: bootstrap a new project

For repos that don't yet have `.pre-commit-config.yaml` / `.gitleaks.toml`
installed. Runs once per repo.

```bash
cd /path/to/new/project
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh \
  --install-hook            # optional: auto-stage on every commit

# Verify: shake out any existing issues in the working tree.
pre-commit run --all-files
```

What `bootstrap-project.sh` does:

1. Drops `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the repo
   (skips if already present unless `--force`). The redactor is a pinned
   remote hook (`repo: …/agent-skills`, `rev: ahh-v1.1.0`), **not** a
   vendored `scripts/redact_secrets.py` — so `pre-commit autoupdate`
   keeps it current everywhere.
2. Runs `pre-commit install` (or `uvx pre-commit@4 install` if
   pre-commit isn't on `PATH`).
3. Audits `.gitignore` / `.git/info/exclude` for patterns that would
   silently hide an agent artifact dir — warns without editing.
4. Checks `~/.claude/settings.json` for `plansDirectory`; prints the
   one-line patch if missing.
5. With `--install-hook`: writes a `prepare-commit-msg` hook that calls
   `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only --allow-empty` so every
   `git commit` auto-attaches the current session file.

Migrating a repo off the **old vendored layout** (a committed
`scripts/redact_secrets.py` + a `- repo: local` redact hook):

```bash
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh --migrate
```

removes the vendored script and rewrites the local hook into the pinned
remote hook, leaving your other hooks and `.gitleaks.toml` untouched
(idempotent; safe to re-run).

## Workflow C: post-leak remediation

When `scan-staged.sh` reports exit `10`/`20`, or the user says "I
committed / pushed a secret":

1. **STOP** the user from running `git push --force` reflexively.
2. Read `references/remediation.md` end-to-end.
3. Walk the user through **step 1 (rotate)** regardless of blast
   radius. Only after rotation does the question of scrubbing history
   become worth discussing.
4. Use the decision tree in the runbook to pick the right git action.

## Gotchas

- **SpecStory >= 2.4.0 already redacts on write — plan around it, not
  against it.** Since
  [PR #235](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/pull/235) shipped in
  v2.4.0 (2026-07-20), the CLI redacts secrets via the
  [Betterleaks](https://github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks) ruleset **by
  default**, covering both local markdown and cloud sync, writing
  `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`. Measured coverage is 36 of 54 class/context pairs;
  15 are ours alone (every webhook rule, plus every custom key in prose
  context — betterleaks catches many classes only in `KEY=value` form via its
  entropy-based `generic-api-key` rule). So: **keep this layer, but never
  rewrite what SpecStory already cleaned.** `redact_secrets.py` writes the
  same `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` sentinel and `.gitleaks.toml` allowlists it, so
  a cleaned transcript is left untouched and pre-commit stops demanding a
  re-`git add`. Full matrix + knobs in
  [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md).
  Only `[redaction] enabled` is configurable upstream — the PR's
  `extra_patterns` did not survive the Betterleaks rewrite, so repo-specific
  rules stay our job. For SpecStory older than 2.4.0 (or with redaction
  disabled), run `redact_secrets.py --fix --legacy`.
- **`plansDirectory` project-level sometimes ignored.** Claude Code
  issue [#19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537)
  reports project-level `plansDirectory` being ignored in some
  versions. After running a `/plan`, verify the file actually landed
  where you expected before relying on `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`
  picking it up. User-level config (`~/.claude/settings.json` with
  `"plansDirectory": "./.claude/plans"`) is the recommended default.
- **`gitleaks protect` is deprecated.** Since v8.19.0 use
  `gitleaks git --staged --redact` (pre-commit) and
  `gitleaks dir <path>` (working directory). The older commands still
  work but emit a deprecation notice. This skill uses the modern
  syntax everywhere.
- **`pre-commit install` is per-clone.** Each teammate must run
  `pre-commit install` in their own clone for hooks to fire. CI cannot
  be trusted as the single gate — it's second-chance, not last-chance.
- **Transcript files can be huge.** A long SpecStory session can exceed
  2 MB. The template bumps `check-added-large-files` to `--maxkb=2048`
  to avoid false positives, but a very long session can still overflow.
  If you hit the limit, rotate sessions (`specstory run claude`
  creates a fresh file) instead of raising the cap further.
- **Session-UUID divergence between SpecStory CLI and VS Code
  extension.** The extension autosaves into `.specstory/history/`
  continuously; the CLI (`specstory run claude`) creates one file per
  invocation. If both are active you can end up with two transcripts
  for what feels like "one session" — mtime-newest wins in
  `find-session.sh`.
- **Global `core.hooksPath` means bare repos aren't protected.** The
  chezmoi setup's global hook runs `.pre-commit-config.yaml` IF it
  exists — so a repo without `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has no
  protection. Run `bootstrap-project.sh` before the first commit with
  agent artifacts, not after.
- **Active SpecStory writer can defeat the redact loop.** The standard
  `git add → git commit → pre-commit auto-fixes → re-stage → re-commit`
  flow assumes the file is **quiescent** during the commit. SpecStory's
  `specstory_*_watch` daemon tails the agent transcript continuously,
  so if the chat captured `ps -axo args`-style output that contained an
  unrelated daemon's secret in argv (e.g. SpecStory's own
  `--cloud-token …` flag), every diagnostic command (`grep`, `sed -n
  '<line>p'`, `cat | head | tail`) prints the secret again, SpecStory
  appends it to the transcript, and the redact-then-restage cycle
  never converges. Symptom: pre-commit says "Successfully redacted N
  file(s)" but `gitleaks-system` immediately fails on the same line,
  re-running `git add && git commit` doesn't help, and `grep -c
  '<secret-prefix>' file` shows the count *increasing* over commit
  attempts. **Workaround**: a single atomic
  `python3 -c "<in-place re.sub>" && git add <file> && git commit -m
  "..."` pipeline so the index is frozen before any new specstory write
  lands. **Don't** print, grep, or diff the secret line during the
  recovery — every print echoes back into the transcript. Diagnose with
  `lsof <file>` (looking for `specstory_*` writers) instead. See
  `pitfalls/redact-secrets-loop-with-active-specstory-writer.md` in
  upstream chezmoi for the full debugging trail.
  **Fixed sub-case:** the *bare-phrase* variant of this loop — where the
  redactor's own `PRIVATE KEY` substring match kept flagging prose that
  merely *discusses* private keys (this skill's docs, or a chat about
  redaction) with **no real secret present** — no longer happens.
  `redact_secrets.py` now scopes to key *headers* (the
  `detect-private-key` BLACKLIST), so prose mentions are ignored and
  converge immediately. The atomic-commit workaround above is still
  needed for the harder case: a **real** secret an active writer keeps
  re-appending. When only the substring redactor (`redact-agent-secrets`)
  trips while `gitleaks` + `detect-private-key` pass, it's the false
  positive — verify with `gitleaks git --staged` and, if clean, commit
  with `SKIP=redact-agent-secrets` (keeps the real gates active).

## Available scripts

- **`scripts/find-session.sh [--format=specstory|claude|both] [--json]`**
  Discover the current agent session files for `$PWD`. TSV default,
  `--json` for structured callers. Never exits non-zero (always 0,
  empty fields signal absence).

- **`scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh [--session-only] [--include-all-plans] [--dry-run] [--allow-empty]`**
  `git add` the right agent artifacts before the next commit.
  `--session-only` stages only the current SpecStory + newest plan;
  default stages every dirty `*.md` in every configured artifact dir.
  Refuses to run if there are no code changes (prevents "commit just
  transcript"); override with `--allow-empty`.

- **`scripts/scan-staged.sh [--redact] [--verbose]`**
  Run `gitleaks git --staged` with agent-friendly exit codes
  (0 clean / 10 redacted / 20 leaks / 30 gitleaks missing). JSON lines
  on stdout, prose diagnostics on stderr.

- **`scripts/probe-specstory-redaction.py [--json] [--keep] [--dry-run]`**
  Measure which secret classes SpecStory's native redaction covers, by
  synthesizing a Claude Code session and rendering it twice (with and without
  `--no-redact-secrets`). Prints a coverage matrix and the residual set our
  layer must still handle. Exit 30 when specstory isn't installed.

- **`scripts/bootstrap-project.sh [--from-chezmoi] [--migrate] [--install-hook] [--force] [--dry-run]`**
  Install `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the current
  repo, wire the hook to the installed skill's redactor, then run
  `pre-commit install`. Audits
  `.gitignore` and `~/.claude/settings.json` for misconfigurations
  (warns, never silently edits).

## Bundled assets

- `assets/artifact-dirs.txt` — the canonical list of agent artifact
  directories (SpecStory, Claude plans, Cursor plans + rules, OpenCode
  plans, Spec-kit, Codex). Consumed by `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` and
  by `bootstrap-project.sh` when rendering the pre-commit `files:`
  regex.
- `assets/pre-commit-config.yaml.template` — minimal
  `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with `redact-agent-secrets` + gitleaks +
  standard hygiene hooks.
- `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` — portable subset of the chezmoi
  `.gitleaks.toml` with custom rule IDs + a path-scoped allowlist for
  agent artifact dirs.
- `assets/redact_secrets.py` — the redactor, published to consuming repos
  as the pinned `redact-agent-secrets` pre-commit hook (root
  `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`). Writes `[REDACTED:<rule-id>]`, the sentinel
  SpecStory also writes natively; `--legacy` writes the pre-2.4.0
  placeholders instead. Release procedure in
  `references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`.

## Reference files

- [`references/transcript-session-discovery.md`](references/transcript-session-discovery.md)
  — SpecStory / Claude session layouts and the `$PWD → slug` algorithm.
  Read when `find-session.sh` returns empty or ambiguous results.
- [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md)
  — three-layer defense (redact → gitleaks → `scan-staged.sh`),
  allowlist design, sync procedure for the bundled redactor. Read
  when tuning rules or debugging unexpected pre-commit failures.
- [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md)
  — what SpecStory >= 2.4.0 redacts on its own, measured per secret class and
  per context, plus the upstream PRs, config knobs, and why our layer is still
  load-bearing. Read before changing anything about redaction placeholders.
- [`references/remediation.md`](references/remediation.md) —
  rotate-first runbook for "I committed / pushed a secret". Read
  **before** any `git filter-repo` / `git push --force` action.

## Tests

The skill ships with a three-level test suite under
[`tests/`](tests/README.md). Run from repo root:

```bash
make test-skill
```

- `test_redact_secrets.py` — pytest for pure redactor functions.
- `test_gitleaks_corpus.py` — golden-corpus fixtures staged in tmp git
  repos, asserting real-key shapes fire and example shapes are
  allowlisted only inside configured artifact dirs.
- `test_scan_staged.sh` — exit-code contract for
  `scripts/scan-staged.sh` (0 / 20 / 30 / 2).
- `test_specstory_coverage.py` — locks in that SpecStory still redacts by
  default and still writes `[REDACTED:<label>]`; skips without the CLI.

The corpus + shell tests skip gracefully when `gitleaks` isn't on
`PATH`. See [`tests/README.md`](tests/README.md) for what each
regression the suite locks in.
